`docs/reference/regex.md`:

```md
# Regular expressions

A regular expression is a pattern for text: "starts with `BP_`", "ends in a number", "contains *potion*, in any case". In Grembyte they are useful in the JavaScript of [scripts](../guide/scripts.md), [hook templates](../guide/templates.md), method hooks and the options of choice parameters, wherever names or texts of the game are picked, cleaned up or taken apart. They are JavaScript's regular expressions; this page covers the part needed for that. If JavaScript itself is new to you, start with [JavaScript in Grembyte](javascript.md).

The filters in Grembyte's own windows (catalog, code explorer, trace, monitor) are no regular expressions: they keep the rows containing every word typed.

## Writing one

```js
const potion = /potion/i;              // a literal between slashes, flags after it
const set = new RegExp("^" + name);    // built from text at run time
```

| Method | Gives | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `re.test(text)` | `true` if the pattern occurs | `/^BP_/.test(obj.className)` |
| `text.match(re)` | the first match and its groups, or `null` | `"Gold: 600".match(/\d+/)[0]` → `"600"` |
| `text.matchAll(re)` | every match (needs the `g` flag) | `[..."a1 b22".matchAll(/\d+/g)].map(m => m[0])` → `["1", "22"]` |
| `text.replace(re, by)` | the text with the match replaced (every match with `g`) | `"BP_Hero_C_2".replace(/_\d+$/, "")` → `"BP_Hero_C"` |
| `text.split(re)` | the parts between matches | `"a, b;c".split(/[,;]\s*/)` → `["a", "b", "c"]` |
| `text.search(re)` | the position of the first match, or -1 | `"x=5".search(/\d/)` → `2` |

## Building blocks

| Pattern | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `abc` | the characters `abc` |
| `.` | any character except a line break |
| `\d` / `\D` | a digit / anything else |
| `\w` / `\W` | a letter, digit or `_` / anything else |
| `\s` / `\S` | white space (space, tab, line break) / anything else |
| `[abc]` | one of `a`, `b`, `c` |
| `[a-z0-9_]` | one character from these ranges |
| `[^abc]` | one character that is none of them |
| `^` / `$` | the start / the end of the text |
| `\b` | a word boundary: `\bgold\b` finds `gold`, not `golden` |
| `a|b` | `a` or `b` |
| `(…)` | a group: what it matched is kept (`m[1]`, `m[2]`, …) |
| `(?<name>…)` | a named group (`m.groups.name`) |
| `(?:…)` | a group that keeps nothing, just for `|` or a quantifier |
| `(?=…)` / `(?!…)` | followed by / not followed by, without consuming it |

### How often

| Quantifier | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `a?` | `a` or nothing |
| `a*` | any number of `a`, also none |
| `a+` | at least one `a` |
| `a{3}` / `a{2,5}` / `a{2,}` | exactly 3 / 2 to 5 / at least 2 |
| `a+?`, `a*?` | as few as possible instead of as many (*lazy*) |

### Flags

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `i` | ignore case: `/potion/i` finds `Potion` |
| `g` | every match (`matchAll`, `replace` of all) |
| `m` | `^` and `$` at every line, not only at the start and end of the text |
| `s` | `.` matches line breaks too |
| `u` | full Unicode (`\u{1F600}`, letters of every script with `\p{L}`) |

### Characters with a meaning

`. * + ? ^ $ ( ) [ ] { } | \ /` mean something in a pattern. To match one of them literally, put a backslash before it: `AttributeSetCore\.Might`, `\(Clone\)`, `\$`. When a pattern is built from text with `new RegExp`, the backslash itself is written twice in the string: `new RegExp("\\d+")`.

## In Grembyte

**Unreal names with a running number.** Unreal often numbers objects anew on every load: `AttributeSet_Health_2147445233`, `BP_Hero_C_1`. Cut the number off, or look for the start:

```js
const set = ctx.gas.findSet(/^AttributeSet_Health/);      // its name, or null
const base = obj.name.replace(/_\d+$/, "");               // "BP_Hero_C_1" -> "BP_Hero_C"
```

**Picking objects by name.** Count the enemies whose class starts with `BP_Enemy_` or `BP_Boss_`:

```js
let count = 0;
ctx.forEach("Actor", actor => { if (/^BP_(Enemy|Boss)_/.test(actor.className)) count++; });
return count;
```

**Options of a choice parameter.** Only the potions of the game's item list, sorted by name (Gothic 1 Remake, see the [Unreal page](../engines/unreal.md#example-a-script-with-a-choice-parameter)):

```js
return ctx.call("CheatModeHelper:GetAllItems", "")
  .filter(item => /^ItFo_Potion/.test(item.className))
  .map(item => ({ label: String(item.m_Name), value: item.className }))
  .sort((a, b) => a.label.localeCompare(b.label));
```

**Numbers from a text.** A label or log line of the game holds a value:

```js
const text = "Mana: 12.5 / 50";
const m = text.match(/Mana:\s*(?<now>[\d.]+)\s*\/\s*(?<max>\d+)/);
if (m) ctx.log(`mana ${Number(m.groups.now)} of ${Number(m.groups.max)}`);
```

**Checking a text parameter.** A script asks for a name: refuse anything but letters, digits and `_`:

```js
if (!/^\w{1,32}$/.test(ctx.args.name)) return "Only letters, digits and _ (at most 32)";
```

**Byte patterns are something else.** `ctx.native.scan("48 8B 05 ?? ?? ?? ??")` takes hex bytes with `??` for any byte, not a regular expression (see [ctx.native](script-context.md#native-code-ctxnative)).

## Pitfalls

- **`g` and `test`:** a regular expression with the `g` flag remembers where its last match ended (`lastIndex`), so calling `test` again on another text may start in the middle. Use `g` only with `matchAll` and `replace`.
- **Greedy matches:** `".+"` in `"a" and "b"` matches all of `"a" and "b"`; `".+?"` matches `"a"`.
- **Anchors:** without `^` and `$` a pattern may match anywhere: `/\d+/.test("Level 3 hero")` is true. `/^\d+$/` wants nothing but digits.
- **Hooks run often:** a hook template runs on every write of a value. A literal `/…/` costs nothing there; building patterns with `new RegExp` on every call does.
- **Not for everything:** nested structures (JSON, brackets inside brackets) are beyond regular expressions; `JSON.parse` reads JSON.

## Trying patterns

[regex101](https://regex101.com/) explains a pattern piece by piece and shows what it matches; choose the flavor *ECMAScript (JavaScript)*. In Grembyte, a script with `ctx.log(text.match(/…/))` shows the match on real game text.

```

`docs/reference/script-context.md`:

```md
# Script context (`ctx`)

The object a script in the [Scripts](../guide/scripts.md) tab receives. It is separate from the [hook context](hook-context.md).

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.find(className[, objectName])` | Find a live object in Unity or Unreal. In Unity these are Unity objects (GameObjects, components); plain C# objects are reached through `ctx.static`. Unreal also accepts the object's name within its outer; class default objects and Widget Blueprint templates are not returned. |
| `ctx.findClass(className)` | Unreal: get a class object, for example for a `TSubclassOf` parameter. |
| `ctx.forEach(className, callback)` | Call `callback` for each live object of the class; stop early by returning `false`. |
| `ctx.outerName(object)` | Unreal: get an object's name including its outer, useful with `ctx.find`. |
| `ctx.call(method, ...args)` | Call a static game method, by a dotted name or the `Namespace.Class:Method` form shown in catalogs. A parameter list after it, as **Copy signature** gives it, is ignored: the method taking as many arguments as given is called. |
| `ctx.static(field)` | Mono and IL2CPP: read a static field, e.g. `ctx.static("HermesQuest.GameState.Current")` – the way to objects that are no Unity objects. |
| `ctx.gas` | Unreal games with the Gameplay Ability System: `attributes()` lists the sets; `get(name)` returns `{base, current}`, or `null` if there is no player; `setBase(name, value)` changes the base value through the game's code, keeping active effects; `findSet(regex)` returns the name of the player's first set the regular expression (a `RegExp` or its text) matches, or `null`. Names are `"Attribute"` or `"Set.Attribute"`; a set whose object Unreal numbers anew on every load (`AttributeSet_Health_2147445233`) is also found without the number (`"AttributeSet_Health.Health"`). |
| `ctx.native` | Machine code without an engine: find functions by their bytes and call them. See [below](#native-code-ctxnative). |
| `ctx.args` | Values of the script's parameters, by name. |
| `ctx.lang` | Current app language: `"de"` or `"en"`. |
| `ctx.log(...)` | Write to the script log. |
| `ctx.state` | Per-script state kept between runs. |
| `ctx.runs` | Number of earlier runs. |
| `ctx.scriptId` | The script's id. |

## Object wrappers

Objects of the game – from `ctx.find`, `ctx.forEach`, `ctx.static` and method results in scripts, `ctx.this`, object arguments and results in [method hooks](hook-context.md#method-hooks) – are wrappers. Every use reads from or writes to the game at that moment:

| Use | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Read a field or property (a property runs its getter in the game) | `player.Health`, `player.IsDead` |
| Write a field, or a property (which calls its setter) | `player.Stats.Gold = 500` |
| Call a method, instance or static, with its result | `player.Heal(10)` |
| Read or write a static field of the object's class (Mono, IL2CPP), the same as `ctx.static` | `gameState.s_playerCharacter` |
| The class name | `player.className` |
| The address of the object | `player.address` |
| Unity: the name of a GameObject or component, else `null`; Unreal: the object's name | `player.name` |
| Unity: a component of a GameObject (or of a component's GameObject) by class name, or `null` | `attacker.component("CharacterStats")` |
| Call a method by name, read a field or a property by name | `player.call("Heal", 10)`, `player.field("Gold")`, `player.get("IsDead")` |

The wrapper's own names come first: `name`, `className`, `address`, `field`, `get`, `call` and `component`. If the game has a field or method of one of these names, use `.field("name")`, `.get("name")` or `.call("name", …)`.

A wrapper returned from the script is shown as the result and can be opened in the object inspector.

## Native code (`ctx.native`)

Works in every game; in games without an engine adapter it is the way into the game (see [Scripts in native games](../guide/scripts.md#scripts-in-native-games)). Addresses are Frida `NativePointer`s; where a function takes one, a number or a text like `"0x140257270"` works too.

| Function | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `module([name])` | The game's executable as a Frida module (`name`, `base`, `size`, `path`), or the loaded module of that name. Under Wine this is the `.exe`, not what Frida's `Process.mainModule` reports. |
| `scan(pattern[, module])` | The one address where the byte pattern is found in the module (default: the executable). `pattern` is hex bytes with `??` (or `?`) for any byte, e.g. `"48 8B 05 ?? ?? ?? ?? C3"`; spaces are optional. No match or several matches throw an error, so a pattern that an update broke does not call the wrong code. Results are remembered while the module stays loaded. |
| `scanAll(pattern[, module])` | Every address where the pattern is found, lowest first. |
| `rip(address, dispOffset, length)` | The target of an x64 instruction's RIP-relative operand: the 32-bit displacement at `address + dispOffset`, counted from the instruction's end at `address + length`. `cmp dword [rip+x], 0` (`83 3D x x x x 00`) has `rip(at, 2, 7)`; `mov rax, [rip+x]` (`48 8B 05 x x x x`) has `rip(at, 3, 7)`. |
| `fn(address, returnType, argTypes[, abi])` | A callable native function (Frida's `NativeFunction`), e.g. `fn(at, "void", ["int", "uint8"])(11, 0)`. Types are Frida's: `"void"`, `"int"`, `"uint8"`, `"float"`, `"pointer"` and so on. The calling convention defaults to the platform's (Windows x64 under Wine, System V on Linux). |


```

`docs/wine-proton.md`:

```md
# Wine and Proton

Grembyte works with Windows games running under Wine or Steam's Proton on Linux. Scans, writes and the pointer scan read the game's memory as with any process. For write watches and value hooks, Frida is the default, but the Linux `ptrace` backend can do both without injecting into the game (see [32-bit games](#32-bit-games)). Engine tools, native trace and monitor, and scripts use Frida inside the game and need its Windows gadget.

## The Frida gadget

`frida.attach` crashes Wine processes. Instead, Grembyte loads Frida's Windows build of its *gadget* into the game as an ordinary DLL. Inside the game it sees PE modules, Windows threads and the Win64 calling convention the way the game does, and Grembyte connects to it over a local TCP port.

The gadget has to match the installed Frida version and the game's architecture: `frida-gadget-<version>-windows-<x86|x86_64>.dll`. Grembyte caches it in its data folder (`~/.local/share/grembyte/gadget/`, see [files](reference/files.md)). The gadget listens on `127.0.0.1` only, so it is not reachable from other computers. Grembyte checks a downloaded gadget's SHA-256 checksum against the one GitHub publishes for that Frida release (releases from before 2025 list none; Grembyte then logs a warning).

**Automatic downloads are off by default.** When the matching gadget is missing as you select a Wine/Proton game, Grembyte asks whether to download it from GitHub:

- Approving downloads it and turns automatic downloads on for future missing gadgets.
- Declining leaves them off.

You can also enable automatic downloads in advance under **Settings → General … → Wine/Proton → Automatically download the Wine/Proton Frida gadget**.

**File → Check Frida Gadget Version …** checks locally for the gadget matching the installed Frida version – for the selected game's architecture, or for both x86 and x86_64 when none is selected – and offers a one-time download. It does not query GitHub for a newer Frida release. While Frida uses a Wine gadget, the status bar adds **(Update available)** when the matching gadget file is missing.

The gadget stays loaded until the game exits.

## Loading the gadget

A small Windows program, `grembyte-inject-x86_64.exe` or `grembyte-inject-x86.exe`, loads the gadget: Grembyte starts it with the game's Wine and prefix, and it loads the DLL into the game with `CreateRemoteThread` on `LoadLibraryW`. If that fails, Grembyte falls back to ptrace for 64-bit games: it parks one of the game's threads at a Windows function the game calls often and lets that thread load the DLL.

The helper executables are not in the repository. Grembyte builds them the first time a Wine game needs them, with MinGW or zig; the [installation](getting-started/installation.md#for-windows-games-under-wine-or-proton) lists the packages per distribution. To build them by hand:

```bash
sh grembyte/attach/inject/build.sh
```

They land in `build/inject/`; `GREMBYTE_INJECT_DIR` points Grembyte to executables elsewhere.

## 32-bit games

The helper also loads the x86 gadget into 32-bit games, and the engine tools work there. Value hooks, however, need 64-bit code: for 32-bit Wine/Proton games Grembyte picks the ptrace backend for the watch and hooks by itself.

## Known limits

- **Large traces** of tens of thousands of methods froze or crashed games under Wine. Grembyte limits the trace there (5000 methods by default, see [settings](guide/settings.md)).
- **Steam Linux Runtime:** the helper runs outside Steam's container and needs the shared `/tmp` and `/dev/shm`.

```

// Errors whose text grembyte renders in the user's language (see messages.py):
// the message carries a catalog key and its values, marked so grembyte finds
// them in an RPC error, a stack or a sent payload.
function grembyteMessage(key, params) {
  const values = JSON.stringify(params || {}, (name, value) =>
    (typeof value === 'bigint' || value instanceof NativePointer || value instanceof Int64
      || value instanceof UInt64) ? value.toString() : value)
    .replace(/⟦/g, '\\u27e6').replace(/⟧/g, '\\u27e7');
  return `⟦grembyte:${key}:${values}⟧`;
}

function grembyteError(key, params) {
  return new Error(grembyteMessage(key, params));
}

`grembyte/agent/platform.js`:

```js
let threadSpawner = null;

function spawnThread(start, arg) {
  if (threadSpawner === null) {
    if (Process.platform === 'windows') {
      const kernel32 = Process.getModuleByName('kernel32.dll');
      const create = new NativeFunction(kernel32.getExportByName('CreateThread'),
        'pointer', ['pointer', 'size_t', 'pointer', 'pointer', 'uint32', 'pointer']);
      const close = new NativeFunction(kernel32.getExportByName('CloseHandle'),
        'int', ['pointer']);
      threadSpawner = (routine, parameter) => {
        const thread = create(NULL, 0, routine, parameter, 0, NULL);
        if (thread.isNull())
          throw grembyteError('error.platform.create_thread');
        close(thread);
      };
    } else {
      const create = new NativeFunction(Module.getGlobalExportByName('pthread_create'),
        'int', ['pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer']);
      const detach = new NativeFunction(Module.getGlobalExportByName('pthread_detach'),
        'int', ['pointer']);
      threadSpawner = (routine, parameter) => {
        const handle = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize);
        const code = create(handle, NULL, routine, parameter);
        if (code !== 0)
          throw grembyteError('error.platform.pthread_create', { code });
        detach(handle.readPointer());
      };
    }
  }
  threadSpawner(start, arg);
}

function watchUnmaps(onUnmap) {
  if (Process.platform !== 'windows')
    return Interceptor.attach(Module.getGlobalExportByName('munmap'), {
      onEnter(args) {
        onUnmap(args[0], args[0].add(args[1]));
      }
    });
  // Under Wine the game's Windows code frees memory through ntdll.
  const MEM_DECOMMIT = 0x4000, MEM_RELEASE = 0x8000, MEM_FREE = 0x10000;
  // MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION: BaseAddress, AllocationBase, RegionSize, State
  const wide = Process.pointerSize === 8;
  const INFO_SIZE = wide ? 48 : 28;
  const ALLOCATION_BASE = wide ? 8 : 4, REGION_SIZE = wide ? 24 : 12, STATE = wide ? 32 : 16;
  const currentProcess = ptr(wide ? '0xffffffffffffffff' : '0xffffffff');
  const query = new NativeFunction(
    Process.getModuleByName('kernel32.dll').getExportByName('VirtualQuery'),
    'pointer', ['pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer']);
  const ntdll = Process.getModuleByName('ntdll.dll');
  function allocationEnd(base) {
    // Size 0 means the whole allocation at ``base``; its regions all have
    // ``base`` as AllocationBase.
    const info = Memory.alloc(INFO_SIZE);
    let cursor = base;
    while (!query(cursor, info, ptr(INFO_SIZE)).isNull()
           && info.add(ALLOCATION_BASE).readPointer().equals(base)
           && info.add(STATE).readU32() !== MEM_FREE)
      cursor = info.readPointer().add(info.add(REGION_SIZE).readPointer());
    return cursor;
  }
  const listeners = [
    Interceptor.attach(ntdll.getExportByName('NtFreeVirtualMemory'), {
      onEnter(args) {
        if (!args[0].equals(currentProcess)
            || (args[3].toUInt32() & (MEM_DECOMMIT | MEM_RELEASE)) === 0)
          return;
        const start = args[1].readPointer();
        const size = args[2].readPointer();
        onUnmap(start, size.isNull() ? allocationEnd(start) : start.add(size));
      }
    }),
    Interceptor.attach(ntdll.getExportByName('NtUnmapViewOfSection'), {
      onEnter(args) {
        if (args[0].equals(currentProcess))
          onUnmap(args[1], allocationEnd(args[1]));
      }
    })
  ];
  return { detach() { listeners.forEach(listener => listener.detach()); } };
}

let mainThread = null;

function mainThreadId() {
  if (mainThread !== null)
    return mainThread;
  if (Process.platform !== 'windows') {
    mainThread = Process.id;
    return mainThread;
  }
  const kernel32 = Process.getModuleByName('kernel32.dll');
  const fn = (name, ret, args) => new NativeFunction(kernel32.getExportByName(name), ret, args);
  const open = fn('OpenThread', 'pointer', ['uint32', 'int', 'uint32']);
  const times = fn('GetThreadTimes', 'int', ['pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer']);
  const close = fn('CloseHandle', 'int', ['pointer']);
  const THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION = 0x0800;
  const filetimes = Memory.alloc(4 * 8);  // creation, exit, kernel, user
  let first = null;
  for (const thread of Process.enumerateThreads()) {
    const handle = open(THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, 0, thread.id);
    if (handle.isNull())
      continue;
    const ok = times(handle, filetimes, filetimes.add(8), filetimes.add(16), filetimes.add(24));
    close(handle);
    if (!ok)
      continue;
    const created = BigInt(filetimes.readU64().toString());
    if (first === null || created < first.created
        || (created === first.created && thread.id < first.id))
      first = { id: thread.id, created };
  }
  if (first === null)
    return Process.id;  // not cached: try again next time
  mainThread = first.id;
  return mainThread;
}

// Unity games out of focus may stop running frames: the main thread then
// waits in GetMessage for its window's next message, and calls nothing an
// engine's main-thread hook (runtime_invoke) sees. wakeMainThread hooks the
// main thread's next GetMessage and posts it an empty message (WM_NULL, which
// programs ignore), so ``onMain`` runs there, between two passes of its
// message loop. Windows (and Wine) only; elsewhere it does nothing.
//
// The thread then sleeps in the hooked GetMessage again, and Frida waits for
// it to leave before the script can unload: detaching posts another empty
// message, so it leaves at once.

const WM_NULL = 0;

function wakeMainThread(onMain) {
  // [listener] to detach once ``onMain`` did its work; [] if not Windows.
  if (Process.platform !== 'windows')
    return [];
  const user32 = Process.findModuleByName('user32.dll');
  const post = user32 === null ? null : user32.findExportByName('PostThreadMessageW');
  if (post === null)
    return [];
  const postMessage = new NativeFunction(post, 'int', ['uint32', 'uint32', 'pointer', 'pointer']);
  const main = mainThreadId();
  const listeners = [];
  for (const name of ['GetMessageA', 'GetMessageW']) {
    const address = user32.findExportByName(name);
    if (address !== null)
      listeners.push(Interceptor.attach(address, {
        onEnter() {
          if (Process.getCurrentThreadId() === main)
            onMain();
        }
      }));
  }
  if (listeners.length === 0)
    return [];
  postMessage(main, WM_NULL, NULL, NULL);
  return [{
    detach() {
      listeners.forEach(listener => listener.detach());
      postMessage(main, WM_NULL, NULL, NULL);
    }
  }];
}

let threadPauser = null;

function pauseThreads() {
  if (Process.platform !== 'windows')
    return null;
  if (threadPauser === null) {
    const kernel32 = Process.getModuleByName('kernel32.dll');
    const fn = (name, ret, args) => new NativeFunction(kernel32.getExportByName(name), ret, args);
    threadPauser = {
      open: fn('OpenThread', 'pointer', ['uint32', 'int', 'uint32']),
      suspend: fn('SuspendThread', 'uint32', ['pointer']),
      resume: fn('ResumeThread', 'uint32', ['pointer']),
      context: fn('GetThreadContext', 'int', ['pointer', 'pointer']),
      close: fn('CloseHandle', 'int', ['pointer'])
    };
  }
  const THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME = 0x0002, THREAD_GET_CONTEXT = 0x0008;
  const SUSPEND_FAILED = 0xffffffff;
  // CONTEXT differs between x64 and x86 in size, layout and flag values.
  const wide = Process.pointerSize === 8;
  const CONTEXT_SIZE = wide ? 0x4d0 : 0x2cc, CONTEXT_FLAGS = wide ? 0x30 : 0;
  const CONTEXT_CONTROL = wide ? 0x100001 : 0x10001;
  const t = threadPauser;
  const self = Process.getCurrentThreadId();
  const handles = [];
  for (const thread of Process.enumerateThreads()) {
    if (thread.id === self)
      continue;
    const handle = t.open(THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME | THREAD_GET_CONTEXT, 0, thread.id);
    if (handle.isNull())
      continue;  // ended meanwhile
    if (t.suspend(handle) === SUSPEND_FAILED) {
      t.close(handle);
      continue;
    }
    handles.push(handle);
  }
  // SuspendThread only asks the thread to stop; reading its context returns
  // once it has. CONTEXT must be 16-byte aligned.
  const context = Memory.alloc(CONTEXT_SIZE + 16).add(15)
    .and(ptr(wide ? '0xfffffffffffffff0' : '0xfffffff0'));
  for (const handle of handles) {
    context.add(CONTEXT_FLAGS).writeU32(CONTEXT_CONTROL);
    t.context(handle, context);
  }
  return handles;
}

function resumeThreads(paused) {
  if (paused === null)
    return;
  for (const handle of paused) {
    threadPauser.resume(handle);
    threadPauser.close(handle);
  }
}

let codeAllocator = null;

function allocateCode(size) {
  // Executable memory that stays when the agent unloads: game threads may
  // still run code there (VirtualAlloc, or mmap).
  if (codeAllocator === null) {
    if (Process.platform === 'windows') {
      const virtualAlloc = new NativeFunction(
        Process.getModuleByName('kernel32.dll').getExportByName('VirtualAlloc'),
        'pointer', ['pointer', 'size_t', 'uint32', 'uint32']);
      const MEM_COMMIT_RESERVE = 0x3000, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE = 0x40;
      codeAllocator = length => virtualAlloc(NULL, length, MEM_COMMIT_RESERVE,
                                             PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE);
    } else {
      const mmap = new NativeFunction(Module.getGlobalExportByName('mmap'), 'pointer',
                                      ['pointer', 'size_t', 'int', 'int', 'int', 'long']);
      const PROT_RWX = 7, MAP_PRIVATE_ANONYMOUS = 0x22;
      codeAllocator = length => {
        const memory = mmap(NULL, length, PROT_RWX, MAP_PRIVATE_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
        return memory.equals(ptr(-1)) ? NULL : memory;
      };
    }
  }
  const memory = codeAllocator(size);
  if (memory.isNull())
    throw grembyteError('error.platform.code_alloc', { size });
  return memory;
}

let programModuleFound = null;

function programModule() {
  // The game's executable. Under Wine Frida's Process.mainModule is just the
  // first module it lists (e.g. netapi32.dll or uxtheme.dll); Windows itself
  // knows better.
  if (programModuleFound !== null)
    return programModuleFound;
  if (Process.platform === 'windows') {
    const getModuleHandle = new NativeFunction(
      Process.getModuleByName('kernel32.dll').getExportByName('GetModuleHandleW'),
      'pointer', ['pointer']);
    const module = Process.findModuleByAddress(getModuleHandle(NULL));
    if (module !== null) {
      programModuleFound = module;
      return module;
    }
  }
  programModuleFound = Process.mainModule;
  return programModuleFound;
}

```

`grembyte/agent/platform.py`:

```py
"""Platform layer of the Frida agents: what differs between Linux and Windows.

A native game shows the agent Linux; a Wine/Proton game shows it Windows,
because Frida runs there as its Windows gadget (see wine_gadget.py). Engine
adapters and features use these helpers instead of calling either system's
API themselves.

``spawnThread(start, arg)``
    Run the native function ``start(arg)`` on a new thread nobody waits for
    (``pthread_create``, or ``CreateThread`` under Wine). Throws on failure.
``watchUnmaps(onUnmap)``
    Call ``onUnmap(start, end)`` before memory is unmapped or released, while
    it is still mapped (``munmap``; under Wine ``NtFreeVirtualMemory`` and
    ``NtUnmapViewOfSection``). Returns a listener with ``detach()``.
``mainThreadId()``
    The id of the process's first thread, where Unity runs its player loop.
    On Linux that is the process id; Windows gives threads ids of their own,
    so there it is the thread created first (``GetThreadTimes``).
``pauseThreads()`` / ``resumeThreads(paused)``
    Stop every thread of the game while the agent changes code in bulk, and
    let them run again. Frida's own threads keep running: they are not in
    ``Process.enumerateThreads()``. Windows only (``SuspendThread``, which Wine
    delays until a thread holds none of its internal locks); elsewhere
    ``pauseThreads`` returns null and does nothing. Under Wine, game threads
    entering freshly hooked code while Frida still hooks more could deadlock
    on a lock inside Frida's Windows gadget; Linux has no such problem.
``allocateCode(size)``
    Executable memory that is never freed, not even when the agent unloads
    (``VirtualAlloc``, or ``mmap``): for code game threads may still run.
``programModule()``
    The game's executable as a Frida module. Under Wine ``Process.mainModule``
    is just the first module Frida lists; ``GetModuleHandleW(NULL)`` knows.
"""

from grembyte.agent.source import MESSAGES_SOURCE, load_agent_source

PLATFORM_AGENT_SOURCE = MESSAGES_SOURCE + load_agent_source(__file__)

```

"""Load the JavaScript of a Frida agent from the .js file next to its module."""

from pathlib import Path


def load_agent_source(module_file, name=None):
    """Return the text of ``name`` (default: the module's name with .js) beside ``module_file``."""
    path = Path(module_file)
    return (path.with_name(name) if name else path.with_suffix(".js")).read_text(encoding="utf-8")


# Prepended to every agent source that reports errors (see grembyte.core.messages).
MESSAGES_SOURCE = load_agent_source(__file__, "messages.js")

`grembyte/attach/frida_attach.py`:

```py
"""Open a Frida session on a target process, native or Wine/Proton.

``frida.attach`` injects Frida's Linux agent, which crashes Wine processes:
it looks up the main program through the program headers the kernel recorded
for ``wine-preloader``, where nothing is mapped (Frida 17.23/17.24, Proton
11). For those, the session goes through the Windows build of
Frida's gadget instead (wine_gadget.py), which grembyte loads into the game
once and every worker then shares.

The session handed out records itself in the activity log (activity.py):
the agents loaded and unloaded, every RPC, script errors, and why the
session ended. It stands in for Frida's session and script otherwise.

The gadget under Wine closes the connection on any message from grembyte
larger than 128 KiB (Frida 17.24.3, Proton Experimental; agent to grembyte is
not limited). Larger agents go there through a small loader that receives
the source in parts and evaluates it.

Only one Frida host per game: each host process injects an agent of its
own, and two agents hooking the same function (Mono's runtime_invoke, which
every Unity feature uses to reach the main thread) crash the game when they
unhook in the wrong order. The sessions of one grembyte share one agent. So
``attach_alone`` refuses to attach while the game holds a Frida runtime of
another host (``error.attach.foreign_frida``).
Under Wine every grembyte connects to the same gadget and shares it.
"""

import threading
import time

import frida

from grembyte.attach import wine_gadget
from grembyte.core import activity, messages
from grembyte.platform import frida_agents, is_wine_process

# What Frida raises when attaching, loading or talking to an agent fails.
FRIDA_ERRORS = (
  frida.AddressInUseError,
  frida.ExecutableNotFoundError,
  frida.ExecutableNotSupportedError,
  frida.InvalidArgumentError,
  frida.InvalidOperationError,
  frida.NotSupportedError,
  frida.OperationCancelledError,
  frida.PermissionDeniedError,
  frida.ProcessNotFoundError,
  frida.ProcessNotRespondingError,
  frida.ProtocolError,
  frida.ServerNotRunningError,
  frida.TimedOutError,
  frida.TransportError,
)

# Raised by exports_sync calls when the agent-side RPC handler throws.
CLEANUP_ERRORS = FRIDA_ERRORS + (frida.RPCException, RuntimeError)

# Agents above this size are sent to the gadget in parts.
GADGET_SOURCE_LIMIT = 100_000
# Characters per part; even escaped as \uXXXX in JSON it stays below the limit.
GADGET_SOURCE_PART = 16_000
GADGET_LOAD_TIMEOUT = 30.0
LOADER_MESSAGE = "grembyte:source"
LOADED_KEY = "grembyte:loaded"
# Indirect eval runs the agent as global code, as Frida would.
LOADER_SOURCE = f"""\
const parts = [];
function onPart(message) {{
  if (message.part !== undefined) {{
    parts.push(message.part);
    recv('{LOADER_MESSAGE}', onPart);
    return;
  }}
  const source = parts.join('');
  parts.length = 0;
  try {{
    (0, eval)(source + '\\n//# sourceURL=/agent.js');
  }} finally {{
    send({{ '{LOADED_KEY}': true }});
  }}
}}
recv('{LOADER_MESSAGE}', onPart);
"""


_own_lock = threading.Lock()
# pid -> the Frida runtimes found right after this process attached: its agent
_own_agents = {}


def attach_alone(pid):
    """``frida.attach(pid)``, refused if the game holds a Frida runtime of
    another host: another grembyte or Frida tool, or a game with the gadget.

    A runtime this process noted after an earlier attach is its own, also
    while it unloads. One it did not note (a session opened past
    attach_session) is its own if attaching added no new agent: the sessions
    of one host share theirs. A new agent next to an unknown one means that
    one belongs to someone else; the new session is closed before any script
    runs in it."""
    before = frida_agents(pid)
    with _own_lock:
        unknown = (before or set()) - _own_agents.get(pid, set())
    session = frida.attach(pid)
    after = frida_agents(pid)
    if unknown and after is not None and after - before:
        try:
            session.detach()
        except CLEANUP_ERRORS:
            pass
        raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError("error.attach.foreign_frida", pid=pid)
    if after:
        with _own_lock:
            _own_agents[pid] = after
    return session


def attach_session(pid):
    """Return a Frida session on ``pid``; raises on failure.

    Under Wine the agent sees the process as Windows does: PE modules such as
    ``mono-2.0-bdwgc.dll``, ``Process.platform === 'windows'`` and the Win64
    calling convention.
    """
    wine = is_wine_process(pid)
    session_number, kind = activity.current_session()
    began = time.monotonic()
    try:
        session = wine_gadget.connect(pid) if wine else attach_alone(pid)
    except Exception as error:
        activity.record("attach_failed", pid=pid, session=session_number, kind=kind,
                        via="gadget" if wine else "frida.attach",
                        error=messages.describe(error))
        raise
    activity.record("attached", pid=pid, session=session_number, kind=kind,
                    via="gadget" if wine else "frida.attach",
                    seconds=round(time.monotonic() - began, 3))
    return RecordedSession(session, pid, session_number, kind, gadget=wine)


FRIDA_THREAD_NAME = "frida-events"


def _name_frida_thread():
    # Frida calls back from a thread of its own, which Python calls "Dummy-<n>".
    thread = threading.current_thread()
    if thread.name.startswith("Dummy-"):
        thread.name = FRIDA_THREAD_NAME


class RecordedSession:
    """A Frida session that notes its scripts and its end in the activity log."""

    def __init__(self, session, pid, number, kind, gadget=False):
        self._session = session
        self.pid = pid
        self.number = number
        self.kind = kind
        self.gadget = gadget
        session.on("detached", self._on_detached)

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return getattr(self._session, name)

    def _on_detached(self, reason, crash=None):
        _name_frida_thread()
        fields = {}
        if crash is not None:
            fields["crash"] = {"summary": getattr(crash, "summary", None),
                               "report": (getattr(crash, "report", "") or "")[:4000]}
        activity.flush()
        activity.record("detached", pid=self.pid, session=self.number, kind=self.kind,
                        reason=str(reason), in_flight=activity.in_flight(), **fields)

    def create_script(self, source, *args, **kwargs):
        if self.gadget and len(source.encode()) > GADGET_SOURCE_LIMIT:
            script = self._session.create_script(LOADER_SOURCE, *args, **kwargs)
            return RecordedScript(script, self, len(source), deferred=source)
        script = self._session.create_script(source, *args, **kwargs)
        return RecordedScript(script, self, len(source))

    def detach(self):
        activity.record("detach", pid=self.pid, session=self.number, kind=self.kind)
        return self._session.detach()


def _is_loaded_message(message):
    payload = message.get("payload")
    return (message.get("type") == "send" and isinstance(payload, dict)
            and payload.get(LOADED_KEY) is True)


class RecordedScript:
    """A Frida script that notes its loading, unloading, RPCs and errors."""

    def __init__(self, script, session, size, deferred=None):
        self._script = script
        self._session = session
        self._size = size
        # The agent's source when the script is the gadget loader
        self._deferred = deferred
        self.agent = f"{session.kind or 'agent'}#{activity.new_agent()}"
        self._loaded = None
        self._exports = None

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return getattr(self._script, name)

    def _fields(self):
        return {"agent": self.agent, "pid": self._session.pid, "session": self._session.number}

    def on(self, signal, callback):
        if signal == "message":
            original = callback

            def callback(message, data):  # pylint: disable=function-redefined
                _name_frida_thread()
                if _is_loaded_message(message):
                    return None
                if message.get("type") == "error":
                    activity.record("agent_error", **self._fields(),
                                    description=message.get("description"),
                                    where=f"{message.get('fileName', '')}:"
                                          f"{message.get('lineNumber', '')}")
                return original(message, data)
        return self._script.on(signal, callback)

    def load(self):
        began = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = self._script.load()
            if self._deferred is not None:
                self._load_deferred()
        except Exception as error:
            activity.record("agent_load_failed", **self._fields(), error=messages.describe(error))
            raise
        self._loaded = time.monotonic()
        activity.record("agent_loaded", **self._fields(), size=self._size,
                        seconds=round(self._loaded - began, 3))
        return result

    def _load_deferred(self):
        # Like Frida's load: returns once the agent's global code has run;
        # its errors arrive as "error" messages.
        loaded = threading.Event()

        def on_message(message, _data):
            if _is_loaded_message(message):
                loaded.set()

        source, self._deferred = self._deferred, None
        self._script.on("message", on_message)
        try:
            for start in range(0, len(source), GADGET_SOURCE_PART):
                self._script.post({"type": LOADER_MESSAGE,
                                   "part": source[start:start + GADGET_SOURCE_PART]})
            self._script.post({"type": LOADER_MESSAGE})
            if not loaded.wait(GADGET_LOAD_TIMEOUT):
                raise frida.TimedOutError("Timed out while loading the agent through the gadget")
        finally:
            self._script.off("message", on_message)

    def unload(self):
        activity.flush(self.agent)
        began = time.monotonic()
        try:
            return self._script.unload()
        finally:
            activity.record("agent_unloaded", **self._fields(),
                            lived=None if self._loaded is None
                            else round(began - self._loaded, 3),
                            seconds=round(time.monotonic() - began, 3))

    @property
    def exports_sync(self):
        if self._exports is None:
            self._exports = RecordedExports(self._script.exports_sync, self.agent)
        return self._exports


class RecordedExports:
    """An agent's RPC exports, timed into the activity log."""

    def __init__(self, exports, agent):
        self._exports = exports
        self._agent = agent

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        function = getattr(self._exports, name)
        agent = self._agent

        def call(*args, **kwargs):
            handle = activity.rpc_started(agent, name)
            try:
                result = function(*args, **kwargs)
            except Exception as error:
                activity.rpc_ended(handle, messages.describe(error).split("\n", 1)[0])
                raise
            activity.rpc_ended(handle)
            return result
        call.__name__ = name
        return call

```

`grembyte/attach/inject/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Build grembyte-inject for 64- and 32-bit Wine games into build/inject/ of the
# repository (or $OUT_DIR); the executables are not kept in git.
# Uses MinGW when installed (sudo dnf install mingw64-gcc mingw32-gcc), else zig
# (pip install ziglang) through $PYTHON (Grembyte passes its own Python, so a
# ziglang in its virtual environment is found), else python3.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-../../../build/inject}"
mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"
FLAGS="-O2 -s -Wall -o"
LIBS="-lshell32"
FAILED=0

# build <output> <compiler command...>
build() {
    out=$OUT_DIR/$1
    shift
    if "$@" inject.c $FLAGS "$out" $LIBS; then
        echo "OK:     $out"
    else
        echo "FAILED: $out" >&2
        FAILED=1
    fi
}

if command -v x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc >/dev/null && command -v i686-w64-mingw32-gcc >/dev/null; then
    echo "Toolchain: MinGW"
    build grembyte-inject-x86_64.exe x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc
    build grembyte-inject-x86.exe i686-w64-mingw32-gcc
else
    ZIG="${ZIG:-${PYTHON:-python3} -m ziglang}"
    echo "Toolchain: zig ($ZIG)"
    build grembyte-inject-x86_64.exe $ZIG cc -target x86_64-windows-gnu
    build grembyte-inject-x86.exe $ZIG cc -target x86-windows-gnu
fi

if [ "$FAILED" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Build succeeded."
else
    echo "Build failed." >&2
    exit 1
fi

```

`grembyte/attach/inject/inject.c`:

```c
/*
 * grembyte-inject: load a DLL into another process of the same Wine prefix.
 *
 * grembyte runs this with the wine and WINEPREFIX of a running game, so it
 * talks to the game's own wineserver. It uses the standard Windows route
 * (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread on LoadLibraryW)
 * and exits; no ptrace or breakpoint is involved.
 *
 *   grembyte-inject list
 *       One line per process:
 *       "<pid>\t<creation, Unix ms>\t<exe name>\t<32 or 64, 0 if unknown>".
 *   grembyte-inject inject <pid> <dll path> [LoadLibraryW address, hex]
 *       Prints "ok <module low 32 bits>" and exits 0, or "error <text>" and
 *       a non-zero code. Without an address the helper's own LoadLibraryW is
 *       used, which Wine maps at the same address in every process of a
 *       prefix.
 *
 * Build with MinGW or zig, once per architecture (see build.sh).
 */
#include <windows.h>
#include <tlhelp32.h>
#include <shellapi.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <wchar.h>

#define INJECT_TIMEOUT_MS 20000

static int fail(const char *what)
{
    printf("error %s (Windows error %lu)\n", what, GetLastError());
    fflush(stdout);
    return 2;
}

/* FILETIME (100 ns since 1601) to milliseconds since the Unix epoch. */
static unsigned long long unix_ms(FILETIME time)
{
    ULARGE_INTEGER value;
    value.LowPart = time.dwLowDateTime;
    value.HighPart = time.dwHighDateTime;
    return (value.QuadPart - 116444736000000000ULL) / 10000ULL;
}

/* 32 or 64 for another process, 0 if unknown. A 32-bit process on a 64-bit
   system runs under WoW64; on a purely 32-bit Wine everything is 32-bit. */
static int process_bits(HANDLE process)
{
    BOOL target_wow = FALSE, self_wow = FALSE;

    if (!IsWow64Process(process, &target_wow) ||
        !IsWow64Process(GetCurrentProcess(), &self_wow))
        return 0;
    if (target_wow)
        return 32;
    return sizeof(void *) == 4 && !self_wow ? 32 : 64;
}

static int list_processes(void)
{
    HANDLE snapshot = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0);
    PROCESSENTRY32W entry;

    if (snapshot == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)
        return fail("CreateToolhelp32Snapshot");
    entry.dwSize = sizeof(entry);
    if (Process32FirstW(snapshot, &entry)) {
        do {
            unsigned long long created = 0;
            int bits = 0;
            HANDLE process = OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, FALSE,
                                         entry.th32ProcessID);
            if (process) {
                FILETIME creation, exit_time, kernel, user;
                if (GetProcessTimes(process, &creation, &exit_time, &kernel, &user))
                    created = unix_ms(creation);
                bits = process_bits(process);
                CloseHandle(process);
            }
            /* UTF-8, so non-ASCII exe names survive the pipe to grembyte. */
            char name[MAX_PATH * 4];
            WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, entry.szExeFile, -1, name, sizeof(name),
                                NULL, NULL);
            printf("%lu\t%llu\t%s\t%d\n", entry.th32ProcessID, created, name, bits);
        } while (Process32NextW(snapshot, &entry));
    }
    CloseHandle(snapshot);
    fflush(stdout);
    return 0;
}

static int inject(DWORD pid, const wchar_t *dll, ULONG_PTR load_library)
{
    SIZE_T size = (wcslen(dll) + 1) * sizeof(wchar_t);
    HANDLE process, thread;
    LPVOID remote;
    DWORD code = 0, waited;

    if (!load_library)
        load_library = (ULONG_PTR)GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleW(L"kernel32.dll"),
                                                 "LoadLibraryW");
    if (!load_library)
        return fail("LoadLibraryW not found");

    process = OpenProcess(PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD | PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION |
                          PROCESS_VM_OPERATION | PROCESS_VM_WRITE | PROCESS_VM_READ,
                          FALSE, pid);
    if (!process)
        return fail("OpenProcess");
    remote = VirtualAllocEx(process, NULL, size, MEM_COMMIT | MEM_RESERVE,
                            PAGE_READWRITE);
    if (!remote) {
        CloseHandle(process);
        return fail("VirtualAllocEx");
    }
    if (!WriteProcessMemory(process, remote, dll, size, NULL)) {
        VirtualFreeEx(process, remote, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
        CloseHandle(process);
        return fail("WriteProcessMemory");
    }
    thread = CreateRemoteThread(process, NULL, 0, (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)load_library,
                                remote, 0, NULL);
    if (!thread) {
        VirtualFreeEx(process, remote, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
        CloseHandle(process);
        return fail("CreateRemoteThread");
    }
    waited = WaitForSingleObject(thread, INJECT_TIMEOUT_MS);
    if (waited != WAIT_OBJECT_0) {
        /* The thread may still read the path: leave the buffer allocated. */
        CloseHandle(thread);
        CloseHandle(process);
        printf("error LoadLibraryW did not return within %d ms\n", INJECT_TIMEOUT_MS);
        fflush(stdout);
        return 3;
    }
    GetExitCodeThread(thread, &code);
    CloseHandle(thread);
    VirtualFreeEx(process, remote, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
    CloseHandle(process);
    if (!code) {
        printf("error LoadLibraryW returned NULL\n");
        fflush(stdout);
        return 4;
    }
    printf("ok %lx\n", code);
    fflush(stdout);
    return 0;
}

int main(void)
{
    int argc = 0;
    wchar_t **argv = CommandLineToArgvW(GetCommandLineW(), &argc);

    if (argv && argc == 2 && !wcscmp(argv[1], L"list"))
        return list_processes();
    if (argv && (argc == 4 || argc == 5) && !wcscmp(argv[1], L"inject")) {
        DWORD pid = wcstoul(argv[2], NULL, 10);
        ULONG_PTR address = argc == 5 ? (ULONG_PTR)wcstoull(argv[4], NULL, 16) : 0;
        return inject(pid, argv[3], address);
    }
    printf("usage: grembyte-inject list | inject <pid> <dll> [LoadLibraryW hex]\n");
    return 1;
}

```

`grembyte/attach/ptrace_engine.py`:

```py
"""Shared ptrace machinery for hardware-watchpoint tools.

This is the injection-free core both the ptrace watch backend and the ptrace
hook backend build on. It drives the Linux ``ptrace`` API the way gdb does:
attach to every thread of a target, program the CPU debug registers (DR0-DR3
hold up to four watched addresses, DR7 their enable/length/condition bits, DR6
reports which one fired), resume the threads, and dispatch the SIGTRAPs that
accesses raise. Nothing is injected, so it works on targets Frida cannot
instrument, most notably Wine/Proton processes.

ptrace requires that every call for a tracee come from the one OS thread that
attached it, so a subclass runs its whole lifecycle inside a ``QThread``'s
``run``. The tracer must be 64-bit; the register layout here is x86-64's.
"""

import ctypes
import errno
import logging
import os
import signal
import sys
import time

from capstone import (  # pylint: disable=import-error
    CS_ARCH_X86,
    CS_MODE_32,
    CS_MODE_64,
    CS_AC_READ,
    CS_AC_WRITE,
    CS_OP_MEM,
    Cs,
)
from PySide6.QtCore import QThread  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core import messages
from grembyte.core.pointer import module_bases
from grembyte.platform import read_mappings


# ptrace request numbers (see <sys/ptrace.h>).
PTRACE_CONT = 7
PTRACE_DETACH = 17
PTRACE_PEEKUSER = 3
PTRACE_POKEUSER = 6
PTRACE_ATTACH = 16
PTRACE_SETOPTIONS = 0x4200
PTRACE_GETEVENTMSG = 0x4201
PTRACE_O_TRACECLONE = 0x00000008
PTRACE_EVENT_CLONE = 3

# x86-64 syscall number for tgkill(2); the debug-register layout below is
# x86-64's too, so this core is x86-64 only.
SYS_TGKILL = 234

# Offsets into ``struct user`` on x86-64: the general registers come first,
# the eight debug registers sit at u_debugreg[0..7].
USER_REGS_RIP = 128
USER_REGS_CS = 136
DEBUGREG_BASE = 848
DR_ADDRESS = [DEBUGREG_BASE + slot * 8 for slot in range(4)]  # DR0..DR3
DR6 = DEBUGREG_BASE + 6 * 8
DR7 = DEBUGREG_BASE + 7 * 8
WATCHPOINT_SLOTS = 4

# waitpid flags: __WALL also reaps thread (clone) children; __WNOTHREAD keeps
# to the tracees of the calling thread, so children other threads of grembyte
# started (subprocesses) are left to them.
_WALL = 0x40000000
_WNOTHREAD = 0x20000000
# os.WNOHANG is POSIX-only; fall back to Linux's value so the module still
# imports on Windows.
_WAIT_ANY = getattr(os, "WNOHANG", 1) | _WALL | _WNOTHREAD
# DR6 bits B0-B3: which watchpoint slot fired.
_DR6_SLOTS = 0xF

# x86 segment selector a thread runs under: 0x33 for 64-bit code, 0x23 for
# 32-bit (compat) code such as a 32-bit Wine process under a 64-bit kernel.
_CS_64BIT = 0x33

MAX_INSTRUCTION_SIZE = 15
# x86 decoding self-synchronizes: count how many earlier decode chains land on
# a candidate's start to tell the real instruction from a spurious decode.
SYNC_WINDOW = 48

_LENGTH_BITS = {1: 0b00, 2: 0b01, 4: 0b11, 8: 0b10}

log = logging.getLogger("grembyte.ptrace")

# ptrace is Linux's. Elsewhere this module still imports (wine_gadget needs
# its constants), but every ptrace call fails.
if sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
    _libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6", use_errno=True)
    _libc.ptrace.restype = ctypes.c_long
    _libc.ptrace.argtypes = [
        ctypes.c_long, ctypes.c_long, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p,
    ]
else:
    _libc = None


def _ptrace(request, pid, addr, data):
    """Call ``ptrace`` and raise OSError on failure."""
    if _libc is None:
        raise messages.LocalizedOSError("error.ptrace.linux_only", errno.ENOSYS,
                                       platform=sys.platform)
    ctypes.set_errno(0)
    result = _libc.ptrace(request, pid, ctypes.c_void_p(addr), ctypes.c_void_p(data))
    err = ctypes.get_errno()
    if result == -1 and err != 0:
        raise OSError(err, os.strerror(err))
    return result


def tgkill(pid, tid, sig):
    """Send ``sig`` to thread ``tid`` of process ``pid`` (tgkill(2))."""
    if _libc is None:
        raise messages.LocalizedOSError("error.ptrace.linux_only", errno.ENOSYS,
                                       platform=sys.platform)
    _libc.syscall(SYS_TGKILL, pid, tid, int(sig))


def _peek_user(pid, offset):
    """Read one word from the tracee's ``struct user`` as an unsigned value."""
    return _ptrace(PTRACE_PEEKUSER, pid, offset, 0) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF


def combined_dr7(slots):
    """Return the DR7 value that arms every slot in ``slots``.

    ``slots`` maps a slot index (0-3) to ``(size, reads)``. ``reads`` picks the
    condition: x86 offers write-only and read/write, but no read-only, so a
    read watch also traps writes.
    """
    value = 0
    for slot, (size, reads) in slots.items():
        length_bits = _LENGTH_BITS.get(size)
        if length_bits is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported watch size: {size}")
        condition = 0b11 if reads else 0b01  # 11 = read/write, 01 = write
        value |= 1 << (slot * 2)  # local enable for this slot
        value |= (condition | (length_bits << 2)) << (16 + slot * 4)
    return value


def watch_alignment_error(address, size):
    """Why a hardware watchpoint cannot cover ``size`` bytes at ``address``, or None.

    The CPU watches 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes at an address aligned to that length;
    the kernel refuses anything else (EINVAL).
    """
    if size not in _LENGTH_BITS:
        return messages.text("error.ptrace.watch_size", size=size)
    if address % size:
        return messages.text("error.ptrace.unaligned", address=f"{address:#x}", size=size)
    return None


def build_dr7(size, reads):
    """DR7 for a single watchpoint in slot 0 (kept for the watch backend)."""
    return combined_dr7({0: (size, reads)})


def _memory_operands(instruction):
    return [op for op in instruction.operands if op.type == CS_OP_MEM]


def _votes(engine, code, start):
    """Count decode chains ending before ``start`` that land exactly on it."""
    votes = 0
    for offset in range(max(0, start - SYNC_WINDOW), start):
        cursor = offset
        while cursor < start:
            chunk = next(engine.disasm(code[cursor:start], cursor, count=1), None)
            if chunk is None or chunk.size == 0:
                break
            cursor += chunk.size
        if cursor == start:
            votes += 1
    return votes


def decode_access(code, pc_offset, bits, reads):
    """Decide whether the instruction ending at ``pc_offset`` reads/writes.

    ``code`` holds bytes leading up to (not including) the trap PC, with the PC
    at index ``pc_offset``. A data breakpoint is a trap, so the PC is the
    instruction *after* the access. Returns ``(read, write)``; an undecodable
    access is reported as a write, which never hides a real write.
    """
    engine = Cs(CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_64 if bits == 64 else CS_MODE_32)
    engine.detail = True
    best = None  # (read, write) of the best-scoring candidate
    best_votes = -1
    for start in range(max(0, pc_offset - MAX_INSTRUCTION_SIZE), pc_offset):
        instruction = next(engine.disasm(code[start:pc_offset], start, count=1), None)
        if instruction is None or start + instruction.size != pc_offset:
            continue
        operands = _memory_operands(instruction)
        if not operands:
            continue
        votes = _votes(engine, code, start)
        if votes > best_votes:
            best_votes = votes
            best = (
                any(op.access & CS_AC_READ for op in operands),
                any(op.access & CS_AC_WRITE for op in operands),
            )
    if best is None:
        return (bool(reads), True)
    read, write = best
    if not reads:
        write = True  # a write watch only traps on writes
    return (read, write)


class PtraceWatchpointEngine(QThread):
    """Attach to a process and dispatch hardware-watchpoint traps.

    Subclasses fill :attr:`_slots` (``{slot: (address, size, reads)}``, up to
    :data:`WATCHPOINT_SLOTS` entries) and implement :meth:`_handle_trap`. The
    whole lifecycle must run inside :meth:`run`, because ptrace binds a tracee
    to the thread that attached it.
    """

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.pid = pid
        self._armed = set()
        self._slots = {}
        self._target_gone = False
        self._mappings = []
        self._bases = {}

    # -- introspection ------------------------------------------------------

    def _load_mappings(self):
        self._mappings = read_mappings(self.pid)
        self._bases = module_bases(self._mappings)

    def _site(self, pc):
        """Return ``module+offset`` for ``pc``, or its hex address."""
        for mapping in self._mappings:
            if mapping.start <= pc < mapping.end and mapping.module is not None:
                return f"{mapping.module}+{pc - self._bases[mapping.module]:#x}"
        return hex(pc)

    @staticmethod
    def _pc_bits(tid):
        """Return ``(pc, bits)`` of a stopped thread (bits: 32 or 64)."""
        pc = _peek_user(tid, USER_REGS_RIP)
        segment = _peek_user(tid, USER_REGS_CS)
        bits = 64 if segment == _CS_64BIT else 32
        if bits == 32:
            pc &= 0xFFFFFFFF
        return pc, bits

    @staticmethod
    def _explain(error):
        if error.errno == 1:  # EPERM
            return messages.text("error.ptrace.denied")
        if error.errno == 3:  # ESRCH
            return messages.text("error.ptrace.gone")
        return str(error)

    # -- attaching / arming -------------------------------------------------

    def _attach_all(self):
        """Attach every current thread and arm it. Returns warnings."""
        warnings = []
        for _ in range(2):  # a second pass catches threads born while attaching
            for tid in self._list_threads():
                if tid in self._armed:
                    continue
                try:
                    self._attach_thread(tid)
                    self._armed.add(tid)
                except OSError as error:
                    warnings.append(messages.text("error.ptrace.thread", thread=tid,
                                                  error=self._explain(error)))
        return warnings

    def _list_threads(self):
        try:
            return [int(entry) for entry in os.listdir(f"/proc/{self.pid}/task")]
        except OSError:
            return []

    def _attach_thread(self, tid):
        _ptrace(PTRACE_ATTACH, tid, 0, 0)
        deliver = 0
        try:
            _waited, status = os.waitpid(tid, _WALL)
            if not os.WIFSTOPPED(status):
                raise messages.LocalizedOSError("error.ptrace.thread_ended", errno.ESRCH)
            # The first stop may be the target's own signal: it is delivered
            # when the thread goes on; the attach's SIGSTOP follows later.
            if os.WSTOPSIG(status) != signal.SIGSTOP:
                deliver = os.WSTOPSIG(status)
            _ptrace(PTRACE_SETOPTIONS, tid, 0, PTRACE_O_TRACECLONE)
            self._arm(tid)
        except OSError:
            # Let go of the thread rather than leave it stopped.
            try:
                _ptrace(PTRACE_DETACH, tid, 0, deliver)
            except OSError:
                pass
            raise
        _ptrace(PTRACE_CONT, tid, 0, deliver)

    def _arm(self, tid):
        """Write the current slot set into one stopped thread's registers."""
        dr7 = combined_dr7({slot: (size, reads)
                            for slot, (_addr, size, reads) in self._slots.items()})
        for slot, (address, _size, _reads) in self._slots.items():
            _ptrace(PTRACE_POKEUSER, tid, DR_ADDRESS[slot], address)
        _ptrace(PTRACE_POKEUSER, tid, DR6, 0)
        _ptrace(PTRACE_POKEUSER, tid, DR7, dr7)

    def _reprogram(self):
        """Re-arm every thread after the slot set changed.

        POKEUSER needs a stopped thread, so the threads are halted (see
        _stop_threads), their registers rewritten, and resumed. A thread whose
        registers cannot be written goes on with its old watchpoints.
        """
        stopped = self._stop_threads(self._armed)
        for tid in stopped:
            try:
                self._arm(tid)
            except OSError as error:
                log.warning("Thread %d: watchpoints not changed: %s", tid, error)
            self._resume(tid, 0)
        missed = self._armed - stopped
        if missed:
            log.warning("Threads %s did not stop; their watchpoints stay as they were",
                        sorted(missed))

    def _stop_threads(self, tids, timeout=2.0):
        """Halt the threads ``tids``; return those halted, which stay stopped.

        Each gets a SIGSTOP, and only that stop counts as halted. Whatever else
        a thread reports meanwhile is dealt with as the event loop would: a
        watchpoint trap is acknowledged, the target's own signals are
        delivered (a suspend request of Wine or a garbage collector must not
        get lost), a thread that clones goes on. Threads born meanwhile are
        halted from their first stop and returned as well.
        """
        waiting = set(tids)
        for tid in waiting:
            self._tgkill(tid, signal.SIGSTOP)
        stopped = set()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while waiting and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            try:
                tid, status = os.waitpid(-1, _WAIT_ANY)
            except ChildProcessError:
                break
            if tid == 0:
                time.sleep(0.001)
                continue
            if os.WIFEXITED(status) or os.WIFSIGNALED(status):
                self._thread_gone(tid)
                waiting.discard(tid)
                stopped.discard(tid)
                continue
            if not os.WIFSTOPPED(status):
                continue
            if status >> 16 == PTRACE_EVENT_CLONE:
                self._resume(tid, 0)  # its SIGSTOP is still to come
                continue
            stop_signal = os.WSTOPSIG(status)
            if stop_signal == signal.SIGSTOP:
                self._armed.add(tid)  # also a new thread, stopped at its birth
                stopped.add(tid)
                waiting.discard(tid)
                continue
            if stop_signal == signal.SIGTRAP and self._acknowledge_trap(tid) is not None:
                self._resume(tid, 0)  # a watchpoint hit: not acted on while halting
                continue
            self._resume(tid, stop_signal)
        return stopped

    def _resume(self, tid, deliver):
        """Let a stopped thread go on, delivering signal ``deliver`` (0: none)."""
        try:
            _ptrace(PTRACE_CONT, tid, 0, deliver)
        except OSError:
            self._armed.discard(tid)

    def _thread_gone(self, tid):
        self._armed.discard(tid)
        if tid == self.pid:
            self._target_gone = True
            self.requestInterruption()

    # -- event loop ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _pump(self):
        """Handle one ptrace event. Returns False when none was pending."""
        try:
            tid, status = os.waitpid(-1, _WAIT_ANY)
        except ChildProcessError:
            self.requestInterruption()
            return False
        if tid == 0:
            return False
        if os.WIFEXITED(status) or os.WIFSIGNALED(status):
            self._thread_gone(tid)
            return True
        if not os.WIFSTOPPED(status):
            return True

        if status >> 16 == PTRACE_EVENT_CLONE:
            # The new thread reports its own first stop, before or after this
            # event; it is taken in there.
            self._resume(tid, 0)
            return True

        stop_signal = os.WSTOPSIG(status)
        deliver = 0
        if stop_signal == signal.SIGSTOP:
            if tid not in self._armed:
                self._take_in(tid)
            # else: a SIGSTOP of ours that came late
        elif stop_signal == signal.SIGTRAP:
            deliver = self._dispatch_trap(tid)
        else:
            deliver = stop_signal  # pass the target's own signals through
        self._resume(tid, deliver)
        return True

    def _take_in(self, tid):
        """Arm a thread born traced (PTRACE_O_TRACECLONE), stopped at its birth."""
        self._armed.add(tid)
        try:
            _ptrace(PTRACE_SETOPTIONS, tid, 0, PTRACE_O_TRACECLONE)
            self._arm(tid)
        except OSError as error:
            log.warning("New thread %d: watchpoints not set: %s", tid, error)

    def _acknowledge_trap(self, tid):
        """Clear and return the watchpoint bits of a SIGTRAP stop, or None if not ours.

        A SIGTRAP with no watchpoint bit is the target's own (an int3 or a
        single step, which Wine uses for its exceptions) and must reach it.
        """
        try:
            dr6 = _peek_user(tid, DR6)
        except OSError:
            return None
        if not dr6 & _DR6_SLOTS:
            return None
        try:
            _ptrace(PTRACE_POKEUSER, tid, DR6, 0)
        except OSError:
            pass
        return dr6 & _DR6_SLOTS

    def _dispatch_trap(self, tid):
        """Handle a SIGTRAP stop; return the signal to deliver (0: none)."""
        bits = self._acknowledge_trap(tid)
        if bits is None:
            return signal.SIGTRAP
        try:
            pc, mode = self._pc_bits(tid)
        except OSError:
            return 0
        for slot in self._slots:
            if bits & (1 << slot):
                self._handle_trap(tid, slot, pc, mode)
        return 0

    def _handle_trap(self, tid, slot, pc, bits):
        """Act on a watchpoint hit; implemented by subclasses."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    # -- detaching ----------------------------------------------------------

    def _detach_all(self):
        """Stop every armed thread, clear its watchpoints, and detach cleanly.

        PTRACE_DETACH only works on a stopped thread, and detaching without
        clearing DR7 would leave an armed watchpoint with no tracer, so the
        next access raises SIGTRAP and kills the target. So each thread is
        halted first (_stop_threads, which waits for the very SIGSTOP it sent:
        one left pending would stop the whole process after the detach).
        """
        for timeout in (2.0, 3.0):
            if not self._armed:
                break
            for tid in self._stop_threads(self._armed, timeout):
                self._disarm_and_detach(tid)
                self._armed.discard(tid)
        if self._armed:
            # Still traced: they detach when this thread ends, armed.
            log.warning("Threads %s did not stop and could not be detached cleanly",
                        sorted(self._armed))
        self._armed.clear()

    def _tgkill(self, tid, sig):
        """Send ``sig`` to one thread of the target."""
        tgkill(self.pid, tid, sig)

    @staticmethod
    def _disarm_and_detach(tid):
        for offset in (DR7, DR6):
            try:
                _ptrace(PTRACE_POKEUSER, tid, offset, 0)
            except OSError:
                pass
        try:
            _ptrace(PTRACE_DETACH, tid, 0, 0)
        except OSError:
            pass

```

`grembyte/attach/wine_gadget.py`:

```py
"""Load Frida's Windows gadget into a Wine/Proton game.

``frida.attach`` fails on Wine processes (its Linux agent cannot locate the
program behind ``wine-preloader``). The Windows build of Frida's gadget,
``frida-gadget.dll``, does not: loaded as an ordinary DLL it sees PE modules,
Windows threads and the Win64 ABI the way the game does, and exposes a Frida
session over a local TCP port.

To load it into an already-running game, grembyte first runs a small Windows
helper inside the game's wineserver (wine_helper.py), which loads the DLL with
``CreateRemoteThread`` on ``LoadLibraryW``. Should that fail, it falls back to
calling ``LoadLibraryW`` on one of the game's own threads via ptrace (64-bit
games only): it parks a thread at a Windows function the game calls often (a
software ``int3``), points the thread at ``LoadLibraryW`` with the gadget path,
lets it return to an ``int3`` trap, then restores the saved registers and
detaches. Either way grembyte then connects with
``add_remote_device("127.0.0.1:<port>")``.
"""

import ctypes
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import lzma
import os
import re
import signal
import socket
import struct
import threading
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import frida

from grembyte.attach import wine_helper
from grembyte.core import activity, settings
from grembyte.core.messages import LocalizedError
from grembyte.platform import process_start_time
from grembyte.platform.wine import RawMemory, pe_export, pe_images
from grembyte.attach.ptrace_engine import (
    _WAIT_ANY,
    _WALL,
    DR6,
    DR7,
    PTRACE_ATTACH,
    PTRACE_CONT,
    PTRACE_DETACH,
    PTRACE_EVENT_CLONE,
    PTRACE_O_TRACECLONE,
    PTRACE_POKEUSER,
    PTRACE_SETOPTIONS,
    _ptrace,
    tgkill,
)

log = logging.getLogger("grembyte.wine_gadget")

METHOD_AUTO = "auto"
METHOD_HELPER = "helper"
METHOD_PTRACE = "ptrace"

PTRACE_GETREGS = 12
PTRACE_SETREGS = 13

GADGET_PORT_BASE = 27100
GADGET_PORT_COUNT = 64
_GADGET_URL = ("https://github.com/frida/frida/releases/download/"
               "{version}/frida-gadget-{version}-windows-{arch}.dll.xz")
# The release's assets with the SHA-256 GitHub computed for each (``digest``).
_RELEASE_URL = "https://api.github.com/repos/frida/frida/releases/tags/{version}"
# PE machine types of the gadget
_PE_MACHINES = {"x86": 0x14C, "x86_64": 0x8664}

# Functions a game reaches from a clean Windows call boundary, where a borrowed
# thread has a valid context. A windowed game pumps messages every frame, so
# the message-pump entries fire within one frame; the timing and wait calls
# cover games that are between frames or otherwise idle. A software breakpoint
# is set on each that exists, and the first thread to reach one is borrowed.
_HOT_CANDIDATES = (
    ("win32u.dll", "NtUserPeekMessage"),
    ("win32u.dll", "NtUserGetMessage"),
    ("user32.dll", "PeekMessageW"),
    ("user32.dll", "PeekMessageA"),
    ("user32.dll", "GetMessageW"),
    ("kernelbase.dll", "GetSystemTimeAsFileTime"),
    ("kernelbase.dll", "QueryPerformanceCounter"),
    ("kernelbase.dll", "Sleep"),
    ("kernelbase.dll", "WaitForSingleObjectEx"),
)

# ``struct user_regs_struct`` field order on x86-64.
_REG_NAMES = (
    "r15", "r14", "r13", "r12", "rbp", "rbx", "r11", "r10", "r9", "r8",
    "rax", "rcx", "rdx", "rsi", "rdi", "orig_rax", "rip", "cs", "eflags",
    "rsp", "ss", "fs_base", "gs_base", "ds", "es", "fs", "gs",
)


class _Regs(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [(name, ctypes.c_uint64) for name in _REG_NAMES]


class GadgetError(LocalizedError, RuntimeError):
    """The gadget could not be loaded."""


# -- gadget file management ---------------------------------------------------

def gadget_dir():
    """Directory where grembyte keeps downloaded gadget DLLs.

    It lives under the user's data home (never /tmp), so the Steam/Proton
    container can map it into the game's Z: drive.
    """
    data_home = os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME") or Path.home() / ".local" / "share"
    path = Path(data_home) / "grembyte" / "gadget"
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def gadget_path(bits, version=None):
    """The expected gadget DLL for this Frida version and process bitness."""
    version = version or frida.__version__
    arch = "x86" if bits == 32 else "x86_64"
    return gadget_dir() / f"frida-gadget-{version}-windows-{arch}.dll"


def ensure_gadget(bits, version=None, download=True, progress=None):
    """Return the path to the Windows gadget DLL for ``bits``, fetching it once.

    The DLL is named for the Frida version so an upgrade pulls a matching one.
    ``download=False`` returns an existing file or raises, never reaching out.
    ``progress`` receives (downloaded bytes, total bytes), with -1 for an
    unknown total.
    """
    version = version or frida.__version__
    arch = "x86" if bits == 32 else "x86_64"
    target = gadget_path(bits, version)
    if target.exists():
        return target
    if not download:
        raise GadgetError("error.gadget.not_present", path=target)
    url = _GADGET_URL.format(version=version, arch=arch)
    try:
        digest = _published_digest(version, url.rsplit("/", 1)[1])
        chunks = []
        received = 0
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response:
            headers = getattr(response, "headers", None)
            total = int(headers.get("Content-Length", 0)) if headers else 0
            if progress is not None:
                progress(0, total or -1)
            while True:
                chunk = response.read(64 * 1024)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                chunks.append(chunk)
                received += len(chunk)
                if progress is not None:
                    progress(received, total or -1)
        compressed = b"".join(chunks)
        if digest is not None and hashlib.sha256(compressed).hexdigest() != digest:
            raise GadgetError("error.gadget.digest", url=url, digest=digest)
        dll = lzma.decompress(compressed)
        if not _is_pe(dll, arch):
            raise GadgetError("error.gadget.not_pe", url=url, arch=arch)
        # Written in full or not at all: a cut-off file would be taken as the gadget.
        partial = target.with_name(target.name + ".part")
        partial.write_bytes(dll)
        os.replace(partial, target)
    except (OSError, ValueError, lzma.LZMAError) as error:
        raise GadgetError("error.gadget.download", url=url, error=error) from error
    return target


def _published_digest(version, name):
    """The SHA-256 GitHub lists for asset ``name`` of the release, or None if none.

    Raises OSError or ValueError when the release cannot be read: no gadget is
    used that could not be checked.
    """
    request = urllib.request.Request(_RELEASE_URL.format(version=version),
                                     headers={"Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response:
        release = json.load(response)
    for asset in release.get("assets", []):
        if asset.get("name") == name:
            digest = asset.get("digest") or ""
            if digest.startswith("sha256:"):
                return digest.removeprefix("sha256:").lower()
            # Releases from before GitHub computed digests (2025) list none.
            log.warning("GitHub lists no SHA-256 for %s", name)
            return None
    raise ValueError(f"release {version} has no asset {name}")


def _is_pe(data, arch):
    """Whether ``data`` starts like a PE image for ``arch``."""
    if len(data) < 0x40 or data[:2] != b"MZ":
        return False
    offset = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, 0x3C)[0]
    if offset + 6 > len(data) or data[offset:offset + 4] != b"PE\0\0":
        return False
    return struct.unpack_from("<H", data, offset + 4)[0] == _PE_MACHINES[arch]


def _windows_path(unix_path):
    """Map a Unix path under the gadget dir to the Z: drive Wine exposes."""
    return "Z:" + str(unix_path).replace("/", "\\")


def write_config(dll_path, port):
    """Write the gadget's .config beside the DLL; return its path.

    Listen mode with ``on_load: resume`` lets the game keep running until
    grembyte connects.
    """
    config = Path(str(dll_path)[:-4] + ".config")
    config.write_text(json.dumps({
        "interaction": {
            "type": "listen",
            "address": "127.0.0.1",
            "port": port,
            "on_load": "resume",
        }
    }), encoding="utf-8")
    return config


def _free_port():
    """Pick a loopback port the gadget can bind, from a stable range."""
    for port in range(GADGET_PORT_BASE, GADGET_PORT_BASE + GADGET_PORT_COUNT):
        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as probe:
            try:
                probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
                return port
            except OSError:
                continue
    raise GadgetError("error.gadget.no_port")


# -- ptrace loader ------------------------------------------------------------

def _get_regs(tid):
    regs = _Regs()
    _ptrace(PTRACE_GETREGS, tid, 0, ctypes.addressof(regs))
    return regs


def _set_regs(tid, regs):
    _ptrace(PTRACE_SETREGS, tid, 0, ctypes.addressof(regs))


def _list_threads(pid):
    try:
        return [int(entry) for entry in os.listdir(f"/proc/{pid}/task")]
    except OSError:
        return []


class _Tracee:
    """A ptrace attachment to every thread of a Wine process.

    Only a convenience wrapper for the one-shot loader below: it attaches all
    threads (and those born meanwhile), lets the caller plant breakpoints and
    single out the thread that hits one, and always detaches cleanly so the
    game keeps running.

    While the caller waits for that thread, the others run: stopping them
    could stop one that holds a lock LoadLibraryW needs. Whatever they report
    goes through ``service``: their own signals are delivered (Wine's suspend
    requests and exceptions must not get lost), and one that hits an ``int3``
    of ours is rewound to it and kept stopped until the ``int3`` is gone.
    """

    def __init__(self, pid):
        self.pid = pid
        self._attached = set()
        self._stopped = set()   # attached threads stopped right now
        self._pending = {}      # tid -> signal to deliver when it goes on
        self._breakpoints = {}  # address -> original byte, int3 there now
        self._planted = set()   # every address an int3 of ours was at
        self._parked = set()    # rewound at an int3 of ours, kept stopped

    def attach(self):
        """Attach and stop every thread; new threads are traced from birth."""
        for _ in range(2):  # a second pass catches threads born while attaching
            for tid in _list_threads(self.pid):
                if tid not in self._attached:
                    self._attach_thread(tid)
        if not self._attached:
            raise GadgetError("error.gadget.ptrace")

    def _attach_thread(self, tid):
        try:
            _ptrace(PTRACE_ATTACH, tid, 0, 0)
            _waited, status = os.waitpid(tid, _WALL)
        except (OSError, ChildProcessError):
            return
        if not os.WIFSTOPPED(status):
            return
        # The first stop may be the game's own signal: delivered when the
        # thread goes on; the attach's SIGSTOP follows later.
        if os.WSTOPSIG(status) != signal.SIGSTOP:
            self._pending[tid] = os.WSTOPSIG(status)
        try:
            _ptrace(PTRACE_SETOPTIONS, tid, 0, PTRACE_O_TRACECLONE)
        except OSError:
            pass
        self._attached.add(tid)
        self._stopped.add(tid)

    def set_breakpoints(self, memory, addresses):
        """Plant software ``int3`` breakpoints at ``addresses``.

        One byte in shared code traps whichever thread reaches it, so this does
        not depend on hardware debug registers (which do not fire under Wine).
        """
        for address in addresses:
            if address in self._breakpoints:
                continue
            self._breakpoints[address] = memory.read(address, 1)
            self._planted.add(address)
            memory.write(address, b"\xCC")

    def clear_breakpoints(self, memory, addresses=None):
        """Restore the bytes the breakpoints overwrote (all, or ``addresses``).

        Threads kept stopped at one of them may go on then: they run the
        original instruction.
        """
        for address in list(self._breakpoints if addresses is None else addresses):
            original = self._breakpoints.pop(address, None)
            if original is not None:
                memory.write(address, original)
