```js
      case 'name': {
        const [index, number] = nameOf(String(value));
        address.writeU32(index);
        address.add(4).writeU32(number);
        return;
      }
      case 'bool':
        writeValue(type, address, value);
        return;
      default:
        throw grembyteError('error.unreal.script_unpassable', { type: type.name });
    }
  }

  const nameIndexes = new Map();

  function nameOf(text) {
    // [index, number] of an FName the game knows: one an object is named
    // (Name_3 is Name with number 4).
    let found = nameIndexes.get(text);
    if (found !== undefined)
      return found;
    const s = objects();
    const match = /^(.*)_(\d+)$/.exec(text);
    for (let i = 0; i < s.address.length && found === undefined; i++) {
      const base = nameText(s.name[i], 0);
      if (base === text)
        found = [s.name[i], 0];
      else if (match !== null && base === match[1] && String(Number(match[2])) === match[2])
        found = [s.name[i], Number(match[2]) + 1];
    }
    if (found === undefined)
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.unknown_fname', { name: text });
    nameIndexes.set(text, found);
    return found;
  }

  function classChain(klass) {
    const chain = [];
    for (let current = Number(klass.toString()); current !== 0; current = superOf(current))
      chain.push(ptr(current));
    return chain;  // the class first, UObject last
  }

  function classNameMatches(klass, name) {
    // By its name (BP_Player_C) or C++ name (ABP_Player_C, UAlabamaCheatManager)
    const own = nameOfAddress(Number(klass.toString()));
    return own === name || cppName(Number(klass.toString())) === name;
  }

  const classesByName = new Map();

  function findClass(name) {
    // A loaded class (or struct) by its name, e.g. "AlabamaCheatManager".
    reflection();
    const cached = classesByName.get(name);
    if (cached !== undefined && isObject(cached))
      return cached;
    const s = objects();
    const kinds = new Map();
    for (let i = 0; i < s.address.length; i++) {
      if (s.outer[i] === 0 || !isClass(s, s.klass[i], kinds))
        continue;
      const klass = ptr(s.address[i]);
      if (classNameMatches(klass, name)) {
        classesByName.set(name, klass);
        return klass;
      }
    }
    throw grembyteError('error.unreal.no_class', { name });
  }

  // Functions found by name: scripts run each run's calls again, and a search
  // by name reads the object table when its snapshot is old (on the game thread)
  const methodsByName = new Map();

  function cachedMethod(key, find) {
    const cached = methodsByName.get(key);
    if (cached !== undefined && isObject(cached))
      return cached;
    const found = find();
    methodsByName.set(key, found);
    return found;
  }

  function findMethod(klass, name, argumentCount, wantStatic) {
    return cachedMethod(`${klass}|${name}|${argumentCount}|${wantStatic}`,
                        () => searchMethod(klass, name, argumentCount, wantStatic));
  }

  function searchMethod(klass, name, argumentCount, wantStatic) {
    // The UFunction ``name`` of the class or a base class taking
    // ``argumentCount`` arguments; ``wantStatic`` true/false or null for any.
    for (const current of classChain(klass)) {
      for (const fn of functionsOf(current)) {
        if (fn.name !== name)
          continue;
        const signature = signatureOf(fn.address);
        if ((wantStatic === null || !signature.instance === wantStatic)
            && signature.params.length === argumentCount)
          return fn.address;
      }
    }
    throw grembyteError(wantStatic ? 'error.unreal.no_static_function' : 'error.unreal.no_function',
                      { owner: layout(klass).name, name, count: argumentCount });
  }

  function methods(klass) {
    // [{ name, method, static, owner }] of the UFunctions of ``klass`` and its
    // base classes, the most derived first (an override once), for the
    // object inspector.
    reflection();
    const seen = new Set();
    const result = [];
    for (const current of classChain(klass)) {
      const owner = layout(current).name;
      for (const fn of functionsOf(current)) {
        if (seen.has(fn.name))
          continue;
        seen.add(fn.name);
        let instance = true;
        try {
          instance = signatureOf(fn.address).instance;
        } catch (_error) {
          // listed anyway; calling it reports the problem
        }
        result.push({ name: fn.name, method: fn.address, owner, static: !instance });
      }
    }
    return result;
  }

  function virtualMethod(object, fn) {
    // What ProcessEvent should run for ``fn`` on ``object``: the override of
    // its class (a Blueprint's event graph, a subclass's implementation).
    const klass = object.add(OBJECT_CLASS).readPointer();
    return cachedMethod(`${klass}|${fn}`, () => {
      const name = fieldName(fn.add(OBJECT_NAME));
      for (const current of classChain(klass)) {
        const found = functionsOf(current).find(candidate => candidate.name === name);
        if (found !== undefined)
          return found.address;
      }
      return fn;
    });
  }

  const defaultObjects = new Map();

  function defaultObject(klass) {
    // The class default object (Default__Name) a class's static functions run on.
    const cached = defaultObjects.get(klass.toString());
    if (cached !== undefined && isObject(cached))
      return cached;
    const found = searchDefaultObject(klass);
    defaultObjects.set(klass.toString(), found);
    return found;
  }

  function searchDefaultObject(klass) {
    const s = objects();
    const wanted = `Default__${nameOfAddress(Number(klass.toString()))}`;
    const i = s.address.findIndex((address, k) => s.klass[k] === Number(klass.toString())
      && objectName(s, k) === wanted);
    if (i < 0)
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.not_found', { name: wanted });
    return ptr(s.address[i]);
  }

  // className|name -> the object findObject found last: checked, not
  // searched for again (a search reads every object, tens of milliseconds on
  // the game thread)
  const foundObjects = new Map();

  function outerName(object) {
    // "AttributeStatsWidget.PointsAvailableTracker": the object's name after
    // its outer's; a widget's outer is the WidgetTree of the widget showing it.
    if (!isObject(object))
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.no_object', { address: object });
    const name = fieldName(object.add(OBJECT_NAME));
    let outer = object.add(OBJECT_OUTER).readPointer();
    if (!outer.isNull() && isObject(outer)
        && fieldName(outer.add(OBJECT_CLASS).readPointer().add(OBJECT_NAME)) === 'WidgetTree')
      outer = outer.add(OBJECT_OUTER).readPointer();
    return outer.isNull() || !isObject(outer) ? name
      : `${fieldName(outer.add(OBJECT_NAME))}.${name}`;
  }

  function isNamed(object, named) {
    // Whether ``object`` is named ``named``: a name, or one as outerName gives
    if (named === null)
      return true;
    return named.includes('.') ? outerName(object) === named
      : fieldName(object.add(OBJECT_NAME)) === named;
  }

  // RF_ClassDefaultObject, RF_ArchetypeObject
  const RF_TEMPLATE = 0x10 | 0x20;

  function isTemplate(s, i, classKinds) {
    // Whether object ``i`` is no object the game uses: a class default object,
    // an archetype, or a part of one or of a class (a widget in a Widget
    // Blueprint's tree, the template of the widgets shown).
    for (let k = i; k !== undefined; k = s.index.get(s.outer[k])) {
      if (objectName(s, k).startsWith('Default__') || (s.flags[k] & RF_TEMPLATE) !== 0
          || (k !== i && isClass(s, s.klass[k], classKinds)))
        return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  function stillFound(object, klass, named) {
    // Whether a cached object is still alive, of the class (or a subclass)
    // and, if given, named ``named``.
    if (!isObject(object) || !isNamed(object, named))
      return false;
    return classChain(object.add(OBJECT_CLASS).readPointer())
      .some(current => Number(current.toString()) === klass);
  }

  function searchObjects(klass, named, limit) {
    // Up to ``limit`` live objects of class ``klass`` (or a subclass) named
    // ``named`` (see isNamed), in the snapshot of the object table.
    const s = objects();
    const kinds = new Map();
    const classKinds = new Map();
    const derives = k => {
      let result = kinds.get(k);
      if (result === undefined) {
        result = false;
        for (let current = k; current !== 0; current = superOf(current)) {
          if (current === klass) {
            result = true;
            break;
          }
        }
        kinds.set(k, result);
      }
      return result;
    };
    const ownName = named === null ? null : named.substring(named.lastIndexOf('.') + 1);
    const found = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < s.address.length && found.length < limit; i++) {
      if (!derives(s.klass[i]) || (ownName !== null && objectName(s, i) !== ownName))
        continue;
      const object = ptr(s.address[i]);
      try {
        if (isObject(object) && !isTemplate(s, i, classKinds) && isNamed(object, named))
          found.push(object);
      } catch (_error) {
        // freed meanwhile
      }
    }
    return found;
  }

  function findObject(className, named = null) {
    // A live object (no class default object or template) of the class
    // ``className`` or a subclass, e.g. findObject("AlabamaCheatManager");
    // with ``named`` the one of that name, e.g. findObject("BP_Hero_C",
    // "BP_Hero_C_1"), or of that name in its outer (see outerName). null if none.
    reflection();
    const klass = Number(findClass(className).toString());
    const key = `${className}|${named}`;
    const cached = foundObjects.get(key);
    if (cached !== undefined && stillFound(cached, klass, named))
      return cached;
    foundObjects.delete(key);
    for (let fresh = 0; fresh < 2; fresh++) {
      const [object] = searchObjects(klass, named, 1);
      if (object !== undefined) {
        foundObjects.set(key, object);
        return object;
      }
      snapshot = null;  // the object may be newer than the snapshot
    }
    return null;
  }

  function findObjects(className, named = null) {
    // All live objects findObject could give, read from the object table anew
    reflection();
    const klass = Number(findClass(className).toString());
    snapshot = null;
    // (Frida's JavaScript on Windows has no Infinity: it is NaN there.)
    return searchObjects(klass, named, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER);
  }

  // --- Object browser: every live object, by its class ---------------------------
  // One pass over the object table groups the objects by their exact class.
  // Class default objects, archetypes and their parts (see isTemplate), and
  // the reflection objects (packages, classes, functions, structs, enums)
  // are left out unless ``internal`` asks for them. Memory reads only: on
  // the agent's thread, also while the game is paused.

  // Engine classes a game has one object of (or of a subclass of them); the
  // first of a class's chain names its role
  const SINGLETON_BASES = new Set(['GameEngine', 'Engine', 'GameInstance', 'Subsystem',
    'GameModeBase', 'GameStateBase', 'WorldSettings', 'GameUserSettings', 'AssetManager',
    'GameViewportClient', 'LocalPlayer', 'PlayerController', 'CheatManager']);
  // Instances a class lists at most (the filter narrows them)
  const MAX_INSTANCES = 5000;

  function filterWords(filter) {
    // The words all of which a name must contain (case does not matter)
    return String(filter || '').toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(word => word !== '');
  }

  function matchesWords(text, words) {
    const lower = text.toLowerCase();
    return words.every(word => lower.includes(word));
  }

  function browseState(internal) {
    // What the browser asks of every object, cached by class: whether it is
    // shown (reflection objects only with ``internal``) and whether index i
    // is a template.
    const L = ue.layout;
    const s = objects();
    const reflectionKinds = new Set([L.structClass, L.enumClass, L.packageClass]);
    const classKinds = new Map();
    const shownClasses = new Map();
    const shown = klass => {
      let result = shownClasses.get(klass);
      if (result === undefined) {
        result = klass !== 0;
        for (let current = klass; result && current !== 0 && !internal;
          current = superOf(current)) {
          if (reflectionKinds.has(current))
            result = false;
        }
        shownClasses.set(klass, result);
      }
      return result;
    };
    // isTemplate for every object, each outer's answer kept: games keep
    // hundreds of thousands of objects, mostly in a few outers. 0: not known
    // yet, 1: no template, 2: one (or a part of one or of a class).
    const insideTemplate = new Uint8Array(s.address.length);
    const ownTemplate = i => objectName(s, i).startsWith('Default__')
      || (s.flags[i] & RF_TEMPLATE) !== 0;
    const inside = i => {
      // Whether an object in outer ``i`` is part of a template or a class
      const path = [];
      let k = i, result = false;
      for (; k !== undefined; k = s.index.get(s.outer[k])) {
        if (insideTemplate[k] !== 0) {
          result = insideTemplate[k] === 2;
          break;
        }
        path.push(k);
        if (ownTemplate(k) || isClass(s, s.klass[k], classKinds)) {
          result = true;
          break;
        }
      }
      for (const known of path)
        insideTemplate[known] = result ? 2 : 1;
      return result;
    };
    const isTemplateObject = i => {
      if (ownTemplate(i))
        return true;
      const outer = s.index.get(s.outer[i]);
      return outer !== undefined && inside(outer);
    };
    const isShown = i => {
      try {
        return shown(s.klass[i]) && (internal || !isTemplateObject(i));
      } catch (_error) {
        return false;  // freed meanwhile
      }
    };
    return { s, isShown };
  }

  function classPackage(s, klass) {
    // The catalog's group of the package a class is in (/Script/Engine,
    // /Game/Blueprints), or '' if it is in none
    let i = s.index.get(klass);
    while (i !== undefined && s.outer[i] !== 0)
      i = s.index.get(s.outer[i]);
    return i === undefined ? '' : packageGroup(objectName(s, i));
  }

  function singletonRole(klass) {
    // The engine class (SINGLETON_BASES) ``klass`` is or derives from, or null
    for (let current = klass; current !== 0; current = superOf(current)) {
      const name = nameOfAddress(current);
      if (SINGLETON_BASES.has(name))
        return name;
    }
    return null;
  }

  function browseClasses(options = {}) {
    // The classes with live objects: [{klass, name, cppName, package, count,
    // role, matched}], read from the object table anew. ``filter`` (words):
    // ``matched`` is how many of a class's objects are named so; ``internal``
    // also counts templates and reflection objects.
    reflection();
    snapshot = null;
    const { s, isShown } = browseState(Boolean(options.internal));
    const words = filterWords(options.filter);
    const byClass = new Map();
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < s.address.length; i++) {
      if (!isShown(i))
        continue;
      const klass = s.klass[i];
      let entry = byClass.get(klass);
      if (entry === undefined) {
        entry = { count: 0, matched: 0 };
        byClass.set(klass, entry);
      }
      entry.count++;
      total++;
      if (words.length > 0 && matchesWords(objectName(s, i), words))
        entry.matched++;
    }
    const classes = [];
    for (const [klass, entry] of byClass) {
      let name;
      try {
        name = nameOfAddress(klass);
      } catch (_error) {
        continue;
      }
      if (name === null)
        continue;  // a class that is no object of the table (any more)
      let role = null, cpp = name;
      try {
        role = singletonRole(klass);
        cpp = cppName(klass);
      } catch (_error) {
        // a class whose chain cannot be read: no role
      }
      classes.push({ klass: ptr(klass).toString(), name, cppName: cpp,
                     package: classPackage(s, klass), count: entry.count, role,
                     matched: entry.matched });
    }
    classes.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
    return { classes, objects: total };
  }

  function browseInstances(klass, options = {}) {
    // The live objects of exactly class ``klass`` (as browseClasses lists
    // it): {instances: [{address, name, outer}], count, truncated}, with
    // ``filter`` those named so, at most ``limit``.
    reflection();
    const wanted = Number(ptr(klass).toString());
    const { s, isShown } = browseState(Boolean(options.internal));
    const words = filterWords(options.filter);
    const limit = options.limit > 0 ? options.limit : MAX_INSTANCES;
    const instances = [];
    let count = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < s.address.length; i++) {
      if (s.klass[i] !== wanted || !isShown(i))
        continue;
      const name = objectName(s, i);
      if (words.length > 0 && !matchesWords(name, words))
        continue;
      count++;
      if (instances.length >= limit)
        continue;
      const outer = s.index.get(s.outer[i]);
      instances.push({ address: ptr(s.address[i]).toString(), name,
                       outer: outer === undefined ? null : objectName(s, outer) });
    }
    instances.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
    return { instances, count, truncated: count > instances.length };
  }

  // --- Gameplay Ability System: the player's attributes -----------------------------
  // GAS games keep attributes (Health, Might, DamageOutgoingMult ...) as
  // FGameplayAttributeData (vtable, BaseValue, CurrentValue) in UAttributeSet
  // subobjects of the actor owning the UAbilitySystemComponent: the player's
  // pawn or player state. CurrentValue is BaseValue with the active effects
  // applied, and GAS computes it anew; damage calculations read attributes
  // through GAS too. So a value written to memory does not last: the base
  // value is set through the game's own code instead, a static UFunction
  // taking (UAbilitySystemComponent*, FGameplayAttribute, float), e.g.
  // Avowed's AlabamaAbilitySystemBlueprintLibrary:
  // SetFloatAttributeBaseFromAbilitySystemComponent. GAS then computes the
  // current value with the effects (a +1 bonus stays one, a x1.4 one scales).
  // Games with AngelscriptGAS (Gothic 1 Remake) have no such function; their
  // attribute sets set it themselves: AngelscriptAttributeSet:
  // TrySetAttributeBaseValue(FName, float), called on the set.

  // FGameplayAttribute's TFieldPath<FProperty> (Attribute): ResolvedField,
  // ResolvedOwner (a weak pointer to the declaring class), Path (TArray<FName>,
  // the game keeps the attribute's name only).
  const FIELD_PATH_OWNER = 8, FIELD_PATH_PATH = 16;
  // How often a found setter (or none) is looked for again
  const SETTER_SEARCH_AGE = 30000;
  // { fn, signature, name, setClass } or null; undefined: not looked for.
  // setClass: the attribute set class whose sets it is called on, else NULL.
  let attributeSetter;
  let setterSearched = 0;
  let playerParts = null;  // { pawn, owners, sets, asc } found last

  function isAttributeData(type) {
    if (type.kind !== KIND.VALUETYPE || type.klass === undefined)
      return false;
    const names = layout(type.klass).fields.map(field => field.name);
    return names.includes('BaseValue') && names.includes('CurrentValue');
  }

  function attributeFields(klass) {
    return layout(klass).fields.filter(field => isAttributeData(field.type));
  }

  function propertyOf(klass, name) {
    // The field (see layout) of an object's property, or undefined
    return layout(klass).fields.find(field => field.name === name);
  }

  function pointerProperty(object, name) {
    const field = propertyOf(object.add(OBJECT_CLASS).readPointer(), name);
    if (field === undefined)
      return NULL;
    const value = object.add(field.offset).readPointer();
    return !value.isNull() && isObject(value) ? value : NULL;
  }

  function searchPlayerParts() {
    // The attribute sets and the ability system component of the first local
    // player: owned by its pawn or player state.
    const controller = findObject('PlayerController');
    if (controller === null)
      return null;
    const pawn = pointerProperty(controller, 'Pawn');
    if (pawn.isNull())
      return null;
    const owners = [pawn, pointerProperty(controller, 'PlayerState')].filter(o => !o.isNull());
    const owned = object => owners.some(owner => object.add(OBJECT_OUTER).readPointer()
      .equals(owner));
    // One read of the object table for both (findObjects reads it anew)
    snapshot = null;
    const all = name => searchObjects(Number(findClass(name).toString()), null,
                                      Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER);
    const sets = all('AttributeSet').filter(owned);
    const components = all('AbilitySystemComponent').filter(owned);
    // The component of the owner with the sets
    const asc = components.find(component => sets.some(set =>
      set.add(OBJECT_OUTER).readPointer().equals(component.add(OBJECT_OUTER).readPointer())))
      || components[0] || NULL;
    return { pawn, owners, sets, asc };
  }

  function currentPlayerParts() {
    // The player's parts found last while still current, else searched anew
    // (a search reads every object: not on every refresh).
    const parts = playerParts;
    if (parts !== null) {
      try {
        const controller = findObject('PlayerController');
        const current = controller === null ? NULL : pointerProperty(controller, 'Pawn');
        if (current.equals(parts.pawn) && parts.sets.every(set => isObject(set)
            && parts.owners.some(owner => set.add(OBJECT_OUTER).readPointer().equals(owner)))
            && (parts.asc.isNull() || isObject(parts.asc)))
          return parts;
      } catch (_error) {
        // freed meanwhile: search again
      }
    }
    playerParts = searchPlayerParts();
    return playerParts;
  }

  function setName(set) {
    return fieldName(set.add(OBJECT_NAME));
  }

  function gasAttributes() {
    // { owner, ownerClass, ownerAddress, setter, component, sets: [{ name,
    // className, attributes: [{ name, base, current }] }] } of the player, or
    // null without one (e.g. in the menu). Games without GAS keep the
    // player's values in fields of the pawn: the window opens it in the
    // object inspector by ownerAddress.
    reflection();
    const parts = currentPlayerParts();
    if (parts === null)
      return null;
    const setter = findAttributeSetter();
    return {
      owner: fieldName(parts.pawn.add(OBJECT_NAME)),
      ownerClass: layout(parts.pawn.add(OBJECT_CLASS).readPointer()).name,
      ownerAddress: parts.pawn.toString(),
      setter: setter === null ? null : setter.name,
      component: !parts.asc.isNull(),
      sets: parts.sets.map(set => {
        const klass = set.add(OBJECT_CLASS).readPointer();
        return {
          name: setName(set),
          className: layout(klass).name,
          attributes: attributeFields(klass).map(field => {
            const data = layout(field.type.klass).fields;
            const at = name => set.add(field.offset)
              .add(data.find(entry => entry.name === name).offset).readFloat();
            return { name: field.name, base: at('BaseValue'), current: at('CurrentValue') };
          })
        };
      })
    };
  }

  function findAttributeSetter() {
    // The game's UFunction setting an attribute's base value (see above), or
    // null; found by its parameters among the UFunctions named
    // (Try)Set...Attribute...Base: a static one taking the component, else
    // one of an attribute set taking the attribute's name.
    if (attributeSetter !== undefined
        && (attributeSetter !== null || Date.now() - setterSearched < SETTER_SEARCH_AGE))
      return attributeSetter;
    setterSearched = Date.now();
    attributeSetter = null;
    const s = objects();
    const functionClass = ue.layout.functionClass;
    const setBase = findClass('AttributeSet');
    let onSet = null;
    for (let i = 0; i < s.address.length; i++) {
      if (s.klass[i] !== functionClass
          || !/^(Try)?Set\w*Attribute\w*Base/.test(objectName(s, i)))
        continue;
      const fn = ptr(s.address[i]);
      let signature;
      try {
        signature = signatureOf(fn);
      } catch (_error) {
        continue;
      }
      const owner = fn.add(OBJECT_OUTER).readPointer();
      const setter = { fn, signature, setClass: NULL,
                       name: `${nameOfAddress(Number(owner.toString()))}:${objectName(s, i)}` };
      const isNumber = parameter => parameter !== undefined
        && [KIND.R4, KIND.R8].includes(parameter.type.kind);
      const [component, attribute, value] = signature.params;
      if (!signature.instance && isNumber(value) && component.type.kind === KIND.CLASS
          && /AbilitySystemComponent/.test(component.type.name)
          && attribute.type.name === 'FGameplayAttribute' && !attribute.type.byref) {
        attributeSetter = setter;
        break;
      }
      const [name, number] = signature.params;
      if (onSet === null && signature.instance && signature.params.length === 2
          && name.type.engine === 'name' && isNumber(number)
          && classChain(owner).some(klass => klass.equals(setBase)))
        onSet = Object.assign(setter, { setClass: owner });
    }
    if (attributeSetter === null)
      attributeSetter = onSet;
    return attributeSetter;
  }

  function findAttribute(parts, name) {
    // The set and field of "Set.Attribute" or "Attribute" (the first set
    // with it). "Set" may leave out the number Unreal gives the set's object
    // anew on every load: "AttributeSet_Health" for "AttributeSet_Health_2147445233".
    name = String(name);
    const dot = name.indexOf('.');
    const wantedSet = dot < 0 ? null : name.substring(0, dot);
    const attribute = dot < 0 ? name : name.substring(dot + 1);
    for (const set of parts.sets) {
      const found = wantedSet === null ? null : setName(set);
      if (found !== null && found !== wantedSet && found.replace(/_\d+$/, '') !== wantedSet)
        continue;
      const field = attributeFields(set.add(OBJECT_CLASS).readPointer())
        .find(entry => entry.name === attribute);
      if (field !== undefined)
        return { set, field };
    }
    throw grembyteError('error.unreal.no_player_attribute', { name });
  }

  function writeGameplayAttribute(type, address, field, keep) {
    // An FGameplayAttribute naming ``field`` as the game makes one
    const parts = layout(type.klass).fields;
    const at = name => {
      const part = parts.find(entry => entry.name === name);
      if (part === undefined)
        throw grembyteError('error.unreal.gameplay_attribute_field', { name });
      return address.add(part.offset);
    };
    const name = field.name;
    const text = Memory.alloc(2 * (name.length + 1));
    text.writeUtf16String(name);
    const path = Memory.alloc(8);
    Memory.copy(path, field.property.add(ue.layout.fieldName), 8);
    keep.push(text, path);
    const nameAt = at('AttributeName');
    nameAt.writePointer(text);
    nameAt.add(Process.pointerSize).writeS32(name.length + 1);
    nameAt.add(Process.pointerSize + 4).writeS32(name.length + 1);
    const owner = field.owner;
    const index = owner.add(OBJECT_INDEX).readS32();
    const item = ue.objects.table.readPointer().add(8 * Math.floor(index / CHUNK)).readPointer()
      .add((index % CHUNK) * ue.objects.itemSize);
    const fieldPath = at('Attribute');
    fieldPath.writePointer(field.property);
    // FWeakObjectPtr: object index and serial number (none yet: resolved by the path)
    const serial = item.add(Process.pointerSize + 8).readS32();
    fieldPath.add(FIELD_PATH_OWNER).writeS32(serial === 0 ? -1 : index);
    fieldPath.add(FIELD_PATH_OWNER + 4).writeS32(serial);
    fieldPath.add(FIELD_PATH_PATH).writePointer(path);
    fieldPath.add(FIELD_PATH_PATH + Process.pointerSize).writeS32(1);
    fieldPath.add(FIELD_PATH_PATH + Process.pointerSize + 4).writeS32(1);
    at('AttributeOwner').writePointer(owner);
  }

  function gasSetBase(name, value) {
    // Set the base value of the player's attribute "Set.Attribute" or
    // "Attribute" through the game's setter; game thread only. Gives
    // { base, current } afterwards.
    if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value))
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.not_a_number', { value: String(value) });
    if (!isGameThread())
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.attribute_game_thread');
    reflection();
    const parts = currentPlayerParts();
    if (parts === null)
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.no_player');
    const setter = findAttributeSetter();
    if (setter !== null && setter.setClass.isNull() && parts.asc.isNull())
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.no_ability_system');
    if (setter === null)
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.no_base_setter');
    const { set, field } = findAttribute(parts, name);
    const { signature } = setter;
    const parms = Memory.alloc(Math.max(signature.parmsSize, 8));
    parms.writeByteArray(new ArrayBuffer(Math.max(signature.parmsSize, 8)));
    const writeNumber = number => {
      if (number.type.kind === KIND.R8)
        parms.add(number.offset).writeDouble(value);
      else
        parms.add(number.offset).writeFloat(value);
    };
    const isFalse = (type, offset) => type.engine === 'bool'
      && (parms.add(offset + type.byteOffset).readU8() & type.byteMask) === 0;
    let notFound;
    if (setter.setClass.isNull()) {
      const [component, attribute, number, found] = signature.params;
      const keep = [];
      parms.add(component.offset).writePointer(parts.asc);
      writeGameplayAttribute(attribute.type, parms.add(attribute.offset), field, keep);
      writeNumber(number);
      invoke(setter.fn, null, parms);
      notFound = found !== undefined && isFalse(found.type, found.offset);
    } else {
      // On the set, by the attribute's name: the FName its property has
      if (!classChain(set.add(OBJECT_CLASS).readPointer())
        .some(klass => klass.equals(setter.setClass)))
        throw grembyteError('error.unreal.no_base_setter');
      const [attribute, number] = signature.params;
      Memory.copy(parms.add(attribute.offset), field.property.add(ue.layout.fieldName), 8);
      writeNumber(number);
      invoke(setter.fn, set, parms);
      notFound = signature.returnOffset >= 0
        && isFalse(signature.returns, signature.returnOffset);
    }
    if (notFound)
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.attribute_not_found', { name });
    const data = layout(field.type.klass).fields;
    const read = entry => set.add(field.offset)
      .add(data.find(part => part.name === entry).offset).readFloat();
    return { base: read('BaseValue'), current: read('CurrentValue') };
  }

  return {
    id: 'unreal',
    refresh,
    // All code lies in modules: it is named module+offset.
    locate: () => (module === null ? undefined : null),
    name: () => null,
    describe: () => null,
    identify: () => null,
    compile,
    resolve,
    assemblies,
    classes,
    methodsByToken,
    nativeSymbols,
    checkAll: methods => methods.map(() => false),
    compileAll,
    describeAll: addresses => addresses.map(() => null),
    cancelBatches: () => 0,
    batchesRunning: () => false,
    releaseCode,
    prepare,
    callFrame,
    classOf,
    layout,
    readValue,
    valueJs,
    writeValue,
    // UObjects need no write barrier
    writeReference: (_owner, address, pointer) => address.writePointer(pointer),
    // Unreal has no getters to evaluate.
    properties: () => [],
    drainMain,
    onMainThread,
    signatureOf,
    findClass,
    findMethod,
    findObject,
    findObjects,
    outerName,
    // The inspector's title: an object by its FName
    instanceName: uobjectName,
    browseClasses,
    browseInstances,
    gasAttributes,
    gasSetBase,
    classChain,
    objectClassName: object => layout(classOf(object)).name,
    virtualMethod,
    methods,
    elements,
    invoke,
    writeParameter,
    newString: () => {
      throw grembyteError('error.unreal.no_string_objects');
    },
    onRuntimeThread: work => new Promise(resolve => resolve(work())),
    // The monitor shows Unity's object names; here the UObject's FName.
    unityName: uobjectName,
    // For checks and troubleshooting: where the reflection was found.
    reflection: () => {
      const found = reflection();
      return { module: module.name, names: found.names, objects: found.objects.table,
               itemSize: found.objects.itemSize, layout: found.layout };
    }
  };
})();

registerEngine(unreal);

```

`grembyte/engines/unreal/agent.py`:

```py
"""Unreal Engine games: their reflection data (UClass, UFunction, FProperty).

An Unreal game is native code; what Mono's embedding API is for Mono games
is Unreal's reflection here, which the engine keeps for Blueprints,
serialization and networking. Nothing is exported for it in a shipping
build, so the agent snippet in agent.js finds two globals in the data of the
game's executable by their shape:

``FNamePool``
    Every FName's text, in blocks; the first block starts with ``None`` and
    ``ByteProperty``. Unreal Engine 4.23 and later.
``GUObjectArray``
    Every UObject (classes, functions, packages, actors ...), in chunks of
    65536 items, each item starting with the object's address.

Where UStruct, FField, FProperty and UFunction keep their fields differs
between engine versions and build settings; the agent measures it on
objects every game has (CoreUObject's ``Class``, ``Object``, ``Vector``,
``Transform`` and ``Object:ExecuteUbergraph``).

``UNREAL_AGENT_SOURCE`` is the Unreal engine adapter of the agent: it
defines ``unreal`` and registers it (see grembyte/engines/base.py for the
contract). The catalog's assemblies are packages: ``/Script/<Module>`` for
the classes of a C++ module, and for Blueprints, which have a package each,
their first folder (``/Game/Blueprints``). The methods are UFunctions; the
token naming one is a hash of package, class and function name, since
object indexes change between runs.

The trace hooks a native UFunction's exec thunk (its ``Func``), and gives a
Blueprint function a stub of its own as ``Func`` that jumps on to the script
interpreter (``releaseCode`` restores them). Either way it sees calls through
``ProcessEvent`` and from Blueprint code, not C++ calling C++ directly (the
native trace sees those), nor Blueprint code calling a Blueprint function of
its own class directly (the interpreter does not pass ``Func`` for that).

For the method monitor, ``prepare`` answers ``frame: true`` and
``callFrame`` finds a call's arguments in its ``FFrame`` (Node, Object, Code,
Locals): through ProcessEvent the frame is the function's own and Locals its
parameters; called from Blueprint code, a native function gets the caller's
frame with Code at the argument expressions, of which the simple ones
(``EX_LocalVariable``, ``EX_InstanceVariable``, constants, ``EX_Self``) are
decoded. ``layout`` and ``readValue`` read objects and structs through their
FProperties (FString, FName, TArray, bitfield bools, weak pointers).
"""

from grembyte.agent.source import load_agent_source


UNREAL_AGENT_SOURCE = load_agent_source(__file__)

```

`grembyte/features/assemblies.py`:

```py
"""The assemblies the catalog and the Mono trace read.

A game loads dozens of assemblies; most of the game logic usually sits in a
few (``Assembly-CSharp`` and the game's own libraries). The user can pick
them once per program (see grembyte.ui.widgets.assemblies); the selection is
saved and limits the catalog and the trace to them. Without a selection both
use every assembly that is not part of the framework, as before; the
catalog reads framework assemblies on request.
"""


def chosen_assemblies(names, selection, engine):
    """The loaded assemblies (``names``) to read, in their order.

    ``selection`` is the set of selected names, empty for none; then all
    assemblies that are not part of the framework of ``engine``.
    """
    if selection:
        return [name for name in names if name in selection]
    return [name for name in names if not engine.is_framework_assembly(name)]


def missing_assemblies(names, selection):
    """The selected assemblies the game has not loaded (now), sorted."""
    return sorted(set(selection) - set(names))

```

`grembyte/features/call_graph.py`:

```py
"""Call graph: which methods a C# method calls, and which call it.

Read from the methods' IL code (ECMA-335 partition III), not from running
them: the engine adapter hands out a method's code (``methodBodies``), the
calls in it (``call``, ``callvirt``, ``newobj``, ``ldftn`` ...) name their
target by a metadata token, and the adapter says which method a token names
(``resolveTokens``). What a method calls shows in the order of its code.

Who calls a method needs the calls of every method of the assemblies looked
at: an index per assembly (``build_call_index``), kept in the catalog cache
like the classes (see grembyte.features.catalog_cache). A call into another
assembly names its target by that assembly's token, so the index notes the
builds it was made with and is made anew when they differ
(``read_call_index``): the same build of a library may meet another
UnityEngine in another game.

The C# compiler moves the body of an ``async`` method or an iterator into
the ``MoveNext`` method of a class it generates (``Outer.<Load>d__0``); the
graph shows such a method under the method it came from (``async_owner``).
Calls of virtual methods and interfaces name the method they were compiled
against, not the override that runs.
"""

import itertools
import queue
import re
import struct
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass

import frida
from PySide6.QtCore import QThread, Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core import logs, messages
from grembyte.core import sessions
from grembyte.attach.frida_attach import CLEANUP_ERRORS, FRIDA_ERRORS, attach_session
from grembyte.engines.registry import resolve_engine
from grembyte.features import catalog_cache, games
from grembyte.features.assemblies import chosen_assemblies
from grembyte.features.catalog import (
    AGENT_SOURCE,
    CatalogMethod,
    catalog_method_from_identity,
    catalog_methods,
)

# --- IL code ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Opcodes that name a method, and how the graph shows them
CALL_OPCODES = {0x28: "call", 0x6F: "callvirt", 0x73: "newobj", 0x27: "jmp",
                0xFE06: "ldftn", 0xFE07: "ldvirtftn"}
# Operand sizes of the one-byte opcodes; all others have none.
_OPERANDS = {
    **dict.fromkeys((0x0E, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x1F, 0xDE, *range(0x2B, 0x38)), 1),
    **dict.fromkeys((0x20, 0x22, 0x27, 0x28, 0x29, 0x6F, 0x70, 0x71, 0x72, 0x73, 0x74, 0x75,
                     0x79, 0x7B, 0x7C, 0x7D, 0x7E, 0x7F, 0x80, 0x81, 0x8C, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0xA3,
                     0xA4, 0xA5, 0xC2, 0xC6, 0xD0, 0xDD, *range(0x38, 0x45)), 4),
    0x21: 8, 0x23: 8,
}
# ... and of the two-byte ones (0xFE xx)
_OPERANDS_FE = {0x06: 4, 0x07: 4, 0x09: 2, 0x0A: 2, 0x0B: 2, 0x0C: 2, 0x0D: 2, 0x0E: 2,
                0x12: 1, 0x15: 4, 0x16: 4, 0x19: 1, 0x1C: 4}
_SWITCH = 0x45
# Metadata tables a call's token may point into: MethodDef, MemberRef, MethodSpec
METHOD_DEF, MEMBER_REF, METHOD_SPEC = 0x06, 0x0A, 0x2B


def calls_in(code):
    """``(opcode name, token)`` of the calls in IL ``code``, in the order of the code.

    Stops at code it cannot decode (its calls so far stay).
    """
    calls = []
    at, end = 0, len(code)
    while at < end:
        opcode = code[at]
        at += 1
        if opcode == 0xFE:
            if at >= end:
                break
            opcode = 0xFE00 | code[at]
            at += 1
            size = _OPERANDS_FE.get(opcode & 0xFF, 0)
        elif opcode == _SWITCH:
            if at + 4 > end:
                break
            size = 4 + 4 * struct.unpack_from("<I", code, at)[0]
        else:
            size = _OPERANDS.get(opcode, 0)
        if at + size > end:
            break
        if opcode in CALL_OPCODES:
            token = struct.unpack_from("<I", code, at)[0]
            if token >> 24 in (METHOD_DEF, MEMBER_REF, METHOD_SPEC):
                calls.append((CALL_OPCODES[opcode], token))
        at += size
    return calls


def split_bodies(buffer):
    """``{token: code}`` of a ``methodBodies`` answer (records: token, size, code)."""
    bodies, at = {}, 0
    while at + 8 <= len(buffer):
        token, size = struct.unpack_from("<II", buffer, at)
        bodies[token] = bytes(buffer[at + 8:at + 8 + size])
        at += 8 + size
    return bodies


# --- Index ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Methods per request to the agent
CHUNK = 1000


def method_tokens(classes):
    """The tokens of the methods of a catalog ``classes`` answer."""
    return [entry[4] for _class_name, methods in classes for entry in methods]


def build_call_index(assembly, classes, read_bodies, resolve, progress=None):
    """The calls of every method of ``assembly`` (``classes``: its catalog answer).

    ``read_bodies(tokens)`` returns ``{token: IL code}``, ``resolve(tokens)``
    ``[assembly, token, signature]`` (or None) for each token in the code;
    ``progress(done, total)`` hears how far it is. The index is JSON:
    ``{"targets": [[assembly, token, signature], ...],
    "calls": [[caller token, [[opcode name, target index], ...]], ...]}``.
    """
    tokens = method_tokens(classes)
    own = {entry[4]: entry[5] for _class_name, methods in classes for entry in methods}
    found = []
    for start in range(0, len(tokens), CHUNK):
        if progress is not None:
            progress(start, len(tokens))
        chunk = tokens[start:start + CHUNK]
        bodies = read_bodies(chunk)
        found.extend((token, calls_in(bodies.get(token, b""))) for token in chunk)
    # What each token names: the assembly's own methods are known, others asked for.
    named = {token: [assembly, token, signature] for token, signature in own.items()}
    unknown = sorted({token for _caller, calls in found for _op, token in calls} - named.keys())
    for start in range(0, len(unknown), CHUNK):
        chunk = unknown[start:start + CHUNK]
        named.update(zip(chunk, resolve(chunk)))
    targets, index_of = [], {}
    calls = []
    for caller, found_calls in found:
        listed = []
        for opcode, token in found_calls:
            target = named.get(token)
            if target is None:
                continue
            key = tuple(target)
            if key not in index_of:
                index_of[key] = len(targets)
                targets.append(list(target))
            listed.append([opcode, index_of[key]])
        if listed:
            calls.append([caller, listed])
    if progress is not None:
        progress(len(tokens), len(tokens))
    return {"targets": targets, "calls": calls}


def read_call_index(engine, assembly, mvid, mvids, build):
    """The call index of ``assembly`` (its ``mvid``) in a process whose
    assemblies have ``mvids`` ({name: mvid}).

    From the catalog cache if it was made with the same builds of the
    assemblies it refers to, else ``build()`` makes it (and it is kept).
    """
    def made():
        index = build()
        referred = {target[0] for target in index["targets"]} - {assembly}
        index["references"] = {name: mvids.get(name) for name in sorted(referred)}
        return index

    index, cached = catalog_cache.read_cached(engine, assembly, mvid, made,
                                              kind=catalog_cache.CALLS)
    if cached and any(mvids.get(name) != referred
                      for name, referred in index.get("references", {}).items()):
        index = catalog_cache.read_cached(engine, assembly, mvid, made, fresh=True,
                                          kind=catalog_cache.CALLS)[0]
    return index


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Call:
    """One call in the graph: how (``opcode``) and the method (a CatalogMethod)."""

    opcode: str
    method: CatalogMethod


# ``Outer.<Load>d__0``: the class the compiler made of an async method or iterator
_STATE_MACHINE = re.compile(r"^(?P<outer>.+)\.<(?P<name>[^>]+)>d__\d+$")


def async_owner(method):
    """``(class name, method name)`` of the async method or iterator whose body
    ``method`` (a ``MoveNext``) is, else None."""
    if method.name != "MoveNext":
        return None
    found = _STATE_MACHINE.match(method.class_name)
    return None if found is None else (found["outer"], found["name"])


def state_machines(method, methods):
    """The ``MoveNext`` methods among ``methods`` that hold the body of ``method``."""
    return [other for other in methods if other.assembly == method.assembly
            and async_owner(other) == (method.class_name, method.name)]


def callees_of(index, method, lookup, engine="mono"):
    """The Calls ``method`` makes, by the index of its assembly.

    ``lookup(assembly, token)`` is the CatalogMethod of a method if known.
    """
    for caller, listed in index["calls"]:
        if caller == method.token:
            return [Call(opcode, _method_of(index["targets"][target], lookup, engine))
                    for opcode, target in listed]
    return []


def callers_in(index, method, methods_by_token):
    """The Calls of the methods in ``index`` that call ``method``.

    ``methods_by_token``: the CatalogMethods of the index's assembly.
    """
    targets = {position for position, (target_assembly, token, _signature)
               in enumerate(index["targets"])
               if target_assembly == method.assembly and token == method.token}
    found = []
    for caller, listed in index["calls"]:
        opcodes = [opcode for opcode, target in listed if target in targets]
        if opcodes and caller in methods_by_token:
            found.append(Call(opcodes[0], methods_by_token[caller]))
    return found


def _method_of(target, lookup, engine):
    target_assembly, token, signature = target
    known = lookup(target_assembly, token)
    # A generic instance has its definition's token but another signature.
    if known is not None and known.signature == signature:
        return known
    return catalog_method_from_identity({"engine": engine, "image": target_assembly,
                                         "token": token, "method": signature})


# --- Worker -----------------------------------------------------------------

class NotCached(Exception):
    """What a question needs is neither in the catalog cache nor readable:
    the game is not running (offline, see CallGraphWorker)."""


class _OfflineApi:
    """Stands in for the agent of a game that is not running: it knows the
    game's assemblies (a KnownGame, see grembyte.features.games), nothing else."""

    def __init__(self, game):
        self.game = game

    def assemblies(self):
        return self.game.assemblies

    def classes(self, name):
        raise NotCached(name)

    def method_bodies(self, name, _tokens):
        raise NotCached(name)

    def resolve_tokens(self, name, _tokens):
        raise NotCached(name)


class CallGraphWorker(QThread):
    """Keep a Frida session open and answer call graph questions about a process.

    The public methods are safe to call from the GUI thread and return a
    request id; answers come back through the signals. ``selection`` (the
    user's assembly selection, see grembyte.features.assemblies) decides which
    assemblies are searched for callers.

    With ``game`` (a KnownGame) instead of a running process the answers come
    from the catalog cache alone; a question it cannot answer fails with
    ``NOT_CACHED``, and callers are searched in the assemblies indexed before.
    """

    # request id, method (CatalogMethod), its Calls, the Calls of its body
    # in a compiler-made MoveNext (async methods, iterators)
    callees_found = Signal(int, object, object, object)
    # request id, method, the Calls of the methods that call it, the
    # assemblies not searched (offline: no call index in the cache)
    callers_found = Signal(int, object, object, object)
    # request id, message (NOT_CACHED: offline, not in the cache)
    request_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # assemblies indexed so far, of how many, the one at hand
    progress = Signal(int, int, str)
    worker_failed = Signal(str)

    NOT_CACHED = "not cached"

    _requests = itertools.count(1)

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None, engine=None, selection=(), game=None):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments,too-many-positional-arguments
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.pid = pid
        self.game = game
        self.engine = resolve_engine(pid, engine) if game is None else engine
        self.selection = frozenset(selection)
        self._commands = queue.Queue()
        self._detached = threading.Event()
        # assembly -> (mvid, classes, {token: CatalogMethod}, call index or None)
        self._known = {}
        self._mvids = None

    def callees(self, method):
        """What ``method`` (a CatalogMethod) calls; expect callees_found."""
        return self._ask("callees", method)

    def callers(self, method):
        """Which methods call ``method``; expect callers_found (and progress)."""
        return self._ask("callers", method)

    def _ask(self, action, method):
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put((action, request_id, method))
        return request_id

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.CATALOG)
    def run(self):
        if self.game is not None:
            self._serve(_OfflineApi(self.game))
            return
        session = None
        script = None
        try:
            session = attach_session(self.pid)
            sessions.SESSIONS.set_frida_session(self, session)
            session.on("detached", lambda _reason, _crash: self._detached.set())
            script = session.create_script(AGENT_SOURCE)
            script.load()
            self._serve(script.exports_sync)
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (frida.RPCException, OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.worker_failed.emit(messages.describe(error))
        finally:
            for close in (script and script.unload, session and session.detach):
                if close:
                    try:
                        close()
                    except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                        logs.cleanup_failed(error)

    def _serve(self, api):
        while not self.isInterruptionRequested() and not self._detached.is_set():
            try:
                action, request_id, method = self._commands.get(timeout=0.05)
            except queue.Empty:
                continue
            try:
                if action == "callees":
                    self._answer_callees(api, request_id, method)
                else:
                    self._answer_callers(api, request_id, method)
            except NotCached:
                self.request_failed.emit(request_id, self.NOT_CACHED)
            except frida.RPCException as error:
                self.request_failed.emit(request_id, messages.describe(error))

    # --- Answers ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def _answer_callees(self, api, request_id, method):
        _mvid, classes, methods = self._assembly(api, method.assembly)
        machines = state_machines(method, methods.values())
        index = self._stored_index(api, method.assembly)
        if index is None:
            # Not indexed yet: read just these methods instead of the assembly.
            wanted = {method.token} | {machine.token for machine in machines}
            index = build_call_index(
                method.assembly,
                [[class_name, [entry for entry in entries if entry[4] in wanted]]
                 for class_name, entries in classes],
                lambda tokens: split_bodies(api.method_bodies(method.assembly, tokens)),
                lambda tokens: api.resolve_tokens(method.assembly, tokens))
        body = [call for machine in machines
                for call in callees_of(index, machine, self._lookup, self.engine.id)]
        self.callees_found.emit(request_id, method,
                                callees_of(index, method, self._lookup, self.engine.id), body)

    def _answer_callers(self, api, request_id, method):
        names = chosen_assemblies(list(self._assembly_mvids(api)), self.selection, self.engine)
        if method.assembly not in names:
            names.append(method.assembly)
        found, missing = [], []
        for done, name in enumerate(names):
            self.progress.emit(done, len(names), name)
            if self.isInterruptionRequested():
                return
            try:
                found.extend(callers_in(self._index(api, name), method,
                                        self._assembly(api, name)[2]))
            except NotCached:
                missing.append(name)
        self.progress.emit(len(names), len(names), "")
        self.callers_found.emit(request_id, method, found, missing)

    # --- What is known of the assemblies ----------------------------------------
    def _assembly_mvids(self, api):
        if self._mvids is None:
            found = api.assemblies()
            if self.game is None:
                games.remember(self.pid, self.engine.id, found)
            self._mvids = {a["name"]: a.get("mvid") for a in found}
        return self._mvids

    def _assembly(self, api, name):
        """(mvid, classes, {token: CatalogMethod}) of assembly ``name``."""
        if name not in self._known:
            mvid = self._assembly_mvids(api).get(name)
            classes = catalog_cache.read_classes(self.engine.id, name, mvid,
                                                 lambda: api.classes(name))[0]
            methods = {method.token: method
                       for method in catalog_methods(name, classes, self.engine.id)}
            self._known[name] = (mvid, classes, methods, None)
        return self._known[name][:3]

    def _lookup(self, assembly, token):
        """The CatalogMethod of a method of an assembly read already, else None."""
        known = self._known.get(assembly)
        return None if known is None else known[2].get(token)

    def _stored_index(self, api, name):
        """The call index of ``name`` if made already (and still fitting), else None."""
        if self._known[name][3] is None:
            try:
                self._index(api, name, build=False)
            except NotCached:
                return None
        return self._known[name][3]

    def _index(self, api, name, build=True):
        """The call index of assembly ``name`` (see build_call_index); without
        ``build`` only one from the cache (else NotCached)."""
        mvid, classes, methods = self._assembly(api, name)
        index = self._known[name][3]
        if index is None:
            def make():
                if not build:
                    raise NotCached(name)
                return build_call_index(
                    name, classes,
                    lambda tokens: split_bodies(api.method_bodies(name, tokens)),
                    lambda tokens: api.resolve_tokens(name, tokens))
            index = read_call_index(self.engine.id, name, mvid, self._assembly_mvids(api), make)
            self._known[name] = (mvid, classes, methods, index)
        return index

```

`grembyte/features/catalog.py`:

```py
"""Catalog of the classes and methods a game's managed runtime has loaded.

A short Frida session asks the engine adapter (see grembyte/engines) for the
loaded assemblies and, assembly by assembly, for their classes and methods.
Reading a class may make the runtime load it, so framework assemblies (for
Mono: mscorlib, System, UnityEngine, ...) are only read when asked for: they
are large and rarely what one looks for.
"""

import re
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace

import frida
from PySide6.QtCore import QThread, Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core import logs, messages
from grembyte.core import sessions
from grembyte.engines.registry import ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE, resolve_engine
from grembyte.attach.frida_attach import CLEANUP_ERRORS, FRIDA_ERRORS, attach_session
from grembyte.agent.source import load_agent_source
from grembyte.features import catalog_cache, games
from grembyte.features.assemblies import chosen_assemblies


# Also the call graph's agent (see grembyte.features.call_graph)
AGENT_SOURCE = ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE + load_agent_source(__file__)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CatalogMethod:
    """One method of the catalog."""

    assembly: str
    class_name: str
    name: str
    parameters: str
    return_type: str
    static: bool
    token: int
    # ``Namespace.Class:Method (int,single)`` as the runtime names it
    signature: str
    engine: str = "mono"
    argument_names: tuple = field(default=(), compare=False)

    @property
    def display_signature(self):
        """The method signature with parameter names, for UI display."""
        if not self.argument_names:
            return self.signature
        head, separator, parameters = self.signature.partition(" (")
        if not separator or not parameters.endswith(")"):
            return self.signature
        types = split_type_arguments(parameters[:-1])
        named = [
            f"{type_name} {self.argument_names[index] if index < len(self.argument_names) else f'arg{index}'}"
            for index, type_name in enumerate(types)
        ]
        return f"{head} ({','.join(named)})"

    def identity(self):
        """What finds the method in the running game (see HookSpec.managed)."""
        return {"engine": self.engine, "image": self.assembly, "file": None,
                "token": self.token, "method": self.signature}


def csharp_name(text, engine="mono"):
    """``text`` with Mono's nested class names as C# writes them:
    ``StrongholdAdventure/Type`` reads ``StrongholdAdventure.Type``.

    For display only; signatures keep Mono's form, by which hooks and
    ``ctx.call`` find methods. Other engines' names (Unreal's paths) stay.
    """
    return text.replace("/", ".") if engine == "mono" and text else text


def short_name(signature):
    """``Class:Method`` of ``Namespace.Class:Method (params)``."""
    class_name, _, method = signature.split(" (")[0].partition(":")
    return f"{class_name.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]}:{method}"


# ``Ns.Class`2`` at the end of a signature's class part: a generic class
# without type arguments, i.e. its definition.
_GENERIC_DEFINITION = re.compile(r"`(\d+)$")
# The type parameters Mono shows in a class name: ``Ns.Map<TKey,TValue>``
_TYPE_PARAMETERS = re.compile(r"<([^<>]*)>$")


def generic_parameters(method):
    """The type parameters of the generic class a method was defined in, else ().

    Such a method (``R3.ReactiveProperty`1:set_Value (T)``) has no code of
    its own, only its instances have (see with_type_arguments).
    """
    found = _GENERIC_DEFINITION.search(method.signature.split(":", 1)[0])
    if found is None:
        return ()
    named = _TYPE_PARAMETERS.search(method.class_name)
    if named is not None:
        return tuple(name.strip() for name in named.group(1).split(","))
    count = int(found.group(1))
    return ("T",) if count == 1 else tuple(f"T{index}" for index in range(1, count + 1))


def split_type_arguments(text):
    """``int, Ns.Map`2<int,string>`` -> ``["int", "Ns.Map`2<int,string>"]``."""
    arguments, depth, current = [], 0, ""
    for char in text:
        depth += {"<": 1, ">": -1}.get(char, 0)
        if char == "," and depth == 0:
            arguments.append(current.strip())
            current = ""
        else:
            current += char
    arguments.append(current.strip())
    return [argument for argument in arguments if argument]


def with_type_arguments(method, arguments):
    """The method of a generic class's instance, e.g. ``ReactiveProperty`1<int>``.

    The signature keeps the definition's parameters (``(T)``); the agent
    binds the class to ``arguments`` (see resolveMethod in the Mono agent).
    """
    head, _, rest = method.signature.partition(":")
    listed = ", ".join(arguments)
    class_name, count = _TYPE_PARAMETERS.subn(f"<{listed}>", method.class_name)
    return replace(method, signature=f"{head}<{listed}>:{rest}",
                   class_name=class_name if count else f"{method.class_name}<{listed}>")


def catalog_method_from_identity(identity):
    """A CatalogMethod for a method known by its identity (e.g. of a hook).

    The return type and whether it is static are not part of the identity;
    the method monitor learns them when it starts.
    """
    signature = identity["method"]
    head, _, parameters = signature.partition(" ")
    class_name, _, name = head.partition(":")
    return CatalogMethod(identity["image"], class_name, name, parameters or "()", "?", False,
                         identity["token"], signature, identity.get("engine") or "mono")


def catalog_methods(assembly, classes, engine="mono"):
    """Turn the agent's ``classes`` answer for ``assembly`` into CatalogMethods."""
    result = []
    for class_name, methods in classes:
        for entry in methods:
            name, parameters, return_type, static, token, signature, *metadata = entry
            # Mono and IL2CPP add parameter names after the trace flags; older
            # cache entries and other engines have no such field.
            argument_names = (
                tuple(metadata[-1])
                if engine in ("mono", "il2cpp") and len(metadata) >= 3
                and isinstance(metadata[-1], list) else ()
            )
            result.append(CatalogMethod(
                assembly, class_name, name, parameters, return_type, bool(static), token,
                signature, engine, argument_names,
            ))
    return result


class CatalogWorker(QThread):
    """Read the catalog of a process.

    Emits ``assemblies_found`` with all loaded assemblies first, then
    ``assembly_loaded`` for each one it reads: those named in ``assemblies``,
    or else the loaded ones of ``selection`` (the user's assembly selection,
    see grembyte.features.assemblies), or else every assembly that is not part
    of the framework. ``engine`` is the adapter (see grembyte/engines),
    detected if not given.

    An assembly read before in the same build comes from the catalog cache
    (see grembyte.features.catalog_cache), announced by ``assembly_cached``
    before its ``assembly_loaded``; ``fresh`` reads every one anew.
    """

    assemblies_found = Signal(object)
    # assembly name, its methods (CatalogMethod)
    assembly_loaded = Signal(str, object)
    # assembly name: its methods come from the cache
    assembly_cached = Signal(str)
    # assembly name, error message
    assembly_failed = Signal(str, str)
    catalog_failed = Signal(str)

    def __init__(self, pid, assemblies=None, parent=None, engine=None, selection=(),
                 fresh=False):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments,too-many-positional-arguments
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.pid = pid
        self.assemblies = assemblies
        self.selection = frozenset(selection)
        self.fresh = fresh
        self.engine = resolve_engine(pid, engine)
        self._detached = threading.Event()

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.CATALOG)
    def run(self):
        session = None
        script = None
        try:
            session = attach_session(self.pid)
            sessions.SESSIONS.set_frida_session(self, session)
            session.on("detached", lambda _reason, _crash: self._detached.set())
            script = session.create_script(AGENT_SOURCE)
            script.load()
            api = script.exports_sync
            found = api.assemblies()
            games.remember(self.pid, self.engine.id, found)
            self.assemblies_found.emit(found)
            names = self.assemblies
            if names is None:
                names = chosen_assemblies([a["name"] for a in found], self.selection,
                                          self.engine)
            mvids = {a["name"]: a.get("mvid") for a in found}
            for name in names:
                if self.isInterruptionRequested() or self._detached.is_set():
                    break
                try:
                    classes = self._classes(api, name, mvids.get(name))
                    self.assembly_loaded.emit(
                        name, catalog_methods(name, classes, self.engine.id))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.assembly_failed.emit(name, messages.describe(error))
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (frida.RPCException, OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.catalog_failed.emit(messages.describe(error))
        finally:
            if script is not None:
                try:
                    script.unload()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
            if session is not None:
                try:
                    session.detach()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)

    def _classes(self, api, name, mvid):
        """The agent's ``classes`` answer for ``name``, from the cache if it has it."""
        classes, cached = catalog_cache.read_classes(
            self.engine.id, name, mvid, lambda: api.classes(name), self.fresh)
        if cached:
            self.assembly_cached.emit(name)
        return classes


class EngineSymbolsWorker(QThread):
    """Ask the game's engine adapter for the names of its compiled code.

    IL2CPP names every C# method's code in GameAssembly, Unreal every native
    UFunction's exec thunk (see ``nativeSymbols`` in the adapters).
    ``found`` carries [(address in the process, name), ...].
    """

    found = Signal(object)
    failed = Signal(str)

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None, engine=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.pid = pid
        self.engine = resolve_engine(pid, engine)

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.CATALOG)
    def run(self):
        session = None
        script = None
        try:
            session = attach_session(self.pid)
            sessions.SESSIONS.set_frida_session(self, session)
            script = session.create_script(AGENT_SOURCE)
            script.load()
            symbols = [(int(address, 16), name)
                       for address, name in script.exports_sync.native_symbols()]
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.found.emit(symbols)
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (frida.RPCException, OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.failed.emit(messages.describe(error))
        finally:
            if script is not None:
                try:
                    script.unload()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
            if session is not None:
                try:
                    session.detach()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)


class CachedCatalogWorker(QThread):
    """Read the catalog of a game that is not running from the catalog cache.

    ``game`` is a KnownGame (see grembyte.features.games): the builds it loaded
    when it was read last. The signals are CatalogWorker's; an assembly whose
    build is not in the cache (never read, or pruned) gives
    ``assembly_failed`` with ``NOT_CACHED``.
    """

    assemblies_found = Signal(object)
    assembly_loaded = Signal(str, object)
    assembly_cached = Signal(str)
    assembly_failed = Signal(str, str)
    catalog_failed = Signal(str)

    NOT_CACHED = "not cached"

    def __init__(self, game, assemblies=None, parent=None, engine=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.game = game
        self.assemblies = assemblies
        self.engine = engine

    def run(self):
        found = self.game.assemblies
        self.assemblies_found.emit(found)
        names = self.assemblies
        if names is None:
            names = chosen_assemblies([a["name"] for a in found], (), self.engine)
        mvids = self.game.mvids()
        for name in names:
            if self.isInterruptionRequested():
                break
            classes = catalog_cache.load(self.engine.id, name, mvids.get(name))
            if classes is None:
                self.assembly_failed.emit(name, self.NOT_CACHED)
                continue
            self.assembly_cached.emit(name)
            self.assembly_loaded.emit(name, catalog_methods(name, classes, self.engine.id))
```
