```py
        separator = "" if returns.endswith("*") else " "
        lines.append(f"{returns}{separator}{name}({', '.join(arguments) or 'void'})")
        return lines

    def _find_targets(self):
        function = self.function
        for instruction in self.instructions:
            if _mnemonic(instruction).startswith(("j", "loop")) and instruction.operands and \
                    instruction.operands[0].type == X86_OP_IMM:
                target = instruction.operands[0].imm
                if function.start <= target < function.end:
                    self.targets.add(target)

    def _emit(self, text, instruction, defines=None, expression=None, uses=None,
              target=None):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments,too-many-positional-arguments,too-many-locals
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        operands = instruction.operands
        memory = frozenset(self._global_target(instruction, operand)
                           for operand in operands if operand.type == X86_OP_MEM)
        written = frozenset({self._global_target(instruction, operands[0])}) \
            if operands and operands[0].type == X86_OP_MEM else frozenset()
        writes = set()
        for register_id in instruction.regs_access()[1]:
            family = self._family(instruction, register_id)
            if family is not None:
                writes.add(family)
        if uses is None:
            uses = self._reads(instruction)
        reads_memory = memory if mnemonic != "lea" else frozenset()
        notes = list(self.notes)
        if instruction is self.current:
            # A folded-in value reads what its assignment read
            for family in self.substituted:
                folded = self.substitutes[family]
                uses = (uses - {family}) | folded.uses
                reads_memory |= folded.reads_memory
                notes += folded.notes
        movable = mnemonic not in ("call", "ret", "pop") and \
            not mnemonic.startswith(("j", "loop")) and \
            not text.startswith(("asm(", "if (", "return"))
        line = _Line(text, instruction.address, defines=defines, expression=expression,
                     uses=frozenset(uses), writes=frozenset(writes), target=target,
                     reads_memory=reads_memory, writes_memory=written, movable=movable,
                     notes=tuple(notes))
        self.lines.append(line)
        self.emitted.append(line)

    # --- registers ----------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _family(instruction, register_id):
        found = _FAMILIES.get(instruction.reg_name(register_id))
        return found[0] if found else None

    def _register(self, instruction, register_id):
        """A register as read: the value folded into this use, its argument
        name while it holds the argument, else its name."""
        name = instruction.reg_name(register_id)
        found = _FAMILIES.get(name)
        if found is None:
            return name
        if instruction is self.current and found[0] in self.substitutes:
            self.substituted.add(found[0])
            return _atom(self.substitutes[found[0]].expression)
        if found[0] in self.parameters:
            return self.parameters[found[0]]
        return name

    def _sized(self, family, type_):
        """``family``'s register at the width of a signature type (rdi, int -> edi)."""
        if family in self.parameters:
            return self.parameters[family]
        if family.startswith("xmm"):
            return family
        widths = _BY_WIDTH.get(family, {})
        return widths.get(_TYPE_WIDTHS.get(type_, 8), family)

    def _reads(self, instruction):
        families = set()
        for register_id in instruction.regs_access()[0]:
            family = self._family(instruction, register_id)
            if family is not None:
                families.add(family)
        return frozenset(families)

    # --- operands -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _global_target(self, instruction, operand):
        """The address a memory operand names directly (RIP-relative or absolute), or None."""
        memory = operand.mem
        if memory.index:
            return None
        if memory.base:
            if instruction.reg_name(memory.base) != "rip":
                return None
            return instruction.address + instruction.size + memory.disp
        if not self.index.absolute_addresses:
            return None
        target = memory.disp & ((1 << self.image.bits) - 1)
        return target if self.image.contains(target) else None

    def _address_of(self, target):
        """A global's address as C: a string, a function, &name, or the number."""
        index = self.index
        text = index.string_at(target)
        if text is not None:
            return index.describe(target)
        section = self.image.section_at(target)
        if section is not None and not section.writable and not section.executable and \
                self.image.read(target, 1) == b"\0":
            return '""'  # an empty string, often the end of another one
        name = self.image.names.get(target) or self.image.imports.get(target)
        if name is not None:
            return name if section is not None and section.executable else f"&{name}"
        if index.function_starting(target) is not None:
            return index.name(target)
        return f"0x{target:x}"

    def _global_value(self, target, size, c_type):
        """A global's value as C: its name, or a read-only constant; else None."""
        # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements
        image = self.image
        if target in image.names:
            return image.names[target]
        if target in image.imports:
            return image.imports[target].rsplit("!", 1)[-1]
        section = image.section_at(target)
        if section is None or section.writable or section.executable:
            return None
        raw = image.read(target, size)
        if len(raw) != size:
            return None
        if c_type in ("float", "double") and size in (4, 8):
            return _float_literal(raw, size == 4)
        if size in (1, 2, 4) and c_type in _SIGNED.values():
            return _number(int.from_bytes(raw, "little", signed=True))
        if size in (1, 2, 4) and c_type in _UNSIGNED.values():
            return _number(int.from_bytes(raw, "little"))
        found = self.index.describe(target)
        if found.startswith("→ "):
            return found[2:]
        return None

    def _address_text(self, instruction, operand, decimal=False, width=None):
        """The address of a memory operand: ``rax + 0x28``, ``rbx + rcx * 4``.
        ``width`` names the registers at that width (lea eax, [rdx + rdx * 4]
        computes edx + edx * 4)."""
        memory = operand.mem
        parts = []

        def register(register_id):
            name = self._register(instruction, register_id)
            found = _FAMILIES.get(name)
            if width is None or found is None:
                return name
            return _BY_WIDTH[found[0]].get(width, name)

        if memory.segment:
            parts.append(instruction.reg_name(memory.segment))
        if memory.base:
            parts.append(register(memory.base))
        if memory.index:
            index = register(memory.index)
            parts.append(f"{index} * {memory.scale}" if memory.scale != 1 else index)
        text = " + ".join(parts)
        if memory.disp or not parts:
            displacement = abs(memory.disp) if parts else memory.disp
            number = _number(displacement, hexadecimal=not decimal)
            if not parts:
                text = number
            else:
                text += (" - " if memory.disp < 0 else " + ") + number
        return text

    def _memory(self, instruction, operand, c_type):
        target = self._global_target(instruction, operand)
        if target is not None:
            value = self._global_value(target, operand.size, c_type)
            if value is not None:
                return value
            return f"*({c_type} *)0x{target:x}"
        address = self._address_text(instruction, operand)
        if " " in address:
            address = f"({address})"
        return f"*({c_type} *){address}"

    def _memory_type(self, instruction, operand, signedness=None):
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        if _is_sse(mnemonic) and operand.size in (4, 8) and \
                not mnemonic.lstrip("v").startswith(("cvtsi2", "movd", "movq")):
            return "float" if operand.size == 4 else "double"
        table = {"signed": _SIGNED, "unsigned": _UNSIGNED}.get(signedness, _PLAIN)
        return table.get(operand.size, "uint64_t")

    def _operand(self, instruction, operand, signedness=None, hexadecimal=False,
                 address_ok=False):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments,too-many-positional-arguments
        """An operand as C. ``signedness`` ("signed", "unsigned") picks the
        types of memory and casts registers to unsigned ones."""
        if operand.type == X86_OP_REG:
            name = self._register(instruction, operand.reg)
            if signedness == "unsigned" and not name.startswith("xmm"):
                return f"({_UNSIGNED.get(operand.size, 'uint64_t')}){name}"
            return name
        if operand.type == X86_OP_IMM:
            value = operand.imm
            if address_ok and self.index.absolute_addresses and value >= 0x10000 and \
                    self.image.contains(value):
                return self._address_of(value)
            if signedness == "unsigned" and value < 0:
                value &= (1 << (8 * (operand.size or 8))) - 1
            return _number(value, hexadecimal)
        if operand.type == X86_OP_MEM:
            return self._memory(instruction, operand,
                                self._memory_type(instruction, operand, signedness))
        return instruction.op_str

    def _assign(self, instruction, destination, expression, overwrite=True):
        """``destination = expression;``. Overwriting a register ends its
        argument name, so the destination is named by the register itself."""
        if destination.type == X86_OP_REG:
            family = self._family(instruction, destination.reg)
            name = instruction.reg_name(destination.reg) if overwrite else \
                self._register(instruction, destination.reg)
            self._emit(f"{name} = {expression};", instruction,
                       defines=family if overwrite else None, expression=expression,
                       uses=self._reads(instruction), target=name)
        else:
            target = self._operand(instruction, destination)
            self._emit(f"{target} = {expression};", instruction)

    def _asm(self, instruction):
        text = f"{instruction.mnemonic} {instruction.op_str}".strip()
        self._emit(f'asm("{text}");', instruction)

    # --- conditions -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def _condition(self, code):  # pylint: disable=too-many-branches
        flags = self.flags
        if flags is None:
            return "/* flags */"
        instruction = flags.instruction
        source = f"{instruction.mnemonic} {instruction.op_str}".strip()
        if flags.stale:
            return f"/* flags of {source} */"
        operands = instruction.operands
        text = None
        if flags.kind == "cmp" and len(operands) == 2:
            if code in _SIGNED_CONDITIONS:
                signed = "signed" if code not in ("e", "ne") else None
                left = self._operand(instruction, operands[0], signed)
                right = self._operand(instruction, operands[1], signed)
                text = f"{left} {_SIGNED_CONDITIONS[code]} {right}"
            elif code in _UNSIGNED_CONDITIONS:
                left = self._operand(instruction, operands[0], "unsigned")
                right = self._operand(instruction, operands[1], "unsigned")
                text = f"{left} {_UNSIGNED_CONDITIONS[code]} {right}"
            elif code in ("s", "ns"):
                left = self._operand(instruction, operands[0], "signed")
                right = self._operand(instruction, operands[1], "signed")
                text = f"{left} - {right} {'<' if code == 's' else '>='} 0"
        elif flags.kind in ("test", "zero") and code in _ZERO_CONDITIONS:
            left = self._operand(instruction, operands[0], "signed", hexadecimal=True)
            if flags.kind == "test" and len(operands) == 2 and \
                    (operands[1].type != X86_OP_REG or operands[0].type != X86_OP_REG or
                     operands[0].reg != operands[1].reg):
                right = self._operand(instruction, operands[1], hexadecimal=True)
                left = f"({left} & {right})"
            text = f"{left} {_ZERO_CONDITIONS[code]}"
        elif flags.kind == "result" and code in ("e", "ne", "s", "ns"):
            left = self._operand(instruction, operands[0], "signed")
            text = f"{left} {_ZERO_CONDITIONS[code]}"
        elif flags.kind == "float" and len(operands) == 2:
            left = self._operand(instruction, operands[0])
            right = self._operand(instruction, operands[1])
            relations = {"a": ">", "ae": ">=", "b": "<", "be": "<=", "e": "==", "ne": "!="}
            if code in relations:
                text = f"{left} {relations[code]} {right}"
            elif code in ("p", "np"):
                text = f"{'' if code == 'p' else '!'}isunordered({left}, {right})"
        if text is None:
            return f"/* flags of {source} */"
        self.notes.extend(flags.notes)
        return text

    def _set_flags(self, instruction):
        """The flags after ``instruction``."""
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        name = mnemonic[1:] if mnemonic.startswith("v") else mnemonic
        if mnemonic in _KEEP_FLAGS or name in _KEEP_FLAGS or \
                mnemonic.startswith(("j", "set", "cmov", "vmov")):
            return
        kind = None
        if name == "cmp":
            kind = "cmp"
        elif name == "test":
            kind = "test"
        elif name in ("comiss", "ucomiss", "comisd", "ucomisd"):
            kind = "float"
        elif name in ("and", "or", "xor"):
            kind = "zero"
        elif name in ("add", "sub", "inc", "dec", "neg", "shl", "sal", "sar", "shr"):
            kind = "result"
        self.flags = None if kind is None else _Flags(kind, instruction,
                                                      self._reads(instruction),
                                                      notes=tuple(self.notes))

    # --- calls ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _stub(self, target):
        """The import a stub at ``target`` jumps to (a PLT entry, a thunk), or None."""
        for instruction in self.index.instructions(target, target + 16, limit=3):
            if instruction.mnemonic in ("endbr64", "endbr32", "nop"):
                continue
            if _mnemonic(instruction) == "jmp" and instruction.operands and \
                    instruction.operands[0].type == X86_OP_MEM:
                slot = self._global_target(instruction, instruction.operands[0])
                if slot in self.image.imports:
                    return self.image.imports[slot].rsplit("!", 1)[-1]
            break
        return None

    def _callee(self, instruction, operand):
        """(name as C, Signature or None) of what a call or jump goes to."""
        # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements
        index = self.index
        if operand.type == X86_OP_IMM:
            target = operand.imm
            name = self.image.names.get(target)
            if name is not None and name in self.imports:
                return name.rsplit("!", 1)[-1], None
            if index.function_starting(target) is not None or name is not None:
                return index.name(target), index.signature(target)
            stub = self._stub(target)
            if stub is not None:
                return stub, None
            return index.where(target) or f"sub_{target:x}", None
        if operand.type == X86_OP_MEM:
            target = self._global_target(instruction, operand)
            if target is not None:
                if target in self.image.imports:
                    return self.image.imports[target].rsplit("!", 1)[-1], None
                if target in self.image.names:
                    return self.image.names[target], None
            return f"(*{self._operand(instruction, operand)})", None
        return f"(*{self._operand(instruction, operand)})", None

    def _fold(self, candidates):
        """({family: expression}, {family: register}) of the assignments to
        ``candidates`` before a call: those taken out of the body to become
        its arguments, and those that stay (something in between needs the
        register, or changes what it reads). Compilers mix other work into
        setting up the arguments (keeping the last result: ``lbl_gold = rax``);
        an assignment is moved past such a statement if neither changes
        what the other reads."""
        folded, kept = {}, {}
        taken = []
        used, written = set(), set()  # by the statements after the one looked at
        memory_written = set()
        start = max(0, len(self.lines) - FOLD_WINDOW)
        for position in range(len(self.lines) - 1, start - 1, -1):
            line = self.lines[position]
            if line.label or not line.movable:
                break
            if line.defines in candidates and line.defines not in written and \
                    line.defines not in used and not line.uses & written and \
                    not _overlaps(line.reads_memory, memory_written):
                folded[line.defines] = line.expression
                taken.append(position)
            else:
                memory_written |= line.writes_memory
                if line.defines in candidates and line.defines not in written and \
                        line.defines not in used:
                    kept[line.defines] = line.target
            used |= line.uses
            written |= line.writes | ({line.defines} if line.defines else set())
        for position in taken:
            self.notes.extend(self.lines[position].notes)
            del self.lines[position]
        return folded, kept

    def _arguments(self, signature):  # pylint: disable=too-many-locals
        """The arguments of a call, as C: the callee's guessed parameters and
        the argument registers the caller sets right before the call (a
        function that only passes an argument on does not show it in its
        signature). Registers no statement sets are named by themselves."""
        if self.convention == "x86":
            return "..."
        integers, vectors = _ARGUMENTS[self.convention]
        folded, kept = self._fold(set(integers) | set(vectors))
        for family, register in kept.items():
            folded.setdefault(family, register)
        types = {parameter.register: parameter.type
                 for parameter in signature.parameters} if signature is not None else {}
        present = set(folded) | set(types)

        def value(register):
            return folded.get(register) or self._sized(register, types.get(register, "pointer"))

        texts = []
        if self.convention == "sysv":
            for registers in (integers, vectors):
                count = max((registers.index(r) + 1 for r in present if r in registers),
                            default=0)
                texts += [value(register) for register in registers[:count]]
            full = integers[-1] in present
        else:
            count = max((max(integers.index(r) if r in integers else -1,
                             vectors.index(r) if r in vectors else -1) + 1 for r in present),
                        default=0)
            for position in range(count):
                integer, vector = integers[position], vectors[position]
                floating = vector in folded or (vector in types and integer not in folded)
                texts.append(value(vector if floating else integer))
            full = count == len(integers)
        if (signature.more_possible if signature is not None else full):
            texts.append("...")  # more on the stack
        return ", ".join(texts)

    def _call(self, instruction):
        name, signature = self._callee(instruction, instruction.operands[0])
        text = f"{name}({self._arguments(signature)})"
        result = self.index.call_result(instruction.address) if self.wide else None
        if result is not None:
            family, width, _type = result
            register = family if family.startswith("xmm") else \
                _BY_WIDTH.get(family, {}).get(width, family)
            self._emit(f"{register} = {text};", instruction)
        else:
            self._emit(f"{text};", instruction)

    def _return_value(self):
        signature = self.returns
        if signature is None:
            return "return eax;" if not self.wide else "return;"
        if signature.returns == "void":
            return "return;"
        family = "xmm0" if signature.returns in ("float", "double") else "rax"
        return f"return {self._sized(family, signature.returns)};"

    def _tail_call(self, instruction, operand):
        name, signature = self._callee(instruction, operand)
        text = f"{name}({self._arguments(signature)})"
        own = self.returns.returns if self.returns is not None else "void"
        if own != "void" and (signature is None or signature.returns != "void"):
            self._emit(f"return {text};", instruction)
        else:
            self._emit(f"{text};", instruction)
            self._emit("return;", instruction)
            self.lines[-1].address = None

    # --- instructions ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def _translate(self, instruction):
        read_ids, write_ids = instruction.regs_access()
        reads = {self._family(instruction, r) for r in read_ids} - {None}
        writes = {self._family(instruction, r) for r in write_ids} - {None}
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        zeroing = _zeroing(instruction)
        if zeroing:
            reads = set()
        self.current = instruction
        self.notes = self._chain_notes(instruction)
        self.substitutes = self._substitutions(instruction, reads)
        self.substituted = set()
        self.emitted = []
        self._statement(instruction, zeroing)
        # The assignments folded into this instruction's statement go
        for family in self.substituted:
            folded = self.substitutes[family]
            self.lines = [line for line in self.lines if line is not folded]
        self._update_pending(instruction, reads, writes)
        self._update_chains(instruction, writes)
        self.current = None
        self.substitutes = {}
        # Bookkeeping: arguments overwritten, flags changed or made stale
        overwritten = writes - reads
        if mnemonic == "call":
            overwritten |= _VOLATILE[self.convention]
        for family in overwritten:
            self.parameters.pop(family, None)
        flags = self.flags
        self._set_flags(instruction)
        if self.flags is flags and flags is not None and writes & flags.families:
            flags.stale = True

    # --- folding a value into its one use -----------------------------------------
    def _substitutions(self, instruction, reads):
        """{family: _Line} of the pending assignments this instruction may fold
        in: it names the register once, as a value it does not also change,
        and nothing reads the register afterwards."""
        if not self.pending:
            return {}
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        name = mnemonic[1:] if mnemonic.startswith("v") else mnemonic
        if mnemonic in ("cmp", "test", "call", "ret", "push", "pop") or \
                name in ("comiss", "ucomiss", "comisd", "ucomisd") or \
                mnemonic.startswith(("j", "set", "cmov", "loop")):
            return {}
        result = {}
        for family in reads:
            line = self.pending.get(family)
            if line is not None and self._occurrences(instruction, family) == 1 and \
                    self._dead_after(family):
                result[family] = line
        return result

    def _occurrences(self, instruction, family):
        """How often the instruction names ``family`` as a value it reads
        (many if it also changes it: add eax, … cannot take eax's value)."""
        operands = instruction.operands
        pure = _mnemonic(instruction).lstrip("v") in _PURE
        count = 0
        for position, operand in enumerate(operands):
            if operand.type == X86_OP_REG and self._family(instruction, operand.reg) == family:
                if position == 0 and not pure:
                    return 2
                if position > 0 or not pure:
                    count += 1
            elif operand.type == X86_OP_MEM:
                for register_id in (operand.mem.base, operand.mem.index):
                    if register_id and self._family(instruction, register_id) == family:
                        count += 1
        return count

    def _overwrites(self, instruction, family):
        """Whether the instruction replaces all of ``family``'s value."""
        operands = instruction.operands
        name = _mnemonic(instruction).lstrip("v")
        for register_id in instruction.regs_access()[1]:
            found = _FAMILIES.get(instruction.reg_name(register_id))
            if found is None or found[0] != family:
                continue
            if not family.startswith("xmm"):
                return found[1] >= 4  # 32 bits clear the upper half
            if name in ("pxor", "xorps", "xorpd") and len(operands) >= 2 and \
                    all(o.type == X86_OP_REG and o.reg == operands[0].reg for o in operands):
                return True
            return name in _SSE_MOVES and len(operands) == 2 and \
                (operands[1].type == X86_OP_MEM or name in ("movaps", "movapd", "movups",
                                                            "movupd", "movdqa", "movdqu"))
        return False

    def _dead_after(self, family):  # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements
        """Whether ``family``'s value is not read after the current
        instruction (straight-line code only: a branch or label ends the look)."""
        if self._overwrites(self.current, family):
            return True
        following = self.instructions[self.position + 1:self.position + 1 + LIVENESS_WINDOW]
        for instruction in following:
            if instruction.address in self.targets:
                return False
            mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
            if not _zeroing(instruction) and family in self._reads(instruction):
                return False
            if mnemonic == "call":
                integers, vectors = _ARGUMENTS.get(self.convention, ((), ()))
                if family in integers or family in vectors:
                    return False
                if family in _VOLATILE[self.convention]:
                    return True
                continue
            if mnemonic in ("ret", "retf"):
                returns = self.returns.returns if self.returns is not None else "int"
                if family == "rax":
                    return returns in ("void", "float", "double")
                return family != "xmm0" or returns not in ("float", "double")
            if mnemonic.startswith(("j", "loop")):
                return False
            if self._overwrites(instruction, family):
                return True
        return False

    def _update_pending(self, instruction, reads, writes):
        """Keep the assignments that may still be folded into a later use."""
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        if mnemonic in ("call", "ret", "retf") or mnemonic.startswith(("j", "loop")) or \
                any(line.text.startswith("asm(") for line in self.emitted):
            self.pending.clear()
        else:
            memory_written = {self._global_target(instruction, operand)
                              for operand in instruction.operands
                              if operand.type == X86_OP_MEM and operand.access & CS_AC_WRITE}
            if mnemonic == "push":
                memory_written.add(None)
            for family, line in list(self.pending.items()):
                if family in reads or family in writes or line.uses & writes or \
                        _overlaps(line.reads_memory, frozenset(memory_written)):
                    del self.pending[family]
        for line in self.emitted:
            if self._foldable(line):
                self.pending[line.defines] = line

    def _foldable(self, line):
        """Whether a statement assigns a whole register a value that may be
        folded into a later use (an 8- or 16-bit write keeps the rest)."""
        found = _FAMILIES.get(line.target or "")
        if not line.defines or not line.movable or line.expression is None or found is None:
            return False
        if found[1] < 4 and not line.defines.startswith("xmm"):
            return False
        return any(kept is line for kept in self.lines)  # not taken as an argument

    # --- pointer chains -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def _chain(self, instruction, operand):
        """(root, offset, …) of a memory operand reached from a global, or None."""
        memory = operand.mem
        if memory.index or not memory.base:
            return None
        chain = self.chains.get(self._family(instruction, memory.base))
        return chain + (memory.disp,) if chain is not None else None

    def _chain_notes(self, instruction):
        notes = []
        for operand in instruction.operands:
            if operand.type == X86_OP_MEM:
                chain = self._chain(instruction, operand)
                if chain is not None:
                    notes.append(chain)
        return notes

    def _update_chains(self, instruction, writes):
        """The registers holding a pointer read along a chain from a global
        after ``instruction``: a load of a global or through a chain starts or
        extends one, a copy takes it along, any other write ends it."""
        before = dict(self.chains)
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        for family in writes:
            self.chains.pop(family, None)
        if mnemonic == "call":
            for family in _VOLATILE[self.convention]:
                self.chains.pop(family, None)
        operands = instruction.operands
        pointer = 8 if self.wide else 4
        if mnemonic != "mov" or len(operands) != 2 or operands[0].type != X86_OP_REG or \
                operands[0].size != pointer:
            return
        destination = self._family(instruction, operands[0].reg)
        source = operands[1]
        chain = None
        if source.type == X86_OP_MEM:
            target = self._global_target(instruction, source)
            if target is not None:
                if target not in self.image.imports:
                    chain = (self._root(target),)
            else:
                saved, self.chains = self.chains, before
                chain = self._chain(instruction, source)
                self.chains = saved
        elif source.type == X86_OP_REG:
            chain = before.get(self._family(instruction, source.reg))
        if chain is not None and destination is not None:
            self.chains[destination] = chain

    def _root(self, target):
        """A global as the start of a pointer chain: its name, else module+offset."""
        return self.image.names.get(target) or f"{self.module}+0x{target - self.image.base:x}"

    def _frame(self, instruction):
        """Whether the instruction only keeps registers or builds the stack frame."""
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        operands = instruction.operands
        if mnemonic in ("push", "pop") and operands and operands[0].type == X86_OP_REG:
            return self._family(instruction, operands[0].reg) in _SAVED[self.convention]
        if len(operands) == 2 and operands[0].type == X86_OP_REG and \
                self._family(instruction, operands[0].reg) in ("rsp", "rbp"):
            if mnemonic in ("sub", "add", "and") and operands[1].type == X86_OP_IMM:
                return True
            if mnemonic in ("mov", "lea"):
                source = operands[1]
                register = source.reg if source.type == X86_OP_REG else \
                    source.mem.base if source.type == X86_OP_MEM else 0
                return bool(register) and \
                    self._family(instruction, register) in ("rsp", "rbp")
        return False

    def _statement(self, instruction, zeroing):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements,too-many-branches
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        operands = instruction.operands
        if mnemonic in _SKIP or (mnemonic.startswith("nop")) or self._frame(instruction):
            return
        if zeroing:
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], "0")
            return
        if mnemonic in ("cmp", "test") or mnemonic.lstrip("v") in (
                "comiss", "ucomiss", "comisd", "ucomisd"):
            return
        if mnemonic == "call" and operands:
            self._call(instruction)
            return
        if mnemonic in ("ret", "retf"):
            self._emit(self._return_value(), instruction)
            return
        if mnemonic.startswith("j") or mnemonic.startswith("loop"):
            self._jump(instruction)
            return
        if self._integer(instruction) or self._sse(instruction):
            return
        self._asm(instruction)

    def _jump(self, instruction):  # pylint: disable=too-many-branches
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        operands = instruction.operands
        if not operands:
            self._asm(instruction)
            return
        operand = operands[0]
        if mnemonic == "jmp":
            if operand.type == X86_OP_IMM:
                target = operand.imm
                if self.function.start <= target < self.function.end:
                    self._emit(f"goto loc_{target:x};", instruction)
                elif self.index.function_starting(target) is not None or \
                        target in self.image.names or self._stub(target) is not None:
                    self._tail_call(instruction, operand)
                else:
                    where = self.index.where(target)
                    self._emit(f"goto 0x{target:x};" + (f"  /* {where} */" if where else ""),
                               instruction)
            elif operand.type == X86_OP_MEM and \
                    self._global_target(instruction, operand) in self.image.imports:
                self._tail_call(instruction, operand)
            else:
                self._emit(f"goto *{self._operand(instruction, operand)};", instruction)
            return
        if mnemonic in ("jecxz", "jrcxz"):
            condition = f"{mnemonic[1:-1]} == 0"
        elif mnemonic.startswith("loop"):
            self._asm(instruction)
            return
        else:
            condition = self._condition(_condition_code(mnemonic))
        if operand.type != X86_OP_IMM:
            self._asm(instruction)
            return
        target = operand.imm
        if self.function.start <= target < self.function.end:
            label = f"loc_{target:x}"
        else:
            label = self.index.where(target) or f"0x{target:x}"
        self._emit(f"if ({condition}) goto {label};", instruction)

    def _integer(self, instruction):
        """General-purpose instructions; False if not one of them."""
        # pylint: disable=too-many-branches,too-many-locals,too-many-statements
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        operands = instruction.operands
        count = len(operands)
        operand = self._operand
        if mnemonic in ("mov", "movabs") and count == 2:
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0],
                         operand(instruction, operands[1], address_ok=True))
        elif mnemonic in ("movzx", "movsx", "movsxd") and count == 2:
            signedness = "unsigned" if mnemonic == "movzx" else "signed"
            source = operands[1]
            if source.type == X86_OP_REG:
                table = _UNSIGNED if signedness == "unsigned" else _SIGNED
                text = f"({table[source.size]}){self._register(instruction, source.reg)}"
            else:
                text = operand(instruction, source, signedness)
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], text)
        elif mnemonic == "lea" and count == 2:
            source = operands[1]
            target = self._global_target(instruction, source)
            if target is not None:
                text = self._address_of(target)
            else:
                narrow = operands[0].size < 8
                text = self._address_text(instruction, source, decimal=narrow,
                                          width=operands[0].size if narrow else None)
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], text)
        elif mnemonic in _INTEGER_OPERATORS and count == 2:
            hexadecimal = mnemonic in ("and", "or", "xor")
            self._emit(f"{operand(instruction, operands[0])} {_INTEGER_OPERATORS[mnemonic]}= "
                       f"{operand(instruction, operands[1], hexadecimal=hexadecimal)};",
                       instruction)
        elif mnemonic == "imul" and count == 3:
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], f"{operand(instruction, operands[1])} * "
                         f"{operand(instruction, operands[2])}")
        elif mnemonic in ("shl", "sal", "sar", "shr") and count == 1:
            self._emit(f"{operand(instruction, operands[0])} "
                       f"{'>>' if mnemonic in ('sar', 'shr') else '<<'}= 1;", instruction)
        elif mnemonic == "shr" and count == 2:
            target = operands[0]
            if target.type == X86_OP_REG:
                name = self._register(instruction, target.reg)
                self._emit(f"{name} = ({_UNSIGNED[target.size]}){name} >> "
                           f"{operand(instruction, operands[1])};", instruction)
            else:
                self._emit(f"{operand(instruction, target, 'unsigned')} >>= "
                           f"{operand(instruction, operands[1])};", instruction)
        elif mnemonic in ("inc", "dec") and count == 1:
            self._emit(f"{operand(instruction, operands[0])}"
                       f"{'++' if mnemonic == 'inc' else '--'};", instruction)
        elif mnemonic in ("neg", "not") and count == 1:
            text = operand(instruction, operands[0])
            self._emit(f"{text} = {'-' if mnemonic == 'neg' else '~'}{text};", instruction)
        elif mnemonic.startswith("set") and count == 1:
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0],
                         self._condition(_condition_code(mnemonic)), overwrite=False)
        elif mnemonic.startswith("cmov") and count == 2:
            condition = self._condition(_condition_code(mnemonic))
            self._emit(f"if ({condition}) {self._register(instruction, operands[0].reg)} = "
                       f"{operand(instruction, operands[1])};", instruction)
        elif mnemonic in ("cdqe", "cwde", "cbw"):
            source, target, c_type = {"cdqe": ("eax", "rax", "int32_t"),
                                      "cwde": ("ax", "eax", "int16_t"),
                                      "cbw": ("al", "ax", "int8_t")}[mnemonic]
            self._emit(f"{target} = ({c_type}){self._family_name(source)};", instruction)
        elif mnemonic in ("cdq", "cqo", "cwd"):
            source, target = {"cdq": ("eax", "edx"), "cqo": ("rax", "rdx"),
                              "cwd": ("ax", "dx")}[mnemonic]
            self._emit(f"{target} = {self._family_name(source)} < 0 ? -1 : 0;", instruction)
        elif mnemonic == "push" and count == 1:
            self._emit(f"push({operand(instruction, operands[0], address_ok=True)});",
                       instruction)
        elif mnemonic == "pop" and count == 1:
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], "pop()")
        else:
            return False
        return True

    def _family_name(self, register):
        """``register``, or its argument name while it holds the argument."""
        family = _FAMILIES[register][0]
        return self.parameters.get(family, register)

    def _sse(self, instruction):
        """Scalar SSE and AVX instructions; False if not one of them."""
        # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements,too-many-branches
        mnemonic = _mnemonic(instruction)
        operands = instruction.operands
        vex = mnemonic.startswith("v")
        name = mnemonic[1:] if vex else mnemonic
        # AVX names three operands, the first one only written: vaddss xmm0, xmm1, xmm2
        sources = operands[1:] if vex and len(operands) == 3 else operands
        operand = self._operand
        if name in _SSE_MOVES and len(operands) in (2, 3):
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], operand(instruction, operands[-1]))
        elif name in ("movd", "movq") and len(operands) == 2:
            if all(o.type == X86_OP_REG for o in operands):
                return False
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], operand(instruction, operands[1]))
        elif name[:3] in _SSE_OPERATORS and name[3:] in ("ss", "sd") and len(sources) == 2:
            symbol = _SSE_OPERATORS[name[:3]]
            left, right = (operand(instruction, o) for o in sources)
            if vex and len(operands) == 3:
                self._assign(instruction, operands[0], f"{left} {symbol} {right}")
            else:
                self._emit(f"{left} {symbol}= {right};", instruction)
        elif name[:3] in ("min", "max") and name[3:] in ("ss", "sd") and len(sources) == 2:
            function = "f" + name[:3] + ("f" if name.endswith("ss") else "")
            left, right = (operand(instruction, o) for o in sources)
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], f"{function}({left}, {right})")
        elif name in ("sqrtss", "sqrtsd") and sources:
            function = "sqrtf" if name == "sqrtss" else "sqrt"
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0],
                         f"{function}({operand(instruction, sources[-1])})")
        elif name in ("cvtsi2ss", "cvtsi2sd", "cvtss2sd", "cvtsd2ss") and sources:
            c_type = "float" if name.endswith("ss") else "double"
            source = sources[-1]
            text = operand(instruction, source, "signed") if source.type == X86_OP_MEM \
                else operand(instruction, source)
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0], f"({c_type}){text}")
        elif name in ("cvttss2si", "cvttsd2si") and len(operands) == 2:
            c_type = _SIGNED.get(operands[0].size, "int32_t")
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0],
                         f"({c_type}){operand(instruction, operands[1])}")
        elif name in ("cvtss2si", "cvtsd2si") and len(operands) == 2:
            function = "lrintf" if name == "cvtss2si" else "lrint"
            self._assign(instruction, operands[0],
                         f"{function}({operand(instruction, operands[1])})")
        else:
            return False
        return True

```

`grembyte/features/ptrace_watch.py`:

```py
"""A ptrace-backed hardware watchpoint monitor for process memory.

This is an alternative to the Frida watch backend (see write_watch.py). Instead
of injecting an agent it drives the Linux ``ptrace`` API directly, so it works
on targets Frida cannot instrument, most notably Wine/Proton processes. The
low-level ptrace machinery lives in :mod:`grembyte.attach.ptrace_engine`; this
module turns watchpoint traps into the hit records the UI shows.
"""

import errno
import time

from PySide6.QtCore import Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core import messages, sessions
from grembyte.core.memory import read_memory
from grembyte.attach.ptrace_engine import (
    MAX_INSTRUCTION_SIZE,
    SYNC_WINDOW,
    PtraceWatchpointEngine,
    build_dr7,
    decode_access,
    watch_alignment_error,
)

__all__ = ["PtraceWriteWatchWorker", "build_dr7", "decode_access"]


class PtraceWriteWatchWorker(PtraceWatchpointEngine):
    """Report writes (and, with ``reads``, reads) via ptrace watchpoints.

    Matches :class:`grembyte.features.write_watch.WriteWatchWorker`'s interface so
    the two backends are interchangeable. Each hit tells whether its
    instruction ``read`` and/or ``write``-s the target.
    """

    monitor_ready = Signal(int, str)
    hits_ready = Signal(object)
    monitor_warning = Signal(str)
    monitor_failed = Signal(str)
    monitor_stopped = Signal()

    FLUSH_INTERVAL = 0.1

    def __init__(self, pid, address, size, parent=None, reads=False):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments
        super().__init__(pid, parent)
        self.address = address
        self.size = size
        self.reads = reads
        self._slots = {0: (address, size, reads)}
        self._pending = {}
        self._access_cache = {}

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.PTRACE_WATCH)
    def run(self):
        """Attach, report hits until stopped, then detach cleanly."""
        try:
            self._monitor()
        except OSError as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.monitor_failed.emit(self._explain(error))
        finally:
            self._detach_all()
            self.monitor_stopped.emit()

    def _monitor(self):
        unaligned = watch_alignment_error(self.address, self.size)
        if unaligned is not None:
            raise OSError(errno.EINVAL, unaligned)
        self._load_mappings()
        warnings = self._attach_all()
        if not self._armed:
            raise messages.LocalizedOSError("error.ptrace_watch.no_thread", 1)
        self.monitor_ready.emit(len(self._armed), "")
        for message in warnings:
            self.monitor_warning.emit(message)

        last_flush = time.monotonic()
        while not self.isInterruptionRequested():
            if not self._pump():
                if time.monotonic() - last_flush >= self.FLUSH_INTERVAL:
                    self._flush()
                    last_flush = time.monotonic()
                time.sleep(0.002)
        self._flush()
        if self._target_gone:
            self.monitor_failed.emit(messages.text("error.ptrace.exited"))

    def _handle_trap(self, tid, slot, pc, bits):
        read, write = self._access_of(pc, bits)
        key = hex(pc)
        hit = self._pending.get(key)
        now = int(time.time() * 1000)
        if hit is not None:
            hit["count"] += 1
            hit["read"] = hit["read"] or read
            hit["write"] = hit["write"] or write
            hit["threadId"] = tid
            hit["time"] = now
            return
        self._pending[key] = {
            "pc": key,
            "site": self._site(pc),
            "value": None,
            "read": read,
            "write": write,
            "threadId": tid,
            "count": 1,
            "time": now,
        }

    def _access_of(self, pc, bits):
        cached = self._access_cache.get(pc)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        start = max(0, pc - (SYNC_WINDOW + MAX_INSTRUCTION_SIZE))
        data, readable = read_memory(self.pid, start, pc - start)
        if not all(readable):
            access = (self.reads, True)
        else:
            access = decode_access(bytes(data), len(data), bits, self.reads)
        self._access_cache[pc] = access
        return access

    def _read_value(self):
        data, readable = read_memory(self.pid, self.address, self.size)
        if not all(readable):
            return "unreadable"
        return " ".join(f"{byte:02x}" for byte in data)

    def _flush(self):
        if not self._pending:
            return
        hits = list(self._pending.values())
        self._pending.clear()
        value = self._read_value()
        for hit in hits:
            hit["value"] = value
        self.hits_ready.emit(hits)

```

`grembyte/features/rtti.py`:

```py
"""C++ class names from run-time type information, without symbols.

Polymorphic C++ classes carry their name for ``typeid`` and
``dynamic_cast``, also in stripped builds. Through it the module's
virtual function tables (vtables) and the virtual methods in them get names,
``CGameSprite::vftable`` and ``CGameSprite::vf12`` (slot 12).

MSVC (PE): a type descriptor holds the decorated name (``.?AVCGameSprite@@``)
16 bytes (x64) or 8 bytes (x86) after its start. A complete object locator
points to it (x64: as an RVA, signature 1, with its own RVA as a check;
x86: as an address, signature 0), and the slot in front of each vtable points
to the locator.

Itanium (GCC, Clang; ELF): a typeinfo object holds a pointer to the mangled
type name (``11CGameSprite``) after its own vtable pointer. Each vtable starts
with the offset to the top of the object and a pointer to the typeinfo; the
virtual methods follow. In a position-independent module these pointers are
relative relocations (``Image.relocations``).

Only the primary vtable (offset 0) names methods; secondary vtables (multiple
inheritance) name the table only. A method in several vtables keeps the name
of the class with the shortest vtable, its most basic class; one found in
different slots (a shared stub such as ``_purecall``, or identical code
folded together) gets none.
"""

import re
import struct

# Slots a vtable has at most
MAX_SLOTS = 1024
_MSVC_NAME = re.compile(rb"\.\?A[VU][\x21-\x7e]{1,4096}?@@\0")
_ITANIUM_NAME = re.compile(r"[\w$]{2,}")


def rtti_names(image):
    """address -> name of the vtables and virtual methods ``image`` describes."""
    try:
        if image.format == "pe":
            tables = _msvc_vtables(image)
        else:
            tables = _itanium_vtables(image)
    except (struct.error, ValueError, IndexError):
        return {}
    return _name_tables(image, tables)


def _name_tables(image, tables):
    """Names for [(vtable address, class, offset, [method addresses])]."""
    names = {}
    owners = {}  # method -> (slots of the owner's vtable, class, slot)
    shared = set()
    for address, name, offset, methods in tables:
        names[address] = f"{name}::vftable" if offset == 0 else \
            f"{name}::vftable@0x{offset:x}"
        if offset != 0:
            continue
        for slot, method in enumerate(methods):
            known = owners.get(method)
            if known is not None and known[2] != slot:
                shared.add(method)
            if known is None or len(methods) < known[0]:
                owners[method] = (len(methods), name, slot)
    for method, (_count, name, slot) in owners.items():
        if method not in shared and method not in image.names:
            names[method] = f"{name}::vf{slot}"
    return names


def _executable(image, address):
    section = image.section_at(address)
    return section is not None and section.executable


def _data_sections(image):
    return [section for section in image.sections if not section.executable and section.raw_size]


def _words(image, section, width):
    """(address, value) of the aligned words in a section's file data."""
    data = image.section_bytes(section)
    start = (-section.address) % width
    fmt = "<Q" if width == 8 else "<I"
    usable = start + (len(data) - start) // width * width
    for index, (value,) in enumerate(struct.iter_unpack(fmt, data[start:usable])):
        yield section.address + start + index * width, value


def _methods(image, pointer_at, first):
    methods = []
    width = 8 if image.bits == 64 else 4
    for slot in range(MAX_SLOTS):
        target = pointer_at(first + slot * width)
        if target is None or not _executable(image, target):
            break
        methods.append(target)
    return methods


# --- MSVC -----------------------------------------------------------------------

def msvc_class_name(decorated):
    """``.?AVInner@Outer@@`` -> ``Outer::Inner``; templates as ``vector<…>``."""
    body = decorated[4:]
    if body.endswith("@@"):
        body = body[:-2]
    if body.startswith("?$"):
        return body[2:].split("@", 1)[0] + "<…>"
    parts = []
    for part in body.split("@"):
        if not part:
            break
        parts.append("`anonymous namespace'" if part.startswith("?A") else part)
    return "::".join(reversed(parts)) or decorated


def _msvc_vtables(image):
    wide = image.bits == 64
    width = 8 if wide else 4
    sections = _data_sections(image)
    descriptors = {}  # type descriptor (RVA on x64, address on x86) -> class
    for section in sections:
        data = image.section_bytes(section)
        for match in _MSVC_NAME.finditer(data):
            descriptor = section.address + match.start() - 2 * width
            decorated = match.group(0)[:-1].decode("ascii")
            descriptors[descriptor - image.base if wide else descriptor] = \
                msvc_class_name(decorated)
    if not descriptors:
        return []
    locators = {}  # locator address -> (class, offset)
    for section in sections:
        for address, value in _words(image, section, 4):
            if value not in descriptors:
                continue
            locator = address - 12
            header = image.read(locator, 24 if wide else 16)
            if len(header) < (24 if wide else 16):
                continue
            signature, offset = struct.unpack_from("<Ii", header, 0)
            if wide:
                if signature != 1 or struct.unpack_from("<I", header, 20)[0] != \
                        locator - image.base:
                    continue
            elif signature != 0:
                continue
            locators[locator] = (descriptors[value], offset)
    if not locators:
        return []

    def pointer_at(address):
        raw = image.read(address, width)
        return int.from_bytes(raw, "little") if len(raw) == width else None

    tables = []
    for section in sections:
        for address, value in _words(image, section, width):
            found = locators.get(value)
            if found is None:
                continue
            first = address + width
            methods = _methods(image, pointer_at, first)
            if methods:
                tables.append((first, found[0], found[1], methods))
    return tables


# --- Itanium ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def itanium_class_name(mangled):
    """``11CGameSprite`` -> ``CGameSprite``, ``N5Outer5InnerE`` -> ``Outer::Inner``;
    template arguments as ``<…>``. None for anything else."""
    position = 0
    nested = mangled.startswith("N")
    if nested:
        position = 1
    parts = []
    while position < len(mangled):
        character = mangled[position]
        if character.isdigit():
            digits = re.match(r"\d+", mangled[position:]).group(0)
            position += len(digits)
            length = int(digits)
            if length == 0 or position + length > len(mangled):
                return None
            parts.append(mangled[position:position + length])
            position += length
        elif mangled.startswith("St", position):
            parts.append("std")
            position += 2
        elif character == "I" and parts:
            end = _template_end(mangled, position + 1)
            if end is None:
                return None
            parts[-1] += "<…>"
            position = end
        elif character == "E" and nested and position == len(mangled) - 1:
            position += 1
            nested = False
        else:
            return None
        if not nested and parts != ["std"] and position < len(mangled) \
                and mangled[position] != "I":
            return None
    if nested or not parts:
        return None
    return "::".join(parts)


def _template_end(mangled, position):
    """The position after the ``E`` closing template arguments starting at ``position``."""
    depth = 1
    while position < len(mangled):
        character = mangled[position]
        if character.isdigit():
            digits = re.match(r"\d+", mangled[position:]).group(0)
            position += len(digits) + int(digits)
            continue
        if character == "L":  # a literal: L <type> <number> E
            end = mangled.find("E", position)
            if end < 0:
                return None
            position = end + 1
            continue
        if character in "IN":
            depth += 1
        elif character == "E":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return position + 1
        position += 1
    return None


def _itanium_vtables(image):
    width = 8 if image.bits == 64 else 4
    relocated = dict(image.relocations)
    absolute = image.base >= 0x10000 or not relocated

    def pointer_at(address):
        if address in relocated:
            return relocated[address]
        if not absolute:
            return None
        raw = image.read(address, width)
        return int.from_bytes(raw, "little") if len(raw) == width else None

    sections = _data_sections(image)
    slots = list(relocated.items())
    if absolute:
        for section in sections:
            slots.extend(_words(image, section, width))
    type_names = {}  # typeinfo address -> class
    for where, target in slots:
        if target == 0 or not image.contains(target) or _executable(image, target):
            continue
        text = _c_string(image, target)
        if text is None or not _ITANIUM_NAME.fullmatch(text):
            continue
        name = itanium_class_name(text)
        if name is not None:
            type_names[where - width] = name
    if not type_names:
        return []
    tables = []
    for where, target in slots:
        name = type_names.get(target)
        if name is None:
            continue
        raw = image.read(where - width, width)
        if len(raw) != width:
            continue
        offset = -int.from_bytes(raw, "little", signed=True)
        if offset < 0 or offset > 0x100000:
            continue
        first = where + width
        methods = _methods(image, pointer_at, first)
        if methods:
            tables.append((first, name, offset, methods))
    return tables


def _c_string(image, address, limit=512):
    raw = image.read(address, limit)
    end = raw.find(b"\0")
    if end <= 0:
        return None
    try:
        return raw[:end].decode("ascii")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return None

```

`grembyte/features/script_memory.js`:

```js
// --- Memory accesses under a watchpoint ----------------------------------------
// (see grembyte/features/scripts.py)
//
// A write or access watch (grembyte/features/write_watch.js) arms a hardware
// watchpoint on every thread, the game thread scripts run on included. Frida
// guards its memory accesses (ptr.readS32(), ptr.writeS32(), …) and reports a
// trap inside them as an error, "breakpoint triggered", although the access
// has happened: the processor traps right after it. The watch agent never
// sees that trap.
//
// So the readers and writers of NativePointer try Frida's access first, and
// only on such a trap repeat it through a small compiled copy whose
// exceptions go to the process's handlers, where the watch agent takes the
// trap and lets the copy finish. A write is checked first: Frida's write has
// stored the value already, and is only repeated if it has not.

(function guardMemoryAccessesFromWatchTraps() {
  const POINTER = Process.pointerSize;
  // C long: 4 bytes on Windows, else a pointer's size
  const LONG = Process.platform === 'windows' ? 4 : POINTER;
  const SIZES = {
    S8: 1, U8: 1, S16: 2, U16: 2, Short: 2, UShort: 2,
    S32: 4, U32: 4, Int: 4, UInt: 4, Float: 4,
    S64: 8, U64: 8, Double: 8, Long: LONG, ULong: LONG, Pointer: POINTER
  };

  function isWatchTrap(error) {
    return /breakpoint|single.?step/i.test(String(error));
  }

  // Compiled at the first trap: a script that never meets one needs no compiler
  let copy = null;
  function nativeCopy() {
    if (copy === null) {
      // One instruction per access of 1 to 8 bytes, as the game's own code does
      const module = new CModule(`
void copy (void * to, const void * from, unsigned long size)
{
  if (size == 1)
    *(volatile unsigned char *) to = *(volatile const unsigned char *) from;
  else if (size == 2)
    *(volatile unsigned short *) to = *(volatile const unsigned short *) from;
  else if (size == 4)
    *(volatile unsigned int *) to = *(volatile const unsigned int *) from;
  else if (size == 8)
    *(volatile unsigned long long *) to = *(volatile const unsigned long long *) from;
  else
  {
    volatile unsigned char * target = to;
    volatile const unsigned char * source = from;
    unsigned long i;
    for (i = 0; i != size; i++)
      target[i] = source[i];
  }
}
`);
      const fn = new NativeFunction(module.copy, 'void', ['pointer', 'pointer', 'ulong'],
                                    { exceptions: 'propagate' });
      copy = (to, from, size) => fn(to, from, size);
      copy.module = module;  // kept alive with the function
    }
    return copy;
  }

  // Bytes of a write as it should land in memory
  function sameBytes(target, expected, size) {
    const stored = Memory.alloc(size);
    nativeCopy()(stored, target, size);
    const a = new Uint8Array(stored.readByteArray(size));
    const b = new Uint8Array(expected.readByteArray(size));
    return a.every((byte, index) => byte === b[index]);
  }

  const prototype = NativePointer.prototype;
  for (const [type, size] of Object.entries(SIZES)) {
    const read = prototype[`read${type}`];
    const write = prototype[`write${type}`];
    if (typeof read === 'function') {
      prototype[`read${type}`] = function () {
        try {
          return read.call(this);
        } catch (error) {
          if (!isWatchTrap(error))
            throw error;
          // The trap proves the memory is there: the native copy is safe
          const buffer = Memory.alloc(size);
          nativeCopy()(buffer, this, size);
          return read.call(buffer);
        }
      };
    }
    if (typeof write === 'function') {
      prototype[`write${type}`] = function (value) {
        try {
          return write.call(this, value);
        } catch (error) {
          if (!isWatchTrap(error))
            throw error;
          const buffer = Memory.alloc(size);
          write.call(buffer, value);
          if (!sameBytes(this, buffer, size))
            nativeCopy()(this, buffer, size);
          return this;
        }
      };
    }
  }

  const readByteArray = prototype.readByteArray;
  prototype.readByteArray = function (length) {
    try {
      return readByteArray.call(this, length);
    } catch (error) {
      if (!isWatchTrap(error) || !(length > 0))
        throw error;
      const buffer = Memory.alloc(length);
      nativeCopy()(buffer, this, length);
      return readByteArray.call(buffer, length);
    }
  };

  const writeByteArray = prototype.writeByteArray;
  prototype.writeByteArray = function (bytes) {
    try {
      return writeByteArray.call(this, bytes);
    } catch (error) {
      const length = bytes.byteLength !== undefined ? bytes.byteLength : bytes.length;
      if (!isWatchTrap(error) || !(length > 0))
        throw error;
      const buffer = Memory.alloc(Math.max(length, 1));
      writeByteArray.call(buffer, bytes);
      // A copy of many bytes stops at the first one watched: write them all
      if (!sameBytes(this, buffer, length))
        nativeCopy()(this, buffer, length);
      return this;
    }
  };
})();

```

`grembyte/features/script_native.js`:

```js
// --- Native scripts: the game thread without an engine, and ctx.native ---------
// (see grembyte/features/scripts.py)
//
// Scripts run on the game thread. Engine adapters know it (Unreal:
// ProcessEvent, Mono and IL2CPP: Unity's main thread). A game without one, a
// native game with an engine of its own, has no such entry; there the agent
// waits for a function the game calls every frame on its main thread. It
// hooks those of NATIVE_FRAME_FUNCTIONS the game exports and watches them for
// NATIVE_PROBE_MS: the first in the list that ran on the process's first
// thread (mainThreadId) is taken, else the first that ran on another thread.
// The order matters: SDL_PollEvent calls PeekMessageW under Wine, and jobs
// should run after SDL's whole call, not in the middle of it. The first in
// the list is taken as soon as it runs on the main thread; if nothing ran
// while watching, the first call after it. Jobs run when it returns.
//
// ctx.native helps scripts to find code by its bytes instead of by fixed
// addresses, which move with every patch of the game.

const NATIVE_FRAME_FUNCTIONS = [
  'SDL_PollEvent', 'SDL_PumpEvents', 'SDL_GL_SwapWindow',
  'glfwPollEvents', 'glfwSwapBuffers',
  'PeekMessageW', 'PeekMessageA', 'SwapBuffers', 'wglSwapBuffers',
  'glXSwapBuffers', 'eglSwapBuffers', 'vkQueuePresentKHR',
  // GTK and other GLib programs: returns after each event, at least every
  // time a timer fires
  'g_main_context_iteration'
];
// How long a job may wait for the game thread (ms)
const NATIVE_MAIN_TIMEOUT = 3000;
// How long frame functions are watched for one on the main thread before one
// running on another thread is taken (ms)
const NATIVE_PROBE_MS = 500;

const nativeMain = {
  queue: [],
  candidates: null,  // [{ name, address, listener, thread, main }]
  chosen: null,      // the candidate whose returns run the jobs
  thread: null,      // and the thread they run on
  mainThread: null,
  draining: false,
  probeTimer: null,
  probing: false
};

function onGameThread(work) {
  // A promise of work()'s result, computed on the game thread: through the
  // engine adapter, or natively without one.
  return engine.refresh() ? engine.onMainThread(work) : nativeOnMainThread(work);
}

function nativeOnMainThread(work) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const job = { work, resolve, reject, timer: null };
    nativeMain.queue.push(job);
    job.timer = setTimeout(() => {
      dropNativeJob(job);
      reject(nativeMain.chosen === null
        ? grembyteError('error.native.no_frame_call',
                      { names: nativeMain.candidates === null ? ''
                        : nativeMain.candidates.map(candidate => candidate.name).join(', ') })
        : grembyteError('error.native.game_thread_timeout',
                      { name: nativeMain.chosen.name }));
    }, NATIVE_MAIN_TIMEOUT);
    try {
      watchFrameFunctions();
    } catch (error) {
      dropNativeJob(job);
      clearTimeout(job.timer);
      reject(error);
    }
  });
}

function dropNativeJob(job) {
  const index = nativeMain.queue.indexOf(job);
  if (index >= 0)
    nativeMain.queue.splice(index, 1);
}

function watchFrameFunctions() {
  // Hook the frame functions the game exports, once.
  if (nativeMain.candidates !== null)
    return;
  // Known here, not first in a hook on a game thread (it lists the threads)
  nativeMain.mainThread = mainThreadId();
  const candidates = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const name of NATIVE_FRAME_FUNCTIONS) {
    const address = Module.findGlobalExportByName(name);
    if (address === null || seen.has(address.toString()))
      continue;
    seen.add(address.toString());
    candidates.push({ name, address, listener: null, thread: null, main: false });
  }
  if (candidates.length === 0)
    throw grembyteError('error.native.no_frame_function',
                      { names: NATIVE_FRAME_FUNCTIONS.join(', ') });
  nativeMain.candidates = candidates;
  for (const candidate of candidates)
    candidate.listener = Interceptor.attach(candidate.address, {
      onLeave() {
        frameFunctionReturned(candidate);
      }
    });
  nativeMain.probing = true;
  nativeMain.probeTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    nativeMain.probeTimer = null;
    nativeMain.probing = false;
    if (nativeMain.chosen !== null)
      return;
    const called = candidates.find(candidate => candidate.main)
      || candidates.find(candidate => candidate.thread !== null);
    if (called !== undefined)
      chooseFrameFunction(called, called.main ? nativeMain.mainThread : called.thread);
  }, NATIVE_PROBE_MS);
}

function frameFunctionReturned(candidate) {
  const thread = Process.getCurrentThreadId();
  if (nativeMain.chosen === null) {
    if (thread === nativeMain.mainThread)
      candidate.main = true;
    else if (candidate.thread === null)
      candidate.thread = thread;
    // While watching only the first in the list is taken at once; after it,
    // whatever runs first
    if ((candidate.main && candidate === nativeMain.candidates[0]) || !nativeMain.probing)
      chooseFrameFunction(candidate, thread);
    else
      return;
  }
  if (candidate !== nativeMain.chosen || thread !== nativeMain.thread)
    return;
  drainNativeJobs();
}

function chooseFrameFunction(candidate, thread) {
  nativeMain.chosen = candidate;
  nativeMain.thread = thread;
  if (nativeMain.probeTimer !== null) {
    clearTimeout(nativeMain.probeTimer);
    nativeMain.probeTimer = null;
  }
  // The others are detached on the agent's thread, not inside a game's call
  setTimeout(() => {
    for (const other of nativeMain.candidates || [])
      if (other !== candidate && other.listener !== null) {
        other.listener.detach();
        other.listener = null;
      }
  }, 0);
}

function drainNativeJobs() {
  // Jobs queued while one runs wait for the next frame; a job calling the
  // frame function itself runs nothing anew.
  if (nativeMain.draining || nativeMain.queue.length === 0)
    return;
  nativeMain.draining = true;
  try {
    for (const job of nativeMain.queue.splice(0)) {
      clearTimeout(job.timer);
      try {
        job.resolve(job.work());
      } catch (error) {
        job.reject(error);
      }
    }
  } finally {
    nativeMain.draining = false;
  }
}

let nativeThreadReported = false;

function nativeThreadNews() {
  // The frame function scripts run in, once after it was chosen (for the
  // script log): { name, thread, main }; else undefined
  if (nativeThreadReported || nativeMain.chosen === null || engine.refresh())
    return undefined;
  nativeThreadReported = true;
  return { name: nativeMain.chosen.name, thread: nativeMain.thread,
           main: nativeMain.thread === nativeMain.mainThread };
}

function disposeNative() {
  if (nativeMain.probeTimer !== null)
    clearTimeout(nativeMain.probeTimer);
  for (const candidate of nativeMain.candidates || [])
    if (candidate.listener !== null)
      candidate.listener.detach();
  for (const job of nativeMain.queue.splice(0)) {
    clearTimeout(job.timer);
    job.reject(grembyteError('error.native.disposed'));
  }
  nativeMain.candidates = null;
  nativeMain.chosen = null;
  nativeMain.thread = null;
  nativeMain.probing = false;
  nativeThreadReported = false;
}

// --- ctx.native ---------------------------------------------------------------

// Matches of a pattern in a module, by base, path and pattern: code does not
// move while the module stays loaded.
const nativeScans = new Map();

function nativeAddress(value, what) {
  if (value instanceof NativePointer)
    return value;
  if (typeof value === 'number' || typeof value === 'bigint'
      || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() !== ''))
    return ptr(value.toString());
  if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && typeof value.handle === 'object'
      && value.handle instanceof NativePointer)
    return value.handle;
  throw grembyteError('error.native.address', { what, value: displayText(value) });
}

function nativeModule(name) {
  // The game's executable, or the module of that name
  if (name === undefined || name === null || name === '')
    return programModule();
  const module = Process.findModuleByName(String(name));
  if (module === null)
    throw grembyteError('error.native.no_module', { name: String(name) });
  return module;
}

function nativePattern(pattern) {
  // Frida's pattern from "48 8B ?? 05" ("?" is "??" too); bytes may also be
  // written without spaces ("488B??05")
  if (typeof pattern !== 'string')
    throw grembyteError('error.native.pattern', { pattern: displayText(pattern) });
  let tokens = pattern.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(token => token !== '');
  if (tokens.length === 1 && tokens[0].length > 2)
    tokens = tokens[0].match(/\?\?|\?|[0-9a-fA-F?]{2}/g) || [];
  tokens = tokens.map(token => (token === '?' ? '??' : token));
  if (tokens.length === 0 || tokens.some(token => !/^[0-9a-fA-F?]{2}$/.test(token))
      || tokens.every(token => token === '??'))
    throw grembyteError('error.native.pattern', { pattern });
  return tokens.join(' ').toLowerCase();
}

function nativeScanAll(pattern, moduleName) {
  // Every address where the bytes are found in the module, lowest first
  const module = nativeModule(moduleName);
  const wanted = nativePattern(pattern);
  const key = `${module.base}|${module.path}|${wanted}`;
  let hits = nativeScans.get(key);
  if (hits === undefined) {
    hits = [];
    // A file page may be mapped twice (on Linux the end of .rodata and the
    // start of the RELRO data share one): bytes at one file offset count once,
    // where they are mapped first.
    const fileOffsets = new Set();
    const ranges = module.enumerateRanges('r--').sort((a, b) => a.base.compare(b.base));
    for (const range of ranges) {
      let matches;
      try {
        matches = Memory.scanSync(range.base, range.size, wanted);
      } catch (error) {
        continue;  // a range unmapped or guarded meanwhile has nothing to find
      }
      for (const match of matches) {
        if (range.file) {
          const offset = range.file.offset + match.address.sub(range.base).toUInt32();
          if (fileOffsets.has(offset))
            continue;
          fileOffsets.add(offset);
        }
        hits.push(match.address);
      }
    }
    nativeScans.set(key, hits);
  }
  return hits.slice();
}

function nativeScan(pattern, moduleName) {
  // The one address where the bytes are found; none or several is an error
  const hits = nativeScanAll(pattern, moduleName);
  const module = nativeModule(moduleName).name;
  if (hits.length === 0)
    throw grembyteError('error.native.pattern_missing', { pattern, module });
  if (hits.length > 1)
    throw grembyteError('error.native.pattern_ambiguous',
                      { pattern, module, count: hits.length });
  return hits[0];
}

function nativeRip(address, dispOffset, length) {
  // The target of an x64 instruction's RIP-relative operand: its 32-bit
  // displacement at ``dispOffset`` counts from the instruction's end
  // (``length`` bytes after its start).
  const at = nativeAddress(address, 'rip');
  if (!Number.isInteger(dispOffset) || !Number.isInteger(length) || dispOffset < 0
      || length < dispOffset + 4 || length > 15)
    throw grembyteError('error.native.rip_operand', { dispOffset: displayText(dispOffset),
                                                    length: displayText(length) });
  return at.add(length).add(at.add(dispOffset).readS32());
}

function nativeFunction(address, returnType, argTypes, abi) {
  // A callable native function (Frida's NativeFunction); ``abi`` only when
  // it is not the platform's (win64 under Wine, sysv on Linux). Exceptions
  // in the call go to the process's handlers: a write watch on what the
  // game code writes takes its trap there and the call runs to its end
  // (Frida's default would abort it midway with "breakpoint triggered").
  const at = nativeAddress(address, 'fn');
  if (!Array.isArray(argTypes))
    throw grembyteError('error.native.arg_types');
  const options = { exceptions: 'propagate' };
  if (abi !== undefined && abi !== null)
    options.abi = abi;
  return new NativeFunction(at, returnType, argTypes, options);
}

const nativeContext = Object.freeze({
  module: nativeModule,
  scan: nativeScan,
  scanAll: nativeScanAll,
  rip: nativeRip,
  fn: nativeFunction
});

```

`grembyte/features/scripts.py`:

```py
"""Scripts: JavaScript that calls game code by time, e.g. a cheat every minute.

A script is a function body (like the ``code`` of a method script, see
``grembyte.hooks.transforms``) that runs on the game thread, where game code
may be called (``engine.onMainThread``; Unreal: the next time it enters
ProcessEvent, Mono: mono_runtime_invoke on Unity's main thread). When it
runs is its ``mode``:

``"once"``    some ``seconds`` after it is started (each time grembyte attaches)
``"repeat"``  every ``seconds``; the next run is timed when one has ended
``"manual"``  only when asked (``run_now``): by the user, or by its ``hotkey``
              while the game has the focus (see grembyte.core.hotkeys)

A game without an engine adapter (a native game with an engine of its own)
has no such entry: there the agent runs scripts when a function the game
calls every frame returns, e.g. ``SDL_PollEvent`` on its main thread (see
grembyte/features/script_native.js); the first run reports which one
(``gameThread`` of 'script-run').

The body gets one ``ctx`` object:

    ctx.find("ClassName")   a live object of that class or a subclass
                            (Unreal, Unity), e.g. ctx.find("AlabamaCheatManager");
                            Unreal: searched for once (tens of ms on the
                            game thread), then only checked while it lives
    ctx.find("ClassName", "ObjectName")   the one of that name, e.g.
                            ctx.find("UnityEngine.GameObject", "Player(Clone)")
                            or ctx.find("BP_Hero_C", "BP_Hero_C_1"); Unreal
                            also by the name in its outer (ctx.outerName),
                            e.g. "AttributeStatsWidget.PointsAvailableTracker".
                            Class default objects and templates (a widget of
                            a Widget Blueprint's tree) are never found.
    ctx.forEach("ClassName", obj => ...)   calls the function for every object
                            ctx.find could give (until it returns false) and
                            gives how many; Unreal: reads every object anew
    ctx.outerName(obj)      Unreal: the object's name after its outer's,
                            "AttributeStatsWidget.PointsAvailableTracker" (a
                            widget's outer is the widget showing it)
    ctx.call("Namespace.Class.Method", ...args)   call a static game method
                     (also "Namespace.Class:Method", as the catalog names it)
    ctx.gas          Unreal games with the Gameplay Ability System: the
                     player's attributes. ctx.gas.get("Might") or
                     ctx.gas.get("AttributeSetCore.Might"): {base, current}
                     (null without a player); ctx.gas.setBase(name, value)
                     sets the base value through the game's own code, which
                     applies the active effects to it; ctx.gas.attributes()
                     lists the sets (see ScriptWorker.gas_attributes).
                     A set numbered anew on every load
                     ("AttributeSet_Health_2147445233") is also found
```
