```js
      continue;
    const similarity = contextSimilarity(spec.signature || {}, candidate.context);
    const distance = Math.abs(offset - spec.managed.offset);
    if (best === null || similarity > best.similarity
        || (similarity === best.similarity && distance < best.distance))
      best = { address, similarity, distance };
  }
  if (best === null || best.similarity < TRAINING_MIN_SIMILARITY)
    throw grembyteError('error.hooks.write_moved', { method: spec.managed.method });
  return best.address;
}

async function addHookResolving(spec) {
  // addHook for a hook known by its C# method: find the write site first.
  if (spec.managed !== null && spec.module === null && spec.writePc === null
      && spec.trapPc === null) {
    try {
      spec = { ...spec, writePc: (await resolveManaged(spec)).toString() };
    } catch (error) {
      if (spec.signature === null)
        throw error;
      // Not compiled or loaded yet, or the game changed: train instead.
      send({ kind: 'managed-failed', hookId: spec.id, error: String(error) });
    }
  }
  return addHook(spec);
}

function addHook(spec) {
  if (hooks.has(spec.id) || trainings.has(spec.id))
    throw grembyteError('error.hooks.exists', { id: spec.id });
  if (spec.signature !== null && spec.module === null && spec.writePc === null
      && spec.trapPc === null)
    return startTraining(spec);
  const io = VALUE_IO[spec.valueType];
  if (io === undefined)
    throw grembyteError('error.hooks.value_type', { type: spec.valueType });
  if (spec.callerDepth < 0 || spec.callerDepth > MAX_CALLER_DEPTH)
    throw grembyteError('error.hooks.caller_depth', { max: MAX_CALLER_DEPTH });
  const target = spec.address === null ? null : ptr(spec.address);
  const transform = compileTransform(spec.transform);

  let writeIns, writeOp;
  const writePc = spec.module !== null ? moduleAddress(spec)
    : spec.writePc !== null ? ptr(spec.writePc) : null;
  const existingSite = writePc === null ? undefined : sites.get(writePc.toString());
  if (existingSite !== undefined) {
    writeIns = existingSite.writeIns;
    writeOp = existingSite.writeOp;
  } else if (writePc !== null) {
    writeIns = Instruction.parse(writePc);
    writeOp = writeOperand(writeIns);
    if (writeOp === null)
      throw grembyteError('error.hooks.not_a_write',
                        { instruction: String(writeIns), address: writeIns.address });
  } else {
    const candidate = resolveWriteInstruction(ptr(spec.trapPc), target, io.size);
    writeIns = candidate.ins;
    writeOp = candidate.op;
  }

  const site = existingSite !== undefined ? existingSite
    : spec.breakpoint === true ? installBreakpointSite(writeIns, writeOp)
      : installSite(writeIns, writeOp, spec.shortJump === true);
  if (site.fast !== undefined && site.hooks.size >= FAST_MAX_HOOKS)
    throw grembyteError('error.hooks.site_full', { count: FAST_MAX_HOOKS });
  const learned = resolveCallers(spec.callers, writeIns.address);
  const hook = {
    id: spec.id,
    site,
    target,
    valueType: spec.valueType,
    io,
    filterAddress: spec.filterAddress,
    pointer: spec.pointer === null ? null : {
      module: spec.pointer.module,
      baseOffset: spec.pointer.baseOffset,
      offsets: spec.pointer.offsets,
      base: null
    },
    callerDepth: spec.callerDepth,
    callers: learned.keys,
    foreignCallers: new Set(),
    ambiguousReported: false,
    transform,
    transformSpec: spec.transform,
    enabled: spec.enabled,
    debug: false,
    pending: new Map(),
    stats: { count: 0, last: null },
    errorReported: false
  };
  site.hooks.set(spec.id, hook);
  hooks.set(spec.id, hook);
  if (site.fast !== undefined) {
    initFastHook(hook);
    updateFastSite(site);
    if (fastRangesAt === 0)
      refreshFastRanges();
  }
  if (learned.dropped > 0) {
    reportCallers(hook);  // saved without them
    send({ kind: 'callers-dropped', hookId: spec.id, count: learned.dropped });
  }

  return {
    id: spec.id,
    writeInstruction: describeInstruction(site),
    resumePc: site.writeIns.next.toString(),
    trampoline: site.code === null ? null : site.code.toString(),
    patchSize: site.patchSize,
    breakpoint: site.breakpoint ? site.slot : null,
    cave: site.cave === null ? null : site.cave.toString(),
    operandSize: site.writeOp.size,
    callers: hook.callers.size,
    transform: spec.transform.kind
  };
}

// --- Training -------------------------------------------------------------
// A hook on JIT code with a pointer target is saved with the bytes of its
// write instruction and of the code around it. After a restart, a hardware
// watchpoint on the target finds the instruction again: the hook is
// installed at the first write whose code matches.

function startTraining(spec) {
  const io = VALUE_IO[spec.valueType];
  if (io === undefined)
    throw grembyteError('error.hooks.value_type', { type: spec.valueType });
  if (spec.pointer === null)
    throw grembyteError('error.hooks.training_pointer');
  compileTransform(spec.transform);
  const training = {
    id: spec.id,
    spec,
    io,
    pointer: { ...spec.pointer, base: null },
    target: null,
    slot: null,
    debug: false,
    seen: 0,
    rejected: 0,
    reported: null
  };
  trainings.set(spec.id, training);
  if (!trainingPaused) {
    startTrainingWatch();
    updateTrainings();
  }
  return { id: spec.id, training: true };
}

function startTrainingWatch() {
  if (trainingTimer !== null)
    return;
  ensureExceptionHandler();
  // No thread observer: setting a watchpoint starts a helper thread, and
  // reporting it to the observer while the agent sets one deadlocks.
  // New threads are armed by this timer instead.
  trainingTimer = setInterval(updateTrainings, 500);
}

function stopTrainingWatch() {
  if (trainingTimer === null)
    return;
  clearInterval(trainingTimer);
  trainingTimer = null;
  for (const training of trainings.values()) {
    if (training.slot !== null && training.target !== null) {
      training.target = null;
      for (const thread of Process.enumerateThreads())
        armTraining(thread, training);
    }
  }
  // A trap raised just before the watchpoints were removed may still be on
  // its way; let it reach the handler before its threads are forgotten.
  // Keeping them longer would swallow the traps of a write watch.
  Thread.sleep(0.1);
  trainingThreads.clear();
}

function setTrainingPaused(paused) {
  trainingPaused = paused;
  if (paused) {
    stopTrainingWatch();
  } else if (trainings.size > 0) {
    startTrainingWatch();
    updateTrainings();
  }
  return trainings.size;
}

function armThreadForTrainings(thread) {
  for (const training of trainings.values()) {
    if (training.target !== null)
      armTraining(thread, training);
  }
}

function armTraining(thread, training) {
  if (training.slot === null)
    return;
  try {
    if (training.target === null) {
      thread.unsetHardwareWatchpoint(training.slot);
    } else {
      thread.setHardwareWatchpoint(training.slot, training.target, training.io.size, 'w');
      trainingThreads.add(thread.id);
    }
  } catch (_error) {
    // The thread exited, or it is the agent's own.
  }
}

function freeDebugSlot() {
  const used = new Set(Array.from(trainings.values(), t => t.slot));
  for (const site of sites.values()) {
    if (site.breakpoint)
      used.add(site.slot);
  }
  return DEBUG_SLOTS.find(slot => !used.has(slot)) ?? null;
}

function updateTrainings() {
  for (const training of trainings.values()) {
    if (training.slot === null)
      training.slot = freeDebugSlot();
    if (training.slot === null)
      continue;
    // The chain leads elsewhere e.g. after loading a game, or nowhere yet.
    const target = resolvePointer(training.pointer);
    const unchanged = target === null ? training.target === null
      : training.target !== null && target.equals(training.target);
    if (unchanged)
      continue;
    training.target = target;
    for (const thread of Process.enumerateThreads())
      armTraining(thread, training);
  }
  // Threads started since the last update.
  for (const thread of Process.enumerateThreads()) {
    if (!trainingThreads.has(thread.id))
      armThreadForTrainings(thread);
  }
}

function stopTraining(training) {
  trainings.delete(training.id);
  if (training.slot !== null && training.target !== null) {
    training.target = null;
    for (const thread of Process.enumerateThreads())
      armTraining(thread, training);
  }
  if (trainings.size === 0)
    stopTrainingWatch();
}

function onTrainingException(details) {
  if (!trainingThreads.has(Process.getCurrentThreadId()))
    return false;
  if (trainingTimer === null)
    return true;  // a late trap after the training watch stopped
  trainingHits.push(details.context.pc);
  if (!trainingScheduled) {
    // Hooks are installed outside the exception handler.
    trainingScheduled = true;
    setTimeout(processTrainingHits, 0);
  }
  return true;
}

function processTrainingHits() {
  trainingScheduled = false;
  for (const pc of trainingHits.splice(0)) {
    for (const training of Array.from(trainings.values())) {
      if (training.target !== null)
        tryTraining(training, pc);
    }
  }
}

function trainingCandidate(training, pc) {
  // A write that is hooked already runs relocated in its trampoline.
  for (const site of sites.values()) {
    if (site.code !== null && pc.compare(site.code) >= 0
        && pc.compare(site.code.add(Process.pageSize)) < 0)
      return { ins: site.writeIns, bytes: site.bytes, context: site.context };
  }
  const { ins } = resolveWriteInstruction(pc, training.target, training.io.size);
  const site = sites.get(ins.address.toString());
  if (site !== undefined)
    return { ins, bytes: site.bytes, context: site.context };
  return { ins, bytes: hexBytes(ins.address.readByteArray(ins.size)), context: codeContext(ins) };
}

function matchingBytes(expected, actual, fromEnd) {
  const count = Math.min(expected.length, actual.length) / 2;
  let same = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const a = fromEnd ? expected.length - 2 * (i + 1) : 2 * i;
    const b = fromEnd ? actual.length - 2 * (i + 1) : 2 * i;
    if (expected.substr(a, 2) === actual.substr(b, 2))
      same++;
  }
  return [same, count];
}

function contextSimilarity(expected, actual) {
  const [sameBefore, before] = matchingBytes(expected.before || '', actual.before, true);
  const [sameAfter, after] = matchingBytes(expected.after || '', actual.after, false);
  return before + after === 0 ? 1 : (sameBefore + sameAfter) / (before + after);
}

function tryTraining(training, pc) {
  let candidate;
  try {
    candidate = trainingCandidate(training, pc);
  } catch (_error) {
    training.rejected++;
    return;
  }
  training.seen++;
  const similarity = contextSimilarity(training.spec.signature, candidate.context);
  if (candidate.bytes !== training.spec.instructionBytes
      || similarity < TRAINING_MIN_SIMILARITY) {
    training.rejected++;
    return;
  }
  stopTraining(training);
  try {
    const info = addHook({
      ...training.spec, writePc: candidate.ins.address.toString(), signature: null,
      managed: null
    });
    hooks.get(training.id).debug = training.debug;
    info.similarity = similarity;
    send({ kind: 'trained', hookId: training.id, info });
  } catch (error) {
    send({ kind: 'training-failed', hookId: training.id, error: String(error) });
  }
}

function trainingEvents() {
  const events = [];
  for (const training of trainings.values()) {
    const state = {
      hookId: training.id,
      paused: trainingPaused,
      resolved: training.target !== null,
      waiting: training.slot === null,
      seen: training.seen,
      rejected: training.rejected
    };
    const key = JSON.stringify(state);
    if (key !== training.reported) {
      training.reported = key;
      events.push(state);
    }
  }
  return events;
}

function removeHook(id) {
  const training = trainings.get(id);
  if (training !== undefined) {
    stopTraining(training);
    return true;
  }
  const hook = hooks.get(id);
  if (hook === undefined)
    return false;
  hooks.delete(id);
  hook.site.hooks.delete(id);
  if (hook.fast !== undefined) {
    fast.enable(hook.fast, 0);
    retiredFastHooks.push(hook.fast);
    updateFastSite(hook.site);
  }
  if (hook.site.hooks.size === 0)
    uninstallSite(hook.site);
  return true;
}

function requireHook(id) {
  const hook = hooks.get(id);
  if (hook === undefined)
    throw grembyteError('error.hooks.unknown', { id });
  return hook;
}

function flushStats() {
  const events = [];
  for (const hook of hooks.values()) {
    takeFastStats(hook);
    if (hook.stats.count === 0)
      continue;
    const last = hook.stats.last;
    events.push({
      hookId: hook.id,
      count: hook.stats.count,
      last: last === null ? null : { ...last, address: last.address.toString() }
    });
    hook.stats.count = 0;
  }
  if (events.length > 0)
    send({ kind: 'events', events });
  const training = trainingEvents();
  if (training.length > 0)
    send({ kind: 'training', events: training });
  if (debugEvents.length > 0 || debugDropped.size > 0) {
    send({
      kind: 'debug',
      events: debugEvents.splice(0),
      dropped: Object.fromEntries(debugDropped)
    });
    debugDropped.clear();
  }
  if (hookLogs.length > 0 || hookLogsDropped.size > 0) {
    send({ kind: 'hook-logs', lines: hookLogs.splice(0),
           dropped: Object.fromEntries(hookLogsDropped) });
    hookLogsDropped.clear();
  }
}

let flushTicks = 0;
const flushTimer = setInterval(() => {
  engineFound = engine.refresh();
  if (flushTicks % RANGES_REFRESH_TICKS === 0)
    refreshFastRanges();
  if (++flushTicks % SITE_CHECK_TICKS === 0) {
    checkSites();
    if (profiling) {
      const profile = profileEvents();
      if (profile.length > 0)
        send({ kind: 'profile', sites: profile });
    }
  }
  // Enumerating threads while one handles a write watch's trap deadlocks.
  if (flushTicks % BREAKPOINT_ARM_TICKS === 0 && !trainingPaused && hasBreakpointSites())
    armNewThreads();
  flushStats();
}, 100);
send({
  kind: 'ready',
  arch: Process.arch,
  accessStub: accessStub.toString(),
  accessStubSize: Process.pageSize,
  fastCode: fast === null ? null : fast.codeRange.base.toString(),
  fastCodeSize: fast === null ? 0 : fast.codeRange.size
});

rpc.exports = {
  addHook: addHookResolving,
  removeHook,
  setTrainingPaused,
  setTransform(id, spec) {
    const training = trainings.get(id);
    if (training !== undefined) {
      compileTransform(spec);
      training.spec.transform = spec;
      return true;
    }
    const hook = requireHook(id);
    hook.transform = compileTransform(spec);
    hook.transformSpec = spec;
    hook.errorReported = false;
    configureFastHook(hook);
    return true;
  },
  setRepatch(enabled) {
    repatchReverted = enabled;
    return true;
  },
  setProfiling(enabled) {
    profiling = enabled;
    for (const site of sites.values())
      site.profile = undefined;
    return true;
  },
  setDebug(id, enabled) {
    const training = trainings.get(id);
    if (training !== undefined) {
      training.debug = enabled;
      return true;
    }
    const hook = requireHook(id);
    hook.debug = enabled;
    configureFastHook(hook);
    return true;
  },
  setEnabled(id, enabled) {
    const training = trainings.get(id);
    if (training !== undefined) {
      training.spec.enabled = enabled;
      return true;
    }
    const hook = requireHook(id);
    hook.enabled = enabled;
    if (!enabled)
      hook.pending.clear();
    configureFastHook(hook);
    return true;
  },
  dispose() {
    clearInterval(flushTimer);
    for (const training of Array.from(trainings.values()))
      stopTraining(training);
    if (exceptionHandlerInstalled)
      Thread.sleep(0.1);  // let late traps reach the handler before unloading
    for (const id of Array.from(hooks.keys()))
      removeHook(id);
    // No thread enters a trampoline any more. Those inside, also those
    // waiting for this agent's lock in a callback, get to leave: Thread.sleep
    // lets them have the lock.
    const deadline = Date.now() + DISPOSE_WAIT_MS;
    while (threadsInside.readS32() > 0 && Date.now() < deadline)
      Thread.sleep(0.005);
    Thread.sleep(DISPOSE_GRACE_S);
    flushStats();
    return { threadsInside: threadsInside.readS32() };
  }
};

```

`grembyte/hooks/engine.py`:

```py
"""Frida-backed write hooks that rewrite values right after the game stores them.

The hook targets the instruction that writes the target address (found via a
write watch: the reported trap PC is the instruction *after* the write). The
agent replaces it with a jump into a trampoline (code cave)::

    before(regs)            snapshot the old value if the write hits the target
    <relocated write>
    after(regs)             hand old/new value to the ValueTransform, store result
    <rest of the relocated bytes>
    jmp back

This works independently of how the write is encoded (``add [mem], reg``,
``mov [mem], reg``, ``sub``, ...). Several hooks may share one write site;
they run in the order they were added. Only x86-64 targets are supported.

The jump takes 5 bytes. A tiny function (``mov [rcx+8], edx; ret``) may end
before that, with the next function right behind it. With the setting
``hook_short_jump`` the agent then writes a 2-byte ``jmp rel8`` over the
write instead, to int3 padding within 128 bytes that ends at an aligned
function start, and puts the jump to the trampoline there. Off by default:
padding is found by a heuristic.

A hook either targets one fixed address or, when no address is given (e.g. a
hook restored from module + offset after the game was restarted), whatever
address the hooked instruction writes on each call.

Shared code (``add_gold(&player)`` and ``add_gold(&enemy)``) is told apart by
the caller: a fixed-address hook learns the first ``caller_depth`` return
addresses on the stack of every write that hits its address. After a restart
the address-less hook only runs for writes with one of those learned callers.
Return addresses are found by scanning the stack for values that follow a
call instruction. Without frame pointers the stack also holds stale ones,
left by calls that returned long ago (e.g. into libc or the graphics
driver), in the local variables of the functions running now. A candidate
therefore only counts

- if its call leads to the function it returns from: a direct call's target
  (or where a PLT stub or thunk jumps) must lie in the same module (or both
  in generated code), at most ``MAX_FUNCTION_SIZE`` before the address in
  the function, and not before its start where a symbol tells it. An
  indirect call (``call rax``, virtual methods) cannot be followed; it counts
  within a module, and into generated code (JIT) from anywhere;
- and if it lies above the function's frame: where the function's start is
  known (symbol or direct call), its prologue (``push``, ``sub rsp``) tells
  how much stack it took below its return address at least. With a symbol
  the scan starts right there: ``CALLER_SCAN_SLOTS`` would not reach past
  a frame with kilobytes of locals.

Learned callers that fail the first check (learned before it existed) are
dropped when the hook is installed. The same caller signature can still
show up for other addresses; the agent reports that as ambiguous.

A hook with a pointer chain (``module + base_offset``, then dereference and
add each offset) resolves it on every write and only applies to writes of the
address it leads to. That works the same after a restart, follows objects the
game allocates anew and tells player and enemy apart in shared code.

A write instruction in JIT code has no module + offset that survives a
restart. A hook on it with a pointer target is restored by training instead:
it is saved with the bytes of its write instruction and of the code around
it (``signature``), and after a restart a hardware watchpoint on the target
waits for a write from matching code and installs the hook there.

In Mono games (Unity) the agent names JIT code by its C# method: the write
site (``method`` of the write instruction, or a later ``site-method``
message once a game thread ran it) and the callers in debug events. The
``site-method`` message also identifies the method (``managed``). A hook
saved with it is installed right away after a restart: Mono compiles the
method and the agent finds the write instruction in its code. Training is
the fallback when that fails (``managed-failed``).

Anti-tamper code in some games (e.g. Arxan in Dark Souls III) repairs
patched code: the original write is back and the hook stops without an
error. Once a second the agent compares every site with the bytes it wrote
and reports a change (``site_state``: reverted, changed, repatched,
restored). With the setting ``hook_repatch`` it patches a site whose
original code is back again; off by default, as it races the game's checks.

With the setting ``hook_profiling`` the agent measures every hooked write
and reports once a second per site (``hook_profile``, also in the log): how
often the site ran and how many writes all its hooks skipped, how long a
game thread waited from entering the trampoline until its JavaScript ran
(the agent runs one thread at a time, so other threads in a hook, its
timers and garbage collection make it wait) and how long that ran, in µs
on average and at most, per callback (two per write).

A hook with ``breakpoint`` leaves the game's code untouched: a hardware
breakpoint on the write instruction takes the old value and moves to the
next instruction, where the transform runs and it moves back. Patch checks
cannot see it, but it uses one of the three debug register slots the write
watch leaves (shared with trainings) and each write traps twice.

The trampoline calls C first (``FAST_SOURCE`` in engine.js, a Frida
CModule): it computes the written address, checks the hook's switch, its
fixed target and its learned callers (its own copy of the stack scan,
taught by the JavaScript scan what each return address it met means) and
runs the built-in
manipulations (``ValueTransform.to_agent()["native"]``: multiply, freeze,
clamp, also as copies in templates) itself. JavaScript only runs for what
C cannot decide (scripts, debug mode, caller learning, pointer targets,
unknown stack layouts). The agent's JavaScript runs one thread at a time;
a game thread descheduled there stalled every other hooked thread for a
scheduler slice and dropped frames.

In debug mode a hook reports every call (values, caller, ``ctx.log()``
output, errors with stack) and every write it skipped, with the reason.
At most ``MAX_DEBUG_EVENTS`` events are sent per 100 ms; the rest is counted.
"""

import itertools
import logging
import queue
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import frida
from PySide6.QtCore import QThread, Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core import logs, messages
from grembyte.core import sessions
from grembyte.core import settings
from grembyte.engines.registry import ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE
from grembyte.core.pointer import PointerChain
from grembyte.attach.frida_attach import CLEANUP_ERRORS, FRIDA_ERRORS, attach_session
from grembyte.attach.backends import BACKEND_PTRACE
from grembyte.core.value_types import watch_size_for_type
from grembyte.hooks.transforms import ValueTransform
from grembyte.agent.source import load_agent_source


MAX_CALLER_DEPTH = 4

_profile_log = logging.getLogger("grembyte.hook_profile")


_AGENT_SOURCE = load_agent_source(__file__)


@dataclass
class HookSpec:
    """Where to hook and how to transform the written value.

    Pass ``trap_pc`` (the PC reported by a write watch, i.e. the instruction
    after the write), ``write_pc`` (the write instruction itself) or
    ``module`` and ``module_offset`` (the write instruction relative to its
    module, which stays valid across restarts). ``instruction_bytes`` (hex)
    makes the agent refuse to patch a module whose code has changed.

    With ``filter_address`` the transform only runs when the hooked instruction
    actually writes ``address``; disable it only when the effective address
    cannot be computed reliably. Without an ``address`` the transform applies
    to every address the instruction writes, restricted to the learned
    ``callers`` if there are any.

    ``caller_depth`` is the number of return addresses that identify a caller
    (0 disables caller learning); ``callers`` holds the learned signatures as
    lists of ``(module, offset)`` frames.

    With a ``pointer`` (PointerChain) the hook targets whatever address the
    chain leads to at each write; caller learning is not needed then.

    Instead of a code location, a ``signature`` (``{"before", "after"}``: hex
    code bytes around the write instruction ``instruction_bytes``) together
    with a ``pointer`` lets the agent train: it installs the hook at the first
    write to the target from matching code.

    With ``breakpoint`` the write is hooked by a hardware breakpoint instead
    of a jump patched into the code (see the module docstring).

    ``managed`` (``{image, file, token, method, offset}`` from the agent's
    ``site-method`` message) names the C# method of a write site in Mono JIT
    code: the agent lets Mono compile it and looks for ``instruction_bytes``
    in its code, preferring the code around it given by ``signature``. If
    that fails it falls back to training with the ``signature``.
    """

    # pylint: disable=too-many-instance-attributes
    address: int | None
    value_type: str
    transform: ValueTransform
    trap_pc: int | None = None
    write_pc: int | None = None
    module: str | None = None
    module_offset: int | None = None
    instruction_bytes: str | None = None
    filter_address: bool = True
    enabled: bool = True
    caller_depth: int = 1
    callers: list = field(default_factory=list)
    pointer: PointerChain | None = None
    signature: dict | None = None
    managed: dict | None = None
    breakpoint: bool = False
    label: str = field(default="", compare=False)

    @property
    def training(self):
        """Whether the agent has to find the write instruction first."""
        return (self.signature is not None and self.trap_pc is None
                and self.write_pc is None and self.module is None)

    def __post_init__(self):
        watch_size_for_type(self.value_type)
        if not isinstance(self.transform, ValueTransform):
            raise ValueError("transform must be a ValueTransform instance")
        if self.training:
            if self.pointer is None or not self.instruction_bytes:
                raise ValueError("training needs a pointer and the instruction bytes")
        elif (self.trap_pc is None and self.write_pc is None and self.module is None
              and self.managed is None):
            raise ValueError(
                "HookSpec needs a trap_pc, a write_pc, a module, a method or a signature"
            )
        if (self.managed is not None and not self.instruction_bytes
                and self.trap_pc is None and self.write_pc is None):
            raise ValueError("a method location needs the instruction bytes")
        if (self.module is None) != (self.module_offset is None):
            raise ValueError("module and module_offset must be given together")
        if (self.address is None and self.write_pc is None and self.module is None
                and self.managed is None and not self.training):
            raise ValueError("a trap_pc can only be resolved with an address")
        if not 0 <= self.caller_depth <= MAX_CALLER_DEPTH:
            raise ValueError(f"caller_depth must be between 0 and {MAX_CALLER_DEPTH}")
        if any(len(frames) != self.caller_depth for frames in self.callers):
            raise ValueError("every caller signature needs caller_depth frames")

    def to_agent(self, hook_id):
        return {
            "id": hook_id,
            "address": None if self.address is None else hex(self.address),
            "valueType": self.value_type,
            "trapPc": None if self.trap_pc is None else hex(self.trap_pc),
            "writePc": None if self.write_pc is None else hex(self.write_pc),
            "module": self.module,
            "moduleOffset": self.module_offset,
            "instructionBytes": self.instruction_bytes,
            "filterAddress": self.filter_address,
            "enabled": self.enabled,
            "callerDepth": self.caller_depth,
            "callers": [[list(frame) for frame in frames] for frames in self.callers],
            "pointer": None if self.pointer is None else {
                "module": self.pointer.module,
                "baseOffset": self.pointer.base_offset,
                "offsets": list(self.pointer.offsets),
            },
            "signature": self.signature,
            "managed": self.managed,
            "breakpoint": self.breakpoint,
            "transform": self.transform.to_agent(),
        }


def build_agent_source():
    return ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE + _AGENT_SOURCE


def create_hook_worker(backend, pid, parent=None) -> QThread:
    """Build the hook worker for ``backend`` (``frida`` or ``ptrace``).

    Both workers share the same signals and public methods, so the panel treats
    them alike. The ptrace backend (Option A) needs no injection and works on
    Wine/Proton, but only rewrites values at a data watchpoint; see
    :mod:`grembyte.hooks.ptrace_hook` for what it does not cover.
    """
    if backend == BACKEND_PTRACE:
        from grembyte.hooks.ptrace_hook import (  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
            PtraceHookWorker,
        )
        return PtraceHookWorker(pid, parent)
    return HookWorker(pid, parent)


class HookWorker(QThread):
    """Keep a Frida session open and manage value hooks inside one process.

    The public methods are safe to call from the GUI thread: they enqueue a
    command that the worker thread executes against the agent. Results come
    back through the signals.
    """

    session_ready = Signal(str)
    hook_installed = Signal(int, object)
    # hook id, training state: resolved (target found), waiting (for a free
    # watchpoint), seen and rejected writes; empty when the training starts
    hook_training = Signal(int, object)
    hook_failed = Signal(int, str)
    hook_removed = Signal(int)
    hook_updated = Signal(int)
    hook_events = Signal(object)
    transform_error = Signal(int, str)
    # hook id, learned caller signatures (frames are [module, offset] or None)
    callers_learned = Signal(int, object)
    callers_ambiguous = Signal(int)
    # hook id, number of learned callers dropped as stale return addresses
    callers_dropped = Signal(int, int)
    # hook ids sharing a write site in JIT code, its C# method (Mono games)
    # and what finds it again after a restart (HookSpec.managed)
    site_method = Signal(object, str, object)
    # hook id, why its C# method did not lead to the write site; it trains
    managed_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # hook ids sharing a write site, its state (reverted, changed, repatched,
    # restored), how often the game reverted it and why patching it again
    # failed ("" if it did not)
    site_state = Signal(object, str, int, str)
    # timings per write site, once a second with hook_profiling: dicts with
    # hookIds, calls, skipped, waitAvg, waitMax, runAvg, runMax (µs)
    hook_profile = Signal(object)
    # debug events of hooks in debug mode, events dropped per hook id
    hook_debug = Signal(object, object)
    # ctx.log lines of scripts (also outside debug mode): [{hookId, time, text}],
    # lines dropped per hook id (more than the agent sends at once)
    hook_logs = Signal(object, object)
    # console.log output of the agent and its transforms: level, text
    agent_log = Signal(str, str)
    agent_warning = Signal(str)
    worker_failed = Signal(str)
    worker_stopped = Signal()

    # Shared by all workers so ids stay unique when a worker is replaced.
    _ids = itertools.count(1)

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.pid = pid
        self._commands = queue.Queue()
        self._ready_event = threading.Event()
        self._ready_payload = None
        # (start, end) of the agent's own memory-access code, once it is ready
        self.access_stub = None
        # (start, end) of the agent's C code, which reads and writes targets too
        self.fast_code = None
        self._agent_error = None
        self._detach_reason = None

    def add_hook(self, spec):
        """Queue a hook and return its id; expect hook_installed or hook_failed."""
        hook_id = next(self._ids)
        self._commands.put(("add", hook_id, spec))
        return hook_id

    def remove_hook(self, hook_id):
        self._commands.put(("remove", hook_id, None))

    def set_transform(self, hook_id, transform):
        if not isinstance(transform, ValueTransform):
            raise ValueError("transform must be a ValueTransform instance")
        self._commands.put(("transform", hook_id, transform))

    def set_enabled(self, hook_id, enabled):
        self._commands.put(("enabled", hook_id, bool(enabled)))

    def set_trainings_paused(self, paused, timeout=2.0):
        """Pause or resume all trainings; wait until the agent did it.

        Trainings must rest while a write watch runs in the process.
        Returns False if the agent did not answer in time; with a
        ``timeout`` of None the command is only queued.
        """
        done = threading.Event()
        self._commands.put(("training-paused", 0, (bool(paused), done)))
        return True if timeout is None else done.wait(timeout)

    def set_debug(self, hook_id, enabled):
        """Report every call and skipped write of a hook via hook_debug."""
        self._commands.put(("debug", hook_id, bool(enabled)))

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.HOOKS)
    def run(self):
        session = None
        script = None
        try:
            session = attach_session(self.pid)
            sessions.SESSIONS.set_frida_session(self, session)
            session.on("detached", self._on_session_detached)
            script = session.create_script(build_agent_source())
            script.on("message", self._on_message)
            script.set_log_handler(self._on_log)
            script.load()

            if not self._ready_event.wait(5):
                raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError("error.hooks.load_timeout")
            if self._agent_error:
                raise RuntimeError(self._agent_error)
            ready = self._ready_payload or {}
            if ready.get("accessStub"):
                start = int(ready["accessStub"], 16)
                self.access_stub = (start, start + ready.get("accessStubSize", 0x1000))
            if ready.get("fastCode"):
                start = int(ready["fastCode"], 16)
                self.fast_code = (start, start + ready.get("fastCodeSize", 0x1000))
            script.exports_sync.set_repatch(settings.get("hook_repatch"))
            script.exports_sync.set_profiling(settings.get("hook_profiling"))
            settings.subscribe(self._on_settings_changed)
            self.session_ready.emit(ready.get("arch", ""))

            while (not self.isInterruptionRequested()
                   and self._detach_reason is None
                   and self._agent_error is None):
                try:
                    command = self._commands.get(timeout=0.05)
                except queue.Empty:
                    continue
                self._execute(script, *command)

            if self._agent_error and not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                raise RuntimeError(self._agent_error)
            if self._detach_reason and not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError("error.agent.detached",
                                                     reason=self._detach_reason)
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (ImportError, OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.worker_failed.emit(messages.describe(error))
        finally:
            settings.unsubscribe(self._on_settings_changed)
            if script is not None:
                try:
                    disposed = script.exports_sync.dispose()
                    inside = disposed.get("threadsInside", 0) if isinstance(disposed, dict) else 0
                    if inside:
                        logs.log.warning("Unloading the hook agent with %d game thread(s) "
                                         "still counted in a trampoline", inside)
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
                try:
                    script.unload()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
            if session is not None:
                try:
                    session.detach()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
            self.worker_stopped.emit()

    def _execute(self, script, action, hook_id, argument):
        api = script.exports_sync
        try:
            if action == "add":
                payload = argument.to_agent(hook_id)
                payload["shortJump"] = settings.get("hook_short_jump")
                info = api.add_hook(payload)
                if info.get("training"):
                    self.hook_training.emit(hook_id, {})
                else:
                    info["label"] = argument.label
                    info["transformDescription"] = argument.transform.describe()
                    self.hook_installed.emit(hook_id, info)
            elif action == "remove":
                if api.remove_hook(hook_id):
                    self.hook_removed.emit(hook_id)
            elif action == "transform":
                api.set_transform(hook_id, argument.to_agent())
                self.hook_updated.emit(hook_id)
            elif action == "enabled":
                api.set_enabled(hook_id, argument)
                self.hook_updated.emit(hook_id)
            elif action == "training-paused":
                paused, done = argument
                try:
                    api.set_training_paused(paused)
                finally:
                    done.set()
            elif action == "debug":
                api.set_debug(hook_id, argument)
                self.hook_updated.emit(hook_id)
            elif action == "repatch":
                api.set_repatch(argument)
            elif action == "profiling":
                api.set_profiling(argument)
        except frida.RPCException as error:
            self.hook_failed.emit(hook_id, messages.describe(error))

    def _on_settings_changed(self, changed):
        if "hook_repatch" in changed:
            self._commands.put(("repatch", 0, changed["hook_repatch"]))
        if "hook_profiling" in changed:
            self._commands.put(("profiling", 0, changed["hook_profiling"]))

    def _on_message(self, message, _data):
        if message.get("type") == "error":
            self._agent_error = messages.describe(
                message.get("stack", messages.text("error.hooks.agent_failed")))
            self._ready_event.set()
            return

        if message.get("type") != "send":
            return
        payload = message.get("payload", {})
        kind = payload.get("kind")
        if kind == "ready":
            self._ready_payload = payload
            self._ready_event.set()
        elif kind == "events":
            self.hook_events.emit(payload.get("events", []))
        elif kind == "training":
            for event in payload.get("events", []):
                self.hook_training.emit(event.get("hookId", 0), event)
        elif kind == "trained":
            self.hook_installed.emit(payload.get("hookId", 0), payload.get("info", {}))
        elif kind == "training-failed":
            self.hook_failed.emit(payload.get("hookId", 0),
                                  messages.describe(payload.get("error", "")))
        elif kind == "agent-error":
            self.agent_warning.emit(messages.describe(payload.get("error", "")))
        elif kind == "debug":
            self.hook_debug.emit(
                payload.get("events", []),
                {int(hook_id): count for hook_id, count in payload.get("dropped", {}).items()},
            )
        elif kind == "hook-logs":
            self.hook_logs.emit(
                payload.get("lines", []),
                {int(hook_id): count for hook_id, count in payload.get("dropped", {}).items()},
            )
        elif kind == "callers":
            self.callers_learned.emit(
                payload.get("hookId", 0), payload.get("callers", [])
            )
        elif kind == "site-method":
            self.site_method.emit(
                payload.get("hookIds", []), payload.get("method", ""), payload.get("managed")
            )
        elif kind == "managed-failed":
            self.managed_failed.emit(payload.get("hookId", 0),
                                     messages.describe(payload.get("error", "")))
        elif kind == "profile":
            sites = payload.get("sites", [])
            for site in sites:
                _profile_log.info(
                    "hooks %s: %d calls/s, %d skipped, %d in JS; wait avg %.1f max %.1f us; "
                    "run avg %.1f max %.1f us", site.get("hookIds"), site.get("calls", 0),
                    site.get("skipped", 0), site.get("js", 0), site.get("waitAvg", 0),
                    site.get("waitMax", 0), site.get("runAvg", 0), site.get("runMax", 0))
            self.hook_profile.emit(sites)
        elif kind == "site-state":
            self.site_state.emit(
                payload.get("hookIds", []), payload.get("state", ""),
                payload.get("reverts", 0), messages.describe(payload.get("error") or ""),
            )
        elif kind == "callers-ambiguous":
            self.callers_ambiguous.emit(payload.get("hookId", 0))
        elif kind == "callers-dropped":
            self.callers_dropped.emit(payload.get("hookId", 0), payload.get("count", 0))
        elif kind == "transform-error":
            self.transform_error.emit(
                payload.get("hookId", 0), messages.describe(payload.get("error", ""))
            )

    def _on_log(self, level, text):
        logs.agent_log("hook agent", level, text)
        self.agent_log.emit(level, text)

    def _on_session_detached(self, reason, _crash):
        self._detach_reason = reason

```

`grembyte/hooks/ptrace_hook.py`:

```py
"""A ptrace-backed value hook, as an alternative to the Frida hook engine.

This is "Option A": it does not inject code or patch the game. It sets a
hardware *data* watchpoint on the target address (reusing
:class:`grembyte.attach.ptrace_engine.PtraceWatchpointEngine`); the write traps the
thread *after* it stored the value, and the worker then reads the value back,
runs the hook's :class:`~grembyte.hooks.transforms.ValueTransform` on it (in Qt's
JavaScript engine, the same ``ctx`` the Frida agent uses), and writes the
result back before resuming the thread. Because nothing is injected it works on
Wine/Proton targets.

Compared with the Frida backend this is address-anchored, not
instruction-anchored, which has consequences worth knowing:

* Shared code (``add_gold(&player)`` / ``add_gold(&enemy)``) is told apart for
  free, because only the chosen address is watched -- no caller learning.
* A hook needs a concrete address: a fixed address, or a pointer chain this
  worker resolves. Pointer targets are re-resolved periodically and the
  watchpoint is moved if the object moved.
* The value is corrected just *after* the store, so there is a one-instruction
  window where the game's own value is in memory.
* The CPU offers four data watchpoints, so at most four distinct addresses can
  be hooked at once.
* Training/JIT signatures, caller learning and debug events (Frida-only) are
  not provided.

Only x86-64 targets are supported.
"""

import queue
import struct
import threading
import time

from PySide6.QtCore import Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core import messages, sessions
from grembyte.core.memory import read_memory, write_process_bytes
from grembyte.core.pointer import managed_bases, resolve_chain
from grembyte.attach.ptrace_engine import (
    PtraceWatchpointEngine,
    WATCHPOINT_SLOTS,
    watch_alignment_error,
)
from grembyte.core.value_types import VALUE_TYPES
from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker
from grembyte.hooks.sandbox import TransformSandbox
from grembyte.platform import ProcessMemory


class PtraceHookWorker(PtraceWatchpointEngine):
    """Manage value hooks in one process using ptrace data watchpoints.

    The public methods mirror :class:`grembyte.hooks.engine.HookWorker` and are
    safe to call from the GUI thread: each enqueues a command the worker thread
    runs. Results come back through the signals. The training, caller and debug
    signals exist for interface parity but this backend never emits them.
    """

    session_ready = Signal(str)
    hook_installed = Signal(int, object)
    hook_training = Signal(int, object)
    hook_failed = Signal(int, str)
    hook_removed = Signal(int)
    hook_updated = Signal(int)
    hook_events = Signal(object)
    transform_error = Signal(int, str)
    callers_learned = Signal(int, object)
    callers_ambiguous = Signal(int)
    callers_dropped = Signal(int, int)
    # Frida-only; kept for interface parity
    site_method = Signal(object, str, object)
    managed_failed = Signal(int, str)
    site_state = Signal(object, str, int, str)
    hook_profile = Signal(object)
    # ctx.log lines of scripts (also outside debug mode): [{hookId, time, text}],
    # lines dropped per hook id (more than the agent sends at once)
    hook_logs = Signal(object, object)
    hook_debug = Signal(object, object)
    agent_log = Signal(str, str)
    agent_warning = Signal(str)
    worker_failed = Signal(str)
    worker_stopped = Signal()

    # Pointer targets can move; re-resolve them this often.
    RERESOLVE_INTERVAL = 1.0

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None):
        super().__init__(pid, parent)
        self.access_stub = None  # Frida-only; kept for interface parity
        self.fast_code = None
        self._commands = queue.Queue()
        self._hooks = {}          # hook id -> hook state
        self._addresses = {}      # address -> {"slot", "value_type", "size", "last"}
        self._sandbox = None
        self._dirty = False

    # -- public API (GUI thread) -------------------------------------------

    def add_hook(self, spec):
        """Queue a hook and return its id; expect hook_installed or hook_failed."""
        # Shared with the Frida workers: method hooks sit in the same panel.
        hook_id = next(HookWorker._ids)  # pylint: disable=protected-access
        self._commands.put(("add", hook_id, spec))
        return hook_id

    def remove_hook(self, hook_id):
        self._commands.put(("remove", hook_id, None))

    def set_transform(self, hook_id, transform):
        self._commands.put(("transform", hook_id, transform))

    def set_enabled(self, hook_id, enabled):
        self._commands.put(("enabled", hook_id, bool(enabled)))

    def set_trainings_paused(self, paused, timeout=2.0):
        """No training in this backend; satisfy the HookWorker interface."""
        done = threading.Event()
        self._commands.put(("training-paused", 0, done))
        return True if timeout is None else done.wait(timeout)

    def set_debug(self, hook_id, enabled):
        """Debug events are Frida-only; accepted and ignored."""
        self._commands.put(("debug", hook_id, bool(enabled)))

    # -- worker thread ------------------------------------------------------

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.PTRACE_HOOKS)
    def run(self):
        """Attach, service hook commands and watchpoint traps, then detach."""
        try:
            self._sandbox = TransformSandbox()
            self._load_mappings()
            self._attach_all()
            if not self._armed:
                raise messages.LocalizedOSError("error.hooks.no_thread", errno=1)
            self.session_ready.emit("x86-64")
            self._loop()
        except OSError as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.worker_failed.emit(self._explain(error))
        finally:
            self._detach_all()
            self.worker_stopped.emit()

    def _loop(self):
        last_resolve = time.monotonic()
        while not self.isInterruptionRequested():
            worked = self._drain_commands()
            if time.monotonic() - last_resolve >= self.RERESOLVE_INTERVAL:
                self._reresolve_pointers()
                last_resolve = time.monotonic()
            if self._dirty:
                self._reprogram()
                self._dirty = False
            if not self._pump() and not worked:
                time.sleep(0.002)
        if self._target_gone:
            self.worker_failed.emit(messages.text("error.ptrace.exited"))

    def _drain_commands(self):
        worked = False
        for _ in range(32):  # bounded so traps still get serviced
            try:
                action, hook_id, argument = self._commands.get_nowait()
            except queue.Empty:
                break
            worked = True
            self._dispatch_command(action, hook_id, argument)
        return worked

    def _dispatch_command(self, action, hook_id, argument):
        if action == "add":
            self._add_hook(hook_id, argument)
        elif action == "remove":
            self._remove_hook(hook_id)
        elif action == "transform":
            self._set_transform(hook_id, argument)
        elif action == "enabled":
            self._set_enabled(hook_id, argument)
        elif action == "training-paused":
            argument.set()  # an Event; no trainings to pause

    # -- hook management ----------------------------------------------------

    def _add_hook(self, hook_id, spec):
        if spec.value_type not in VALUE_TYPES:
            self.hook_failed.emit(hook_id, messages.text("error.hooks.unsupported_type",
                                                         type=spec.value_type))
            return
        address = self._resolve_address(spec)
        if address is None:
            self.hook_failed.emit(hook_id, messages.text("error.hooks.unresolved_address"))
            return
        unaligned = watch_alignment_error(address, VALUE_TYPES[spec.value_type].size)
        if unaligned is not None:
            self.hook_failed.emit(hook_id, unaligned)
            return
        slot_info = self._claim_address(address, spec.value_type)
        if slot_info is None:
            self.hook_failed.emit(hook_id, messages.text("error.hooks.no_watchpoint",
                                                         slots=WATCHPOINT_SLOTS))
            return
        agent = spec.transform.to_agent()
        self._hooks[hook_id] = {
            "address": address,
            "pointer": spec.pointer,
            "value_type": spec.value_type,
            "source": agent["source"],
            "params": agent.get("params", {}),
            "enabled": spec.enabled,
        }
        self._dirty = True
        self.hook_installed.emit(
            hook_id, {"site": self._site(address), "address": hex(address)}
        )

    def _remove_hook(self, hook_id):
        hook = self._hooks.pop(hook_id, None)
        if hook is None:
            return
        if self._sandbox is not None:
            self._sandbox.reset_state(hook_id)
        self._release_address(hook["address"])
        self._dirty = True
        self.hook_removed.emit(hook_id)

    def _set_transform(self, hook_id, transform):
        hook = self._hooks.get(hook_id)
        if hook is None:
            return
        agent = transform.to_agent()
        hook["source"] = agent["source"]
        hook["params"] = agent.get("params", {})
        self.hook_updated.emit(hook_id)

    def _set_enabled(self, hook_id, enabled):
        hook = self._hooks.get(hook_id)
        if hook is None:
            return
        hook["enabled"] = enabled
        self.hook_updated.emit(hook_id)

    # -- address / slot bookkeeping ----------------------------------------

    def _claim_address(self, address, value_type):
        info = self._addresses.get(address)
        if info is not None:
            return info
        used = {entry["slot"] for entry in self._addresses.values()}
        free = next((slot for slot in range(WATCHPOINT_SLOTS) if slot not in used), None)
        if free is None:
            return None
        size = VALUE_TYPES[value_type].size
        if watch_alignment_error(address, size) is not None:
            return None  # e.g. a pointer now leading to an unaligned address
        info = {"slot": free, "value_type": value_type, "size": size,
                "last": self._read_value(address, value_type, size)}
        self._addresses[address] = info
        self._slots[free] = (address, size, False)
        return info

    def _release_address(self, address):
        if any(hook["address"] == address for hook in self._hooks.values()):
            return  # another hook still watches it
        info = self._addresses.pop(address, None)
        if info is not None:
            self._slots.pop(info["slot"], None)

    def _reresolve_pointers(self):
        """Follow pointer targets again and move watchpoints that moved."""
        moved = False
        memory = None
        try:
            for hook in self._hooks.values():
                if hook["pointer"] is None:
                    continue
                if memory is None:
                    memory = ProcessMemory(self.pid)
                new_address = resolve_chain(
                    memory, {**self._bases, **managed_bases(self.pid)}, hook["pointer"])
                if new_address is None or new_address == hook["address"]:
                    continue
                old_address = hook["address"]
                info = self._claim_address(new_address, hook["value_type"])
                if info is None:
                    continue  # no free slot; keep watching the old address
                hook["address"] = new_address
                self._release_address(old_address)
                moved = True
        finally:
            if memory is not None:
                memory.close()
        if moved:
            self._dirty = True

    # -- trap handling ------------------------------------------------------

    def _handle_trap(self, tid, slot, pc, bits):
        address = self._slots.get(slot, (None,))[0]
        info = self._addresses.get(address)
        if info is None:
            return
        value_type = info["value_type"]
        size = info["size"]
        new_value = self._read_value(address, value_type, size)
        if new_value is None:
            return
        old_value = info["last"]
        value = new_value
        writer = None
        lines = []
        for hook_id, hook in list(self._hooks.items()):
            if hook["address"] != address or not hook["enabled"]:
                continue
            result = self._sandbox.run(
                hook["source"], hook["params"], old_value, value, value_type,
                state_key=hook_id, address=address, thread_id=tid, hook_id=hook_id)
            now = time.time() * 1000
            lines.extend({"hookId": hook_id, "time": now, "text": text}
                         for text in result.logs)
            if result.error:
                self.transform_error.emit(hook_id, result.error)
                continue
            if not result.kept and result.value is not None:
                value = result.value
                writer = hook_id
        if lines:
            self.hook_logs.emit(lines, {})
        if value != new_value:
            error = self._write_value(address, value, value_type)
            if error is not None:
                self.transform_error.emit(writer, error)
                value = new_value
        info["last"] = value

    # -- value I/O ----------------------------------------------------------

    def _read_value(self, address, value_type, size):
        data, readable = read_memory(self.pid, address, size)
        if not all(readable):
            return None
        return VALUE_TYPES[value_type].unpack(bytes(data))

    def _write_value(self, address, value, value_type):
        """Write ``value``; the reason it could not be written, else None."""
        try:
            data = VALUE_TYPES[value_type].pack(value)
        except (OverflowError, struct.error):
            return messages.text("error.hooks.value_out_of_range", value=value, type=value_type)
        try:
            write_process_bytes(self.pid, address, data)
        except OSError as error:
            return messages.text("error.hooks.write_failed", address=hex(address), error=error)
        return None

    def _resolve_address(self, spec):
        if spec.address is not None:
            return spec.address
        if spec.pointer is not None:
            memory = ProcessMemory(self.pid)
            try:
                return resolve_chain(
                    memory, {**self._bases, **managed_bases(self.pid)}, spec.pointer)
            finally:
                memory.close()
        return None

```

`grembyte/hooks/sandbox.py`:

```py
"""Run a transform function outside the target process, e.g. to test a template.

The function gets the same ``ctx`` as inside the hook agent and its result is
normalized the same way. It runs in Qt's JavaScript engine instead of Frida's,
so Frida APIs such as ``ptr()`` or ``Memory`` are not available. ``ctx.log()``
and ``console.log()`` output is collected. A QCoreApplication must exist.
"""

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from PySide6.QtQml import QJSEngine  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core import messages
from grembyte.core.value_types import VALUE_TYPES


# Same ranges as VALUE_IO in the hook agent: 64-bit integers are passed as
# JavaScript numbers and limited to the exactly representable range.
VALUE_LIMITS = {
    name: None if kind.limits is None else (
        max(kind.limits[0], -(2**53 - 1)), min(kind.limits[1], 2**53 - 1)
    )
    for name, kind in VALUE_TYPES.items()
}

_RUNNER = r"""
(function (fn, data, state, callError) {
  // QJSEngine has no globalThis.
  const global = Function('return this')();
  const logs = [];
  const format = args => args.map(arg => {
    if (typeof arg === 'string')
      return arg;
    try {
      return JSON.stringify(arg);
    } catch (_error) {
      return String(arg);
    }
  }).join(' ');
  const log = (...args) => { logs.push(format(args)); };
  const previousConsole = global.console;
  global.console = { log, info: log, warn: log, error: log, debug: log };
  // Game code is out of reach here (method hooks).
  const call = () => { throw new Error(callError); };
  const ctx = Object.assign({ call }, data, { state, log });
  let result;
  let error = null;
  try {
    result = fn(ctx);
  } catch (e) {
    error = (e && e.stack) ? `${e}\n${e.stack}` : String(e);
  } finally {
    global.console = previousConsole;
  }
  let stateText;
  try {
    stateText = JSON.stringify(state);
  } catch (_error) {
    stateText = String(state);
  }
  return {
    error,
    logs,
    state: stateText,
    kept: error === null && (result === undefined || result === null),
    type: typeof result,
    value: (typeof result === 'number' || typeof result === 'boolean') ? result : null,
    text: result === undefined ? 'undefined' : String(result)
  };
})
"""


@dataclass
class SandboxResult:
    """Outcome of one test run.

    ``value`` is the value the hook would store; with ``kept`` the game's value
    stays. ``error`` is set when the function threw or returned no number.
    """

    value: float | int | None = None
    kept: bool = False
    error: str | None = None
    logs: list = field(default_factory=list)
    state: str = "{}"


def normalize_value(value, value_type):
    """Mirror the agent: finite numbers only; integers truncated and clamped."""
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) \
            or not math.isfinite(value):
        raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.hooks.transform_not_number", value=value)
    limits = VALUE_LIMITS[value_type]
    if limits is None:
        return float(value)
    return min(limits[1], max(limits[0], math.trunc(value)))


class TransformSandbox:
    """Call transform functions with a persistent ``ctx.state``.

    ``ctx.state`` is kept per ``state_key`` (one per hook of the ptrace
    backend); calls without a key share one.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._engine = QJSEngine()
        self._runner = self._engine.evaluate(_RUNNER)
        self._states = {}

    def reset_state(self, state_key=None):
        """Start again with an empty ``ctx.state`` (of every key if None)."""
        if state_key is None:
            self._states.clear()
        else:
            self._states.pop(state_key, None)

    def _state(self, state_key):
        state = self._states.get(state_key)
        if state is None:
            state = self._states[state_key] = self._engine.newObject()
        return state

    def _call(self, fn, data, state_key=None):
        """Run ``fn`` with ``data`` as ctx through the runner."""
        return self._runner.call([fn, self._engine.toScriptValue(data), self._state(state_key),
                                  messages.text("error.hooks.sandbox_call")])

    def run_method(self, source, params, result):
        """Call a method hook's ``source`` like the agent would for ``result``.

        There are no arguments, objects or game calls here: ``ctx.args`` and
        ``ctx.refs`` are empty, ``ctx.this`` and ``ctx.caller`` are null and
        ``ctx.call`` throws.
        """
        fn = self._engine.evaluate(f"({source}\n)")
        if fn.isError():
            return SandboxResult(error=fn.toString())
        if not fn.isCallable():
            return SandboxResult(error=messages.text("error.hooks.not_a_function"))
        data = {"phase": "after", "result": result, "args": {}, "refs": {}, "this": None,
                "caller": None,
                "params": dict(params), "method": "Test", "hookId": 0, "threadId": 0}
        outcome = self._call(fn, data)
        if outcome.isError():
            return SandboxResult(error=outcome.toString())
        outcome = outcome.toVariant()
        sandbox_result = SandboxResult(
            logs=list(outcome.get("logs") or []),
            state=outcome.get("state") or "{}",
            kept=bool(outcome.get("kept")),
            error=outcome.get("error"),
        )
        if sandbox_result.error is None and not sandbox_result.kept:
            value = outcome.get("value")
            sandbox_result.value = outcome.get("text") if value is None else value
        return sandbox_result

    def run(self, source, params, old, new, value_type="int32", *, state_key=None,
            address=None, thread_id=0, hook_id=0):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments
        """Call ``source`` like the hook agent would after a write ``old`` -> ``new``.

        ``address``, ``thread_id`` and ``hook_id`` fill ``ctx.address``,
        ``ctx.threadId`` and ``ctx.hookId`` (the ptrace backend knows them).
        """
        fn = self._engine.evaluate(f"({source}\n)")
        if fn.isError():
            return SandboxResult(error=fn.toString())
        if not fn.isCallable():
            return SandboxResult(error=messages.text("error.hooks.not_a_function"))
        data = {
            "old": old,
            "new": new,
            "delta": new - old,
            "params": dict(params),
            "valueType": value_type,
            "address": "0x0" if address is None else hex(address),
            "writePc": "0x0",
            "threadId": thread_id,
            "hookId": hook_id,
        }
        outcome = self._call(fn, data, state_key)
        if outcome.isError():
            return SandboxResult(error=outcome.toString())
        outcome = outcome.toVariant()
        result = SandboxResult(
            logs=list(outcome.get("logs") or []),
            state=outcome.get("state") or "{}",
            kept=bool(outcome.get("kept")),
            error=outcome.get("error"),
        )
        if result.error is None and not result.kept:
            value = outcome.get("value") if outcome.get("type") == "number" else outcome.get("text")
            try:
                result.value = normalize_value(value, value_type)
            except ValueError as error:
                result.error = str(error)
        return result

```

`grembyte/hooks/saved.py`:

```py
"""The hooks saved in the database, as specs to install them again.

The hook panel installs a program's saved hooks whenever it is attached,
grembyte-cli whenever it starts the game; both build the specs here.
"""

from grembyte.core.pointer import PointerChain
from grembyte.db.repository.hooks import hook_transform
from grembyte.features.method_hooks import MethodHookSpec
from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookSpec


def persistable_callers(callers):
    """Keep the caller signatures whose frames all lie inside a module."""
    return [
        [tuple(frame) for frame in frames]
        for frames in callers
        if all(frame is not None for frame in frames)
    ]


def spec_from_saved(saved):
    """Build the HookSpec that reinstalls a hook saved in the database.

    A hook on JIT code (no module) is found again by its C# method if it
    has one (Mono games), else trained again via its signature.
    """
    jit = not saved.module
    return HookSpec(
        None,
        saved.value_type,
        hook_transform(saved),
        module=None if jit else saved.module,
        module_offset=None if jit else saved.module_offset,
        signature=saved.signature if jit else None,
        managed=saved.managed if jit else None,
        breakpoint=bool(saved.breakpoint),
        instruction_bytes=saved.instruction_bytes,
        enabled=saved.enabled,
        caller_depth=saved.caller_depth,
        callers=persistable_callers(saved.callers),
        pointer=None if saved.pointer is None else PointerChain.from_json(saved.pointer),
        label=saved.label,
    )


def method_spec_from_saved(saved):
    """Build the MethodHookSpec that reinstalls a saved method hook."""
    return MethodHookSpec(saved.managed, hook_transform(saved, kind="method"),
                          enabled=saved.enabled, label=saved.label,
                          phase=saved.phase or "after")

```

`grembyte/hooks/syntax.py`:

```py
"""Syntax check of hook scripts in Frida's JavaScript engine, without a game.

Hook code runs in Frida's engine inside the game. Qt's engine (see
grembyte.hooks.sandbox) knows less of modern JavaScript (object spread, class
fields, BigInt, async) and would reject code that runs fine there, so the
check uses Frida's: a script in Frida's system session, which needs no
target process, compiles the code without running it.

Two kinds of code are checked the way the hooks compile them:

``FUNCTION``
    A template's source, a function expression (``compileTransform`` in
    grembyte/hooks/engine.js: ``eval('(' + source + '\\n)')``).
``BODY``
    A ``code`` parameter, run as ``new Function('ctx', code)`` (see the
    "method_script" example in grembyte.hooks.transforms).

Only syntax is checked; whether the code works shows when it runs. Without
Frida's system session nothing is checked (``check`` returns None).
"""

import atexit
import re
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass

import frida

from grembyte.core import logs
from grembyte.attach.frida_attach import CLEANUP_ERRORS, FRIDA_ERRORS

FUNCTION, BODY = "function", "body"

# Compiles only: new Function never runs the code it is given.
_AGENT_SOURCE = r"""
rpc.exports = {
  check(kind, code) {
    try {
      if (kind === 'function')
        new Function('return (' + code + '\n)');
      else
        new Function('ctx', code);
      return null;
    } catch (e) {
      // e.lineNumber is where new Function was called; the stack's first
      // frame is the place in the compiled code.
      const at = /at <input>:(\d+)/.exec(e.stack || '');
      return [e instanceof SyntaxError, e.message, at === null ? null : Number(at[1])];
    }
  }
};
"""

# The start of a function expression: function, async function, (a) =>, a =>
_FUNCTION_START = re.compile(r"(async\s+)?(function\b|\(|[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\s*=>)")
# Comments before it
_LEADING_COMMENTS = re.compile(r"\s*(//[^\n]*\n|/\*.*?\*/)*\s*", re.DOTALL)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SyntaxIssue:
    """A syntax error: the engine's message and the line in the checked code, if known."""

    message: str
    line: int = None


def looks_like_function(source):
    """Whether a template's source starts like a function expression.

    Only a hint: whether it really is one shows when the hook compiles it.
    """
    return _FUNCTION_START.match(source, _LEADING_COMMENTS.match(source).end()) is not None


class SyntaxChecker:
    """Check hook code in Frida's system session; see the module documentation.

    The session starts with the first check. Safe to use from several threads.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._session = None
        self._script = None
        self._failed = False
        # Lines the engine counts before the checked code, per kind
        self._offsets = {}

    @property
    def available(self):
        """Whether checks can run (the session started, or was not tried yet)."""
        return not self._failed

    def check(self, kind, code):
        """The SyntaxIssue of ``code`` (``FUNCTION`` or ``BODY``), else None.

        None too when the check cannot run.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if not self._start():
                return None
            try:
                answer = self._script.exports_sync.check(kind, code)
            except FRIDA_ERRORS + (frida.RPCException,) as error:
                logs.log.warning("syntax check failed: %s", error)
                return None
        if answer is None:
            return None
        _syntax, message, line = answer
        if line is not None:
            # A missing end shows on the line the check appends: the last one.
            line = min(max(1, line - self._offsets.get(kind, 0)), code.count("\n") + 1)
        return SyntaxIssue(message, line)

    def _start(self):
        if self._script is not None:
            return True
        if self._failed:
            return False
        try:
            session = frida.attach(0)
            script = session.create_script(_AGENT_SOURCE)
            script.load()
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (frida.RPCException, OSError) as error:
            logs.log.warning("syntax check unavailable: %s", error)
            self._failed = True
            return False
        self._session, self._script = session, script
        # A syntax error on the first line tells how many lines come before.
        for kind in (FUNCTION, BODY):
            answer = script.exports_sync.check(kind, "@")
            line = answer[2] if answer is not None else None
            self._offsets[kind] = line - 1 if line is not None else 0
        return True

    def close(self):
        with self._lock:
            script, session = self._script, self._session
            self._script = self._session = None
        for close in (script and script.unload, session and session.detach):
            if close:
                try:
                    close()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)


_checker = None
_checker_lock = threading.Lock()


def checker():
    """The SyntaxChecker the program shares."""
    global _checker  # pylint: disable=global-statement
    with _checker_lock:
        if _checker is None:
            _checker = SyntaxChecker()
            atexit.register(_checker.close)
        return _checker


def check_function(source):
    """The SyntaxIssue of a template's source (a function expression), else None."""
    return checker().check(FUNCTION, source)


def check_body(code):
    """The SyntaxIssue of a ``code`` parameter (a function body), else None."""
    return checker().check(BODY, code)

```

`grembyte/hooks/transforms.py`:

```py
"""Value transforms applied by write hooks inside the target process.

A transform is a JavaScript function expression that runs in the Frida agent
right after the hooked instruction has written the target value. It receives
a single ``ctx`` object and returns the value to store, or ``undefined`` /
``null`` to keep the value the game wrote:

    ctx.old        value before the write
    ctx.new        value the game just wrote
    ctx.delta      ctx.new - ctx.old
    ctx.params     the transform's JSON parameters (see ``ValueTransform.params``)
    ctx.state      per-hook object that persists between calls
    ctx.valueType  e.g. "int32", "uint8" or "float" (see grembyte.core.value_types)
    ctx.address    target address as hex string
    ctx.writePc    address of the hooked write instruction as hex string
    ctx.threadId   id of the writing thread
    ctx.hookId     id of the hook
    ctx.log(...)   output shown in the hook log and the debug window

Integer results are truncated and clamped to the value type's range; int64
and uint64 values are passed as JavaScript numbers and are only exact up to
2**53.

New transforms subclass ``ValueTransform``, set ``kind`` and ``source`` and
register themselves with ``@register_transform``. Declaring ``parameters``
lets the UI build an input form for the transform automatically; labels
fall back to ``title`` / the parameter name.
``ScriptTransform`` accepts an arbitrary function source for one-off
experiments.

Hook templates maintained in the database are ``TransformDefinition``
objects (name, function source, parameters); ``TemplateTransform`` applies
one with concrete parameter values. Their ``kind`` is ``"value"`` for the
write hooks described above or ``"method"`` for method hooks, whose function
gets another ``ctx`` (see ``grembyte.features.method_hooks``). A hook keeps its own copy of the
definition, so later template changes only reach it when they are adopted.
"""

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from grembyte.core.messages import LocalizedValueError


_TRANSFORMS = {}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TransformParameter:
    """Describes one constructor argument of a transform for UI forms.

    ``kind`` is ``"number"``, ``"choice"`` (one of ``choices``) or ``"code"``
    (multi-line text). ``optional`` parameters may be left empty (``None``).
    ``label`` and ``choice_labels`` (parallel to ``choices``) are display
    texts used by templates.
    """

    name: str
    kind: str = "number"
    default: object = None
    choices: tuple = ()
    optional: bool = False
    label: str = ""
    choice_labels: tuple = ()

    def choice_label(self, index):
        """Return the display text of ``choices[index]``."""
        if index < len(self.choice_labels) and self.choice_labels[index]:
            return self.choice_labels[index]
        return str(self.choices[index])

    def to_json(self):
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "label": self.label,
            "kind": self.kind,
            "default": self.default,
            "optional": self.optional,
            "choices": [
                [choice, self.choice_label(index)]
                for index, choice in enumerate(self.choices)
            ],
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data):
        choices = data.get("choices") or []
        return cls(
            name=data["name"],
            kind=data.get("kind", "number"),
            default=data.get("default"),
            choices=tuple(choice for choice, _label in choices),
            optional=bool(data.get("optional", False)),
            label=data.get("label", ""),
            choice_labels=tuple(label for _choice, label in choices),
        )


PARAMETER_NAME = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TransformDefinition:
    """A manipulation as maintained in a hook template or copied into a hook.

    Two definitions are equal when name, source and parameters match;
    ``description`` and ``template_id`` (the template it stems from) do not
    count.
    """

    name: str
    source: str
    parameters: tuple = ()
    description: str = field(default="", compare=False)
    template_id: int | None = field(default=None, compare=False)
    kind: str = "value"  # or "method"

    def parameters_json(self):
        return [parameter.to_json() for parameter in self.parameters]

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, name, source, parameters, description="", template_id=None,
                  kind="value"):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments
        return cls(
            name=name,
            source=source,
            parameters=tuple(TransformParameter.from_json(p) for p in parameters or []),
            description=description or "",
            template_id=template_id,
            kind=kind or "value",
        )


def register_transform(cls):
    """Class decorator that makes a transform available via ``create_transform``."""
    if not cls.kind:
        raise ValueError(f"{cls.__name__} must define a non-empty kind")
    if cls.kind in _TRANSFORMS:
        raise ValueError(f"Transform kind already registered: {cls.kind}")
    _TRANSFORMS[cls.kind] = cls
    return cls


def available_transforms():
    """Return the registered transform classes keyed by kind."""
    return dict(_TRANSFORMS)


def create_transform(kind, **params):
    """Instantiate a registered transform by its kind."""
    try:
        cls = _TRANSFORMS[kind]
    except KeyError as error:
        raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.unknown_kind", kind=kind) from error
    return cls(**params)


def _require_number(name, value):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.not_number", name=name, value=repr(value))
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.not_finite", name=name, value=repr(value))
    return value


class ValueTransform:
    """Base class for a value manipulation executed by the hook agent."""

    kind = ""
    title = ""
    source = ""
    parameters = ()

    def __init__(self, **params):
        self.params = self.validate(params)

    def form_values(self):
        """Return the constructor arguments, e.g. to pre-fill an edit form."""
        return dict(self.params)

    def validate(self, params):
        """Check and normalize the parameters; return the dict sent to the agent."""
        return params

    def to_agent(self):
        return {
            "kind": self.kind,
            "source": self.source,
            "params": self.params,
            "native": native_spec(self.source, self.params),
        }

    def describe(self):
        details = ", ".join(
            f"{key}={value}" for key, value in self.params.items() if value is not None
        )
        return f"{self.kind}({details})"

    def __repr__(self):
```
