`tests/test_former_name.py`:

```py
"""Tests for taking over the files of Hermes Hook, Grembyte's former name."""

from PySide6.QtCore import QSettings  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core.former_name import adopt_folders, adopt_settings


def _old_tree(base):
    old = base / "hermes-hook"
    (old / "gadget").mkdir(parents=True)
    (old / "gadget" / "frida-gadget.dll").write_bytes(b"dll")
    (old / "hermes.db").write_bytes(b"db")
    (old / "hermes.log").write_text("log", encoding="utf-8")
    (old / "hermes.log.1").write_text("older", encoding="utf-8")
    (old / "themes").mkdir()
    (old / "themes" / "hermes_themes_Mine.json").write_text("{}", encoding="utf-8")
    return old


def test_the_old_folder_moves_and_its_files_get_new_names(tmp_path):
    old = _old_tree(tmp_path)
    moved = adopt_folders([tmp_path])
    new = tmp_path / "grembyte"
    assert not old.exists()
    assert (new / "grembyte.db").read_bytes() == b"db"
    assert (new / "grembyte.log").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "log"
    assert (new / "grembyte.log.1").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "older"
    assert (new / "gadget" / "frida-gadget.dll").read_bytes() == b"dll"
    assert (new / "themes" / "grembyte_themes_Mine.json").is_file()
    assert (old, new) in moved
    # Nothing left to do on the next start.
    assert adopt_folders([tmp_path]) == []


def test_what_exists_under_the_new_name_is_kept(tmp_path):
    _old_tree(tmp_path)
    new = tmp_path / "grembyte"
    new.mkdir()
    (new / "grembyte.db").write_bytes(b"new")
    adopt_folders([tmp_path])
    assert (new / "grembyte.db").read_bytes() == b"new"
    # The old database moved along but kept its name, so nothing is lost.
    assert (new / "hermes.db").read_bytes() == b"db"
    assert (new / "gadget" / "frida-gadget.dll").is_file()
    assert not (tmp_path / "hermes-hook").exists()


def test_without_an_old_folder_nothing_happens(tmp_path):
    assert adopt_folders([tmp_path]) == []
    assert not (tmp_path / "grembyte").exists()


def test_qt_settings_are_copied_only_into_empty_ones(tmp_path):
    def ini(name):
        return QSettings(str(tmp_path / name), QSettings.Format.IniFormat)

    old, new = ini("old.ini"), ini("new.ini")
    old.setValue("ui_theme", "Github-Light")
    old.setValue("windows/MainWindow/geometry", "abc")
    old.sync()
    assert adopt_settings(old, new)
    assert new.value("ui_theme") == "Github-Light"
    assert new.value("windows/MainWindow/geometry") == "abc"
    old.setValue("ui_theme", "Solarized-Dark")
    assert not adopt_settings(old, new)
    assert new.value("ui_theme") == "Github-Light"
```

`tests/test_freeze.py`:

```py
"""Tests for writing frozen address-list values back to a process."""

import shutil
import subprocess
import time

import pytest

from grembyte.features import freeze
from grembyte.features.freeze import FreezeWorker, FrozenValue
from grembyte.core.pointer import PointerChain
from grembyte.core.value_types import value_type


class FakeMemory:
    """Seekable, writable memory image addressed by virtual address."""

    def __init__(self, base_address, size, pointers=None):
        self.base_address = base_address
        self.contents = bytearray(size)
        self.position = 0
        self.pointers = pointers or {}

    def write(self, address, data):
        if address < self.base_address:
            raise OSError("bad address")
        offset = address - self.base_address
        self.contents[offset:offset + len(data)] = data

    def read_pointer(self, address, _size=8):
        return self.pointers.get(address)

    def read(self, address, size):
        offset = address - self.base_address
        return bytes(self.contents[offset:offset + size])


def test_write_once_writes_fixed_and_pointer_entries(monkeypatch):
    memory = FakeMemory(0x11000, 0x40, pointers={0x5000 + 0x10: 0x11020})
    monkeypatch.setattr(freeze, "read_mappings", lambda _pid: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(freeze, "chain_bases", lambda _pid, _mappings: {"game": 0x5000})
    worker = FreezeWorker(123)
    worker.set_entry(1, FrozenValue(value_type("int16").pack(-2), address=0x11004))
    worker.set_entry(2, FrozenValue(
        value_type("uint8").pack(200), pointer=PointerChain("game", 0x10, (0x8,)),
    ))

    worker.write_once(memory)

    assert memory.read(0x11004, 2) == value_type("int16").pack(-2)
    assert memory.read(0x11028, 1) == bytes([200])


def test_write_once_skips_unresolved_pointers_and_removed_entries(monkeypatch):
    memory = FakeMemory(0x1000, 0x10)
    monkeypatch.setattr(freeze, "read_mappings", lambda _pid: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(freeze, "chain_bases", lambda _pid, _mappings: {})
    worker = FreezeWorker(123)
    worker.set_entry(1, FrozenValue(b"\x01", pointer=PointerChain("game", 0x10, ())))
    worker.set_entry(2, FrozenValue(b"\x02", address=0x1000))
    worker.remove_entry(2)

    worker.write_once(memory)

    assert memory.contents == bytearray(0x10)


def test_failing_entry_is_reported_once():
    memory = FakeMemory(0x1000, 0x10)
    worker = FreezeWorker(123)
    messages = []
    worker.write_failed.connect(messages.append)
    worker.set_entry(1, FrozenValue(b"\x01", address=0x10))

    worker.write_once(memory)
    worker.write_once(memory)
    assert len(messages) == 1 and "0x10" in messages[0]

    # Changing the entry reports again.
    worker.set_entry(1, FrozenValue(b"\x02", address=0x10))
    worker.write_once(memory)
    assert len(messages) == 2


def test_run_reports_a_missing_process(monkeypatch):
    def fail(*_args, **_kwargs):
        raise FileNotFoundError("no such process")

    monkeypatch.setattr(freeze, "ProcessMemory", fail)
    worker = FreezeWorker(123)
    messages = []
    worker.write_failed.connect(messages.append)

    worker.run()

    assert messages == ["no such process"]


_TARGET_SOURCE = r"""
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>

volatile int32_t g_gold = 100;

int main(void) {
    int value;
    printf("%d %p\n", getpid(), (void *)&g_gold);
    fflush(stdout);
    while (scanf("%d", &value) == 1) {
        g_gold += value;
        printf("%d\n", g_gold);
        fflush(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("gcc") is None, reason="needs gcc")
def test_frozen_value_survives_writes_of_a_real_process(tmp_path):
    source = tmp_path / "target.c"
    source.write_text(_TARGET_SOURCE)
    binary = tmp_path / "target"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O2", str(source), "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    process = subprocess.Popen(
        [str(binary)], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True
    )
    worker = FreezeWorker(0)
    try:
        pid, address = process.stdout.readline().split()
        worker.pid = int(pid)
        worker.set_entry(1, FrozenValue(value_type("int32").pack(5000), address=int(address, 16)))
        worker.start()
        time.sleep(0.3)

        process.stdin.write("1\n")
        process.stdin.flush()
        # The frozen 5000 was in place when the game added 1.
        assert process.stdout.readline().strip() == "5001"
        time.sleep(0.3)
        with open(f"/proc/{pid}/mem", "rb", buffering=0) as memory:
            memory.seek(int(address, 16))
            assert value_type("int32").unpack(memory.read(4)) == 5000
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(2000)
        process.kill()
        process.wait()
```

`tests/test_frida_attach.py`:

```py
"""Grembyte refuses to attach next to another Frida host (frida_attach.py)."""

import subprocess
import sys
import time

import frida
import pytest

from grembyte.attach import frida_attach
from grembyte.core import messages
from grembyte.platform.linux import frida_agents
from tests.test_hooks import linux_only, requires_target

_MAPS = """\
55d0c0000000-55d0c0001000 r-xp 00000000 fd:01 1234 /usr/bin/game
7f0000000000-7f0000100000 r-xp 00000000 00:01 78589 /memfd:frida-agent-64.so (deleted)
7f0000100000-7f0000110000 rw-p 00100000 00:01 78589 /memfd:frida-agent-64.so (deleted)
7f0000200000-7f0000300000 r-xp 00000000 00:01 91191 /memfd:frida-agent-64.so (deleted)
7f0000400000-7f0000500000 r-xp 00000000 fd:01 4321 /opt/game/libfrida-gadget.so
7f0000600000-7f0000601000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0
"""

# Four threads call ``work`` all the time, as a game calls Mono's functions.
_TARGET_SOURCE = r"""
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
__attribute__((noinline)) int work(int x) { int s = 0; for (int i = 0; i < x; i++) s += i * x; return s; }
int (*volatile call)(int) = work;
static void *spin(void *arg) { (void)arg; for (;;) call(50); return 0; }
int main(void) {
    pthread_t threads[4];
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        pthread_create(&threads[i], 0, spin, 0);
    printf("%d\n", getpid());
    fflush(stdout);
    for (;;)
        pause();
}
"""


@linux_only
def test_each_frida_runtime_counts_once(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "42").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "42" / "maps").write_text(_MAPS)
    # Two injected agents (two memfds, one mapped twice) and a gadget
    assert frida_agents(42, proc_root=tmp_path) == {
        ("00:01", "78589"), ("00:01", "91191"), ("fd:01", "4321")}
    (tmp_path / "42" / "maps").write_text(_MAPS.splitlines()[0] + "\n")
    assert frida_agents(42, proc_root=tmp_path) == set()
    assert frida_agents(43, proc_root=tmp_path) is None


@pytest.fixture(name="busy_target")
def fixture_busy_target(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "busy.c").write_text(_TARGET_SOURCE)
    binary = tmp_path / "busy"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O1", "-pthread", str(tmp_path / "busy.c"), "-o", str(binary)],
                   check=True)
    with subprocess.Popen([str(binary)], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True) as process:
        pid = int(process.stdout.readline())
        yield pid
        process.kill()


def _until(condition, seconds=5.0):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        if condition():
            return True
        time.sleep(0.05)
    return False


@linux_only
@requires_target
def test_a_second_frida_host_is_refused_its_own_sessions_are_not(busy_target):
    pid = busy_target
    # Sessions of this process share its agent: a second one is fine
    first = frida_attach.attach_session(pid)
    second = frida_attach.attach_session(pid)
    assert len(frida_agents(pid)) == 1
    second.detach()
    first.detach()
    # Right after detaching, its agent may still be there
    frida_attach.attach_session(pid).detach()
    assert _until(lambda: not frida_agents(pid))
    # A session opened past attach_session shares the agent too
    raw = frida.attach(pid)
    frida_attach.attach_session(pid).detach()
    raw.detach()
    # Its agent unloaded, another host's arrives: not taken for its own
    assert _until(lambda: not frida_agents(pid))

    # Another host process attached (another grembyte, another Frida tool)
    other = subprocess.Popen(
        [sys.executable, "-c",
         f"import frida, sys; s = frida.attach({pid}); print('attached', flush=True); "
         "sys.stdin.readline(); s.detach()"],
        stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    try:
        assert other.stdout.readline().strip() == "attached"
        with pytest.raises(messages.LocalizedRuntimeError) as refused:
            frida_attach.attach_session(pid)
        assert refused.value.key == "error.attach.foreign_frida"
    finally:
        other.communicate("\n", timeout=10)
    # Once it has left (and this process' agent unloaded), attaching works again
    assert _until(lambda: not frida_agents(pid))
    frida_attach.attach_session(pid).detach()
```

```py
def _process_id(sessions, name, path):
    with sessions() as session:
        return session.scalars(
            select(Process.id).where(Process.name == name, Process.path == path)).one()


def _labels(sessions, model, process_id):
    with sessions() as session:
        return [record.label for record in session.scalars(
            select(model).where(model.process_id == process_id).order_by(model.id))]


def test_import_mixes_in_what_the_target_does_not_hold(sessions, repository):
    export = repository.export_game("DarkSoulsIII.ex", pointer_scans=True)
    # A third Proton version: a new process, as attaching saves it.
    with sessions() as session:
        target = Process(name="DarkSoulsIII.ex", path="/steam/Proton 12/wine64-preloader")
        session.add(target)
        session.commit()
        target_id = target.id

    result = repository.import_export(export, target_id)
    assert result.added == {"addresses": 1, "hooks": 1, "method_hooks": 0, "favorites": 0,
                            "scripts": 1, "notes": 0, "pointer_scans": 1}
    assert result.templates == 0  # "Begrenzen" exists with the same code
    with sessions() as session:
        [hook] = session.scalars(select(Hook).where(Hook.process_id == target_id))
        assert session.get(HookTemplate, hook.template_id).name == "Begrenzen"
        [address] = session.scalars(select(Address).where(Address.process_id == target_id))
        scan = session.scalars(
            select(PointerScan).where(PointerScan.address_id == address.id)).one()
        # Imported scans are kept packed like scanned ones.
        assert scan.chains == [] and scan.packed is not None
        assert scan.chain_list() == [
            {"module": "DarkSoulsIII.exe", "base_offset": 0, "offsets": [8]}]
        assert session.get(Process, target_id).path == "/steam/Proton 12/wine64-preloader"
        [script] = session.scalars(select(GameScript).where(GameScript.process_id == target_id))
        assert (script.label, script.mode, script.seconds, script.enabled) == (
            "Souls", "repeat", 2.5, False)

    again = repository.import_export(export, target_id)
    assert sum(again.added.values()) == 0
    assert again.skipped == {"addresses": 1, "hooks": 1, "method_hooks": 0, "favorites": 0,
                             "scripts": 1, "notes": 0}

    # Exports made before scripts were exported hold none.
    for process in export["processes"]:
        del process["scripts"]
    assert sum(repository.import_export(export, target_id).added.values()) == 0


def test_import_replaces_the_targets_entries(sessions, repository):
    poe = _process_id(sessions, "PillarsOfEternity", "/steam/common/PoE/PillarsOfEternity")
    export = repository.export_game("DarkSoulsIII.ex", pointer_scans=True)
    export["processes"][0]["addresses"][0]["label"] = "Souls (imported)"

    result = repository.import_export(export, poe, replace=True)
    assert result.added["addresses"] == 1 and result.added["pointer_scans"] == 1
    assert _labels(sessions, Address, poe) == ["Souls (imported)"]
    assert _labels(sessions, MethodHook, poe) == []
    with sessions() as session:
        assert not list(session.scalars(
            select(FavoriteRecord).where(FavoriteRecord.process_id == poe)))
    # Again: the pointer scan of the replaced address is gone as well.
    repository.import_export(export, poe, replace=True)
    assert _labels(sessions, Address, poe) == ["Souls (imported)"]
    with sessions() as session:
        assert len(list(session.scalars(select(PointerScan)))) == 2


def test_a_changed_template_is_added_under_a_new_name(sessions, repository):
    export = repository.export_game("DarkSoulsIII.ex")
    export["templates"][0]["source"] = "function (ctx) { return 1; }"
    target = _process_id(sessions, "PillarsOfEternity", "/steam/common/PoE/PillarsOfEternity")

    assert repository.import_export(export, target).templates == 1
    assert repository.import_export(export, target).templates == 0
    with sessions() as session:
        [hook] = session.scalars(select(Hook).where(Hook.process_id == target))
        assert session.get(HookTemplate, hook.template_id).name == "Begrenzen (Import)"


def _note_bodies(sessions, process_id):
    with sessions() as session:
        return [(note.title, note.body) for note in session.scalars(
            select(GameNote).where(GameNote.process_id == process_id).order_by(GameNote.id))]


def test_notes_are_exported_and_a_game_with_only_notes_counts(sessions, repository):
    empty = _process_id(sessions, "abrt-dbus", "/usr/sbin/abrt-dbus")
    with sessions() as session:
        session.add(GameNote(process_id=empty, body="## Gold\n`AddGold(int)`"))
        session.commit()
    games = {game.name: game for game in repository.list_games()}
    assert games["abrt-dbus"].counts["notes"] == 1
    [process] = repository.export_game("abrt-dbus")["processes"]
    assert [note["body"] for note in process["notes"]] == ["## Gold\n`AddGold(int)`"]
    assert repository.delete_entries(empty, ["notes"])["notes"] == 1
    assert _note_bodies(sessions, empty) == []


def test_empty_notes_do_not_count_or_export(sessions, repository):

    assert "abrt-dbus" not in {game.name for game in repository.list_games()}
    assert repository.export_game("abrt-dbus")["processes"] == []


def test_notes_count_and_export_alike_when_only_other_space_is_in_them(sessions, repository):

    empty = _process_id(sessions, "abrt-dbus", "/usr/sbin/abrt-dbus")

        session.add(GameNote(process_id=empty, body="\u00a0\f"))

    [exported] = repository.export_game("abrt-dbus")["processes"]
    assert process.counts["notes"] == len(exported["notes"]) == 1


def test_imported_notes_are_merged_and_never_deleted(sessions, repository):
    souls = _process_id(sessions, "DarkSoulsIII.ex", PROTON_GE)
    poe = _process_id(sessions, "PillarsOfEternity", "/steam/common/PoE/PillarsOfEternity")
    with sessions() as session:
        session.add_all([GameNote(process_id=souls, body="Souls: `PlayerGameData`"),
                         GameNote(process_id=poe, body="Gold: `AddGold`")])
        session.commit()
    export = repository.export_game("DarkSoulsIII.ex")
    assert export["processes"][0]["notes"][0]["body"] == "Souls: `PlayerGameData`"

    result = repository.import_export(export, poe, replace=True)
    assert result.added["notes"] == 1
    assert _note_bodies(sessions, poe) == [
        ("", "Gold: `AddGold`\n\n---\n\nSouls: `PlayerGameData`")]
    # Text the note holds already is not appended again
    result = repository.import_export(export, poe)
    assert result.added["notes"] == 0 and result.skipped["notes"] == 1
    assert len(_note_bodies(sessions, poe)) == 1

    # A process without notes takes them as they are; an older export has none
    empty = _process_id(sessions, "abrt-dbus", "/usr/sbin/abrt-dbus")
    repository.import_export(export, empty)
    assert _note_bodies(sessions, empty) == [("", "Souls: `PlayerGameData`")]
    for process in export["processes"]:
        del process["notes"]
    assert repository.import_export(export, empty).added["notes"] == 0
```

```py
def test_merged_text_appends_only_what_is_new():
    assert merged_text("", "Gold") == "Gold"
    assert merged_text("Gold\n", "XP") == "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP"
    assert merged_text("Gold\n\n---\n\nXP", "XP") is None
    assert merged_text("Gold and XP", "XP") == "Gold and XP\n\n---\n\nXP"
    assert merged_text("Gold", "  \n") is None


def test_merged_text_keeps_rules_and_adds_only_new_sections():
    # A rule the user wrote looks like the separator: re-importing adds nothing
    note = "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP"
    assert merged_text(note, note) is None
    assert merged_text(note, "XP\n\n---\n\nGold\n") is None
    # A note merged on another computer brings back only what is new there
    assert merged_text("Gold", "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP") == "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP"
    assert merged_text("Gold\n\n---\n\nXP", "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP\n\n---\n\nItems") == (
        "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP\n\n---\n\nItems")
    assert merged_text("Gold", "XP\n\n---\n\nXP") == "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP"


def test_notes_synced_back_and_forth_do_not_grow(sessions, repository):
    souls = _process_id(sessions, "DarkSoulsIII.ex", PROTON_GE)
    other = _process_id(sessions, "abrt-dbus", "/usr/sbin/abrt-dbus")
    notes = NoteRepository(sessions)
    notes.save_first_note(souls, "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP")
    repository.import_export(repository.export_game("DarkSoulsIII.ex"), other)
    notes.save_first_note(other, notes.first_note(other).body + "\n\n---\n\nItems")
    for _round in range(2):
        repository.import_export(repository.export_game("abrt-dbus"), souls)
        repository.import_export(repository.export_game("DarkSoulsIII.ex"), other)
    expected = "Gold\n\n---\n\nXP\n\n---\n\nItems"
    assert _note_bodies(sessions, souls) == [("", expected)]
    assert _note_bodies(sessions, other) == [("", expected)]

                                                                  repository):

class _FailingRepository(NoteRepository):
    """Notes that can be read but not saved (a locked database)."""

    def save_first_note(self, process_id, body):
        # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
        from sqlalchemy.exc import OperationalError

        raise OperationalError("UPDATE", {}, Exception("database is locked"))


def test_notes_that_cannot_be_saved_are_not_dropped_without_asking(
        qt_app, translations, sessions, repository, monkeypatch):
    # pylint: disable=unused-argument,import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.game_notes import GameNotesDialog

    poe = _process_id(sessions, "PillarsOfEternity", POE)
    souls = _process_id(sessions, "DarkSoulsIII.ex", PROTON_GE)
    dialog = GameNotesDialog(translations, poe, "PillarsOfEternity",
                             repository=_FailingRepository(sessions))
    asked = []
    answer = [False]

    def confirm_discard(error):
        asked.append(str(error))
        return answer[0]

    monkeypatch.setattr(dialog, "confirm_discard", confirm_discard)
    try:
        dialog.show()
        dialog.editor.setPlainText("Gold")
        # Cancel: the dialog stays with its text, on its game
        assert not dialog.close()
        assert dialog.isVisible() and dialog.text() == "Gold" and dialog.dirty
        dialog.reject()
        assert dialog.isVisible()
        assert not dialog.set_process(souls, "DarkSoulsIII.ex")
        assert dialog.process_id == poe and dialog.text() == "Gold"
        assert len(asked) == 3 and "locked" in asked[0]
        assert "locked" in dialog.status.text()
        # Discard: it goes
        answer[0] = True
        assert dialog.set_process(souls, "DarkSoulsIII.ex")
        assert dialog.process_id == souls and dialog.text() == ""
        dialog.editor.setPlainText("Souls")
        assert dialog.close()
        assert len(asked) == 5
    finally:
        answer[0] = True
        dialog.close()

def test_notes_preview_is_formatted_in_the_theme_colors(qt_app, translations, sessions,
                                                         repository):
    # pylint: disable=unused-argument,import-outside-toplevel
    from PySide6.QtGui import QTextCharFormat  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

    from grembyte.ui.styles.themes import ThemeManager
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.code_editor import apply_code_theme

    manager = ThemeManager(user_theme_dir="/tmp/no-grembyte-themes")
    colors = manager.load_theme("Solarized-Light")["colors"]
    poe = _process_id(sessions, "PillarsOfEternity", POE)
    dialog = _dialog(translations, sessions, poe)
    try:
        dialog.editor.setPlainText(
            "## Gold\n- call `AddGold` in [the wiki](https://example.com)\n\n"
            "```js\nconst gold = 42;\n```\n\n| A | B |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n")
        dialog.tabs.setCurrentIndex(1)
        apply_code_theme(colors)
        document = dialog.preview.document()

        def format_at(token):
            cursor = document.find(token)
            cursor.setPosition(cursor.selectionStart() + 1)
            return QTextCharFormat(cursor.charFormat())

        assert format_at("Gold").foreground().color().name() == colors["code_keyword"]
        assert format_at("AddGold").foreground().color().name() == colors["code_string"]
        assert format_at("AddGold").background().color().name() == colors["surface"]
        assert format_at("the wiki").foreground().color().name() == colors["accent"]
        assert format_at("const").foreground().color().name() == colors["code_keyword"]
        assert format_at("42").foreground().color().name() == colors["code_number"]
        code_frame = document.find("const").currentFrame()
        assert code_frame.frameFormat().background().color().name() == colors["surface"]
        assert dialog.preview.toPlainText().count("`") == 0
    finally:
        apply_code_theme(manager.load_theme("Github-Dark")["colors"])
        dialog.close()


def test_fenced_code_lines_count_each_block():
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.markdown_preview import fenced_code_lines

    assert fenced_code_lines("```js\na\n```\n\n```js\nb\nc\n```\n") == [1, 2]
    assert fenced_code_lines("```\n```\n> ```c\n> int x;\n> ```\n- item\n\n  ~~~\n  a\n\n  ~~~\n") == [
```

`tests/test_garbage.py`:

```py
"""Garbage is collected in the GUI thread only (see grembyte.ui.garbage)."""

import gc
import threading
import weakref

from grembyte.ui.garbage import GarbageCollector
from tests.test_hooks import fixture_qt_app  # pylint: disable=unused-import


class _Cycle:  # pylint: disable=too-few-public-methods
    """Refers to itself; tells in which thread it was freed."""

    freed_in = []

    def __init__(self):
        self.me = self

    def __del__(self):
        self.freed_in.append(threading.current_thread())


def test_cycles_are_freed_in_the_gui_thread(qt_app):
    was_enabled = gc.isenabled()
    collector = GarbageCollector(qt_app)
    collector.start()
    try:
        assert not gc.isenabled()

        def leave_garbage():
            alive.append(weakref.ref(_Cycle()))
            # Far over the threshold: Python itself would collect in this thread
            kept.extend([] for _ in range(3 * gc.get_threshold()[0]))

        alive, kept = [], []
        worker = threading.Thread(target=leave_garbage)
        worker.start()
        worker.join()
        assert alive[0]() is not None

        filler = [[] for _ in range(gc.get_threshold()[0] + 1)]
        collector.check()
        assert alive[0]() is None
        assert _Cycle.freed_in == [threading.main_thread()]
        del filler
    finally:
        collector.stop()
    assert gc.isenabled() == was_enabled
```

`tests/test_hermesquest.py`:

```py
"""Grembyte against a build of HermesQuest (test_app/unity), the real Unity Mono runtime.

The build is not in the repository (see test_app/unity/README.md); without
it, or with one older than what a test needs, the tests are skipped. The
game runs without a window (``-batchmode -nographics``).
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from tests.test_hooks import _wait_for, fixture_qt_app  # pylint: disable=unused-import

_BUILD = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "test_app" / "unity" / "Build"
_GAME = (_BUILD / "Windows" / "HermesQuest.exe" if sys.platform == "win32"
         else _BUILD / "Linux" / "HermesQuest.x86_64")

requires_build = pytest.mark.skipif(not _GAME.exists(), reason=f"no HermesQuest build at {_GAME}")

# The token and Mono's name of a method once Assembly-CSharp is loaded, null
# while it is not, 'missing' if the class or method is.
_FIND_METHOD = r"""
let mono;
const f = (name, ret, args) => new NativeFunction(mono.getExportByName(name), ret, args);
rpc.exports = {
  find(namespace, className, name, params) {
    // Unity loads Mono a moment after the start
    mono = Process.enumerateModules().find(m => m.findExportByName('mono_get_root_domain') !== null);
    if (mono === undefined)
      return null;
    const image = f('mono_image_loaded', 'pointer', ['pointer'])(Memory.allocUtf8String('Assembly-CSharp'));
    if (image.isNull())
      return null;
    const thread = f('mono_thread_attach', 'pointer', ['pointer'])(f('mono_get_root_domain', 'pointer', [])());
    try {
      const klass = f('mono_class_from_name', 'pointer', ['pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer'])(
        image, Memory.allocUtf8String(namespace), Memory.allocUtf8String(className));
      if (klass.isNull())
        return 'missing';
      const method = f('mono_class_get_method_from_name', 'pointer', ['pointer', 'pointer', 'int'])(
        klass, Memory.allocUtf8String(name), params);
      if (method.isNull())
        return 'missing';
      return [f('mono_method_get_token', 'uint32', ['pointer'])(method),
              f('mono_method_full_name', 'pointer', ['pointer', 'int'])(method, 1).readUtf8String()];
    } finally {
      f('mono_thread_detach', 'void', ['pointer'])(thread);
    }
  }
};
"""


class _Game:
    def __init__(self, log):
        self.log = log
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(  # pylint: disable=consider-using-with
            [str(_GAME), "-batchmode", "-nographics", "-logFile", str(log), "-seed", "1"])
        self.pid = self.process.pid
        # Attaching right after the start can kill the game: on Linux Frida's
        # thread then comes before glibc set its default stack size
        # ("allocate_stack: assertion failed: size != 0", signal 6). Unity
        # writes its log once the player runs, the process is set up by then.
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 30
        while not (log.exists() and log.stat().st_size) and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if not self.alive():
                raise AssertionError(f"HermesQuest ended at the start ({self.process.returncode})")
            time.sleep(0.1)

    def identity(self, namespace, class_name, name, params):
        """The identity of a method of Assembly-CSharp; skips if the build lacks it."""
        import frida  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

        session = frida.attach(self.pid)
        try:
            script = session.create_script(_FIND_METHOD)
            script.load()
            deadline = time.monotonic() + 30
            found = None
            while found is None and time.monotonic() < deadline:
                found = script.exports_sync.find(namespace, class_name, name, params)
                time.sleep(0.2)
            script.unload()
        finally:
            session.detach()
        if found is None:
            raise AssertionError("HermesQuest did not load Assembly-CSharp")
        if found == "missing":
            pytest.skip(f"the HermesQuest build has no {namespace}.{class_name}:{name}; rebuild it")
        token, method = found
        return {"image": "Assembly-CSharp", "file": None, "token": token, "method": method}

    def alive(self):
        return self.process.poll() is None

    def close(self):
        self.process.kill()
        self.process.wait()


@requires_build
@pytest.mark.parametrize("returns", [False, True])
def test_monitor_leaves_exceptions_thrown_through_the_method_to_the_game(tmp_path, qt_app, returns):
    # Rumors.Tick catches what Rumors.Parse throws for a garbled line, every
    # second or two. A hook that put its own return address on the stack (as
    # Frida's onEnter and onLeave do) hid Tick from Mono's unwinder: the
    # exception went unhandled and Unity ended the game.
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.monitor import MethodMonitorWorker

    game = _Game(tmp_path / "Player.log")
    worker = MethodMonitorWorker(game.pid)
    added, failed, calls = {}, {}, []
    worker.monitor_added.connect(added.__setitem__)
    worker.monitor_failed.connect(failed.__setitem__)
    worker.calls.connect(lambda events, _dropped, _counts: calls.extend(events))
    try:
        identity = game.identity("HermesQuest", "Rumors", "Parse", 1)
        worker.start()
        monitor_id = worker.add_monitor(identity, returns=returns)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: monitor_id in added or monitor_id in failed, timeout=30)
        assert not failed
        assert added[monitor_id]["viaStack"] is False

        # Five rumors, two of them garbled; then another round
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: len(calls) >= (6 if returns else 10) or not game.alive(),
                  timeout=30)
        assert game.alive()
        lines = [call["args"][0]["text"] for call in calls]
        if returns:
            # A call that threw has no result and is not shown.
            assert {call["result"]["text"] for call in calls} == {"3", "1", "12"}
            assert not any(line.startswith(('"seven', '"?')) for line in lines)
        else:
            assert any(line.startswith('"seven:') for line in lines)
            assert any(line.startswith('"?:') for line in lines)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        game.close()
    log = game.log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    assert "UnhandledExceptionEventArgs" not in log
```

`tests/test_hook_callers.py`:

```py
"""Caller learning of hooks: stale return addresses on the stack are not callers."""

import subprocess

from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookSpec
from grembyte.hooks.transforms import MultiplyTransform

from tests.test_hooks import (  # pylint: disable=unused-import
    _Target,
    _trap_pcs,
    _wait_for,
    fixture_qt_app,
    requires_target,
)


# Like a game without frame pointers: noise() descends deep into libc and
# warmup() calls add_gold() one level deeper; then add_gold() runs at the
# same stack depth with a large uninitialised local, which still holds
# libc's return addresses and warmup's return from add_gold() when it writes
# the gold. Only earn() called it.
_TARGET_SOURCE = r"""
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

typedef struct { int32_t gold; int32_t hp; } Character;
Character g_player = { 100, 50 };
Character g_enemy = { 999, 80 };
Character g_dummy = { 0, 0 };
volatile int g_events;
volatile char g_sink;

__attribute__((noinline)) void noise(int value) {
    char text[96];
    snprintf(text, sizeof text, "%d %f %s %x", value, value * 1.5, "noise", value);
    g_sink = text[0];
}

__attribute__((noinline)) void add_gold(Character *c, int32_t amount) {
    volatile char scratch[3000];  /* more than the slots scanned (2 KB) */
    scratch[0] = 1;
    c->gold += amount;
    g_sink = scratch[0];
}

__attribute__((noinline)) void warmup(void) {
    volatile char pad[256];
    pad[0] = 0;
    add_gold(&g_dummy, pad[0]);
    g_events++;  /* a call, not a jump */
}

__attribute__((noinline)) void remove_gold(int32_t amount) { g_player.gold -= amount; }
__attribute__((noinline)) void earn(int32_t amount) {
    noise(amount);
    warmup();
    add_gold(&g_player, amount);
    g_events++;
}

int main(void) {
    char cmd[16];
    int value;
    printf("%d %p\n", getpid(), (void *)&g_player.gold);
    fflush(stdout);
    while (scanf("%15s %d", cmd, &value) == 2) {
        if (strcmp(cmd, "add") == 0) earn(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "sub") == 0) remove_gold(value);
        printf("%d %d\n", g_player.gold, g_enemy.gold);
        fflush(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


def _build(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "target.c").write_text(_TARGET_SOURCE)
    binary = tmp_path / "target"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O2", "-fomit-frame-pointer", "-fPIE", "-pie",
                    str(tmp_path / "target.c"), "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    return binary


def _symbol_offset(binary, name):
    listing = subprocess.run(["nm", str(binary)], check=True, capture_output=True,
                             text=True).stdout
    return next(int(line.split()[0], 16) for line in listing.splitlines()
                if line.split()[-1] == name)


@requires_target
def test_stale_return_addresses_are_not_learned_and_old_ones_dropped(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,too-many-locals
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker

    binary = _build(tmp_path)
    earn = _symbol_offset(binary, "earn")
    target = _Target(binary)
    worker = HookWorker(target.pid)
    installed, learned, dropped, failed, ambiguous = {}, {}, {}, {}, []
    worker.hook_installed.connect(installed.__setitem__)
    worker.callers_learned.connect(learned.__setitem__)
    worker.callers_dropped.connect(dropped.__setitem__)
    worker.hook_failed.connect(failed.__setitem__)
    worker.callers_ambiguous.connect(ambiguous.append)
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        worker.start()
        first = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2),
                                         trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"], caller_depth=1))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: first in installed or failed)
        assert not failed
        assert target.send("add", 5) == (110, 999)  # 100 + 5 * 2
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: first in learned)
        # The caller is earn(), right after its call of add_gold(): not libc,
        # and not warmup(), whose call of add_gold() returned before.
        [[(module, offset)]] = learned[first]
        assert module == "target"
        assert earn < offset < earn + 0x40
        assert not ambiguous

        # Restored after a restart, with a stale frame learned before the check
        site = installed[first]["writeInstruction"]
        worker.remove_hook(first)
        libc = next(name for name in _modules(target.pid) if name.startswith("libc.so"))
        second = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
            None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), module=site["module"],
            module_offset=int(site["moduleOffset"], 16), caller_depth=1,
            callers=[[(module, offset)], [(libc, 0x401d3)]]))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: second in installed or failed)
        assert not failed
        assert dropped[second] == 1
        assert learned[second] == [[[module, offset]]]
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (112, 999)  # the real caller still applies
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


def _modules(pid):
    with open(f"/proc/{pid}/maps", encoding="utf-8") as maps:
        return {line.split()[-1].rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for line in maps if "/" in line}

```

`tests/test_hooks.py`:

```py
"""Tests for value transforms, Frida write hooks and the hook UI."""

import os
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from grembyte.core.pointer import PointerChain

from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookSpec, build_agent_source
from grembyte.hooks.transforms import (
    ClampTransform,
    FreezeTransform,
    MultiplyTransform,
    ScriptTransform,
    TemplateTransform,
    TransformDefinition,
    TransformParameter,
    ValueTransform,
    available_transforms,
    create_transform,
    native_spec,
    register_transform,
)


def test_builtin_transforms_are_registered():
    assert {"multiply", "freeze", "clamp", "script"} <= set(available_transforms())


def test_create_transform_by_kind():
    transform = create_transform("multiply", factor=10)

    assert isinstance(transform, MultiplyTransform)
    assert transform.to_agent()["params"] == {"factor": 10, "direction": "increase"}
    assert "function" in transform.to_agent()["source"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("factory", "message"),
    [
        (lambda: MultiplyTransform("x"), "factor must be a number"),
        (lambda: MultiplyTransform(2, direction="up"), "direction must be one of"),
        (lambda: FreezeTransform(float("nan")), "value must be finite"),
        (lambda: ClampTransform(), "needs a minimum"),
        (lambda: ClampTransform(minimum=5, maximum=1), "must not be greater"),
        (lambda: ScriptTransform("  "), "needs a function source"),
        (lambda: create_transform("teleport"), "Unknown transform kind"),
    ],
)
def test_transform_validation(factory, message):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=message):
        factory()


def test_custom_transforms_can_be_registered():
    @register_transform
    class _Double(ValueTransform):
        kind = "test-double"
        source = "ctx => ctx.new * 2"

    try:
        assert isinstance(create_transform("test-double"), _Double)
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="already registered"):
            register_transform(_Double)
    finally:
        from grembyte.hooks import transforms  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
        del transforms._TRANSFORMS["test-double"]  # pylint: disable=protected-access


def test_builtin_manipulations_are_run_natively():
    assert MultiplyTransform(10).to_agent()["native"] == {
        "op": "multiply", "factor": 10.0, "direction": "increase"}
    assert FreezeTransform(5).to_agent()["native"] == {"op": "freeze", "value": 5.0}
    assert ClampTransform(maximum=7).to_agent()["native"] == {
        "op": "clamp", "minimum": None, "maximum": 7.0}
    # A copy in a template (or an import) counts by its code, not its name.
    copy = TransformDefinition("Clamp (Import)", ClampTransform.source.strip(),
                               ClampTransform.parameters)
    assert TemplateTransform(copy, minimum=350, maximum=407).to_agent()["native"] == {
        "op": "clamp", "minimum": 350.0, "maximum": 407.0}
    assert ScriptTransform("ctx => ctx.new + 1").to_agent()["native"] is None
    changed = ClampTransform.source.replace("value = maximum;", "value = maximum - 1;")
    assert native_spec(changed, {"minimum": None, "maximum": 7}) is None


def test_hook_spec_requires_a_code_location():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="needs a trap_pc, a write_pc, a module, a method or a"):
        HookSpec(0x1000, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2))
    managed = {"image": "Assembly-CSharp", "file": "/x.dll", "token": 0x6000001,
               "method": "Gold:Add (int)", "offset": 0x1a}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="method location needs the instruction bytes"):
        HookSpec(None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), managed=managed)
    spec = HookSpec(None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), managed=managed, instruction_bytes="0137")
    assert not spec.training and spec.to_agent(1)["managed"] == managed
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="training needs a pointer"):
        HookSpec(None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), signature={"before": "", "after": ""},
                 instruction_bytes="0137")
    chain = PointerChain("game", 0x10, (0x8,))
    spec = HookSpec(None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), signature={"before": "", "after": ""},
                    instruction_bytes="0137", pointer=chain)
    assert spec.training and spec.to_agent(1)["signature"] == {"before": "", "after": ""}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="given together"):
        HookSpec(None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), module="game")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="only be resolved with an address"):
        HookSpec(None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), trap_pc=0x401006)


def test_hook_spec_validates_callers():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="caller_depth must be between"):
        HookSpec(0x1000, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), write_pc=0x401000, caller_depth=5)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="needs caller_depth frames"):
        HookSpec(0x1000, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), write_pc=0x401000,
                 caller_depth=2, callers=[[("game", 0x10)]])

    payload = HookSpec(
        None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(2), module="game", module_offset=0x10,
        callers=[[("game", 0x20)]],
    ).to_agent(1)

    assert (payload["callerDepth"], payload["callers"]) == (1, [[["game", 0x20]]])


def test_hook_spec_serializes_module_location():
    spec = HookSpec(
        None, "int32", FreezeTransform(5),
        module="game", module_offset=0x1139, instruction_bytes="0137", enabled=False,
    )

    payload = spec.to_agent(3)

    assert payload["address"] is None
    assert (payload["module"], payload["moduleOffset"]) == ("game", 0x1139)
    assert payload["instructionBytes"] == "0137"
    assert payload["enabled"] is False


def test_hook_spec_serializes_for_agent():
    spec = HookSpec(0x1000, "int32", FreezeTransform(5), trap_pc=0x401006)

    payload = spec.to_agent(7)

    assert payload["id"] == 7
    assert payload["address"] == "0x1000"
    assert payload["trapPc"] == "0x401006"
    assert payload["writePc"] is None
    assert payload["transform"]["kind"] == "freeze"


def test_agent_exports_hook_management():
    source = build_agent_source()

    for name in ("addHook", "removeHook", "setTransform", "setEnabled", "dispose"):
        assert name in source


# --- integration: real process, real hooks --------------------------------

_TARGET_SOURCE = r"""
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

typedef struct { int32_t gold; int32_t hp; } Character;
Character g_player = { 100, 50 };
Character g_enemy = { 999, 80 };
volatile int g_events;

__attribute__((noinline)) void add_gold(Character *c, int32_t amount) { c->gold += amount; }
__attribute__((noinline)) void remove_gold(int32_t amount) { g_player.gold -= amount; }
/* Shared helper with two callers; g_events keeps the calls from becoming jumps. */
__attribute__((noinline)) void give(Character *c, int32_t amount) { add_gold(c, amount); g_events++; }
__attribute__((noinline)) void loot(int32_t amount) { give(&g_player, amount); g_events++; }
__attribute__((noinline)) void bounty(int32_t amount) { give(&g_enemy, amount); g_events++; }

int main(void) {
    char cmd[16];
    int value;
    printf("%d %p\n", getpid(), (void *)&g_player.gold);
    fflush(stdout);
    while (scanf("%15s %d", cmd, &value) == 2) {
        if (strcmp(cmd, "add") == 0) add_gold(&g_player, value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "enemy") == 0) add_gold(&g_enemy, value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "sub") == 0) remove_gold(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "loot") == 0) loot(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "bounty") == 0) bounty(value);
        printf("%d %d\n", g_player.gold, g_enemy.gold);
        fflush(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


def _ptrace_allowed():
    try:
        return Path("/proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope").read_text().strip() == "0"
    except OSError:
        return True


requires_target = pytest.mark.skipif(
    shutil.which("gcc") is None or not _ptrace_allowed(),
    reason="needs gcc and ptrace_scope=0 to attach to a test process",
)

linux_only = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not sys.platform.startswith("linux"), reason="tests Linux behaviour (/proc, files in use)",
)


class _Target:
    def __init__(self, binary):
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [str(binary)], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True
        )
        pid, address = self.process.stdout.readline().split()
        self.pid = int(pid)
        self.address = int(address, 16)

    def send(self, command, value):
        self.process.stdin.write(f"{command} {value}\n")
        self.process.stdin.flush()
        gold, enemy = self.process.stdout.readline().split()
        return int(gold), int(enemy)

    def close(self):
        self.process.kill()
        self.process.wait()


def _trap_pcs(target):
    """Run the real write-watch agent and return the trap PC per command."""
    import frida  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.write_watch import _build_agent_source  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    hits = []
    session = frida.attach(target.pid)
    script = session.create_script(_build_agent_source(target.address, 4))
    script.on(
        "message",
        lambda message, _data: hits.extend(
            message.get("payload", {}).get("hits", [])
        ),
    )
    script.load()
    try:
        pcs = {}
        for command in ("add", "sub"):
            hits.clear()
            target.send(command, 1)
            deadline = time.monotonic() + 2
            while not hits and time.monotonic() < deadline:
                time.sleep(0.02)
            assert hits, f"write watch saw no write for {command}"
            pcs[command] = int(hits[0]["pc"], 16)
        return pcs
    finally:
        script.exports_sync.stop()
        script.unload()
        session.detach()


def _wait_for(app, predicate, timeout=5):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while not predicate():
        if time.monotonic() > deadline:
            raise AssertionError("timed out waiting for hook worker")
        app.processEvents()
        time.sleep(0.01)


@pytest.fixture(name="qt_app", scope="module")
def fixture_qt_app():
    os.environ.setdefault("QT_QPA_PLATFORM", "offscreen")
    from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module,import-outside-toplevel

    return QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])


@pytest.fixture(name="translations")
def fixture_translations():
    from grembyte.ui.localization import load_translations  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    return load_translations("de")


# _TARGET_SOURCE with a thread that writes the gold through add_gold all the
# time: hooks are removed while game threads are inside their trampolines.
# Not in a tight loop: a thread inside the 5 bytes being patched crashes,
# a limitation of every inline hook.
_BUSY_TARGET_SOURCE = _TARGET_SOURCE.replace(
    "#include <unistd.h>\n", "#include <unistd.h>\n#include <pthread.h>\n"
).replace(
    "int main(void) {\n",
    "static void *busy(void *unused) {\n"
    "    (void) unused;\n"
    "    for (;;) {\n"
    "        add_gold(&g_player, 0);\n"
    "        usleep(50);\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    return NULL;\n"
    "}\n\n"
    "int main(void) {\n"
    "    pthread_t thread;\n"
    "    pthread_create(&thread, NULL, busy, NULL);\n",
)


@requires_target
def test_stopping_hooks_while_a_thread_writes_through_them(tmp_path, qt_app):
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    source = tmp_path / "busy.c"
    source.write_text(_BUSY_TARGET_SOURCE)
    binary = tmp_path / "busy"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O2", "-pthread", str(source), "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    target = _Target(binary)
    try:
        # The busy thread writes through the same instruction as "add".
        trap_pc = _trap_pcs(target)["add"]
        for _round in range(5):
            worker = HookWorker(target.pid)
            installed = {}
            worker.hook_installed.connect(lambda hook_id, info: installed.update({hook_id: info}))
            worker.start()
            # A script runs in JavaScript: the busy thread waits for the agent's lock.
            hook_id = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
                target.address, "int32", ScriptTransform("ctx => ctx.new"),
                trap_pc=trap_pc,
            ))
            _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: hook_id in installed)
            time.sleep(0.2)
            worker.requestInterruption()
            assert worker.wait(10000)
        assert target.process.poll() is None
        assert target.send("add", 1)[0] >= 101
    finally:
        target.close()


def _build_target(tmp_path, optimization="-O2", *flags):
    source = tmp_path / "target.c"
    source.write_text(_TARGET_SOURCE)
    binary = tmp_path / "target"
    subprocess.run(
        ["gcc", optimization, *flags, str(source), "-o", str(binary)], check=True
    )
    return binary


@requires_target
@pytest.mark.parametrize("optimization", ["-O0", "-O2"])
def test_hook_worker_rewrites_values(tmp_path, qt_app, optimization):
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path, optimization))
    worker = HookWorker(target.pid)
    installed, failed, errors = {}, {}, {}
    worker.hook_installed.connect(lambda hook_id, info: installed.update({hook_id: info}))
    worker.hook_failed.connect(lambda hook_id, message: failed.update({hook_id: message}))
    worker.transform_error.connect(lambda hook_id, message: errors.update({hook_id: message}))
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        assert target.send("add", 0) == (100, 999)

        worker.start()
        add_id = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
            target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10), trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"]
        ))
        sub_id = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
            target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(0, direction="decrease"),
            trap_pc=trap_pcs["sub"],
        ))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: {add_id, sub_id} <= set(installed) | set(failed))
        assert not failed

        assert target.send("add", 100) == (100 + 1000, 999)
        assert target.send("sub", 30) == (1100, 999)
        # Shared code: the add hook must not touch the enemy's gold.
        assert target.send("enemy", 100) == (1100, 1099)

        worker.set_transform(add_id, FreezeTransform(5))
        worker.set_enabled(sub_id, False)
        worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
            target.address, "int32", ScriptTransform("ctx => { throw new Error('boom'); }"),
            trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"],
        ))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: len(installed) + len(failed) == 3)
        assert not failed
        assert target.send("sub", 1) == (1099, 1099)
        target.send("add", 7)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: errors)
        assert "boom" in next(iter(errors.values()))

        removed = []
        worker.hook_removed.connect(removed.append)
        worker.remove_hook(add_id)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: removed)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_hook_works_while_its_target_is_write_watched(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    import frida

    from grembyte.features.write_watch import _build_agent_source
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker

    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path))
    worker = HookWorker(target.pid)
    installed, errors = {}, {}
    worker.hook_installed.connect(lambda hook_id, info: installed.update({hook_id: info}))
    worker.transform_error.connect(lambda hook_id, message: errors.update({hook_id: message}))
    session = None
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        worker.start()
        hook_id = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
            target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10), trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"]
        ))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: hook_id in installed)

        # The write watch arms a hardware watchpoint on the hook's target, so
        # the hook's own write of the new value traps as well.
        session = frida.attach(target.pid)
        script = session.create_script(_build_agent_source(target.address, 4))
        script.load()

        assert target.send("add", 10) == (100 + 100, 999)
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (200 + 10, 999)
        qt_app.processEvents()
        time.sleep(0.2)
        qt_app.processEvents()
        assert not errors
        script.exports_sync.stop()
        script.unload()
    finally:
        if session is not None:
            session.detach()
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


# A setter of 3 bytes ("mov [rdi], esi; ret") with the next function right
# behind it: too little room for the 5-byte jmp. int3 padding follows.
_CRAMPED_ASM = r"""
    .text
    .p2align 4
    .globl setter
setter:
    movl %esi, (%rdi)
    ret
    .globl next_fn
next_fn:
    leal 1(%rdi), %eax
    ret
    .p2align 4, 0xcc
    .globl third_fn
third_fn:
    movl %edi, %eax
    ret
    .section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits
"""

_CRAMPED_SOURCE = r"""
#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
void setter(int *p, int v);
int next_fn(int);
static int gold = 100;
int main(void) {
    char command[16];
    int amount;
    printf("%d %p %p\n", getpid(), (void *)&gold, (void *)setter);
    fflush(stdout);
    while (scanf("%15s %d", command, &amount) == 2) {
        setter(&gold, gold + amount);
        printf("%d %d\n", gold, next_fn(amount));
        fflush(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


@requires_target
@pytest.mark.parametrize("short_jump", [False, True])
def test_short_jump_hooks_a_write_without_room_for_the_jmp(tmp_path, qt_app, short_jump):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.core import settings
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker

    (tmp_path / "target.c").write_text(_CRAMPED_SOURCE)
    (tmp_path / "cramped.S").write_text(_CRAMPED_ASM)
    binary = tmp_path / "target"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O1", str(tmp_path / "target.c"), str(tmp_path / "cramped.S"),
                    "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    process = subprocess.Popen(
        [str(binary)], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True
    )
    pid, address, setter = process.stdout.readline().split()
    target = _Target.__new__(_Target)
    target.process, target.pid, target.address = process, int(pid), int(address, 16)

    settings.apply({"hook_short_jump": short_jump})
    worker = HookWorker(target.pid)
    installed, failed = {}, {}
    worker.hook_installed.connect(lambda hook_id, info: installed.update({hook_id: info}))
    worker.hook_failed.connect(lambda hook_id, message: failed.update({hook_id: message}))
    try:
        worker.start()
        hook_id = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
            target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10), write_pc=int(setter, 16)
        ))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: hook_id in installed or hook_id in failed)
        if not short_jump:
            assert "need 5" in failed[hook_id]
            assert target.send("add", 1) == (101, 2)
            return
        assert not failed
        assert installed[hook_id]["patchSize"] == 2 and installed[hook_id]["cave"]
        # The ret and the next function behind the write are left alone.
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (110, 2)
        assert target.send("add", 5) == (160, 6)
    finally:
        settings.reset()
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


# Like _CRAMPED_ASM, with a second run of int3 padding further on: a cave to
# move to when the game overwrites the first one.
_TWO_CAVES_ASM = r"""
    .text
    .p2align 4
    .globl setter
setter:
    movl %esi, (%rdi)
    ret
    .globl next_fn
next_fn:
    leal 1(%rdi), %eax
    ret
    .p2align 4, 0xcc
    .globl third_fn
third_fn:
    movl %edi, %eax
    ret
    .p2align 4, 0xcc
    .globl fourth_fn
fourth_fn:
    ret
    .section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits
"""


@requires_target
def test_repatch_into_a_new_cave_is_restored_on_removal(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,too-many-locals
    import frida

    from grembyte.core import settings
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker

    (tmp_path / "target.c").write_text(_CRAMPED_SOURCE)
    (tmp_path / "caves.S").write_text(_TWO_CAVES_ASM)
    binary = tmp_path / "target"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O1", str(tmp_path / "target.c"), str(tmp_path / "caves.S"),
                    "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    process = subprocess.Popen(
        [str(binary)], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True
    )
    pid, address, setter = process.stdout.readline().split()
    target = _Target.__new__(_Target)
    target.process, target.pid, target.address = process, int(pid), int(address, 16)
    original = _read_code(target.pid, setter, 3)

    settings.apply({"hook_short_jump": True, "hook_repatch": True})
    worker = HookWorker(target.pid)
    installed, states = {}, []
    worker.hook_installed.connect(lambda hook_id, info: installed.update({hook_id: info}))
    worker.site_state.connect(lambda _ids, state, _reverts, _error: states.append(state))
    try:
        worker.start()
        hook_id = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
            target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10), write_pc=int(setter, 16)
        ))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: hook_id in installed)
        cave = installed[hook_id]["cave"]
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (110, 2)

        # What anti-tamper code does: restore the write and use the padding of
        # the cave for code of its own.
        session = frida.attach(target.pid)
        script = session.create_script(
            f"Memory.patchCode(ptr('{setter}'), 2, c => c.writeByteArray({original[:2]}));"
            f"Memory.patchCode(ptr('{cave}'), 5, c => c.writeByteArray({[0x90] * 5}));")
        script.load()
        script.unload()
        session.detach()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: "repatched" in states)
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (120, 2)
        # The moved short jump is the hook's own: not reported as changed code.
        time.sleep(2.5)
        qt_app.processEvents()
        assert states[states.index("repatched"):] == ["repatched"]

        worker.requestInterruption()
        assert worker.wait(5000)
        assert _read_code(target.pid, setter, 3) == original
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (121, 2)
    finally:
        settings.reset()
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


# A write function made by the interpreter itself: needs no compiler.
_CTYPES_TARGET = r"""
import ctypes, os, sys
WRITE = [0x89, 0x11] if sys.platform == "win32" else [0x89, 0x37]  # mov [rcx|rdi], edx|esi
CODE = bytes(WRITE + [0x90] * 4 + [0xc3])
if sys.platform == "win32":
    alloc = ctypes.windll.kernel32.VirtualAlloc
    alloc.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
    function = alloc(None, 4096, 0x3000, 0x40)
    ctypes.memmove(function, CODE, len(CODE))
else:
    import mmap
    page = mmap.mmap(-1, 4096, prot=mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE | mmap.PROT_EXEC)
    page.write(CODE)
    function = ctypes.addressof(ctypes.c_char.from_buffer(page))
write = ctypes.CFUNCTYPE(None, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int32)(function)
gold = ctypes.c_int32(100)
print(os.getpid(), hex(ctypes.addressof(gold)), hex(function), flush=True)
for line in sys.stdin:
    _command, amount = line.split()
    write(ctypes.addressof(gold), gold.value + int(amount))
    print(gold.value, 0, flush=True)
"""

_CTYPES_WRITE = [0x89, 0x11] if sys.platform == "win32" else [0x89, 0x37]

requires_x64_attach = pytest.mark.skipif(
    platform.machine().lower() not in {"amd64", "x86_64"} or not _ptrace_allowed(),
    reason="needs an x86-64 process to attach to",
)


@requires_x64_attach
def test_hook_reverted_by_the_game_is_reported_and_patched_again(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    import frida

    from grembyte.core import settings
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    target, function = _start_ctypes_target(tmp_path)
    original = _CTYPES_WRITE + [0x90] * 3

    def revert():
        # What anti-tamper code does: restore the original bytes.
        session = frida.attach(target.pid)
        restore = session.create_script(
            f"Memory.patchCode(ptr('{function}'), 5, c => c.writeByteArray({original}));")
        restore.load()
        restore.unload()
        session.detach()

    panel = HookPanel(translations)
    status = lambda: panel.table.item(0, 4).text()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment
    try:
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        panel.add_hook(HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10),
                                write_pc=int(function, 16), label="Gold"), "write")
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status() == "Aktiv")
        assert target.send("add", 1)[0] == 110

        revert()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status() == "Vom Spiel entfernt")
        assert target.send("add", 1)[0] == 111
        assert "Gold" in panel.status_label.text()
        # Paused and resumed, the hook still shows that the game removed it.
        panel.table.selectRow(0)
        panel._toggle_selected()
        panel._toggle_selected()
        assert status() == "Vom Spiel entfernt"

        settings.apply({"hook_repatch": True})
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status() == "Aktiv")
        assert target.send("add", 1)[0] == 121
        revert()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: "2×" in panel.table.item(0, 4).toolTip())
        assert status() == "Aktiv" and target.send("add", 1)[0] == 131
    finally:
        settings.reset()
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()


@requires_x64_attach
def test_hook_edited_while_the_game_exits_is_only_saved(tmp_path, qt_app, translations,
                                                        monkeypatch):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    import types

    from PySide6.QtWidgets import QDialog  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

    from grembyte.ui.widgets import hooks

    target, function = _start_ctypes_target(tmp_path)
    panel = hooks.HookPanel(translations)
    saved = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(panel, "_store", lambda action, *args, **kwargs:
                        saved.append(kwargs) if action == "update_hook" else [])

    class DetachingDialog:  # pylint: disable=too-few-public-methods
        """Accepts after the game has exited (the panel is detached meanwhile)."""

        transform, label, breakpoint = MultiplyTransform(2), "Gold x2", True

        def __init__(self, *_args, **_kwargs):
            pass

        @staticmethod
        def exec():
            panel.set_process(None)
            return QDialog.DialogCode.Accepted

    try:
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        hook_id = panel.add_hook(HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10),
                                          write_pc=int(function, 16), label="Gold"), "write")
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: panel.table.item(0, 4).text() == "Aktiv")
        panel._hooks[hook_id]["saved_id"] = 7
        panel._repository = types.SimpleNamespace(update_hook="update_hook",
                                                  list_templates="list_templates")
        panel.table.selectRow(0)
        monkeypatch.setattr(hooks, "HookDialog", DetachingDialog)
        panel._edit_selected()
        assert saved and saved[0]["label"] == "Gold x2" and saved[0]["breakpoint"]
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()


def _start_ctypes_target(tmp_path):
    """Start _CTYPES_TARGET; returns the _Target and its write function (hex)."""
    script = tmp_path / "target.py"
    script.write_text(_CTYPES_TARGET)
    process = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-I", str(script)],
                               stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    pid, address, function = process.stdout.readline().split()
    target = _Target.__new__(_Target)
    target.process, target.pid, target.address = process, int(pid), int(address, 16)
    return target, function


def _read_code(pid, address, size):
    import frida  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    session = frida.attach(pid)
    code = []
    script = session.create_script(
        f"send(Array.from(new Uint8Array(ptr('{address}').readByteArray({size}))));")
    script.on("message", lambda message, _data: code.extend(message["payload"]))
    script.load()
    script.unload()
    session.detach()
    return code


@requires_x64_attach
def test_hooked_writes_stay_out_of_javascript(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.core import settings
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker

    target, function = _start_ctypes_target(tmp_path)
    settings.apply({"hook_profiling": True})
    worker = HookWorker(target.pid)
    installed, profiles, events = {}, [], []
    worker.hook_installed.connect(lambda hook_id, info: installed.update({hook_id: info}))
    worker.hook_profile.connect(profiles.extend)
    worker.hook_events.connect(events.extend)
    try:
        worker.start()
        hook_id = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10),
                                           write_pc=int(function, 16), caller_depth=0))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: hook_id in installed)
        assert target.send("add", 1)[0] == 110
        assert target.send("add", -5)[0] == 105  # increases only
        assert target.send("add", 2)[0] == 125
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: profiles and sum(p["calls"] for p in profiles) >= 3)
        # The built-in manipulation ran in C: no call went to JavaScript.
        assert sum(p["js"] for p in profiles) == 0
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: sum(e["count"] for e in events) == 3)
        assert events[-1]["last"]["result"] == 125
    finally:
        settings.reset()
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


@requires_x64_attach
def test_breakpoint_hook_leaves_the_code_untouched(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    import dataclasses

    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    target, function = _start_ctypes_target(tmp_path)
    code = _read_code(target.pid, function, 7)
    panel = HookPanel(translations)
    status = lambda: panel.table.item(0, 4).text()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment
    try:
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        hook_id = panel.add_hook(HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10),
                                          write_pc=int(function, 16), breakpoint=True,
                                          label="Gold"), "write")
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status() == "Aktiv")
        assert "Slot 1" in panel.table.item(0, 2).toolTip()
        assert target.send("add", 1)[0] == 110
        assert target.send("add", 2)[0] == 130
        assert _read_code(target.pid, function, 7) == code

        # Switched to a patched jump, the hook is installed anew in place.
        state = panel._hooks[hook_id]
        state["spec"] = dataclasses.replace(state["spec"], breakpoint=False)
        panel._reinstall(hook_id)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: panel.table.rowCount() == 1 and status() == "Aktiv")
        assert "Trampolin" in panel.table.item(0, 2).toolTip()
        assert target.send("add", 1)[0] == 140
        assert _read_code(target.pid, function, 7) != code
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()


def _watch_hits(target, command, reads):
    """Run the watch agent around one command and return its hits."""
    import frida  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.write_watch import _build_agent_source  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    hits = []
    session = frida.attach(target.pid)
    script = session.create_script(_build_agent_source(target.address, 4, reads))
    script.on("message", lambda message, _data: hits.extend(
        message.get("payload", {}).get("hits", [])))
    script.load()
    try:
        result = target.send(command, 1)
        time.sleep(0.3)
        return result, hits
    finally:
        script.exports_sync.stop()
        script.unload()
        session.detach()


@requires_target
def test_access_watch_tells_reads_from_writes(tmp_path):
    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path))
    try:
        _result, hits = _watch_hits(target, "add", reads=True)
        # add [gold], amount reads and writes; printing the gold only reads it.
        assert any(hit["read"] and hit["write"] for hit in hits)
        assert any(hit["read"] and not hit["write"] for hit in hits)
        # The value can be read although every read of it traps.
        assert {hit["value"] for hit in hits} == {"65 00 00 00"}
        _result, hits = _watch_hits(target, "add", reads=False)
        assert hits and all(hit["write"] for hit in hits)
    finally:
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_hook_works_while_its_target_is_access_watched(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path))
    panel = HookPanel(translations)
    errors = []
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        panel.add_hook(
            HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10),
                     trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"], label="Gold"),
            "target+?",
        )
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: panel.table.item(0, 4).text() == "Aktiv")
        panel._worker.transform_error.connect(lambda _id, message: errors.append(message))

        result, hits = _watch_hits(target, "add", reads=True)
        qt_app.processEvents()

        # The hook still reads the old value and writes the multiplied one.
        assert result == (100 + 10, 999)
        assert not errors and panel.table.item(0, 4).text() == "Aktiv"
        # Its own reads of the target are not shown as accesses of the game.
        start, end = panel._worker.access_stub
        assert any(start <= int(hit["pc"], 16) < end for hit in hits)
        assert not any(start <= int(hit["pc"], 16) < end
                       for hit in panel.translate_watch_hits(hits))
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()

def _template(template_id=1, source="ctx => ctx.new * ctx.params.factor", default=2):
    return TransformDefinition(
        "Faktor", source, (TransformParameter("factor", default=default, label="Faktor"),),
        template_id=template_id,
    )

def test_hook_dialog_offers_changed_template(qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,unused-argument,protected-access
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookDialog

    changed = TransformDefinition(
        "Faktor neu", "ctx => ctx.old + ctx.delta * ctx.params.factor",
        (
            TransformParameter("factor", default=2, label="Faktor"),
            TransformParameter("limit", optional=True, label="Grenze"),
        ),
        template_id=1,
    )
    dialog = HookDialog(
        translations, "0x1000", "int32", "game+0x10",
        transform=TemplateTransform(_template(), factor=5),
        templates=[changed],
    )

    assert dialog.template_state() == "changed"
    assert dialog.template_notice.isVisibleTo(dialog)
    assert "Faktor neu" in dialog.template_notice_label.text()

    dialog._adopt_template()

    assert dialog.template_state() is None
    assert not dialog.template_notice.isVisibleTo(dialog)
    assert dialog.template_combo.currentText() == "Faktor neu"
    dialog._accept()
    assert dialog.transform.definition == changed
    assert dialog.transform.definition.template_id == 1
    assert dialog.transform.params == {"factor": 5, "limit": None}
```
