```py
@requires_target
def test_hook_panel_installs_and_removes_hooks(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path))
    panel = HookPanel(translations)
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        hook_id = panel.add_hook(
            HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(3),
                     trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"], label="Gold"),
            "target+0x580",
        )
        status = lambda: panel.table.item(0, 4).text()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status() != "Wird installiert …")
        assert status() == "Aktiv"
        assert "add" in panel.table.item(0, 2).text()

        assert target.send("add", 10)[0] == 100 + 30
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: panel.table.item(0, 5).text() == "1")
        assert panel.table.item(0, 6).text() == "100 → 110 ⇒ 130"

        updated = []
        panel._worker.hook_updated.connect(updated.append)  # pylint: disable=protected-access
        panel.table.selectRow(0)
        panel._toggle_selected()  # pylint: disable=protected-access
        assert status() == "Pausiert"
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: updated)
        assert target.send("add", 10)[0] == 140

        panel._remove_selected()  # pylint: disable=protected-access
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: panel.table.rowCount() == 0)
        assert hook_id not in panel._hooks  # pylint: disable=protected-access
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_hooks_of_an_ended_session_can_be_resumed_in_a_new_one(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from typing import cast

    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker

    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path))
    panel = HookPanel(translations)
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        panel.add_hook(
            HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(3),
                     trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"], label="Gold"),
            "target+0x580",
        )
        status = lambda: panel.table.item(0, 4).text()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status() != "Wird installiert …")
        assert status() == "Aktiv"

        # Ended in the sessions window: the worker removes its hooks and stops.
        worker = cast(HookWorker, panel._worker)
        worker.requestInterruption()  # pylint: disable=no-member
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status() == "Getrennt")
        assert panel._worker is None
        assert target.send("add", 10)[0] == 110  # the game's own code again
        panel.table.selectRow(0)
        assert panel.btn_toggle.isEnabled() and not panel.btn_edit.isEnabled()
        assert panel.btn_toggle.text() == "Fortsetzen"

        panel.btn_toggle.click()
        assert panel._worker not in (None, worker)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status() != "Wird installiert …")
        assert status() == "Aktiv" and panel.table.rowCount() == 1
        assert panel.table.item(0, 0).text() == "Gold"
        assert target.send("add", 10)[0] == 110 + 30
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_write_watch_hits_in_trampolines_count_for_the_hooked_write(
        tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path))
    panel = HookPanel(translations)
    try:
        original = _trap_pcs(target)
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        panel.add_hook(
            HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(3),
                     trap_pc=original["add"], label="Gold"),
            "target+0x580",
        )
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: panel.table.item(0, 4).text() == "Aktiv")

        hooked = _trap_pcs(target)
        # The hooked write runs relocated in the trampoline, the other one not.
        assert hooked["add"] != original["add"]
        assert hooked["sub"] == original["sub"]

        hits = [{"pc": f"{pc:#x}", "site": "?", "count": 1} for pc in hooked.values()]
        translated = panel.translate_watch_hits(hits)
        assert [int(hit["pc"], 16) for hit in translated] == [original["add"], original["sub"]]
        assert translated[0]["site"].startswith("target+0x")
        assert translated[1] == hits[1]
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_saved_hooks_survive_a_restart(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access,too-many-locals,too-many-statements
    from sqlalchemy import create_engine
    from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

    from grembyte.db import models  # noqa: F401  pylint: disable=unused-import
    from grembyte.db.base import Base
    from grembyte.db.repository.hooks import HookRepository
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    engine = create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'grembyte.db'}")
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    repository = HookRepository(sessionmaker(bind=engine))
    binary = _build_target(tmp_path, "-O2", "-fPIE", "-pie")
    process_id = repository.get_or_create_process("target", str(binary))
    status = lambda panel: panel.table.item(0, 4).text()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment

    target = _Target(binary)
    panel = HookPanel(translations, repository=repository)
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        panel.set_process(target.pid, process_id)
        panel.add_hook(
            HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(3),
                     trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"], caller_depth=2, label="Gold"),
            "target+?",
        )
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status(panel) != "Wird installiert …")
        assert status(panel) == "Aktiv"
        [saved] = repository.list_hooks(process_id)
        assert saved.module == "target"
        assert saved.label == "Gold"
        assert saved.callers == []

        # loot() and bounty() share give(); two levels tell them apart.
        assert target.send("loot", 10) == (130, 999)
        assert target.send("bounty", 1) == (130, 1000)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: repository.list_hooks(process_id)[0].callers)
        [[give_frame, loot_frame]] = repository.list_hooks(process_id)[0].callers
        assert give_frame[0] == loot_frame[0] == "target"
        assert "ambiguous" not in next(iter(panel._hooks.values()))
        first_address = target.address
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()

    target = _Target(binary)
    panel = HookPanel(translations, repository=repository)
    try:
        if Path("/proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space").read_text().strip() != "0":
            assert target.address != first_address  # ASLR moved the module
        panel.set_process(target.pid, process_id)
        assert panel.table.rowCount() == 1
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status(panel) != "Wird installiert …")
        assert status(panel) == "Aktiv"
        assert panel.table.item(0, 1).text() == "dynamisch · 1 Aufrufer"

        assert target.send("loot", 10) == (130, 999)
        assert target.send("bounty", 1) == (130, 1000)
        # Unknown callers of add_gold are left alone as well.
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (131, 1000)

        panel.table.selectRow(0)
        panel._toggle_selected()
        assert not repository.list_hooks(process_id)[0].enabled
        panel._remove_selected()
        assert repository.list_hooks(process_id) == []
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()
        engine.dispose()


@requires_target
def test_changed_code_is_not_patched(tmp_path, qt_app):
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookWorker  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path))
    worker = HookWorker(target.pid)
    failed = {}
    worker.hook_failed.connect(lambda hook_id, message: failed.update({hook_id: message}))
    try:
        worker.start()
        hook_id = worker.add_hook(HookSpec(
            None, "int32", MultiplyTransform(3),
            module="target", module_offset=0x1000, instruction_bytes="deadbeef",
        ))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: hook_id in failed)
        assert "has changed" in failed[hook_id]
        assert target.send("add", 10) == (110, 999)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()

@requires_target
def test_debug_mode_reports_calls_and_skipped_writes(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    target = _Target(_build_target(tmp_path))
    panel = HookPanel(translations)
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        hook_id = panel.add_hook(
            HookSpec(target.address, "int32",
                     ScriptTransform("ctx => { ctx.log('delta', ctx.delta); "
                                     "return ctx.old + ctx.delta * 3; }"),
                     trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"], caller_depth=2, label="Gold"),
            "target+?",
        )
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: panel.table.item(0, 4).text() == "Aktiv")
        updated = []
        panel._worker.hook_updated.connect(updated.append)
        panel.table.selectRow(0)
        panel._toggle_debug_selected()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: updated)
        window = panel._debug_window
        assert window.isVisible()
        assert panel.btn_debug.isChecked()
        assert panel.table.item(0, 0).text() == "◉ Gold"

        assert target.send("loot", 10) == (130, 999)
        assert target.send("bounty", 1) == (130, 1000)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: len(window.entries()) >= 2)

        applied, skipped = window.entries()[:2]
        assert (applied["old"], applied["new"], applied["result"]) == (100, 110, 130)
        assert applied["logs"] == ["delta 10"]
        assert applied["address"] == hex(target.address)
        assert applied["caller"].count("target+0x") == 2
        assert skipped["skipped"] == "address"
        assert skipped["caller"] != applied["caller"]
        # Skipped writes show their values too, and go to the address list.
        assert (skipped["old"], skipped["new"]) == (999, 1000)
        requested = []
        panel.address_requested.connect(lambda *args: requested.append(args))
        window.context_menu(skipped).actions()[0].trigger()
        assert requested == [(int(skipped["address"], 16), "int32",
                              f"Gold · {skipped['caller']}")]

        window.close()
        assert not panel.btn_debug.isChecked()
        assert panel.table.item(0, 0).text() == "Gold"
        updated.clear()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: updated)
        target.send("loot", 1)
        time.sleep(0.3)
        qt_app.processEvents()
        assert len(window.entries()) == 2
        # Out of debug mode, what the script logs still shows below the table.
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: f"#{hook_id} Gold: delta 1" in panel.log_view.toPlainText())
        assert f"#{hook_id} Gold: delta 10" in panel.log_view.toPlainText()
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()


# --- Training: hooks on JIT code -------------------------------------------

_JIT_TARGET_SOURCE = r"""
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <unistd.h>

typedef struct { int32_t hp; int32_t gold; } Player;
typedef struct { char pad[0x10]; Player *player; } Game;
Game *g_game;

typedef void (*change_fn)(int32_t *gold, int32_t amount);

/* Like a JIT: the code lands somewhere else on every start and embeds
   constants (think absolute addresses) that differ between runs. */
static change_fn emit(uint8_t *region, size_t offset, uint8_t opcode) {
    uint8_t *code = region + offset;
    uint64_t a = ((uint64_t)rand() << 32) ^ (uint64_t)rand();
    uint64_t b = ((uint64_t)rand() << 32) ^ (uint64_t)rand();
    size_t n = 0;
    code[n++] = 0x55;                                       /* push rbp */
    code[n++] = 0x48; code[n++] = 0x89; code[n++] = 0xe5;   /* mov rbp, rsp */
    code[n++] = 0x48; code[n++] = 0xb8;                     /* movabs rax, a */
    memcpy(code + n, &a, 8); n += 8;
    code[n++] = opcode; code[n++] = 0x37;                   /* add/sub [rdi], esi */
    code[n++] = 0x8b; code[n++] = 0x07;                     /* mov eax, [rdi] */
    code[n++] = 0x48; code[n++] = 0xb9;                     /* movabs rcx, b */
    memcpy(code + n, &b, 8); n += 8;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        code[n++] = 0x90;                                   /* nop */
    code[n++] = 0x5d;                                       /* pop rbp */
    code[n++] = 0xc3;                                       /* ret */
    return (change_fn)code;
}

int main(void) {
    srand(getpid());
    size_t size = 0x10000;
    uint8_t *region = mmap(NULL, size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC,
                           MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
    memset(region, 0xcc, size);
    size_t offset = 0x100 + (size_t)(rand() % 64) * 0x40;
    change_fn add = emit(region, offset, 0x01);
    change_fn sub = emit(region, offset + 0x2000, 0x29);

    g_game = calloc(1, sizeof(Game));
    g_game->player = calloc(1, sizeof(Player));
    g_game->player->gold = 100;
    printf("%d %p %p\n", getpid(), (void *)&g_game->player->gold, (void *)add);
    fflush(stdout);
    char cmd[16];
    int value;
    while (scanf("%15s %d", cmd, &value) == 2) {
        if (strcmp(cmd, "add") == 0)
            add(&g_game->player->gold, value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "sub") == 0)
            sub(&g_game->player->gold, value);
        printf("%d 0\n", g_game->player->gold);
        fflush(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


class _JitTarget(_Target):
    def __init__(self, binary):  # pylint: disable=super-init-not-called
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [str(binary)], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True
        )
        pid, address, add = self.process.stdout.readline().split()
        self.pid = int(pid)
        self.address = int(address, 16)
        self.add_code = int(add, 16)


def _jit_gold_chain(binary):
    """g_game -> player (+0x10) -> gold (+4)."""
    nm = subprocess.run(["nm", str(binary)], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    g_game = next(int(line.split()[0], 16) for line in nm.stdout.splitlines()
                  if line.endswith(" g_game"))
    return PointerChain("target", g_game, (0x10, 0x4))


@requires_target
def test_hook_on_jit_code_is_trained_again_after_a_restart(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access,too-many-locals,too-many-statements
    from sqlalchemy import create_engine
    from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

    from grembyte.db import models  # noqa: F401  pylint: disable=unused-import
    from grembyte.db.base import Base
    from grembyte.db.repository.hooks import HookRepository
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    engine = create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'grembyte.db'}")
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    repository = HookRepository(sessionmaker(bind=engine))
    source = tmp_path / "target.c"
    source.write_text(_JIT_TARGET_SOURCE)
    binary = tmp_path / "target"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O1", "-fPIE", "-pie", str(source), "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    chain = _jit_gold_chain(binary)
    process_id = repository.get_or_create_process("target", str(binary))
    status = lambda panel: panel.table.item(0, 4).text()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment

    target = _JitTarget(binary)
    panel = HookPanel(translations, repository=repository)
    try:
        trap_pcs = _trap_pcs(target)
        panel.set_process(target.pid, process_id)
        panel.add_hook(
            HookSpec(target.address, "int32", MultiplyTransform(10),
                     trap_pc=trap_pcs["add"], pointer=chain, label="Gold"),
            "jit",
        )
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status(panel) != "Wird installiert …")
        assert status(panel) == "Aktiv"
        assert "Training" in panel.status_label.text()
        [saved] = repository.list_hooks(process_id)
        assert saved.module == "" and saved.pointer == chain.to_json()
        assert saved.instruction_bytes == "0137"
        assert len(saved.signature["before"]) == len(saved.signature["after"]) == 64
        first_code = target.add_code
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()

    target = _JitTarget(binary)
    panel = HookPanel(translations, repository=repository)
    try:
        assert target.add_code != first_code
        panel.set_process(target.pid, process_id)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status(panel) == "Training")

        # A write or access watch pauses the training; running both at once
        # deadlocked Frida and crashed the game.
        panel.pause_trainings(True)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: "pausiert" in panel.table.item(0, 4).toolTip())
        for reads in (False, True):
            result, hits = _watch_hits(target, "add", reads=reads)
            assert hits
        assert result == (102, 0) and status(panel) == "Training"
        panel.pause_trainings(False)

        # A write from other code (sub) does not train the hook.
        assert target.send("sub", 7) == (95, 0)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: "1 davon aus anderem Code" in
                  panel.table.item(0, 4).toolTip())
        assert status(panel) == "Training"

        # The first write from the saved code reveals the site ...
        assert target.send("add", 10) == (105, 0)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status(panel) == "Aktiv")
        assert f"{target.add_code + 14:#x}" in panel.table.item(0, 2).toolTip()
        # ... from then on the hook applies.
        assert target.send("add", 10) == (105 + 100, 0)
        assert target.send("sub", 5) == (200, 0)
        assert len(repository.list_hooks(process_id)) == 1

        # Writes keep coming while the training ends and its watchpoints are
        # removed; the program must survive the stray traps of that moment.
        for _ in range(20):
            assert target.send("sub", 1)[0] > 0
        assert target.process.poll() is None
    finally:
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()
        engine.dispose()

```

`tests/test_hotkeys.py`:

```py
"""Hotkeys that run scripts while the game has the focus (see grembyte.core.hotkeys)."""

import os

import pytest

from grembyte.core import hotkeys
from grembyte.core.messages import LocalizedValueError


@pytest.fixture(name="qt_app", scope="module")
def fixture_qt_app():
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    os.environ.setdefault("QT_QPA_PLATFORM", "offscreen")
    from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module
    return QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])


class FakeKeyboard:
    """Stands in for grembyte.platform.keyboard: the test says what is held."""

    def __init__(self, focused=4242):
        self.down = set()
        self.focused = focused
        self.closed = False

    def pressed(self, names):
        return self.down & set(names)

    def focused_pid(self):
        return self.focused

    def close(self):
        self.closed = True


def test_hotkeys_are_read_and_written_as_qt_writes_them():
    assert hotkeys.parse("Ctrl+Shift+G") == hotkeys.Hotkey("G", frozenset({"ctrl", "shift"}))
    assert hotkeys.normalized("shift+control+g") == "Ctrl+Shift+G"
    assert hotkeys.normalized("F9") == "F9"
    assert hotkeys.normalized("Alt+PgDown") == "Alt+PgDown"
    assert hotkeys.normalized("  ") == ""
    for text in ("Ctrl+", "Hyper+G", "Ctrl++"):
        with pytest.raises(LocalizedValueError):
            hotkeys.parse(text)
    with pytest.raises(LocalizedValueError) as error:
        hotkeys.parse("Ctrl+Tab")
    assert error.value.key == "error.hotkeys.key"


def test_a_hotkey_fires_once_per_press_with_exactly_its_modifiers(qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=unused-argument
    keyboard = FakeKeyboard()
    listener = hotkeys.HotkeyListener({4242}, keyboard)
    fired = []
    listener.triggered.connect(fired.append)
    try:
        listener.set_hotkeys(["Ctrl+G", "F9"])
        listener.poll()  # the first reading only notes what is held
        keyboard.down = {"ctrl", "G"}
        listener.poll()
        listener.poll()  # held: not again
        assert fired == ["Ctrl+G"]
        keyboard.down = {"ctrl"}
        listener.poll()
        keyboard.down = {"ctrl", "shift", "G"}  # another modifier as well: not Ctrl+G
        listener.poll()
        keyboard.down = {"F9"}
        listener.poll()
        assert fired == ["Ctrl+G", "F9"]
    finally:
        listener.close()
    assert keyboard.closed


def test_hotkeys_count_only_while_the_game_has_the_focus(qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=unused-argument
    keyboard = FakeKeyboard(focused=1)
    listener = hotkeys.HotkeyListener({4242}, keyboard)
    fired = []
    listener.triggered.connect(fired.append)
    try:
        listener.set_hotkeys(["F9"])
        keyboard.down = {"F9"}
        listener.poll()
        # Held while the focus comes back: only a new press counts
        keyboard.focused = 4242
        listener.poll()
        assert fired == []
        keyboard.down = set()
        listener.poll()
        keyboard.down = {"F9"}
        listener.poll()
        # A window whose process cannot be told does not stop it
        keyboard.down = set()
        listener.poll()
        keyboard.focused = None
        keyboard.down = {"F9"}
        listener.poll()
        assert fired == ["F9", "F9"]
    finally:
        listener.close()


def test_keys_held_when_the_hotkeys_change_do_not_fire(qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=unused-argument
    keyboard = FakeKeyboard()
    keyboard.down = {"F9"}
    listener = hotkeys.HotkeyListener({4242}, keyboard)
    fired = []
    listener.triggered.connect(fired.append)
    try:
        listener.set_hotkeys(["F9"])
        listener.poll()
        assert fired == []
    finally:
        listener.close()


def test_without_a_keyboard_the_listener_reports_nothing(qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=unused-argument
    listener = hotkeys.HotkeyListener({4242}, None)
    listener.set_hotkeys(["F9"])
    listener.poll()
    assert not listener.available


@pytest.mark.skipif(not os.environ.get("DISPLAY") or not os.sys.platform.startswith("linux"),
                    reason="needs an X display")
def test_the_x11_keyboard_knows_the_keys_of_every_hotkey():
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from grembyte.platform.keyboard import X11Keyboard

    keyboard = X11Keyboard()
    try:
        missing = [key for key in hotkeys.KEYS + ("ctrl", "shift", "alt")
                   if not keyboard._keycodes.get(key)]
        assert not missing
        assert keyboard.pressed({"F12"}) <= {"F12"}
        focused = keyboard.focused_pid()
        assert focused is None or focused >= 0
    finally:
        keyboard.close()
```

`tests/test_il2cpp.py`:

```py
"""IL2CPP games, against a stand-in GameAssembly.so.

The stand-in exports the part of IL2CPP's API the adapter uses, over two
images: ``mscorlib.dll`` (framework) and ``Assembly-CSharp.dll`` with
``Game.Hero``. Its methods are real functions in the library, as IL2CPP
compiles them: ``Loot`` calls ``AddGold``; ``Tick`` and ``Idle`` share one
function, as identical functions the linker folds do; ``Attack`` is
abstract and points at a stub like IL2CPP's; ``Game.Bag<T>`` is a generic
class definition. ``Rename`` and ``Place`` are instance methods of the
player object (``Place`` returns a struct through a hidden pointer). A
program linked against the library calls them on commands (``tick``,
``loot N``, ``rename N``, ``place N``) and answers with the gold.
"""

import json
import subprocess
import time

from tests.test_hooks import (  # pylint: disable=unused-import
    _Target,
    _wait_for,
    fixture_qt_app,
    requires_target,
)


_GAME_ASSEMBLY_SOURCE = r"""
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct Class Class;
typedef struct Image { const char *name; Class **classes; size_t count; } Image;
typedef struct Type { const char *name; int kind, byref; Class *klass; } Type;
typedef struct Field { const char *name; Type *type; Class *parent; int offset, flags; } Field;
typedef struct Method Method;
/* Laid out like Il2CppClass where the adapter looks: the image first, the
   field ``klass`` pointing at the class itself, then the fields and, seven
   pointers later, the static data. */
struct Class {
    Image *image;
    const char *name;
    Type type;
    Class *element_class;
    Class *klass;
    Field *fields;
    void *unused[6];
    void *static_fields;
    Class *parent;
    int generic, valuetype, size;
    Method **methods;
    size_t count, field_count;
};
struct Method {
    void *pointer;  /* first, as in IL2CPP's MethodInfo */
    const char *name;
    Class *klass;
    uint32_t token, flags, iflags;
    uint32_t param_count;
    Type *params[3];
    const char *param_names[3];
    Type *returns;
};
typedef struct Assembly { Image *image; } Assembly;
typedef struct String { Class *klass; void *monitor; int32_t length; uint16_t chars[16]; } String;
typedef struct HeroObject { Class *klass; void *monitor; int32_t gold; String *name; } HeroObject;
typedef struct Vec { double x, y, z; } Vec;

static Class hero, bag, string_class, object_class, vec_class;
static Type t_void = {"System.Void", 0x01}, t_int = {"System.Int32", 0x08};
static Type t_float = {"System.Single", 0x0c}, t_string = {"System.String", 0x0e};
static Type t_param = {"T", 0x13}, t_vec = {"Game.Vec", 0x11, 0, &vec_class};
static Type t_hero = {"Game.Hero", 0x12, 0, &hero};
static Type t_bool = {"System.Boolean", 0x02}, t_double = {"System.Double", 0x0d};

int g_gold;
static int g_instances = 7;
static String names[2];
static HeroObject player;

__attribute__((noinline)) void Hero_AddGold(int amount) { g_gold += amount; }
__attribute__((noinline)) void Hero_Tick(float delta) { (void)delta; __asm__ volatile(""); }
__attribute__((noinline)) void Hero_Loot(int amount) {
    __asm__ volatile("");
    Hero_AddGold(amount);
    __asm__ volatile("");
}
__attribute__((noinline)) void Unresolved(void) { abort(); }
__attribute__((noinline)) void Bag_Add(void *item) { (void)item; __asm__ volatile(""); }
__attribute__((noinline)) int String_get_Length(String *s) { return s->length; }
__attribute__((noinline)) void Hero_Rename(HeroObject *self, String *name, void *method) {
    (void)method;
    self->name = name;
}
/* Returns a struct through a hidden pointer, which comes before ``self`` */
__attribute__((noinline)) Vec Hero_Place(HeroObject *self, int steps, void *method) {
    (void)method;
    Vec v = {self->gold, steps, 0};
    return v;
}

__attribute__((noinline)) int Hero_get_Count(void *method) { (void)method; return 7; }
__attribute__((noinline)) int Hero_Roll(HeroObject *self, int min, float scale, int crit,
                                        void *method) {
    (void)method;
    return (int)(min * scale * (crit ? 2 : 1)) + self->gold * 0;
}
__attribute__((noinline)) double Vec_Length(Vec *self, void *method) {
    (void)method;
    return self->x + self->y + self->z;
}

#define STATIC 0x10
#define PUBLIC 0x06
#define ABSTRACT 0x400
static Method m_add = {Hero_AddGold, "AddGold", &hero, 0x06000001, PUBLIC | STATIC, 0, 1,
                       {&t_int}, {"amount"}, &t_void};
static Method m_tick = {Hero_Tick, "Tick", &hero, 0x06000002, PUBLIC, 0, 1,
                        {&t_float}, {"delta"}, &t_void};
static Method m_idle = {Hero_Tick, "Idle", &hero, 0x06000003, PUBLIC, 0, 1,
                        {&t_float}, {"delta"}, &t_void};
static Method m_loot = {Hero_Loot, "Loot", &hero, 0x06000004, PUBLIC | STATIC, 0, 1,
                        {&t_int}, {"amount"}, &t_void};
static Method m_attack = {Unresolved, "Attack", &hero, 0x06000005, PUBLIC | ABSTRACT, 0, 0,
                          {0}, {0}, &t_void};
static Method m_rename = {Hero_Rename, "Rename", &hero, 0x06000007, PUBLIC, 0, 1,
                          {&t_string}, {"name"}, &t_void};
static Method m_place = {Hero_Place, "Place", &hero, 0x06000008, PUBLIC, 0, 1,
                         {&t_int}, {"steps"}, &t_vec};
static Method m_count = {Hero_get_Count, "get_Count", &hero, 0x06000009, PUBLIC | STATIC, 0, 0,
                         {0}, {0}, &t_int};
static Method m_roll = {Hero_Roll, "Roll", &hero, 0x0600000a, PUBLIC, 0, 3,
                        {&t_int, &t_float, &t_bool}, {"min", "scale", "crit"}, &t_int};
static Method m_length_vec = {Vec_Length, "Length", &vec_class, 0x0600000b, PUBLIC, 0, 0,
                              {0}, {0}, &t_double};
static Method m_bag_add = {Bag_Add, "Add", &bag, 0x06000006, PUBLIC, 0, 1,
                           {&t_param}, {"item"}, &t_void};
static Method m_length = {String_get_Length, "get_Length", &string_class, 0x06000001, PUBLIC,
                          0, 0, {0}, {0}, &t_int};
static Method *hero_methods[] = {&m_add, &m_tick, &m_idle, &m_loot, &m_attack, &m_rename,
                                 &m_place, &m_count, &m_roll};
static Method *vec_methods[] = {&m_length_vec};
static Method *bag_methods[] = {&m_bag_add};
static Method *string_methods[] = {&m_length};
static Field hero_fields[] = {
    {"Gold", &t_int, &hero, 0x10, 0x06},
    {"Name", &t_string, &hero, 0x18, 0x06},
    {"Instances", &t_int, &hero, 0, 0x16},
};
static Field vec_fields[] = {
    {"x", &t_double, &vec_class, 0x10, 0x06},
    {"y", &t_double, &vec_class, 0x18, 0x06},
    {"z", &t_double, &vec_class, 0x20, 0x06},
};
static Field string_fields[] = {{"m_stringLength", &t_int, &string_class, 0x10, 0x01}};
static Image game, corlib;
static Class object_class = {.image = &corlib, .name = "Object",
    .type = {"System.Object", 0x1c, 0, &object_class}, .element_class = &object_class,
    .klass = &object_class, .size = 16};
static Class hero = {.image = &game, .name = "Hero", .type = {"Game.Hero", 0x12, 0, &hero},
    .element_class = &hero, .klass = &hero, .fields = hero_fields,
    .static_fields = &g_instances, .parent = &object_class, .size = 0x20,
    .methods = hero_methods, .count = 9, .field_count = 3};
static Class bag = {.image = &game, .name = "Bag", .type = {"Game.Bag<T>", 0x12, 0, &bag},
    .element_class = &bag, .klass = &bag, .parent = &object_class, .generic = 1,
    .methods = bag_methods, .count = 1};
static Class vec_class = {.image = &game, .name = "Vec", .type = {"Game.Vec", 0x11, 0, &vec_class},
    .element_class = &vec_class, .klass = &vec_class, .valuetype = 1, .size = 16 + 24,
    .fields = vec_fields, .field_count = 3, .methods = vec_methods, .count = 1};
static Class string_class = {.image = &corlib, .name = "String",
    .type = {"System.String", 0x0e, 0, &string_class}, .element_class = &string_class,
    .klass = &string_class, .fields = string_fields, .parent = &object_class,
    .methods = string_methods, .count = 1, .field_count = 1};
static Class *game_classes[] = {&hero, &bag, &vec_class};
static Class *corlib_classes[] = {&object_class, &string_class};
static Image game = {"Assembly-CSharp.dll", game_classes, 3};
static Image corlib = {"mscorlib.dll", corlib_classes, 2};
static Assembly a_corlib = {&corlib}, a_game = {&game};
static Assembly *assemblies[] = {&a_corlib, &a_game};
static int domain, thread;

static void make_name(String *s, const char *text) {
    s->klass = &string_class;
    s->length = (int32_t)strlen(text);
    for (int i = 0; i < s->length; i++)
        s->chars[i] = (uint16_t)text[i];
}

void Game_Rename(int which) {
    if (player.klass == NULL) {
        player.klass = &hero;
        player.gold = 30;
        make_name(&names[0], "Miranda");
        make_name(&names[1], "Young Wolf");
    }
    Hero_Rename(&player, &names[which], &m_rename);
}
int Game_Roll(int min) {
    Game_Rename(0);
    return Hero_Roll(&player, min, 1.5f, 1, &m_roll);
}
int Game_Length(int x) {
    Vec v = {x, 1, 2};
    return (int)Vec_Length(&v, &m_length_vec);
}
int Game_Gold(void) { return player.gold; }
int Game_NameLength(void) { return player.name ? player.name->length : -1; }
int Game_Place(int steps) {
    Game_Rename(0);
    return (int)Hero_Place(&player, steps, &m_place).y;
}

void *il2cpp_get_corlib(void) { return &corlib; }
void *il2cpp_domain_get(void) { return &domain; }

    (void)params;

        static struct { void *klass, *monitor; int value; } box;
        box.value = (m->flags & STATIC) ? ((int (*)(Method *))m->pointer)(m)
                                        : ((int (*)(void *, Method *))m->pointer)(obj, m);
        return &box;
    }
    return ((void *(*)(void *, Method *))m->pointer)(obj, m);
}

_GAME_SOURCE = r"""
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

extern int g_gold;
void Hero_Tick(float delta);
void Hero_Loot(int amount);
void Game_Rename(int which);
int Game_Place(int steps);
int Game_Roll(int min);
int Game_Length(int x);
int Game_Gold(void);
int Game_NameLength(void);

int main(void) {
    printf("%d %p\n", getpid(), (void *)&g_gold);
    fflush(stdout);
    char cmd[32];
    int value;
    while (scanf("%31s %d", cmd, &value) == 2) {
        int answer = 0;
        if (strcmp(cmd, "tick") == 0)
            Hero_Tick(0.5f);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "loot") == 0)
            Hero_Loot(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "rename") == 0)
            Game_Rename(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "place") == 0)
            answer = Game_Place(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "roll") == 0)
            answer = Game_Roll(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "length") == 0)
            answer = Game_Length(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "hero") == 0)
            answer = Game_Gold() * 100 + Game_NameLength();
        printf("%d %d\n", g_gold, answer);
        fflush(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


def _build(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "game_assembly.c").write_text(_GAME_ASSEMBLY_SOURCE)
    (tmp_path / "game.c").write_text(_GAME_SOURCE)
    library = tmp_path / "GameAssembly.so"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O0", "-shared", "-fPIC", str(tmp_path / "game_assembly.c"),
                    "-o", str(library)], check=True)
    binary = tmp_path / "fakegame"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O0", str(tmp_path / "game.c"), str(library),
                    "-Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN", "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    return binary


def _run(qt_app, worker, signal):
    found, failed = [], []
    signal.connect(lambda *args: found.append(args))
    worker.catalog_failed.connect(failed.append)
    worker.start()
    _wait_for(qt_app, worker.isFinished)
    qt_app.processEvents()
    assert not failed
    return found


@requires_target
def test_catalog_lists_images_classes_and_methods(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.engines.registry import detect_engine
    from grembyte.features.catalog import CatalogWorker

    target = _Target(_build(tmp_path))
    try:
        engine = detect_engine(target.pid)
        assert engine.id == "il2cpp"

        worker = CatalogWorker(target.pid)
        loaded = {}
        worker.assembly_loaded.connect(loaded.__setitem__)
        found = _run(qt_app, worker, worker.assemblies_found)[0][0]
        # Named without .dll, as Mono names assemblies; the build of
        # GameAssembly stands for their MVID.
        assert [(a["name"], a["file"], a["classes"]) for a in found] == [
            ("mscorlib", "mscorlib.dll", 2), ("Assembly-CSharp", "Assembly-CSharp.dll", 3)]
        assert found[0]["mvid"] and found[0]["mvid"] != found[1]["mvid"]
        # The framework is left out unless asked for.
        assert sorted(loaded) == ["Assembly-CSharp"]
        methods = {m.signature: m for m in loaded["Assembly-CSharp"]}
        assert sorted(methods) == [
            "Game.Bag`1:Add (T)", "Game.Hero:AddGold (int)", "Game.Hero:Attack ()",
            "Game.Hero:Idle (single)", "Game.Hero:Loot (int)", "Game.Hero:Place (int)",
            "Game.Hero:Rename (string)", "Game.Hero:Roll (int,single,bool)",
            "Game.Hero:Tick (single)", "Game.Hero:get_Count ()", "Game.Vec:Length ()"]
        add = methods["Game.Hero:AddGold (int)"]
        assert (add.class_name, add.name, add.parameters, add.return_type, add.static,
                add.token, add.engine, add.argument_names) == (
            "Game.Hero", "AddGold", "(int)", "System.Void", True, 0x06000001, "il2cpp",
            ("amount",))
        assert methods["Game.Bag`1:Add (T)"].class_name == "Game.Bag<T>"
    finally:
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_trace_counts_methods_and_names_their_callers(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.trace import NEW, SAME, TraceWorker, analyze, recording_calls

    target = _Target(_build(tmp_path))
    worker = TraceWorker(target.pid)
    planned, started, began, recorded, failed = [], [], [], [], []
    worker.planned.connect(planned.append)
    worker.started.connect(lambda methods, info: started.append((methods, info)))
    worker.began.connect(began.append)
    worker.recorded.connect(recorded.append)
    worker.command_failed.connect(lambda action, message: failed.append((action, message)))
    worker.worker_failed.connect(lambda message: failed.append(("worker", message)))

    def record(phase, *commands):
        worker.begin(phase)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: phase in began or failed)
        began.clear()
        for command, value in commands:
            target.send(command, value)
        count = len(recorded)
        worker.finish()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: len(recorded) > count or failed)
        assert not failed
        return recorded[-1]

    try:
        worker.start()
        worker.plan([])
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: planned or failed)
        assert not failed
        # Attack is abstract, Bag`1:Add belongs to a generic definition.
        assert planned[0] == {"methods": 9, "skipped": {"abstract": 1, "native": 0, "generic": 1},
                              "assemblies": ["Assembly-CSharp"]}

        worker.trace([])
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: started or failed)
        assert not failed
        methods, info = started[0]
        assert (info["notCompiled"], info["failed"]) == (0, 0)
        # Tick and Idle share their code: hooked once, under the first.
        assert sorted(method.name for method in methods) == [
            "AddGold", "Length", "Loot", "Place", "Rename", "Roll", "Tick", "get_Count"]

        baseline = record("baseline", ("tick", 0), ("tick", 0))
        index = {method.name: i for i, method in enumerate(methods)}
        assert {int(key): count for key, count in baseline["counts"].items()} == {
            index["Tick"]: 2}
        scenario = record("scenario", ("tick", 0), ("loot", 5), ("tick", 0))
        rows = analyze(scenario, baseline)
        assert [(methods[row.method].name, row.verdict, row.calls) for row in rows] == [
            ("Loot", NEW, 1), ("AddGold", NEW, 1), ("Tick", SAME, 2)]
        calls = {methods[call.method].name: call.caller for call in recording_calls(scenario)}
        # Code in GameAssembly is named as the C# method it belongs to.
        assert calls["AddGold"].startswith("Game.Hero:Loot+0x")
        assert calls["Loot"].startswith("fakegame+0x")
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


_NAMING_AGENT = r"""
rpc.exports = {
  ready() {
    return engine.refresh() && engine.locate(ptr(0)) !== undefined;
  },
  names() {
    const library = Process.getModuleByName('GameAssembly.so');
    const at = name => library.getExportByName(name);
    const located = engine.locate(at('Hero_Loot').add(4));
    return {
      loot: engine.describe(at('Hero_Loot').add(4)),
      tick: engine.describe(at('Hero_Tick')),
      // The abstract method's stub is no method's code.
      stub: engine.describe(at('Unresolved')),
      outside: engine.describe(Process.getModuleByName('fakegame').base),
      identity: located ? engine.identify(at('Hero_Loot').add(4)) : null
    };
  },
  async compile(identity) {
    const code = await engine.compile(identity);
    return [code.start.toString(), code.size];
  },
  address: name => Process.getModuleByName('GameAssembly.so').getExportByName(name).toString()
};
"""


@requires_target
def test_code_addresses_are_named_and_found_again(tmp_path):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    import frida

    from grembyte.engines.registry import ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE

    target = _Target(_build(tmp_path))
    session = frida.attach(target.pid)
    try:
        script = session.create_script(ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE + _NAMING_AGENT)
        script.load()
        api = script.exports_sync
        # The table is built on the agent's thread soon after the runtime was found.
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
        while not api.ready():
            assert time.monotonic() < deadline
            time.sleep(0.05)
        names = api.names()
        assert names["loot"] == "Game.Hero:Loot+0x4"
        assert names["tick"] == "Game.Hero:Tick+0x0 [shared with 1]"
        assert names["stub"] is None and names["outside"] is None
        identity = names["identity"]
        assert identity == {"engine": "il2cpp", "image": "Assembly-CSharp",
                            "file": "Assembly-CSharp.dll", "token": 0x06000004,
                            "method": "Game.Hero:Loot (int)", "offset": 4}
        start, size = api.compile(identity)
        assert start == api.address("Hero_Loot") and size > 4
        # A method that changed (another signature) is not taken for the old one.
        changed = json.loads(json.dumps(identity))
        changed["method"] = "Game.Hero:Loot (long)"
        try:
            api.compile(changed)
        except frida.core.RPCException as error:
            assert "method_changed" in str(error) or "no longer" in str(error)
        else:
            raise AssertionError("compile accepted a changed method")
        script.unload()
    finally:
        session.detach()
        target.close()


_RENAME = {"engine": "il2cpp", "image": "Assembly-CSharp", "file": None, "token": 0x06000007,
           "method": "Game.Hero:Rename (string)"}
_PLACE = {"engine": "il2cpp", "image": "Assembly-CSharp", "file": None, "token": 0x06000008,
          "method": "Game.Hero:Place (int)"}


@requires_target
def test_method_monitor_logs_arguments_and_inspects_objects(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.monitor import MethodMonitorWorker

    target = _Target(_build(tmp_path))
    worker = MethodMonitorWorker(target.pid)
    added, calls, inspected, failed = {}, [], {}, {}
    worker.monitor_added.connect(added.__setitem__)
    worker.calls.connect(lambda events, _dropped, _counts: calls.extend(events))
    worker.inspected.connect(inspected.__setitem__)
    worker.inspect_failed.connect(failed.__setitem__)

    def inspect(value_target):
        request = worker.inspect(value_target)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: request in inspected or request in failed)
        return inspected.get(request) or failed[request]

    try:
        worker.start()
        rename = worker.add_monitor(_RENAME, returns=False, objects=True)
        place = worker.add_monitor(_PLACE, returns=True, objects=False)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: rename in added and place in added)
        assert (added[rename]["instance"], added[rename]["params"]) == (
            True, ["System.String name"])
        target.send("rename", 1)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: calls)
        call = calls[0]
        assert call["monitorId"] == rename
        assert call["self"]["text"].startswith("Game.Hero@0x")
        assert call["args"][0]["text"] == '"Young Wolf"'
        # Game_Rename is no method: its code is named module+offset.
        assert call["caller"].startswith("GameAssembly.so+0x")

        calls.clear()
        # The struct result's pointer comes first: self and steps are still found.
        assert target.send("place", 4) == (0, 4)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: any(c["monitorId"] == place for c in calls))
        call = next(c for c in calls if c["monitorId"] == place)
        assert call["self"]["text"].startswith("Game.Hero@0x")
        assert call["args"][0]["text"] == "4"
        assert call["result"]["text"] == "struct Game.Vec"

        contents = inspect(call["self"]["target"])
        assert contents["name"] == "Game.Hero"
        fields = {field["name"]: field for field in contents["fields"]}
        assert [(name, f["static"], f["value"]["text"]) for name, f in fields.items()] == [
            ("Gold", False, "30"), ("Name", False, '"Miranda"'), ("Instances", True, "7")]
        # The static field lies in the class's static data, found by its layout.
        assert fields["Instances"]["address"] is not None
        assert fields["Gold"]["valueType"] == "int32"
        # An address that holds no object is refused instead of read.
        assert "no object" in inspect({"address": "0x10"})
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


_ROLL = {"engine": "il2cpp", "image": "Assembly-CSharp", "file": None, "token": 0x0600000a,
         "method": "Game.Hero:Roll (int,single,bool)"}
_LENGTH = {"engine": "il2cpp", "image": "Assembly-CSharp", "file": None, "token": 0x0600000b,
           "method": "Game.Vec:Length ()"}


def _method_transform(source, **params):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.hooks.transforms import TemplateTransform, TransformDefinition, TransformParameter

    definition = TransformDefinition(
        "test", source, tuple(TransformParameter(name, default=value)
                              for name, value in params.items()), kind="method")
    return TemplateTransform(definition, **params)


@requires_target
def test_method_hooks_change_arguments_fields_and_results(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.method_hooks import MethodHookSpec, MethodHookWorker

    target = _Target(_build(tmp_path))
    worker = MethodHookWorker(target.pid)
    installed, failed, errors, debug = {}, {}, {}, []
    worker.hook_installed.connect(installed.__setitem__)
    worker.hook_failed.connect(failed.__setitem__)
    worker.transform_error.connect(errors.__setitem__)
    worker.hook_debug.connect(lambda entries, _dropped: debug.extend(entries))
    before = """function (ctx) {
      ctx.args.min = 10;            // int in a register
      ctx.args.scale = 3;           // float in an xmm register
      ctx.args.crit = false;        // bool
      ctx.this.Gold = 5;            // an int field
      ctx.this.Name = "Renamed";    // a new string in a reference field
    }"""
    after = """function (ctx) {
      ctx.log(ctx.args.min, ctx.this.Gold, ctx.this.Name, ctx.static("Game.Hero.Instances"));
      return ctx.result + ctx.call("Game.Hero:get_Count");
    }"""
    try:
        worker.start()
        first = worker.add_hook(MethodHookSpec(_ROLL, _method_transform(before), phase="before"))
        second = worker.add_hook(MethodHookSpec(_ROLL, _method_transform(after)))
        struct = worker.add_hook(MethodHookSpec(
            _LENGTH, _method_transform("function (ctx) { return ctx.this.x * 10 + ctx.this.z; }")))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: {first, second, struct} <= set(installed) | set(failed))
        assert not failed, failed
        worker.set_debug(second, True)
        time.sleep(0.2)

        # 10 * 3 without crit, plus get_Count (7) after the call
        assert target.send("roll", 5) == (0, 37)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: debug)
        assert not errors, errors
        assert debug[0]["logs"] == ["10 5 Renamed 7"]
        assert target.send("hero", 0) == (0, 5 * 100 + len("Renamed"))
        # A struct's method: ``this`` is its data. x 4, y 1, z 2 -> 4 * 10 + 2
        assert target.send("length", 4) == (0, 42)

        removed = []
        worker.hook_removed.connect(removed.append)
        for hook_id in (first, second, struct):
            worker.remove_hook(hook_id)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: len(removed) == 3)
        assert target.send("roll", 5) == (0, 15)
        assert target.send("length", 4) == (0, 7)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()

```

`tests/test_localization.py`:

```py
"""The translation catalogs: every text in both languages, every agent message translated."""

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CATALOG_DIR = ROOT / "grembyte" / "ui" / "localization"
LANGUAGES = ("en", "de")
# grembyteError('error.…', …) in the agents; also the keys of a ``cond ? 'a' : 'b'``
_AGENT_KEY = re.compile(r"grembyteError\(\s*(?:[^'()]*\?\s*)?'([\w.]+)'(?:\s*:\s*'([\w.]+)')?")
_PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"\{(\w*)\}")


def _catalog(language):
    return json.loads((CATALOG_DIR / f"{language}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


@pytest.fixture(scope="module", name="catalogs")
def _catalogs():
    return {language: _catalog(language) for language in LANGUAGES}


def test_catalogs_have_the_same_keys(catalogs):
    english = set(catalogs["en"])
    for language, catalog in catalogs.items():
        assert sorted(english - set(catalog)) == [], f"missing in {language}.json"
        assert sorted(set(catalog) - english) == [], f"only in {language}.json"


def test_texts_are_not_empty(catalogs):
    for language, catalog in catalogs.items():
        assert [key for key, text in catalog.items() if not text.strip()] == [], language


def test_translations_keep_their_placeholders(catalogs):
    english = catalogs["en"]
    for language, catalog in catalogs.items():
        differing = [key for key, text in catalog.items()
                     if set(_PLACEHOLDER.findall(text)) != set(_PLACEHOLDER.findall(english[key]))]
        assert differing == [], f"placeholders differ in {language}.json"


def test_agent_messages_are_translated(catalogs):
    used = {}
    for script in (ROOT / "grembyte").rglob("*.js"):
        for match in _AGENT_KEY.finditer(script.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            for key in filter(None, match.groups()):
                used.setdefault(key, script.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix())
    assert len(used) > 100  # the pattern still finds the agents' messages
    for language, catalog in catalogs.items():
        missing = {key: script for key, script in used.items() if key not in catalog}
        assert missing == {}, f"agent messages missing in {language}.json"

```

`tests/test_logs.py`:

```py
"""The application log: files, counting, hooks for what nothing caught."""

import subprocess
import sys
import threading

import pytest
from PySide6.QtCore import QObject, QThread, Signal, qWarning  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from grembyte.core import logs
from grembyte.ui.widgets.log_view import read_log

from tests.test_hooks import _wait_for, fixture_qt_app, linux_only  # pylint: disable=unused-import


@pytest.fixture(name="log_file")
def fixture_log_file(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("GREMBYTE_LOG_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    path = logs.setup()
    hooks = sys.excepthook, threading.excepthook
    yield path
    sys.excepthook, threading.excepthook = hooks
    logs.teardown()


def _text(path):
    for handler in logs.log.handlers:
        handler.flush()
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_setup_writes_to_the_state_directory(log_file, tmp_path):
    assert log_file == tmp_path / "grembyte.log" == logs.log_path()
    logs.log.getChild("test").info("hello %s", "log")
    text = _text(log_file)

    assert "--- Grembyte started" in (tmp_path / "crash.log").read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_errors_are_counted_and_announced(log_file):
    heard = []
    logs.subscribe(lambda: heard.append(logs.error_count()))
    logs.log.warning("only a warning")
    assert logs.error_count() == 0
    logs.log.error("a real one")
    assert logs.error_count() == 1 and heard == [1]
    assert "ERROR    [MainThread] grembyte: a real one" in _text(log_file)


def test_exceptions_nothing_caught_are_logged_not_fatal(log_file, qt_app):
    reported = []
    logs.on_unhandled(lambda summary, details: reported.append((summary, details)))
    logs.install_exception_hooks()

    class Failing(QThread):
        def run(self):
            raise ValueError("broken worker")

    worker = Failing()
    worker.start()
    assert worker.wait(2000)
    thread = threading.Thread(target=lambda: 1 / 0, name="helper")
    thread.start()
    thread.join()
    summaries = [summary for summary, _details in reported]
    assert summaries == ["ValueError: broken worker", "ZeroDivisionError: division by zero"]
    assert "raise ValueError" in reported[0][1]
    text = _text(log_file)
    assert "CRITICAL [helper] grembyte: Unhandled exception in thread helper" in text
    assert "Traceback" in text and logs.error_count() == 2


def test_worker_failures_are_logged_once_per_interval(log_file):
    class Worker(QObject):
        worker_failed = Signal(str)
        hook_failed = Signal(int, str)
        progress = Signal(int)

        pid = 4711

    worker = Worker()
    logs.log_failures(worker)
    worker.worker_failed.emit("target gone")
    worker.worker_failed.emit("target gone")  # the same: once is enough
    worker.hook_failed.emit(3, "bad script")
    worker.progress.emit(5)
    text = _text(log_file)
    assert text.count("worker_failed (pid 4711): target gone") == 1
    assert "hook_failed (pid 4711): 3 | bad script" in text
    assert "progress" not in text


def test_qt_messages_go_to_the_log(log_file):
    qWarning("something odd")
    assert "WARNING  [MainThread] grembyte.qt: something odd" in _text(log_file)


def test_a_crash_leaves_python_stacks_and_is_reported_next_time(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("GREMBYTE_LOG_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    # Not dumpable (prctl PR_SET_DUMPABLE): the crash leaves no core dump
    # and no crash report of the desktop at every test run.
    no_core_dump = ("import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL(None).prctl(4, 0); "
                    if sys.platform == "linux" else "")
    crash = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c",
         no_core_dump + "import os; from grembyte.core import logs; logs.setup(); os.abort()"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
    assert crash.returncode != 0
    stacks = (tmp_path / "crash.log").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "Fatal Python error: Aborted" in stacks and "<string>" in stacks

    path = logs.setup()
    try:
        assert logs.error_count() == 1
        assert "The previous run of Grembyte crashed" in _text(path)
    finally:
        logs.teardown()
    # This run did not crash: the next start is quiet.
    logs.setup()
    try:
        assert logs.error_count() == 0
    finally:
        logs.teardown()


def test_read_log_keeps_problems_with_their_tracebacks(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "grembyte.log"
    path.write_text(
        "2026-10-18 10:00:00,000 INFO     [MainThread] grembyte: started\n"
        "2026-10-18 10:00:01,000 CRITICAL [MainThread] grembyte: Unhandled exception\n"
        "Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
        "ValueError: x\n"
        "2026-10-18 10:00:02,000 INFO     [MainThread] grembyte: more\n"
        "2026-10-18 10:00:03,000 WARNING  [w] grembyte.HookWorker: hook_failed (pid 1): y\n",
        encoding="utf-8")
    assert len(read_log(path)) == 6
    assert read_log(path, problems_only=True) == [
        "2026-10-18 10:00:01,000 CRITICAL [MainThread] grembyte: Unhandled exception",
        "Traceback (most recent call last):", "ValueError: x",
        "2026-10-18 10:00:03,000 WARNING  [w] grembyte.HookWorker: hook_failed (pid 1): y"]
    assert read_log(path, max_lines=2) == read_log(path)[-2:]
    assert read_log(tmp_path / "missing.log") is None


def test_error_dialog_shows_one_box_and_counts_the_rest(log_file, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.log_view import ErrorReporter

    translations = json.loads(
        (Path(logs.__file__).parent.parent / "ui" / "localization" / "de.json").read_text("utf-8"))
    opened = []
    reporter = ErrorReporter(translations, lambda: opened.append(True))
    logs.report_unhandled(*_exc_info(KeyError("first")))

    box = reporter._box

    logs.report_unhandled(*_exc_info(KeyError("second")))

    next(button for button in box.buttons()
         if button.text() == translations["log.open"]).click()
    _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: reporter._box is None)
    assert opened == [True]


def _exc_info(error):
    try:
        raise error
    except KeyError:
        return sys.exc_info()

@linux_only
def test_a_log_whose_folder_was_deleted_is_written_again(tmp_path):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    import logging
    import shutil

    folder = tmp_path / "logs"
    folder.mkdir()
    handler = logs.ReopeningFileHandler(folder / "grembyte.log", encoding="utf-8")
    logger = logging.getLogger("grembyte.test.folder")
    logger.propagate = False
    logger.addHandler(handler)
    try:
        logger.warning("before")
        shutil.rmtree(folder)
        logger.warning("after the folder was deleted")
    finally:
        logger.removeHandler(handler)
        handler.close()
    assert (folder / "grembyte.log").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "after the folder was deleted\n"


def test_a_reopening_log_still_rotates(tmp_path):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    import logging

    handler = logs.ReopeningFileHandler(tmp_path / "small.log", maxBytes=200, backupCount=2,
                                        encoding="utf-8")
    logger = logging.getLogger("grembyte.test.rotation")
    logger.propagate = False
    logger.addHandler(handler)
    try:
        for number in range(30):
            logger.warning("line %02d of a log that is rotated now and then", number)
    finally:
        logger.removeHandler(handler)
        handler.close()
    assert sorted(path.name for path in tmp_path.iterdir()) == [
        "small.log", "small.log.1", "small.log.2"]
    assert "line 29" in (tmp_path / "small.log").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
```

`tests/test_memory.py`:

```py
"""Tests for process memory helpers."""

import builtins
import struct

import pytest

from grembyte.core import memory as memory_module
from grembyte.core.memory import write_process_value
from grembyte.platform import linux


class FakeMemory:
    def __init__(self, base_address, contents):
        self.base_address = base_address
        self.contents = contents
        self.position = 0

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_args):
        return None

    def seek(self, address):
        self.position = address - self.base_address

    def write(self, value):
        end = self.position + len(value)
        self.contents[self.position:end] = value
        self.position = end
        return len(value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("value_type", "value", "expected"),
    [
        ("int32", "0x2a", 42),
        ("double", "3.5", 3.5),
        ("uint8", "255", 255),
        ("int16", "-2", -2),
    ],
)
def test_write_process_value_encodes_and_writes_typed_data(
    monkeypatch, value_type, value, expected
):
    base_address = 0x1000
    contents = bytearray(16)
    fake_memory = FakeMemory(base_address, contents)
    opened = []

    def fake_open(path, mode, buffering):
        opened.append((path, mode, buffering))
        return fake_memory

    monkeypatch.setattr(builtins, "open", fake_open)
    # The fake is /proc: use the Linux backend on every system.
    monkeypatch.setattr(memory_module, "ProcessMemory", linux.ProcessMemory)

    result = write_process_value(123, base_address + 4, value, value_type)

    formats = {"int32": "<i", "double": "<d", "uint8": "<B", "int16": "<h"}
    expected_bytes = struct.pack(formats[value_type], expected)
    assert result == expected
    assert contents[4:4 + len(expected_bytes)] == expected_bytes
    assert opened == [("/proc/123/mem", "r+b", 0)]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("value", "value_type"),
    [("invalid", "int32"), ("2147483648", "int32"), ("1", "unknown"),
     ("256", "uint8"), ("-1", "uint32")],
)
def test_write_process_value_rejects_invalid_input(value, value_type):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        write_process_value(123, 0x1000, value, value_type)
```

```py
"""Categories of writable memory for the pointer scan (grembyte/core/memory_regions.py)."""

import os
import subprocess
import sys

from grembyte.core import memory_regions
from grembyte.core.memory_regions import (
    ENGINE,
    GAME,
    HEAP,
    MAIN,
    STACK,
    SYSTEM,
    UNKNOWN,
    Region,
    classify,
    module_categories,
    selection,
    stack_ranges,
    summarize,
)
from grembyte.platform import Mapping, read_mappings
from grembyte.platform.linux import thread_stack_pointers
from tests.test_hooks import linux_only


def _module(start, end, path, writable=True, name=None):
    return Mapping(start, end, "rw-p" if writable else "r-xp", path,
                   name or os.path.basename(path.replace("\\", "/")), writable)


def _anonymous(start, end, permissions="rw-p", path=""):
    return Mapping(start, end, permissions, path, None, permissions.startswith("rw"))


_PROTON = "/home/me/.steam/steam/steamapps/common"
_PROTON_WINE = "/home/me/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/Proton 9.0/files/lib/wine/x86_64-windows"


def test_modules_of_a_proton_game_are_sorted_by_who_wrote_them():
    game = f"{_PROTON}/Baldurs Gate Enhanced Edition"
    mappings = [
        _module(0x140000000, 0x140001000, f"{game}/Baldur.exe", writable=False),
        _module(0x140001000, 0x140002000, f"{game}/Baldur.exe"),
        _module(0x180000000, 0x180001000, f"{game}/plugins/lua51.dll"),
        _module(0x181000000, 0x181001000, f"{game}/steam_api64.dll"),
        _module(0x182000000, 0x182001000, f"{game}/fmod.dll"),
        _module(0x6ffff0000000, 0x6ffff0001000, f"{_PROTON_WINE}/ntdll.dll"),
        _module(0x6ffff1000000, 0x6ffff1001000,
                "/home/me/.steam/steam/steamapps/compatdata/228280/pfx/drive_c/windows/"
                "system32/vcruntime140.dll"),
        _module(0x7f0000000000, 0x7f0000001000, "/usr/lib64/libc.so.6"),
        _module(0x7f1000000000, 0x7f1000001000,
                "/home/me/.local/share/Steam/ubuntu12_64/gameoverlayrenderer.so"),
    ]

    assert module_categories(mappings, "Baldur.exe") == {
        "Baldur.exe": MAIN,
        "lua51.dll": GAME,
        "steam_api64.dll": ENGINE,
        "fmod.dll": ENGINE,
        "ntdll.dll": SYSTEM,
        "vcruntime140.dll": SYSTEM,
        "libc.so.6": SYSTEM,
        "gameoverlayrenderer.so": UNKNOWN,
    }


def test_engine_runtimes_count_as_engine_wherever_they_lie():
    game = "/games/PillarsOfEternity"
    mappings = [
        _module(0x400000, 0x401000, f"{game}/PillarsOfEternity"),
        _module(0x500000, 0x501000, f"{game}/PillarsOfEternity_Data/Mono/x86_64/libmono.so"),
        _module(0x600000, 0x601000, f"{game}/UnityPlayer.so"),
        _module(0x700000, 0x701000, f"{game}/GameAssembly.so"),
        _module(0x800000, 0x801000, f"{game}/Engine/Binaries/UE4-CoreUObject-Win64-Shipping.dll"),
    ]

    categories = module_categories(mappings, "PillarsOfEternity")

    assert categories["PillarsOfEternity"] == MAIN
    assert {categories[name] for name in categories if name != "PillarsOfEternity"} == {ENGINE}


def test_windows_paths_and_names_ignore_case():
    mappings = [
        _module(0x140000000, 0x140001000, "C:\\Games\\Avowed\\Avowed.exe"),
        _module(0x180000000, 0x180001000, "C:\\Games\\Avowed\\bin\\Oodle.dll"),
        _module(0x7ff800000000, 0x7ff800001000, "C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\KERNEL32.DLL"),

def test_without_a_main_module_nothing_is_a_game_module():
    mappings = [_module(0x400000, 0x401000, "/games/x/game"),
                _module(0x500000, 0x501000, "/games/x/libgame.so")]

    assert set(module_categories(mappings, None).values()) == {UNKNOWN}


def test_stacks_are_the_memory_around_each_stack_pointer():
    # Linux merges neighbouring anonymous mappings, stacks and heap alike
    merged = _anonymous(0x7f0000000000, 0x7f0004000000)
    mappings = [merged, _anonymous(0x7ffe00000000, 0x7ffe00100000, path="[stack]")]
    pointer = 0x7f0001000000

    assert stack_ranges(mappings, [pointer, pointer + 0x100, 0x1234]) == [
        (pointer - memory_regions.STACK_BELOW, pointer + 0x100 + memory_regions.STACK_ABOVE),
        (0x7ffe00000000, 0x7ffe00100000),
    ]
    # ... and never reach beyond their mapping
    assert stack_ranges([merged], [merged.end - 8]) == [
        (merged.end - 8 - memory_regions.STACK_BELOW, merged.end)]


def test_windows_stacks_lie_right_above_their_guard_page():
    mappings = [
        _anonymous(0x1000000, 0x1001000, "---p"),   # guard page
        _anonymous(0x1001000, 0x1010000),           # committed stack
        _anonymous(0x2000000, 0x2100000),           # heap
        _anonymous(0x2100000, 0x2200000, "---p"),   # its reserved rest
    ]

    assert stack_ranges(mappings, None) == [(0x1001000, 0x1010000)]


def test_classify_splits_the_heap_around_stacks():
    mappings = [
        _module(0x400000, 0x401000, "/games/x/game", writable=False),
        _module(0x401000, 0x402000, "/games/x/game"),
        _anonymous(0x1000000, 0x1400000),
        _module(0x7f0000000000, 0x7f0000001000, "/usr/lib64/libc.so.6"),
    ]
    pointer = 0x1200000

    regions = classify(mappings, "game", [pointer])

    low = pointer - memory_regions.STACK_BELOW
    high = pointer + memory_regions.STACK_ABOVE
    assert regions == [
        Region(0x401000, 0x402000, MAIN, "game"),
        Region(0x1000000, low, HEAP),
        Region(low, high, STACK),
        Region(high, 0x1400000, HEAP),
        Region(0x7f0000000000, 0x7f0000001000, SYSTEM, "libc.so.6"),
    ]
    summary = summarize(regions)
    assert summary[STACK].size == high - low
    assert summary[HEAP].size == 0x400000 - (high - low)
    assert summary[MAIN].modules == ["game"] and summary[SYSTEM].modules == ["libc.so.6"]

    ranges, modules = selection(regions, {MAIN, HEAP})
    assert ranges == [(0x401000, 0x402000), (0x1000000, low), (high, 0x1400000)]
    assert modules == {"game"}
    # the heap is always read
    assert selection(regions, {MAIN})[0] == ranges
    assert selection(regions, {MAIN, STACK, SYSTEM})[0] == [
        (0x401000, 0x402000), (0x1000000, 0x1400000), (0x7f0000000000, 0x7f0000001000)]


_WAITING_THREADS = """
import threading, sys
stop = threading.Event()
for _ in range(3):
    threading.Thread(target=stop.wait, daemon=True).start()
print("ready", flush=True)
sys.stdin.readline()
"""


@linux_only
def test_thread_stack_pointers_lie_on_the_threads_stacks():
    # A process of its own: the test process has threads that come and go
    child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", _WAITING_THREADS],
                             stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    try:
        assert child.stdout.readline().strip() == "ready"
        pointers = thread_stack_pointers(child.pid)
        stacks = stack_ranges(read_mappings(child.pid), pointers)
    finally:
        child.communicate("\n")

    assert len(pointers) == 4  # the main thread and the three waiting ones
    assert all(any(start <= pointer < end for start, end in stacks) for pointer in pointers)


@linux_only
def test_thread_stack_pointers_of_a_fake_process(tmp_path):
    tasks = tmp_path / "7" / "task"
    for tid, text in (("7", "running\n"), ("8", "202 0x1 0x2 0x0 0x0 0x0 0x0 0x7ffd1000 0x401000\n"),
                      ("9", "-1 0x7ffd2000 0x401000\n")):
        (tasks / tid).mkdir(parents=True)
        (tasks / tid / "syscall").write_text(text)

    assert sorted(thread_stack_pointers(7, tmp_path)) == [0x7ffd1000, 0x7ffd2000]
    assert not thread_stack_pointers(8, tmp_path)
```

```py
"""Tests for the memory viewer and its memory helpers."""

# pylint: disable=protected-access

import ctypes
import os
import struct

import pytest

from grembyte.core.memory import (
    UnknownModuleError,
    describe_address,
    parse_address,
    parse_chain,
    read_memory,
)
from grembyte.core.pointer import PointerChain
from grembyte.platform import read_mappings
from grembyte.platform.linux import parse_maps


@pytest.fixture(name="qt_app", scope="module")
def fixture_qt_app():
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    os.environ.setdefault("QT_QPA_PLATFORM", "offscreen")
    from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

    return QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])


def _unmapped_gap():
    """Return an address right behind a readable mapping that is followed by a gap."""
    mappings = read_mappings(os.getpid())
    return next(
        current.end for current, following in zip(mappings, mappings[1:])
        if following.start > current.end and "r" in current.permissions
        and not current.path.startswith("[v")
    )


def test_read_memory_reads_own_process():
    buffer = ctypes.create_string_buffer(b"grembyte-ok!", 16)

    data, readable = read_memory(os.getpid(), ctypes.addressof(buffer), 12)

    assert data == b"grembyte-ok!"
    assert all(readable)


def test_read_memory_marks_unmapped_bytes():
    end = _unmapped_gap()

    data, readable = read_memory(os.getpid(), end - 4, 8)

    assert list(readable) == [1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    assert data[4:] == bytes(4)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("text", "expected"),
    [("0x10", 0x10), ("ff", 0xFF), (" 0X7F00 ", 0x7F00), ("game+0x1f0", 0x401F0),
     ("libfoo.so.6 + 10", 0x7F0010),
     ("0x7f55e9339000+0x244", 0x7F55E9339244), ("0x1000 + 0x20 - 8", 0x1018),
     ("game+0x1f0+0x10", 0x40200), ("game-1+0x10", 0x500010), ("game-0x10", 0x3FFF0)],
)
def test_parse_address(text, expected):
    mappings = parse_maps([
        "40000-41000 r-xp 00000000 08:01 1 /opt/game/game",
        "7f0000-7f1000 r-xp 00000000 08:01 2 /usr/lib/libfoo.so.6",
        "500000-501000 r-xp 00000000 08:01 3 /opt/game/game-1",
    ])

    assert parse_address(text, mappings) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", ["", "xyz", "other+0x10", "0x10-0x20", "0x10+", "+0x10"])
def test_parse_address_rejects_invalid_input(text):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        parse_address(text, [])


def test_parse_address_names_the_unknown_module():
    with pytest.raises(UnknownModuleError) as error:
        parse_address("other.so+0x10+0x4", [])
    assert error.value.module == "other.so"


def test_describe_address():
    mappings = parse_maps([
        "40000-41000 r-xp 00000000 08:01 1 /opt/game/game",
        "41000-42000 rw-p 00001000 08:01 1 /opt/game/game",
        "50000-60000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0 [heap]",
    ])

    assert describe_address(mappings, 0x41010) == "game+0x1010 (rw-p)"
    assert describe_address(mappings, 0x50020) == "[heap]+0x20 (rw-p)"
    assert describe_address(mappings, 0x45000) is None


def test_viewer_shows_bytes_values_and_changes(qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from PySide6.QtCore import Qt  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

    from grembyte.ui.localization import load_translations
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.memory_view import BYTES_PER_ROW, MemoryViewerDialog

    buffer = (ctypes.c_ubyte * 64)()
    address = ctypes.addressof(buffer)
    struct.pack_into("<i", buffer, 0, 1637)
    dialog = MemoryViewerDialog(load_translations("de"), os.getpid(), address)
    dialog.live.setChecked(False)  # refreshed by the test
    dialog.show()
    qt_app.processEvents()
    try:
        model = dialog.model
        column = address % BYTES_PER_ROW
        cell = lambda offset: model.index(  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment
            (column + offset) // BYTES_PER_ROW, (column + offset) % BYTES_PER_ROW)

        assert model.base == address - column
        assert model.rows > 1
        assert dialog.selected_address() == address
        assert model.data(cell(0)) == "65" and model.data(cell(1)) == "06"
        assert dialog.value_labels["int32"].text() == "1637"
        assert "[anon]" in dialog.selection_label.text() or "+" in dialog.selection_label.text()

        # A byte that changes is highlighted.
        buffer[1] = 0x07
        dialog.refresh()
        assert model.data(cell(1)) == "07"
        assert model.data(cell(1), Qt.ItemDataRole.ForegroundRole) is not None
        assert model.data(cell(2), Qt.ItemDataRole.ForegroundRole) is None
        assert dialog.value_labels["int32"].text() == str(1637 + 0x100)

        # Scrolling and typed addresses.
        dialog.scroll_rows(2)
        assert model.base == address - column + 2 * BYTES_PER_ROW
        dialog.address_input.setText(hex(address + 0x20))
        dialog._go_to_input()
        assert dialog.selected_address() == address + 0x20
        dialog.address_input.setText("kein-modul+0x10")
        dialog._go_to_input()
        assert "kein-modul" in dialog.status_label.text()
    finally:
        dialog.close()


def test_viewer_shows_unreadable_memory(qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    from grembyte.ui.widgets.memory_view import BYTES_PER_ROW, MemoryViewerDialog

        assert "beendet" in dialog.status_label.text()

        dialog.close()


def test_address_dialog_parses_hex_and_module_addresses(qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,unused-argument
    from grembyte.ui.localization import load_translations
    from grembyte.ui.main_window import AddressInputDialog

    translations = load_translations("de")
    mappings = parse_maps(["40000-41000 r-xp 00000000 08:01 1 /opt/game/game"])
    dialog = AddressInputDialog(lambda text: parse_address(text, mappings), "int16",
                                translations=translations)
    assert dialog.type_combo.currentData() == "int16"

    dialog._accept()

    dialog._accept()

    dialog.address_input.setText("game+0x1f0")
    dialog.description_input.setText("Gold")
    dialog._accept()
    assert dialog.result_entry == ("Gold", 0x401F0, "int16")


_GAME_MAPS = ["40000-41000 r-xp 00000000 08:01 1 /opt/game/game",
              "41000-42000 rw-p 00001000 08:01 1 /opt/game/game"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text, expected", [
    ("game+0x1f0 -> 0x28 -> 0x0", PointerChain("game", 0x1F0, (0x28, 0))),
    ("game+0x1f0=>28=>0", PointerChain("game", 0x1F0, (0x28, 0))),
    ("game+0x1f0 : 0x28 : -8", PointerChain("game", 0x1F0, (0x28, -8))),
    ("game+0x1f0 → 0x28 → 0x0", PointerChain("game", 0x1F0, (0x28, 0))),  # as Grembyte shows it
    ("game+0x100+0xf0 -> +0x28", PointerChain("game", 0x1F0, (0x28,))),
    ("0x411f0 -> 0x28", PointerChain("game", 0x11F0, (0x28,))),  # an address in the module
    ("game+0x1f0", PointerChain("game", 0x1F0, ())),
])
def test_parse_chain(text, expected):
    assert parse_chain(text, parse_maps(_GAME_MAPS)) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", ["", "game+0x1f0 ->", "-> 0x28", "game+0x1f0 -> 0x28 -> zz",
                                  "game+0x1f0 -> -> 8", "0x90000 -> 0x28"])
def test_parse_chain_rejects_what_is_no_chain(text):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        parse_chain(text, parse_maps(_GAME_MAPS))


def test_parse_chain_names_the_unknown_module():
    with pytest.raises(UnknownModuleError) as raised:
        parse_chain("other.so+0x10 -> 0x8", parse_maps(_GAME_MAPS))
    assert raised.value.module == "other.so"


def test_pointer_chain_dialog_shows_where_the_chain_leads(qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,unused-argument,protected-access
    from grembyte.ui.localization import load_translations
    from grembyte.ui.main_window import PointerChainDialog

    translations = load_translations("en")
    mappings = parse_maps(_GAME_MAPS)
    leads = {PointerChain("game", 0x1F0, (0x28, 0)): 0x7F0010}

    def resolve(text):
        chain = parse_chain(text, mappings)
        return chain, leads.get(chain)

    dialog = PointerChainDialog(resolve, "int32", translations=translations)
    assert dialog.type_combo.currentData() == "int32"

    dialog.chain_input.setText("game+0x1f0 ->")
    assert "Not a pointer chain" in dialog.result_label.text()
    dialog._accept()
    assert dialog.result_entry is None

    dialog.chain_input.setText("other+0x10 -> 8")
    assert "“other”" in dialog.result_label.text()

    dialog.chain_input.setText("game+0x1f0 -> 0x40")
    assert "leads nowhere right now" in dialog.result_label.text()

    dialog.chain_input.setText("game+0x1f0 => 0x28 : 0")
    assert dialog.result_label.text() == "game+0x1f0 → 0x28 → 0x0 leads to 0x7F0010 now."
    dialog.description_input.setText("Strength")
    dialog._accept()
    assert dialog.result_entry == ("Strength", PointerChain("game", 0x1F0, (0x28, 0)),
                                   0x7F0010, "int32")
```
