```py
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_method_hook_before_the_call_changes_arguments_and_fields(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.method_hooks import MethodHookSpec, MethodHookWorker

    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path))
    worker = MethodHookWorker(target.pid)
    installed, failed, errors, events, debug = {}, {}, {}, [], []
    worker.hook_installed.connect(installed.__setitem__)
    worker.hook_failed.connect(failed.__setitem__)
    worker.transform_error.connect(errors.__setitem__)
    worker.hook_events.connect(events.extend)
    worker.hook_debug.connect(lambda entries, _dropped: debug.extend(entries))
    before = """function (ctx) {
      ctx.args.min = 10;          // int in a register
      ctx.args.scale = 3;         // float in xmm1
      ctx.args.crit = false;      // bool
      ctx.args.roll = 7;          // ref int: the caller's variable
      ctx.this.Health = 5;        // a field of the instance
      return 1000;                // ignored before the call
    }"""
    after = """function (ctx) {
      ctx.log(ctx.phase, ctx.args.min, ctx.args.scale, ctx.args.crit, ctx.this.Health);
    }"""
    try:
        worker.start()
        first = worker.add_hook(MethodHookSpec(_ROLL_DAMAGE, _method_transform(before),
                                               phase="before"))
        second = worker.add_hook(MethodHookSpec(_ROLL_DAMAGE, _method_transform(after)))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: {first, second} <= set(installed) | set(failed))
        assert not failed, failed
        for hook_id in (first, second):
            worker.set_debug(hook_id, True)
        time.sleep(0.2)

        # 10 * 3 without crit; RollDamage itself writes roll = 42 afterwards.
        assert target.send("roll", 5) == (30, 42)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: len(debug) == 2 and events)
        assert not errors
        changed = next(entry for entry in debug if entry["hookId"] == first)
        # Fields are noted when set, arguments once the script is done.
        assert changed["result"] == "Combat.Health=5, min=10, scale=3, crit=false, roll=7"
        assert changed["old"] == "Combat.Health=100, min=5, scale=1.5, crit=true, roll=-1"
        assert not changed["kept"]
        logged = next(entry for entry in debug if entry["hookId"] == second)
        assert logged["logs"] == ["after 10 3 false 5"]

        # A typo in a field name is reported; the call goes on unchanged.
        worker.set_transform(first, _method_transform(
            "function (ctx) { ctx.this.Helth = 5; }"))
        time.sleep(0.2)
        assert target.send("roll", 5) == (15, 42)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: first in errors)
        assert "Game.Combat has no field or property Helth to set" in errors[first]

        # Switched to after the call, the same hook can replace the result.
        worker.set_transform(first, _method_transform(
            "function (ctx) { return ctx.phase === 'after' ? ctx.result * 2 : undefined; }"))
        worker.set_phase(first, "after")
        time.sleep(0.2)
        assert target.send("roll", 5) == (30, 42)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


def test_hook_dialog_chooses_the_phase_of_method_hooks(qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,unused-argument,protected-access
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookDialog

    dialog = HookDialog(translations, "", "", "", method="Health:DoDamage (single)")
    assert dialog.phase_combo.currentData() == "after"
    assert [dialog.phase_combo.itemText(i) for i in range(2)] == [
        "Nach dem Aufruf: Ergebnis ändern", "Vor dem Aufruf: Argumente und Felder ändern"]
    dialog.phase_combo.setCurrentIndex(1)
    dialog._accept()
    assert dialog.phase == "before"

    editing = HookDialog(translations, "", "", "", transform=dialog.transform,
                         method="Health:DoDamage (single)", phase="before")
    assert editing.phase_combo.currentData() == "before"
    # Value hooks have no phase.
    assert not hasattr(HookDialog(translations, "0x1000", "int32", "game+0x10"), "phase_combo")


@requires_target
def test_panel_saves_the_phase_of_method_hooks(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from sqlalchemy import create_engine
    from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

    from grembyte.db import models  # noqa: F401  pylint: disable=unused-import
    from grembyte.db.base import Base
    from grembyte.db.repository.hooks import HookRepository
    from grembyte.features.method_hooks import MethodHookSpec
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    engine = create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'grembyte.db'}")
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    repository = HookRepository(sessionmaker(bind=engine))
    binary = _build(tmp_path)
    process_id = repository.get_or_create_process("target", str(binary))
    script = "function (ctx) { ctx.args.min = 1; }"
    try:
        for restart in (False, True):
            target, panel = _MonoTarget(binary), HookPanel(translations, repository=repository)
            try:
                panel.set_process(target.pid, process_id)
                if not restart:
                    panel.add_method_hook(MethodHookSpec(
                        _ROLL_DAMAGE, _method_transform(script), label="min", phase="before"))
                _wait_for(qt_app, lambda panel=panel: panel.table.rowCount() == 1
                          and panel.table.item(0, 4).text() == "Aktiv")
                assert panel.table.item(0, 1).text() == "C#-Methode · vor Aufruf"
                # min 1: 1 * 1.5 * 2
                assert target.send("roll", 5) == (3, 42)
            finally:
                panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
                target.close()
        assert [hook.phase for hook in repository.list_method_hooks(process_id)] == ["before"]
    finally:
        engine.dispose()


def test_hook_context_menu_offers_what_fits_the_hook(qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,unused-argument,protected-access
    from grembyte.core.pointer import PointerChain
    from grembyte.hooks.engine import HookSpec
    from grembyte.features.method_hooks import MethodHookSpec
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    panel = HookPanel(translations)
    panel._pid = 1234  # a process, but no worker is needed for the menu
    multiply = MultiplyTransform(2)
    panel._hooks = {
        1: {"spec": HookSpec(0x1000, "int32", multiply, trap_pc=0x10)},
        2: {"spec": HookSpec(None, "int32", multiply, write_pc=0x10,
                             pointer=PointerChain("game", 0x10, (0x8,)))},
        3: {"spec": HookSpec(None, "int32", multiply, write_pc=0x10)},
        4: {"kind": "method", "spec": MethodHookSpec(_ROLL_DAMAGE, _method_transform("x => 1"))},
    }
    watched, monitored = [], []
    panel.watch_requested.connect(lambda spec, reads: watched.append((spec, reads)))
    panel.monitor_requested.connect(monitored.append)

    def actions(hook_id):
        menu = panel.context_menu(hook_id)
        return [(a.text(), a.isEnabled()) for a in menu.actions() if not a.isSeparator()], menu

    for hook_id in (1, 2):
        entries, menu = actions(hook_id)
        assert entries == [("Adress-Überwachung (Schreibzugriffe)", True),
                           ("Adress-Überwachung (alle Zugriffe)", True),
                           ("Methoden-Überwachung", False)]
        menu.actions()[1].trigger()
        assert watched[-1] == (panel._hooks[hook_id]["spec"], True)
    # A hook for every address its code writes watches the one it wrote last.
    entries, _menu = actions(3)
    assert entries == [("Adress-Überwachung (Schreibzugriffe) · noch kein Schreibzugriff", False),
                       ("Adress-Überwachung (alle Zugriffe) · noch kein Schreibzugriff", False),
                       ("Methoden-Überwachung", False)]
    panel._hooks[3]["count"] = 0
    panel._hooks[3]["status"] = "active"
    panel._worker = worker = object()
    panel._on_events(worker, [{"hookId": 3, "count": 1,
                             "last": {"old": 1, "new": 2, "result": 4, "address": "0x2000"}}])
    entries, menu = actions(3)
    assert entries[0] == ("Adress-Überwachung (Schreibzugriffe) · zuletzt 0x2000", True)
    menu.actions()[0].trigger()
    spec, reads = watched[-1]
    assert (spec.address, spec.pointer, spec.write_pc, reads) == (0x2000, None, 0x10, False)
    assert panel._hooks[3]["spec"].address is None
    entries, menu = actions(4)
    assert [enabled for _text, enabled in entries] == [False, False, True]
    menu.actions()[-1].trigger()
    assert monitored == [_ROLL_DAMAGE]


def test_catalog_method_from_a_hook_identity():
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.catalog import catalog_method_from_identity

    method = catalog_method_from_identity(_ROLL_DAMAGE)
    assert (method.assembly, method.class_name, method.name, method.parameters) == (
        "Assembly-CSharp", "Game.Combat", "RollDamage",
        "(int,single,string,bool,Game.DamageType,int&)")
    assert method.identity() == _ROLL_DAMAGE


@requires_target
def test_mono_trace_finds_what_a_scenario_calls(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.catalog import CatalogMethod
    from grembyte.features.trace import NEW, SAME, TraceWorker, analyze, recording_calls

    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path))
    worker = TraceWorker(target.pid)
    planned, started, began, recorded, failed = [], [], [], [], []
    worker.planned.connect(planned.append)
    worker.started.connect(lambda methods, info: started.append((methods, info)))
    worker.began.connect(began.append)
    worker.recorded.connect(recorded.append)
    worker.command_failed.connect(lambda action, message: failed.append((action, message)))
    worker.worker_failed.connect(lambda message: failed.append(("worker", message)))

    def record(phase, *commands):
        worker.begin(phase)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: phase in began or failed)
        began.clear()
        for command, value in commands:
            target.send(command, value)
        count = len(recorded)
        worker.finish()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: len(recorded) > count or failed)
        assert not failed
        return recorded[-1]

    try:
        worker.start()
        worker.plan([])
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: planned or failed)
        assert not failed
        # The generic class's definition has no code to trace.
        assert planned[0] == {"methods": 8, "skipped": {"abstract": 0, "native": 0, "generic": 1},
                              "assemblies": ["Assembly-CSharp"]}

        worker.trace([])
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: started or failed)
        assert not failed
        methods, info = started[0]
        assert (info["notCompiled"], info["failed"]) == (0, 0)
        # get_Broken uses a [ComImport] class: compiling it would hang Mono.
        assert info["skipped"]["com"] == 1
        assert sorted(method.name for method in methods) == [
            "AddGold", "CalcDamage", "RollDamage", "Take", "Update", "get_Count",
            "get_IsPartyMember"]
        index = {method.name: i for i, method in enumerate(methods)}

        # The game's frame loop is noise; looting is what we look for.
        baseline = record("baseline", ("tick", 0), ("tick", 0), ("tick", 0))
        assert {int(key): count for key, count in baseline["counts"].items()} == {
            index["Update"]: 3}
        assert baseline["events"] == []
        scenario = record("scenario", ("tick", 0), ("loot", 5), ("tick", 0))
        rows = analyze(scenario, baseline)
        assert [(methods[row.method].name, row.verdict, row.calls) for row in rows] == [
            ("Take", NEW, 1), ("AddGold", NEW, 1), ("Update", SAME, 2)]
        # The sequence leaves out the noise; Take's JIT code calls AddGold.
        calls = recording_calls(scenario)
        assert [methods[call.method].name for call in calls] == ["Take", "AddGold"]
        assert calls[0].caller.startswith("target+0x")
        assert calls[1].caller.startswith("Game.Loot:Take+0x")
        assert calls[0].time <= calls[1].time
        assert calls[0].thread == target.pid

        # Without a baseline everything the scenario called is new.
        assert [row.verdict for row in analyze(scenario)] == [NEW, NEW, NEW]

        # The methods to choose from: the catalog cache has them now.
        found = []
        worker.candidates_found.connect(lambda methods, skipped: found.append((methods, skipped)))
        worker.candidates()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: found or failed)
        assert not failed
        methods, skipped = found[0]
        assert len(methods) == 8 and skipped["generic"] == 1
        assert all(isinstance(method, CatalogMethod) for method in methods)
        assert (tmp_path / "catalog-cache" / "mono" / "Assembly-CSharp").is_dir()
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


def test_trace_analysis_compares_rates_with_the_baseline():
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.trace import MORE, NEW, SAME, analyze

    baseline = {"phase": "baseline", "duration": 2000, "counts": {"0": 20, "1": 20, "2": 1}}
    # one second: method 0 as usual, 1 five times as often, 2 only two more calls
    scenario = {"phase": "scenario", "duration": 1000, "counts": {"0": 11, "1": 50, "2": 3, "3": 4},
                "events": [[3, 1, 10, "a"], [3, 1, 20, "b"]]}
    rows = analyze(scenario, baseline)
    assert [(row.method, row.verdict) for row in rows] == [(3, NEW), (1, MORE), (2, SAME), (0, SAME)]
    assert rows[0].first == 0 and rows[0].baseline_rate == 0
    assert rows[1].factor == 5
    assert [row.notable for row in rows] == [True, True, False, False]


@requires_target
def test_trace_window_shows_what_the_scenario_called(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.trace import TraceDialog

    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path))
    dialog = TraceDialog(translations, target.pid)
    monitored, hooked = [], []
    dialog.monitor_requested.connect(monitored.append)
    dialog.hook_requested.connect(hooked.append)

    def record(button, *commands):
        button.click()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: dialog.recording_label.text()
                  != translations["trace.recording_starting"])
        for command, value in commands:
            target.send(command, value)
        button.click()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: dialog._state == 2)  # ready again

    try:
        assert not dialog.baseline_button.isEnabled()
        dialog.filter_input.setText("game")
        dialog.trace_button.click()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: dialog.methods or "Fehler" in dialog.status_label.text())
        assert "7 Methoden werden beobachtet (1 übersprungen" in dialog.status_label.text()
        assert dialog.trace_button.text() == translations["trace.stop"]

        record(dialog.baseline_button, ("tick", 0), ("tick", 0))
        assert "Grundrauschen: 1 Methoden" in dialog.status_label.text()
        record(dialog.scenario_button, ("tick", 0), ("add", 2), ("tick", 0))
        assert "davon 1 auffällig" in dialog.status_label.text()
        # Update ran like in the baseline: hidden unless asked for
        assert [dialog.row_model.data(dialog.row_model.index(row, 2))
                for row in range(dialog.row_model.rowCount())] == ["Inventory:AddGold"]
        assert dialog.row_model.data(dialog.row_model.index(0, 6)) == "neu"
        dialog.notable_check.setChecked(False)
        assert dialog.row_model.rowCount() == 2
        assert dialog.sequence_model.rowCount() == 1
        assert dialog.sequence_model.data(dialog.sequence_model.index(0, 4)).startswith("target+0x")

        dialog.sequence_view.selectRow(0)
        assert dialog.selection_label.text() == "Game.Inventory:AddGold (int&,int)"
        dialog.monitor_button.click()
        dialog.hook_button.click()
        assert [method.signature for method in monitored + hooked] == [
            "Game.Inventory:AddGold (int&,int)"] * 2

        dialog.trace_button.click()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: dialog.trace_button.text() == translations["trace.start"]
                  and dialog.trace_button.isEnabled())
        assert dialog.status_label.text() == translations["trace.stopped"]
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (103, 0)
    finally:
        dialog.close()
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_trace_dialog_traces_a_preselection(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,unused-argument
    from PySide6.QtCore import Qt  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.trace import TraceDialog

    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path))
    dialog = TraceDialog(translations, target.pid)
    try:
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: dialog.filter_panel.candidates is not None)
        panel = dialog.filter_panel
        total = len(panel.candidates)
        # The progress bar gave way to the count of the choice.
        assert dialog.loading_bar.isHidden() and not dialog.choice_label.isHidden()
        assert dialog.choice_label.text() == translations["trace.filters_count"].format(
            count=total, total=total)
        # Under Wine the dialog refuses more than its limit (here: one method)
        dialog.limit = 1
        dialog.trace_button.click()
        assert dialog.status_label.text() == translations["trace.wine_limit"].format(
            count=total, limit=1)
        assert dialog._state == 0 and not dialog.methods  # idle, nothing hooked

        money = next(row for row in range(panel.list.count())
                     if panel.list.item(row).text().startswith("Geld"))
        panel.list.item(money).setCheckState(Qt.CheckState.Checked)
        assert dialog.choice_label.text().startswith(
            translations["trace.filters_count"].format(count=1, total=total))
        dialog.trace_button.click()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: dialog.methods or "Fehler" in dialog.status_label.text())
        assert [method.signature for method in dialog.methods] == [
            "Game.Inventory:AddGold (int&,int)"]
        assert not panel.isEnabled()  # no changes while tracing
    finally:
        dialog.close()
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_mono_trace_preparation_can_be_cancelled(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.trace import TraceWorker

    # Compiling takes 0.3 s per method here: 2.4 s for all eight.
    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path), slow_ms=300)
    worker = TraceWorker(target.pid)
    progress, started, failed = [], [], []
    worker.progress.connect(
        lambda step, done, total, current: progress.append((step, done, total, current)))
    worker.started.connect(lambda methods, info: started.append(methods))
    worker.command_failed.connect(lambda action, message: failed.append((action, message)))
    try:
        worker.start()
        worker.trace([])
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: any(step == "compile" for step, *_rest in progress))
        assert ("compile", 0, 7, "Game.Inventory:AddGold (int&,int)") in progress
        # Before: reading the methods to choose from
        assert progress[:2] == [("catalog", 0, 1, "Assembly-CSharp"), ("catalog", 1, 1, "")]
        began = time.monotonic()
        worker.cancel()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: failed)
        assert failed == [("start", "cancelled")]
        assert time.monotonic() - began < 1.5
        assert not started
        # The game was not disturbed.
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (101, 0)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        assert worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_sessions_list_workers_and_cut_one_that_hangs(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.trace import TraceWorker
    from grembyte.core.sessions import SESSIONS, TRACE

    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path), slow_ms=300)
    worker = TraceWorker(target.pid)
    # As if the agent did not answer: stopping alone does not end the trace.
    worker.cancel = lambda: None
    progress = []
    worker.progress.connect(lambda step, *_rest: progress.append(step))
    try:
        worker.start()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: any(s.frida_session for s in SESSIONS.sessions(target.pid)))
        [session] = SESSIONS.sessions(target.pid)
        assert (session.kind, session.worker) == (TRACE, worker)

        worker.trace([])  # compiling takes 2.4 s here
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: "compile" in progress)
        SESSIONS.stop(session)
        assert session.stopping is not None and not session.stuck()
        assert not worker.wait(300)
        session.stopping -= 10  # as if asked long ago
        assert session.stuck()

        began = time.monotonic()
        assert SESSIONS.disconnect(session)
        assert worker.wait(5000)
        assert time.monotonic() - began < 2
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: not SESSIONS.sessions(target.pid))
        # The batch thread finished its C code: the game lives on.
        time.sleep(2.5)
        assert target.send("add", 1) == (101, 0)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_agent_answers_while_mono_works_on_a_thread_of_its_own(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.monitor import MethodMonitorWorker
    from grembyte.features.trace import TraceWorker

    # Compiling a method takes 2 s; all sessions share the agent's thread.
    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path), slow_ms=2000)
    monitor = MethodMonitorWorker(target.pid)
    trace = TraceWorker(target.pid)
    added, planned = [], []
    monitor.monitor_added.connect(lambda monitor_id, _info: added.append(time.monotonic()))
    trace.planned.connect(lambda plan: planned.append(time.monotonic()))
    try:
        monitor.start()
        trace.start()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: trace._script is not None)  # pylint: disable=protected-access
        began = time.monotonic()
        monitor.add_monitor({"image": "Assembly-CSharp", "file": None, "token": 0x06000002,
                             "method": "Game.Loot:Take (int&,int)"})
        time.sleep(0.3)  # compiling now
        trace.plan([])
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: planned and added, timeout=10)
        # The trace was answered while the monitor still waited for Mono.
        assert planned[0] - began < 1.5 < added[0] - began
    finally:
        for worker in (monitor, trace):
            worker.requestInterruption()
            worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_hook_panel_logs_scripts_and_acts_on_several_hooks(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from PySide6.QtCore import QUrl  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module
    from grembyte.features.method_hooks import MethodHookSpec
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.hooks import HookPanel

    target, panel = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path)), HookPanel(translations)
    status = lambda row: panel.table.item(row, 4).text()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment
    try:
        panel.set_process(target.pid)
        logger = panel.add_method_hook(MethodHookSpec(_ROLL_DAMAGE, _method_transform(
            "function (ctx) { ctx.log('rolled', ctx.result); ctx.log(ctx.this); }"),
            label="Logger"))
        doubler = panel.add_method_hook(MethodHookSpec(_ROLL_DAMAGE, _method_transform(
            "function (ctx) { return ctx.result * 2; }"), label="Doppelt"))
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status(0) == status(1) == "Aktiv")
        assert panel._hooks[logger]["display_signature"] == (
            "Game.Combat:RollDamage (System.Int32 min,System.Single scale,System.String name,"
            "System.Boolean crit,Game.DamageType type,System.Int32& roll)"
        )

        # What a script logs shows below the table without debug mode.
        assert target.send("roll", 5) == (30, 42)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: (f"#{logger} Logger: rolled 15" in panel.log_view.toPlainText()
                       and "Inspizieren" in panel.log_view.toPlainText()))
        assert panel._debug_window is None
        panel.log_view.anchorClicked.emit(QUrl("inspect:0"))
        inspector = panel._method_inspections.inspectors[-1]
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: not inspector._pending and inspector.table.rowCount() > 0)
        assert inspector._type_name == "Game.Combat"

        # Both selected: Edit is for one hook only; debug, pause and remove act on both.
        panel.table.selectAll()
        assert panel._selected_hook_ids() == [logger, doubler]
        assert not panel.btn_edit.isEnabled() and panel.btn_debug.isEnabled()
        panel.btn_debug.click()
        assert all(panel._hooks[hook_id]["debug"] for hook_id in (logger, doubler))
        assert panel.btn_debug.isChecked() and panel._debug_window.isVisible()
        panel.btn_debug.click()
        assert not any(panel._hooks[hook_id]["debug"] for hook_id in (logger, doubler))

        panel.btn_toggle.click()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status(0) == status(1) == "Pausiert")
        assert panel.btn_toggle.text() == translations["hooks.resume"]
        time.sleep(0.2)
        assert target.send("roll", 5) == (15, 42)
        panel.btn_toggle.click()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: status(0) == status(1) == "Aktiv")

        # A script's error goes to the log as well.
        panel.table.selectRow(1)
        assert panel.btn_edit.isEnabled()
        panel._method_worker.set_transform(doubler, _method_transform(
            "function (ctx) { return ctx.nothing.here; }"))
        time.sleep(0.2)
        target.send("roll", 5)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: f"#{doubler} Doppelt: Fehler:" in panel.log_view.toPlainText())

        panel.table.selectAll()
        panel.btn_remove.click()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: panel.table.rowCount() == 0)
        assert target.send("roll", 5) == (15, 42)
    finally:
        if panel._debug_window is not None:
            panel._debug_window.close()
        panel.shutdown(timeout_ms=None)
        target.close()


def test_monitor_marks_static_methods(qt_app, translations):  # pylint: disable=unused-argument
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    import dataclasses

    from PySide6.QtCore import Qt  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module
    from grembyte.features.catalog import CatalogMethod
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.method_monitor import CallLogModel, signature_text

    count = CatalogMethod("Assembly-CSharp", "Game.Combat", "get_Count", "()", "System.Int32",
                          True, 0x06000009, "Game.Combat:get_Count ()")
    assert signature_text(count) == "static () → System.Int32"
    assert signature_text(dataclasses.replace(count, static=False)) == "() → System.Int32"

    # A static method's calls say why "this" is empty; an instance method's stay empty.
    model = CallLogModel(translations)
    model.static.add(1)
    model.append([{"monitorId": 1, "args": []}, {"monitorId": 2, "args": []}])
    assert model.data(model.index(0, 3)) == "(statisch)"
    assert model.data(model.index(0, 3), Qt.ItemDataRole.ForegroundRole) is not None
    assert model.data(model.index(1, 3)) == ""
    assert model.data(model.index(1, 3), Qt.ItemDataRole.ForegroundRole) is None


def _hero_health(pid):
    """Where Game.Loop.Current (the last Game.Combat made) keeps its Health."""
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.managed_statics import read_static_areas
    from grembyte.platform import ProcessMemory

    areas = read_static_areas(pid, {"Assembly-CSharp": ["Game.Loop"]})
    with ProcessMemory(pid) as memory:
        return memory.read_pointer(areas[0].address, 8) + 0x20


@requires_target
def test_static_areas_of_marked_assemblies(tmp_path):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.core.pointer import chain_bases, managed_bases
    from grembyte.features.managed_statics import StaticArea, read_static_areas
    from grembyte.platform import ProcessMemory, read_mappings

    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path))
    try:
        target.send("roll", 3)
        areas = read_static_areas(target.pid, {"Assembly-CSharp": None, "Missing": None})

        # Generic definitions and classes without static data are left out.
        assert [(a.assembly, a.class_name, a.size, a.fields) for a in areas] == [
            ("Assembly-CSharp", "Game.Combat", 4, (("Instances", 0),)),
            ("Assembly-CSharp", "Game.Loop", 8, (("Current", 0),))]
        combat = areas[0]
        assert isinstance(combat, StaticArea) and combat.name == "mono:Assembly-CSharp:Game.Combat"
        assert combat.field_at(0) == "Instances" and combat.field_at(4) is None
        with ProcessMemory(target.pid) as memory:
            assert int.from_bytes(memory.read(combat.address, 4), "little") == 7
        # on the heap, in no module
        assert not any(m.start <= combat.address < m.end and m.module is not None
                       for m in read_mappings(target.pid))
        # remembered for this run of the game
        assert managed_bases(target.pid) == {area.name: area.address for area in areas}
        assert chain_bases(target.pid, read_mappings(target.pid))[combat.name] == combat.address
    finally:
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_pointer_scan_starts_in_static_fields_and_filters_after_a_restart(tmp_path):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access
    from grembyte.core import memory_regions, pointer
    from grembyte.platform import main_module
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.pointer_scan import PointerScanWorker

    binary = _build(tmp_path)
    expected = PointerChain("mono:Assembly-CSharp:Game.Loop", 0, (0x20,))
    first = _MonoTarget(binary)
    try:
        first.send("roll", 3)
        health = _hero_health(first.pid)

        def scan(categories):
            worker = PointerScanWorker(
                first.pid, health, max_depth=2, max_offset=0x100, categories=categories,
                main_module=main_module(first.pid), assemblies=("Assembly-CSharp",))
            return worker, worker._scan()

        worker, chains = scan({memory_regions.ASSEMBLIES, memory_regions.HEAP})
        assert expected in chains
        assert all(chain.module.startswith("mono:") for chain in chains)
        assert [area.class_name for area in worker.static_areas] == ["Game.Combat", "Game.Loop"]
        assert expected.text() == "[Assembly-CSharp] Game.Loop+0x0 → 0x20"
        # Without the category the static data is no chain base.
        _worker, chains_without = scan(memory_regions.DEFAULT_CATEGORIES)
        assert expected not in chains_without
    finally:
        first.close()

    second = _MonoTarget(binary)
    try:
        second.send("roll", 5)
        second.send("roll", 6)  # another Hero: the static field moved on
        health = _hero_health(second.pid)
        # The filter looks the bases up itself for the new run of the game.
        pointer._managed_bases.pop(second.pid, None)
        assert expected in PointerScanWorker(second.pid, health, chains=chains)._filter()
    finally:
        second.close()

@pytest.mark.parametrize("generation", ["begin", "blocks", "unity6"])
@requires_target
def test_object_browser_reads_live_objects_with_the_world_stopped(tmp_path, qt_app, generation):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.scripts import ScriptWorker

    defines = {"begin": (), "blocks": ("FAKE_LIVENESS_BLOCKS",),
               "unity6": ("FAKE_LIVENESS_BLOCKS", "FAKE_LIVENESS_UNITY6")}[generation]
    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path, defines))
    worker = ScriptWorker(target.pid)
    answers, failed = [], []
    worker.classes_browsed.connect(lambda _request, answer: answers.append(answer))
    worker.browse_failed.connect(lambda _request, message: failed.append(message))
    worker.instances_browsed.connect(lambda _request, answer: answers.append(answer))
    worker.instances_failed.connect(lambda _request, message: failed.append(message))

    def ask(request, *args):
        answers.clear()
        failed.clear()
        getattr(worker, request)(*args)
        # On Unity's main thread: when the game next runs a script method
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: target.send("tick", 0) and (answers or failed))
        assert not failed, failed
        return answers[0]

    try:
        target.send("spawn", 0)
        worker.start()
        # From the statics (Game.Loop.Current, a plain Game.Inventory) and
        # from the Unity objects; the marks in the vtables masked
        listed = ask("browse_classes")
        classes = {entry["name"]: entry for entry in listed["classes"]}
        assert {name: (entry["count"], entry["package"], entry["role"])
                for name, entry in classes.items()} == {
            "Game.Combat": (2, "Assembly-CSharp", None),
            "Game.Inventory": (1, "Assembly-CSharp", None),
            "UnityEngine.GameObject": (2, "UnityEngine.CoreModule", None)}
        assert listed["objects"] == 5 and not listed["truncated"]
        assert listed["stats"]["stoppedMs"] >= 0
        # Nothing done while the world ran, the root array held by a GC
        # handle, every mark cleared
        assert target.send("liveness", 0) == (0, 1)

        # Unity objects by their names, plain objects by their class
        instances = ask("browse_instances", classes["Game.Combat"]["klass"])
        assert [entry["name"] for entry in instances["instances"]] == ["Miranda", "Young Wolf"]
        instances = ask("browse_instances", classes["Game.Inventory"]["klass"])
        assert [entry["name"] for entry in instances["instances"]] == [None]
        assert target.send("liveness", 0) == (0, 1)  # from the objects read

        listed = ask("browse_classes", "wolf")
        assert {entry["name"]: entry["matched"] for entry in listed["classes"]
                if entry["matched"]} == {"Game.Combat": 1, "UnityEngine.GameObject": 1}
        instances = ask("browse_instances", classes["Game.Combat"]["klass"], "wolf")
        assert [entry["name"] for entry in instances["instances"]] == ["Young Wolf"]
        assert target.send("liveness", 0) == (0, 2)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_object_browser_keeps_as_many_objects_as_the_setting_says(tmp_path, qt_app, monkeypatch):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.core import settings
    from grembyte.features.scripts import ScriptWorker

    get = settings.get
    limit = {"value": 3}
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "get", lambda key: limit["value"]
                        if key == "object_browser_limit" else get(key))
    target = _MonoTarget(_build(tmp_path, ("FAKE_LIVENESS_BLOCKS", "FAKE_LIVENESS_UNITY6")))
    worker = ScriptWorker(target.pid)
    answers, failed = [], []
    worker.classes_browsed.connect(lambda _request, answer: answers.append(answer))
    worker.browse_failed.connect(lambda _request, message: failed.append(message))

    def browse():
        answers.clear()
        worker.browse_classes()
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: target.send("tick", 0) and (answers or failed))
        assert not failed, failed
        return answers[0]

    try:
        target.send("spawn", 0)
        worker.start()
        # 3 of the 5 objects kept, the buffer allocated for 3
        listed = browse()
        assert listed["objects"] == 3 and listed["truncated"]
        assert sum(entry["count"] for entry in listed["classes"]) == 3
        # A larger limit takes effect with the next read
        limit["value"] = 100_000
        listed = browse()
        assert listed["objects"] == 5 and not listed["truncated"]
        # Every mark cleared either way
        assert target.send("liveness", 0)[0] == 0
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()
```

```py
"""The native function monitor: calls of a test game's functions (see native_monitor.py)."""

import subprocess

import pytest

from grembyte.features.native_monitor import (
    argument_name,
    change_numbers,
    parse_location,
    signed,
)

from tests.test_hooks import (  # pylint: disable=unused-import
    _Target,
    _wait_for,
    fixture_qt_app,
    fixture_translations,
    requires_target,
)


_TARGET_SOURCE = r"""
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

struct Hero {
    char name[16];
    int level;
    unsigned char strength;
    unsigned char dexterity;
    short hit_points;
};

static struct Hero hero = { "Imoen", 1, 10, 10, 8 };

/* noinline: each is a function of its own, as in a real game */
__attribute__((noinline)) int roll_abilities(struct Hero *self, int seed) {
    self->strength = (unsigned char)seed;
    self->dexterity = (unsigned char)(seed + 1);
    return self->strength + self->dexterity;
}

__attribute__((noinline)) void rename_hero(struct Hero *self, const char *name) {
    strncpy(self->name, name, sizeof self->name - 1);
}

/* Floating point arguments and result arrive in xmm registers */
static float speed = 1.0f;

__attribute__((noinline)) float set_speed(float factor, double bonus) {
    speed = factor * 2.0f + (float)bonus;
    return speed;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("%d 0\n", getpid());
    fflush(stdout);
    char cmd[16];
    int value;
    while (scanf("%15s %d", cmd, &value) == 2) {
        if (strcmp(cmd, "roll") == 0)
            roll_abilities(&hero, value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "rename") == 0)
            rename_hero(&hero, value ? "Minsc" : "Boo");
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "speed") == 0)
            hero.level = (int)set_speed(value / 2.0f, 0.25);
        printf("%d 0\n", hero.strength);
        fflush(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


def _build(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "game.c").write_text(_TARGET_SOURCE)
    binary = tmp_path / "game"
    subprocess.run(["gcc", "-O1", str(tmp_path / "game.c"), "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    return binary


def test_locations_are_addresses_module_offsets_or_names():
    assert parse_location(" 0x55AAe4095790 ") == {"address": "0x55aae4095790"}
    assert parse_location("BaldursGate+0x606e50") == {"module": "BaldursGate",
                                                      "offset": 0x606e50}
    assert parse_location("libc.so.6 + 16") == {"module": "libc.so.6", "offset": 16}
    assert parse_location("_ZN13CDerivedStatsaSERKS_") == {"name": "_ZN13CDerivedStatsaSERKS_"}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        parse_location("  ")


def test_arguments_values_and_changes_read_as_numbers():
    assert [argument_name(i, "linux") for i in (0, 5, 6)] == ["rdi", "r9", "arg6"]
    assert [argument_name(i, "windows") for i in (0, 3, 4)] == ["rcx", "r9", "arg4"]
    # 32-bit Windows: ecx first (this of MSVC's C++ methods), then the stack
    assert [argument_name(i, "windows", "ia32") for i in (0, 1, 2)] == ["ecx", "arg0", "arg1"]
    assert [argument_name(i, "linux", "ia32") for i in (0, 1)] == ["arg0", "arg1"]
    assert signed("0xffffffffffffffff") == -1
    assert signed("0x11") == 17
    assert change_numbers("0e", "11") == (14, 17)
    assert change_numbers("0800", "1000") == (8, 16)
    assert change_numbers("00" * 9, "11" * 9) is None


@requires_target
def test_native_monitor_logs_arguments_result_caller_and_changes(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.native_monitor import NativeMonitorWorker

    target = _Target(_build(tmp_path))
    worker = NativeMonitorWorker(target.pid)
    added, removed, calls, counts, failed = {}, [], [], {}, []
    worker.added.connect(added.__setitem__)
    worker.removed.connect(removed.append)
    worker.calls.connect(lambda logged, numbers: (calls.extend(logged), counts.update(numbers)))
    worker.add_failed.connect(lambda monitor_id, message: failed.append((monitor_id, message)))
    worker.command_failed.connect(lambda action, message: failed.append((action, message)))
    worker.worker_failed.connect(lambda message: failed.append(("worker", message)))

    def wait(predicate):
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: predicate() or failed)

    try:
        worker.start()
        worker.add(1, {"name": "roll_abilities"})
        worker.add(3, {"name": "no_such_function"})
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: 1 in added and failed)
        assert [monitor_id for monitor_id, _message in failed] == [3]
        assert added[1]["symbol"] == "roll_abilities"
        assert added[1]["where"].startswith("game+0x")
        failed.clear()
        # The same function by module and offset, a second time; then removed
        worker.add(2, parse_location(added[1]["where"]), arguments=2, dump=0)
        wait(lambda: 2 in added)
        assert added[2]["address"] == added[1]["address"]
        worker.remove(2)
        wait(lambda: removed)

        assert target.send("roll", 17) == (17, 0)
        wait(lambda: calls)
        call = calls[0]
        assert worker.platform == "linux"
        assert call["monitorId"] == 1
        assert call["thread"] == target.pid
        assert len(call["args"]) == 4
        assert call["args"][0]["text"] == "Imoen"  # the hero's name starts the struct
        assert int(call["args"][1]["value"], 16) == 17
        assert int(call["result"]["value"], 16) & 0xffffffff == 17 + 18
        assert call["callerWhere"].startswith("game+0x")
        assert call["callerSymbol"].startswith("main")
        # strength and dexterity are side by side, after the name and the level
        assert [(change["arg"], change["offset"], change["before"], change["after"])
                for change in call["changes"]] == [(0, 20, "0a0a", "1112")]
        assert int(call["changes"][0]["address"], 16) == int(call["args"][0]["value"], 16) + 20
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: counts.get(1, {}).get("calls") == 1)

        worker.add(4, {"name": "rename_hero"})
        wait(lambda: 4 in added)
        calls.clear()
        target.send("rename", 1)
        wait(lambda: calls)
        assert calls[0]["args"][1]["text"] == "Minsc"
        assert calls[0]["changes"][0]["offset"] == 0
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()

def test_native_monitor_window_shows_calls_and_changed_fields(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):

        # The raw registers, as before the guess
        dialog.signature_check.setChecked(False)

        assert 'rsi=15' in dialog.log.data(dialog.log.index(0, 3))
        assert dialog.log.data(dialog.log.index(0, 4)) == "31"
        assert dialog.log.data(dialog.log.index(0, 6)) == "1"

        dialog.changes_table.selectRow(0)
        dialog.memory_button.click()

        # Removing a function stops its log; the other one goes on.

        assert dialog.log.data(dialog.log.index(1, 2)) == "rename_hero"
        dialog.changes_check.setChecked(True)

    finally:
        dialog.close()
        target.close()

def test_native_monitor_shows_float_arguments_and_results(tmp_path, qt_app, translations):

def _second_instruction(binary, function):
    """Distance of the second instruction of ``function`` in ``binary`` from its start."""
    listing = subprocess.run(["objdump", "-d", "--no-show-raw-insn", str(binary)],
                             check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    body = listing.split(f"<{function}>:\n", 1)[1].split("\n\n", 1)[0]
    first, second = (int(line.split(":")[0].strip(), 16) for line in body.splitlines()[:2])
    return second - first


@requires_target
def test_an_address_inside_a_function_is_probed_as_an_instruction(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.native_monitor import FUNCTION, INSTRUCTION, NativeMonitorWorker

    binary = _build(tmp_path)
    distance = _second_instruction(binary, "roll_abilities")
    target = _Target(binary)
    worker = NativeMonitorWorker(target.pid)
    added, calls, failed = {}, [], []
    worker.added.connect(added.__setitem__)
    worker.calls.connect(lambda logged, _counts: calls.extend(logged))
    worker.add_failed.connect(lambda monitor_id, message: failed.append((monitor_id, message)))
    worker.worker_failed.connect(lambda message: failed.append(("worker", message)))
    try:
        worker.start()
        # Where the function is: its first instruction, chosen as an instruction
        worker.add(0, {"name": "roll_abilities"}, kind=INSTRUCTION)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: 0 in added or failed)
        assert added[0]["kind"] == INSTRUCTION and "function" not in added[0]
        inside = int(added[0]["address"], 16) + distance
        # Right behind a hooked address: Frida would patch into its jump
        worker.add(5, {"address": hex(inside)})
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: failed)
        assert failed[0][0] == 5 and "too close" in failed[0][1]
        failed.clear()
        worker.remove(0)
        worker.add(1, {"address": hex(inside)})
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: 1 in added or failed)
        assert not failed
        assert added[1]["kind"] == INSTRUCTION
        assert added[1]["functionName"] == "roll_abilities"
        assert added[1]["symbol"].startswith("roll_abilities+0x")
        # The game computes as before: its stack was left alone.
        for value in (12, 13, 14):
            assert target.send("roll", value) == (value, 0)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: len(calls) == 3)
        registers = dict(calls[0]["registers"])
        assert int(registers["rsi"]["value"], 16) == 12
        assert registers["rdi"]["text"] == "Imoen"
        assert "args" not in calls[0]

        # The enclosing function, as the answer names it: its start is
        # patched as far as the probe (a short function), so not both.
        worker.add(2, {"address": added[1]["function"]}, kind=FUNCTION)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: failed)
        assert failed[0][0] == 2 and "too close" in failed[0][1]
        failed.clear()
        worker.remove(1)
        worker.add(3, {"address": added[1]["function"]}, kind=FUNCTION)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: 3 in added or failed)
        assert added[3]["kind"] == FUNCTION and "function" not in added[3]
        calls.clear()
        assert target.send("roll", 9) == (9, 0)
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: calls)
        assert int(calls[0]["result"]["value"], 16) & 0xffffffff == 9 + 10
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()
```

```py
"""The native trace: Stalker follows a test game's threads (see native_trace.py)."""

import subprocess

from grembyte.features.native_trace import (
    NativeFunction,
    TraceModule,
    apply_names,
    foreign_code,
    thread_activity,
)

from grembyte.platform.linux import parse_maps
from tests.test_hooks import (  # pylint: disable=unused-import
    _Target,
    _wait_for,
    fixture_qt_app,
    fixture_translations,
    linux_only,
    requires_target,
)


_TARGET_SOURCE = r"""
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <unistd.h>

static volatile int gold = 100;
static volatile int frames;

/* noinline: each is a function of its own, as in a real game */
__attribute__((noinline)) void frame(int x) { frames += x; }
__attribute__((noinline)) void spend_gold(int amount) { gold -= amount; }
__attribute__((noinline)) void buy_item(int price) { spend_gold(price); }
__attribute__((noinline)) void drink_potion(int amount) { gold += amount; }
/* volatile: called through the pointer, as by a vtable */
static void (*volatile use_item)(int) = drink_potion;

#ifdef MANY_FUNCTIONS
#include "many.h"  /* run_many(): calls thousands of functions, as a big game's code */
#endif

static void *render(void *unused) {
    (void)unused;
    for (;;) {
        frame(1);
        usleep(1000);
    }
    return NULL;
}

/* Crowd the address space like a big game: below the libraries 2.5 GB
   without a gap, then 2.5 GB with a 1 MB hole every 8 MB. A mapping without
   a hint lands in the highest hole; no 4 MB are free within 2 GB of it. */
static void crowd(void) {
    const size_t block = 8u << 20, hole = 1u << 20;
    int flags = MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_NORESERVE;
    mmap(NULL, 2560ul << 20, PROT_NONE, flags, -1, 0);
    for (int i = 0; i < 320; i++) {
        char *p = mmap(NULL, block, PROT_NONE, flags, -1, 0);
        munmap(p + block - hole, hole);
    }
}

int main(void) {
    pthread_t thread;
    if (getenv("CROWD_ADDRESS_SPACE"))
        crowd();
    pthread_create(&thread, NULL, render, NULL);
    printf("%d 0\n", getpid());
    fflush(stdout);
    char cmd[16];
    int value;
    while (scanf("%15s %d", cmd, &value) == 2) {
        if (strcmp(cmd, "tick") == 0)
            frame(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "buy") == 0)
            buy_item(value);
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "use") == 0)
            use_item(value);
#ifdef MANY_FUNCTIONS
        else if (strcmp(cmd, "many") == 0)
            run_many(value);
#endif
        printf("%d 0\n", gold);
        fflush(stdout);
    }
    return 0;
}
"""


def _many_functions(count):
    """C source of ``run_many``, which calls ``count`` functions of their own."""
    lines = ["static volatile int sink;"]
    lines += [f"__attribute__((noinline)) void many_{i}(int x) {{ sink += x * {i} + (x >> 3); }}"
              for i in range(count)]
    lines.append("static void run_many(int x) {")
    lines += [f"    many_{i}(x);" for i in range(count)]
    lines.append("}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def _build(tmp_path, many=0):
    """Compile the test game; ``many``: with that many more functions (command "many")."""
    (tmp_path / "game.c").write_text(_TARGET_SOURCE)
    command = ["gcc", "-O1", "-pthread", str(tmp_path / "game.c"), "-o", str(tmp_path / "game")]
    if many:
        (tmp_path / "many.h").write_text(_many_functions(many))
        command.append("-DMANY_FUNCTIONS")
    subprocess.run(command, check=True)
    return tmp_path / "game"


class _Recorder:
    """A NativeTraceWorker and what its signals said."""

    def __init__(self, qt_app, worker):
        self.app = qt_app
        self.worker = worker
        self.inventory: tuple = ([], [], "")
        self.inventory_ready = False
        self.started = []
        self.began = []
        self.recorded = []
        self.stopped = []
        self.failed = []
        worker.inventory_found.connect(self._on_inventory)
        worker.started.connect(self.started.append)
        worker.began.connect(self.began.append)
        worker.recorded.connect(self.recorded.append)
        worker.stopped.connect(lambda: self.stopped.append(True))
        worker.command_failed.connect(lambda action, message: self.failed.append((action, message)))
        worker.worker_failed.connect(lambda message: self.failed.append(("worker", message)))

    def _on_inventory(self, threads, modules, platform):
        self.inventory = (threads, modules, platform)
        self.inventory_ready = True

    def wait(self, predicate):
        _wait_for(self.app, lambda: predicate() or self.failed)
        assert not self.failed

    def record(self, target, phase, *commands):
        self.worker.begin(phase)
        self.wait(lambda: phase in self.began)
        self.began.clear()
        for command, value in commands:
            target.send(command, value)
        count = len(self.recorded)
        self.worker.finish()
        self.wait(lambda: len(self.recorded) > count)
        return self.recorded[-1]


@requires_target
def test_native_trace_finds_what_a_scenario_calls(tmp_path, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.native_trace import NativeTraceWorker
    from grembyte.features.trace import NEW, SAME, analyze, recording_calls

    target = _Target(_build(tmp_path))
    worker = NativeTraceWorker(target.pid)
    recorder = _Recorder(qt_app, worker)
    try:
        worker.start()
        worker.inventory()
        recorder.wait(lambda: recorder.inventory_ready)
        threads, modules, platform = recorder.inventory
        assert platform == "linux"
        assert {thread.id for thread in threads} >= {target.pid}
        assert all(thread.load is not None for thread in threads)
        # The render thread draws frames; the main thread waits for commands.
        active = {thread.id: thread.active for thread in threads}
        assert active[target.pid] is False
        assert list(active.values()).count(True) == 1
        assert [module.name for module in modules if module.game] == ["game"]

        worker.trace([thread.id for thread in threads], ["game"])
        recorder.wait(lambda: recorder.started)
        started = recorder.started[0]
        assert {key: started[key] for key in ("threads", "failed", "modules", "waiting")} == {
            "threads": len(threads), "failed": 0, "modules": 1,
            "waiting": 0}  # under Windows: not entered yet
        # Linux x86-64: gaps were filled while Stalker made its thread contexts
        assert started["steered"] >= 0

        functions = []
        baseline = recorder.record(target, "baseline", ("tick", 1), ("tick", 2))
        apply_names(functions, baseline)
        assert baseline["events"] == []
        scenario = recorder.record(target, "scenario", ("tick", 3), ("buy", 7), ("use", 2))
        apply_names(functions, scenario)
        assert target.send("tick", 0) == (95, 0)  # the game still runs, bought and drank
        assert (baseline["lost"], scenario["lost"]) == (0, 0)  # no calls lost

        rows = [row for row in analyze(scenario, baseline) if functions[row.method].module == "game"]
        verdicts = {functions[row.method].label: (row.verdict, row.calls) for row in rows}
        assert verdicts["buy_item"] == (NEW, 1)
        assert verdicts["spend_gold"] == (NEW, 1)
        assert verdicts["drink_potion"] == (NEW, 1)  # through the function pointer
        assert verdicts["frame"][0] == SAME
        # The first calls of what is new, in order, on the thread that bought
        calls = [call for call in recording_calls(scenario)
                 if functions[call.method].module == "game"]
        assert [functions[call.method].label for call in calls] == ["buy_item", "spend_gold",
                                                                   "drink_potion"]
        assert {call.thread for call in calls} == {target.pid}
        assert calls[0].time <= calls[1].time <= calls[2].time
        buy = next(function for function in functions if function.label == "buy_item")
        assert buy.location.startswith("game+0x")
        # spend_gold is called from within buy_item
        caller = int(calls[1].caller.removeprefix("game+"), 16)
        assert 0 <= caller - buy.offset < 0x40

        # Another trace after this one: the agent is loaded afresh.
        worker.stop()
        recorder.wait(lambda: recorder.stopped)
        worker.trace([target.pid], ["game"])
        recorder.wait(lambda: len(recorder.started) == 2)
        assert recorder.started[1]["threads"] == 1
        scenario = recorder.record(target, "scenario", ("buy", 1))
        worker.stop()
        recorder.wait(lambda: len(recorder.stopped) == 2)
        # The main thread waits for commands in code Stalker made: once it
        # has returned from there, the agents unload without waiting.
        assert target.send("tick", 0) == (94, 0)
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()


@requires_target
def test_native_trace_survives_a_crowded_address_space(tmp_path, qt_app, monkeypatch):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features.native_trace import NativeTraceWorker

    # Stalker found no room for its code near its thread contexts and wrote
    # to NULL (EVERSPACE crashed 0.4 s after the start).
    monkeypatch.setenv("CROWD_ADDRESS_SPACE", "1")
    target = _Target(_build(tmp_path, many=4000))
    worker = NativeTraceWorker(target.pid)
    recorder = _Recorder(qt_app, worker)
    try:
        worker.start()
        worker.inventory()
        recorder.wait(lambda: recorder.inventory_ready)
        threads, _modules, _platform = recorder.inventory
        worker.trace([thread.id for thread in threads], ["game"])
        recorder.wait(lambda: recorder.started)
        assert recorder.started[0]["steered"] > 0
        functions = []

        scenario = recorder.record(target, "scenario", ("many", 1), ("buy", 5))
        apply_names(functions, scenario)
        assert "buy_item" in {function.label for function in functions}
        assert len(functions) > 4000
        assert target.send("tick", 0) == (95, 0)  # still running
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(5000)
        target.close()

def test_functions_are_named_by_symbol_or_location():

def test_wine_unix_code_outside_the_followed_modules_runs_natively():

        "7f0000000000-7f0000100000 r-xp 00000000 08:01 3 /proton/lib/wine/x86_64-unix/ntdll.so",

@linux_only
def test_thread_activity_is_cpu_share_and_wakeups(tmp_path):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    import os

    ticks = os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK")
    task = tmp_path / "7" / "task"

    def thread(tid, total, switches=0):
        (task / str(tid)).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # utime and stime are fields 14 and 15; the name may hold spaces and ")"
        fields = ["S"] + ["0"] * 10 + [str(total), "0"] + ["0"] * 5
        (task / str(tid) / "stat").write_text(f"{tid} (Main) Thread) " + " ".join(fields))
        (task / str(tid) / "status").write_text(
            f"Name:\tMain\nvoluntary_ctxt_switches:\t{switches}\n"
            "nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches:\t1\n")

    def later(_seconds):
        thread(7, ticks)          # half a CPU over two seconds
        thread(8, 0, switches=3)  # woke up, too briefly for a tick
    for tid in (7, 8, 9):
        thread(tid, 0)
    activity = thread_activity(7, [7, 8, 9, 10], seconds=2, proc_root=str(tmp_path), sleep=later)
    assert activity == {7: (0.5, True), 8: (0.0, True), 9: (0.0, False)}


def test_calls_filter_reads_counts_ranges_bounds_and_multiples():
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    import pytest

    from grembyte.features.trace import calls_filter

    assert calls_filter("") is None
    assert calls_filter(" , ") is None
    assert [calls for calls in range(13) if calls_filter("%3")(calls)] == [0, 3, 6, 9, 12]
    assert [calls for calls in range(9) if calls_filter("2-4, >=7")(calls)] == [2, 3, 4, 7, 8]
    assert [calls for calls in range(6) if calls_filter("<2, 5")(calls)] == [0, 1, 5]
    for text in ("x", "%0", "3-", ">"):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            calls_filter(text)


def test_rows_sort_by_column_and_filter_by_name_and_calls(qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,unused-argument
    from PySide6.QtCore import Qt  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

    from grembyte.features.trace import NEW, SAME, TraceRow
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.native_trace import NativeRowModel
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.trace import RowFilterBar

    functions = [NativeFunction(0x401000, "game", 0x1000, "roll_dice"),
                 NativeFunction(0x402000, "game", 0x2000, "draw_ui"),
                 NativeFunction(0x7f0000, "", None)]
    rows = [TraceRow(0, 3, 1.0, None, NEW, 0), TraceRow(1, 600, 200.0, 190.0, SAME, None),
            TraceRow(2, 7, 2.3, None, NEW, 1)]
    model = NativeRowModel(translations)

    def labels():
        return [model.data(model.index(row, 2)) for row in range(model.rowCount())]

    model.set_items(functions, rows)
    assert labels() == ["roll_dice", "draw_ui", "0x7f0000"]  # as analyze ordered them
    model.sort(3, Qt.SortOrder.DescendingOrder)
    assert labels() == ["draw_ui", "0x7f0000", "roll_dice"]
    model.set_items(functions, rows[:1] + rows[2:])  # the sort stays
    assert labels() == ["0x7f0000", "roll_dice"]
    model.sort(2)
    assert labels() == ["0x7f0000", "roll_dice"]

    bar = RowFilterBar(translations)
    changes = []
    bar.changed.connect(lambda: changes.append(True))

    def shown():
        return [row.method for row in rows if bar.accepts(row, functions[row.method].signature)]

    bar.calls_input.setText("%3")
    assert shown() == [0, 1]
    bar.calls_input.setText("%3x")  # invalid: the last valid filter stays
    assert shown() == [0, 1] and len(changes) == 1
    bar.calls_input.setText("")
    bar.name_input.setText("GAME+0x")
    assert shown() == [0, 1]
    bar.name_input.setText("roll game")
    assert shown() == [0]


def test_under_wine_the_agent_measures_the_threads(qt_app, monkeypatch):
    # pylint: disable=unused-argument,protected-access,import-outside-toplevel
    from grembyte.features import native_trace

    monkeypatch.setattr(native_trace, "is_wine_process", lambda _pid: True)
    worker = native_trace.NativeTraceWorker(123)
    found = []
    worker.inventory_found.connect(lambda threads, modules, _platform:
                                   found.append((threads, modules)))
    asked = []

    class Api:  # pylint: disable=too-few-public-methods
        @staticmethod
        def inventory(*seconds):
            asked.append(seconds)
            return {"platform": "windows", "modules": [], "threads": [
                {"id": 336, "name": "", "state": "running", "load": 0.54},
                {"id": 400, "name": "idle", "state": "running", "load": 0.0},
                {"id": 404, "name": "", "state": "running", "load": None},
            ]}

    worker._run_command(Api(), "inventory", None)
    assert asked == [(native_trace.WINE_LOAD_SECONDS,)]
    threads = found[0][0]
    assert [(t.id, t.load, t.active) for t in threads] == [
        (336, 0.54, True), (400, 0.0, False), (404, None, None)]
```

`tests/test_object_browser.py`:

```py
"""The object browser window (see grembyte.ui.widgets.object_browser)."""

from grembyte.ui.localization import load_translations
from grembyte.ui.widgets.object_browser import (
    GAME_PACKAGES,
    filter_words,
    is_singleton,
    name_matches,
    object_text,
)

from tests.test_scripts import _FakeScriptWorker, fixture_qt_app  # pylint: disable=unused-import


def _entry(name, count, package, role=None, matched=0, klass=None):
    return {"klass": klass or f"0x{abs(hash(name)) % 0xffffff:x}", "name": name,
            "cppName": f"U{name}", "package": package, "count": count, "role": role,
            "matched": matched}


_CLASSES = {"objects": 5009, "classes": [
    _entry("AbilitySystemComponent", 1, "/Script/GameplayAbilities"),
    _entry("BP_Hero_C", 3, "/Game/Blueprints", klass="0x1000"),
    _entry("HeroAttributeSet", 2, "/Script/FakeGame"),
    _entry("Object", 5000, "/Script/CoreUObject"),
    _entry("PlayerController", 1, "/Script/Engine", role="PlayerController"),
    _entry("GameManager", 1, "/Script/FakeGame"),
    _entry("WidgetTree", 1, "/Script/Engine"),
]}


def _is_framework(name):
    return name.startswith(("/Script/Engine", "/Script/CoreUObject", "/Script/Gameplay"))


def test_names_and_singletons():
    assert filter_words("  Hero  SIDE ") == ["hero", "side"]
    hero = _entry("BP_Hero_C", 3, "/Game/Blueprints")
    assert name_matches(hero, ["hero", "ubp"]) and not name_matches(hero, ["side"])
    assert object_text({"name": "BP_Hero_C_0", "address": "0x10"}) == '"BP_Hero_C_0"@0x10'
    # Plain C# objects have no name; strings may have line breaks
    assert object_text({"name": None, "address": "0x20"}, "Game.Inventory") == \
        "Game.Inventory@0x20"
    assert object_text({"name": "a\nb", "address": "0x30"}) == '"a b"@0x30'
    # An engine single-instance class, or a game class with one object
    assert is_singleton(_entry("PlayerController", 1, "/Script/Engine", "PlayerController"),
                        _is_framework)
    assert is_singleton(_entry("GameManager", 1, "/Script/FakeGame"), _is_framework)
    assert not is_singleton(_entry("WidgetTree", 1, "/Script/Engine"), _is_framework)
    assert not is_singleton(_entry("Manager", 2, "/Script/FakeGame"), _is_framework)


def _names(dialog):
    tree = dialog.tree
    return [tree.topLevelItem(row).text(0) for row in range(tree.topLevelItemCount())]


def test_window_lists_classes_and_opens_their_objects(qt_app, monkeypatch):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,unused-argument,protected-access
    from grembyte.ui.widgets import scripts
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.object_browser import ObjectBrowserDialog

    monkeypatch.setattr(scripts, "ScriptWorker", _FakeScriptWorker)
    translations = load_translations("de")
    panel = scripts.ScriptPanel(translations)
    panel.set_process(4242)
    dialog = ObjectBrowserDialog(translations, panel, is_framework=_is_framework)
    try:
        worker = panel._worker
        assert worker.requests[-1] == ("browse_classes", "", False)
        worker.classes_browsed.emit(len(worker.requests), _CLASSES)
        assert len(_names(dialog)) == 7
        assert dialog.status_label.text() == "7 Klassen, 5009 Objekte"
        combo = dialog.package_combo
        assert [combo.itemText(i) for i in range(3)] == [
            "Alle Pakete (5009)", "Nur Spiel (6)", "/Game/Blueprints (3)"]

        # Packages: the game's own, or one
        combo.setCurrentIndex(combo.findData(GAME_PACKAGES))
        assert _names(dialog) == ["BP_Hero_C", "HeroAttributeSet", "GameManager"]
        combo.setCurrentIndex(combo.findData("/Script/Engine"))
        assert _names(dialog) == ["PlayerController", "WidgetTree"]
        combo.setCurrentIndex(0)

        # Singletons: engine roles and game classes with one object
        dialog.singleton_check.setChecked(True)
        assert _names(dialog) == ["PlayerController", "GameManager"]
        assert dialog.tree.topLevelItem(0).text(3) == "PlayerController"
        assert dialog.tree.topLevelItem(1).text(3) == "ein Objekt"
        dialog.singleton_check.setChecked(False)

        # Opening a class asks for its objects; one opens in the inspector
        hero = dialog.tree.topLevelItem(1)
        hero.setExpanded(True)
        assert worker.requests[-1] == ("browse_instances", "0x1000", "", False)
        worker.instances_browsed.emit(len(worker.requests), {
            "count": 3, "truncated": False, "instances": [
                {"address": "0x7f00", "name": "BP_Hero_C_0", "outer": "/Game/Maps/Start"},
                {"address": "0x7f80", "name": "BP_Hero_C_1", "outer": "/Game/Maps/Start"},
                {"address": "0x7fc0", "name": "Sidekick", "outer": "WidgetTree_7"}]})
        assert [hero.child(i).text(0) for i in range(hero.childCount())] == [
            '"BP_Hero_C_0"@0x7f00', '"BP_Hero_C_1"@0x7f80', '"Sidekick"@0x7fc0']
        assert hero.child(2).toolTip(0) == "Sidekick in WidgetTree_7"
        assert not dialog.inspect_button.isEnabled()
        dialog.tree.setCurrentItem(hero.child(0))
        assert dialog.inspect_button.isEnabled()
        opened = []
        monkeypatch.setattr(panel.inspections, "inspect",
                            lambda target, name="", instance_name=None: opened.append(
                                (target, name, instance_name)))
        dialog.inspect_button.click()
        assert opened == [({"address": "0x7f00"}, "BP_Hero_C_0", "BP_Hero_C_0")]

        # The filter: class names at once, objects' names once the agent counted
        dialog.filter_input.setText("side")
        assert _names(dialog) == []
        dialog._filter_timer.timeout.emit()
        assert worker.requests[-1] == ("browse_classes", "side", False)
        matched = {"objects": 5009, "classes": [
            {**entry, "matched": 1 if entry["name"] == "BP_Hero_C" else 0}
            for entry in _CLASSES["classes"]]}
        worker.classes_browsed.emit(len(worker.requests), matched)
        assert _names(dialog) == ["BP_Hero_C"]
        hero = dialog.tree.topLevelItem(0)
        assert hero.text(1) == "1 / 3"
        # Found by its objects only: opened by itself, its objects filtered
        assert hero.isExpanded()
        assert worker.requests[-1] == ("browse_instances", "0x1000", "side", False)
        worker.instances_browsed.emit(len(worker.requests), {
            "count": 1, "truncated": False, "instances": [
                {"address": "0x7fc0", "name": "Sidekick", "outer": "WidgetTree_7"}]})
        assert hero.childCount() == 1

        # A class matching by name shows with all its objects
        dialog.filter_input.setText("hero")
        assert _names(dialog) == ["BP_Hero_C", "HeroAttributeSet"]
        assert dialog.tree.topLevelItem(0).text(1) == "3"

        # Templates and reflection: read anew
        dialog.internal_check.setChecked(True)
        assert worker.requests[-1] == ("browse_classes", "hero", True)
    finally:
        dialog.close()
        panel.set_process(None)
```

```py
"""The offline catalog: games read before, shown from the catalog cache."""

import time

from grembyte.engines.registry import engine_by_id
from grembyte.features import catalog_cache, games
from grembyte.features.call_graph import CallGraphWorker, _OfflineApi
from grembyte.features.catalog import CachedCatalogWorker, catalog_methods

from tests.test_hooks import _wait_for, fixture_qt_app, fixture_translations  # pylint: disable=unused-import

_CLASSES = [["Game.Loot", [
    ["Take", "(int&,int)", "System.Void", True, 0x06000002, "Game.Loot:Take (int&,int)", 16, 0],
    ["Roll", "()", "System.Int32", False, 0x06000003, "Game.Loot:Roll ()", 0, 0]]]]
_ASSEMBLIES = [
    {"name": "Assembly-CSharp", "mvid": "game-mvid", "file": "C:/Game/Assembly-CSharp.dll",
     "classes": 1},
    {"name": "Plugins", "mvid": "plugins-mvid", "file": "C:/Game/Plugins.dll", "classes": 3},
    {"name": "mscorlib", "mvid": None, "file": "C:/Game/mscorlib.dll", "classes": 900},
]


def _remember(monkeypatch, path="C:\\Games\\Dark Heresy\\WH40KDH.exe", pid=4242):
    monkeypatch.setitem(games._programs, pid, path)  # pylint: disable=protected-access
    games.remember(pid, "mono", _ASSEMBLIES)


def test_games_are_remembered_per_program(monkeypatch):
    _remember(monkeypatch)
    time.sleep(0.01)
    _remember(monkeypatch, "/home/frank/Games/Other/Other.x86_64", pid=4243)
    # The same program again replaces its entry.
    _remember(monkeypatch, pid=4244)

    known = games.known_games()
    assert [game.name for game in known] == ["WH40KDH.exe", "Other.x86_64"]
    game = known[0]
    assert game.engine == "mono" and game.path == "C:\\Games\\Dark Heresy\\WH40KDH.exe"
    assert game.mvids() == {"Assembly-CSharp": "game-mvid", "Plugins": "plugins-mvid",
                            "mscorlib": None}
    assert len(list(games.games_dir().glob("*.json"))) == 2


def test_cached_worker_reads_the_catalog_without_a_process(monkeypatch):
    _remember(monkeypatch)
    catalog_cache.store("mono", "Assembly-CSharp", "game-mvid", _CLASSES)
    game = games.known_games()[0]
    worker = CachedCatalogWorker(game, engine=engine_by_id("mono"))
    loaded, failed, cached = {}, {}, []
    worker.assembly_loaded.connect(loaded.__setitem__)
    worker.assembly_failed.connect(failed.__setitem__)
    worker.assembly_cached.connect(cached.append)
    worker.run()  # on this thread: nothing to wait for

    assert loaded == {"Assembly-CSharp": catalog_methods("Assembly-CSharp", _CLASSES)}
    assert cached == ["Assembly-CSharp"]
    # Plugins was never read; mscorlib is framework and not asked for.
    assert failed == {"Plugins": CachedCatalogWorker.NOT_CACHED}


def test_offline_catalog_dialog(monkeypatch, qt_app, translations):
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel,protected-access,unused-argument
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.catalog import CatalogDialog

    _remember(monkeypatch)
    catalog_cache.store("mono", "Assembly-CSharp", "game-mvid", _CLASSES)
    game = games.known_games()[0]
    dialog = CatalogDialog(translations, None, engine=engine_by_id("mono"), game=game)
    monitored = []
    dialog.monitor_requested.connect(monitored.append)
    try:
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: dialog._worker is None)
        assert dialog.model.rowCount() == 2
        assert "(offline, Stand " in dialog.windowTitle() and "WH40KDH.exe" in dialog.windowTitle()
        assert "nicht im Zwischenspeicher: Plugins" in dialog.status_label.text()
        assert dialog.reload_button.isHidden()
        dialog.view.selectRow(0)
        assert dialog.calls_button.isEnabled() and not dialog.monitor_button.isEnabled()
        dialog.view.doubleClicked.emit(dialog.model.index(0, 1))
        assert not monitored
    finally:
        dialog.close()


def test_offline_call_graph_answers_from_the_cache(monkeypatch, qt_app):
    # pylint: disable=protected-access,unused-argument
    _remember(monkeypatch)
    catalog_cache.store("mono", "Assembly-CSharp", "game-mvid", _CLASSES)
    # Take calls Roll; the index was made while the game ran.
    catalog_cache.store("mono", "Assembly-CSharp", "game-mvid",
                        {"targets": [["Assembly-CSharp", 0x06000003, "Game.Loot:Roll ()"]],
                         "calls": [[0x06000002, [["call", 0]]]], "references": {}},
                        kind=catalog_cache.CALLS)
    game = games.known_games()[0]
    worker = CallGraphWorker(None, engine=engine_by_id("mono"), game=game)
    callees, callers, failed = [], [], []
    worker.callees_found.connect(lambda _id, _m, calls, _body: callees.append(calls))
    worker.callers_found.connect(lambda _id, _m, calls, missing: callers.append((calls, missing)))
    worker.request_failed.connect(lambda _id, message: failed.append(message))
    methods = {m.name: m for m in catalog_methods("Assembly-CSharp", _CLASSES)}
    api = _OfflineApi(game)

    worker._answer_callees(api, 1, methods["Take"])
    assert [call.method.name for call in callees[0]] == ["Roll"]
    worker._answer_callers(api, 2, methods["Roll"])
    calls, missing = callers[0]
    assert [call.method.name for call in calls] == ["Take"] and missing == ["Plugins"]

    # A method of an assembly without a call index needs the game.
    catalog_cache.store("mono", "Plugins", "plugins-mvid", _CLASSES)
    worker.start()
    worker.callees(catalog_methods("Plugins", _CLASSES)[0])
    try:
        _wait_for(qt_app, lambda: failed)
        assert failed == [CallGraphWorker.NOT_CACHED]
    finally:
        worker.requestInterruption()
        worker.wait(2000)

def test_catalog_search_accepts_wildcards():
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.catalog import matches  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    method = catalog_methods("Assembly-CSharp", [["Game.PlayerCombat", [
        ["ApplyDamage", "(int)", "System.Void", False, 0x06000004,
         "Game.PlayerCombat:ApplyDamage (int)", 0, 0]]]])[0]
    assert matches(["player*damage"], method)
    assert matches(["game.player?ombat", "apply"], method)
    assert matches(["*"], method) and matches(["player"], method)
    assert not matches(["damage*player"], method)
    assert not matches(["player.damage"], method)  # "." is literal, not "any character"


def test_catalog_search_finds_parameter_and_return_types():
    from grembyte.ui.widgets.catalog import matches  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    purchase, preset = catalog_methods("/Script/Alabama", [["AlabamaCheatManager", [
        ["PurchaseAttribute", "(EPrimaryAttribute,int32)", "void", False, 1,
         "AlabamaCheatManager:PurchaseAttribute (EPrimaryAttribute,int32)", 0, 0],
        ["GetPreset", "(FName)", "EPrimaryAttribute", False, 2,
         "AlabamaCheatManager:GetPreset (FName)", 0, 0]]]], engine="unreal")
    assert matches(["type:eprimaryattribute"], purchase)
    assert matches(["type:*attribute", "cheat"], preset)  # the return type, with the class
    assert not matches(["eprimaryattribute"], purchase)  # plain words: class and name
    assert not matches(["type:purchase"], purchase)
```
